The museum keeps its most valuable paintings upstairs.
The hotel gave us its nicest room.
My grandparents ate at the town's oldest bakery every Sunday.
Lake Baikal is the world's deepest lake.
It's this year's biggest film.
She's the company's youngest manager.
That was last night's most exciting moment.
The school's best students won prizes.
Is this your most comfortable chair?
What's your biggest problem at work?
Our loudest neighbor plays the drums at night.
Our closest neighbors live a mile away.
Have you seen the band's newest video?
My best friend's oldest sister is a pilot.
I like this phone. Its best feature is the camera.
Our hardest job this week is cleaning the garage.
Tell me about your happiest childhood memory.

examples.heading: ① our / their + 最高級 + 名詞

items.en: We're sending our latest catalogs to all our customers.
items.zh: 我們要把最新的型錄寄給所有顧客。

items.en: People wear their best clothes to the festival.
items.zh: 大家穿上自己最好的衣服去參加節慶。

items.en: Our biggest customer is a hotel chain.
items.zh: 我們最大的客戶是一家連鎖飯店。

items.en: Their youngest child just started school.
items.zh: 他們最小的孩子剛開始上學。

items.en: Our newest store opens next month.
items.zh: 我們最新的分店下個月開幕。

items.en: Their cheapest room was still too expensive for us.
items.zh: 他們最便宜的房間對我們來說還是太貴。

examples.heading: ② my / your / his / her + 最高級 + 名詞

items.en: He showed me his latest paintings.
items.zh: 他給我看他最新的畫作。

items.en: Her greatest fear is flying.
items.zh: 她最怕的是坐飛機。

items.en: Bring your strongest bag for the books.
items.zh: 帶你最耐用的袋子來裝書。

items.en: My earliest memory is of my grandmother's garden.
items.zh: 我最早的記憶是我奶奶的花園。

items.en: His fastest time was under ten seconds.
items.zh: 他最快的成績不到十秒。

examples.heading: ③ its + 最高級 + 名詞

items.en: The company sold its oldest factory.
items.zh: 公司把最老的工廠賣掉了。

items.en: The team played its best game of the season.
items.zh: 這支球隊打出了本季最好的一場比賽。

items.en: The museum keeps its most valuable paintings upstairs.
items.zh: 博物館把最珍貴的畫放在樓上。

items.en: The hotel gave us its nicest room.
items.zh: 飯店給了我們最好的房間。

examples.heading: ④ 名詞's + 最高級 + 名詞

items.en: My grandparents ate at the town's oldest bakery every Sunday.
items.zh: 我爺爺奶奶每個星期天都去鎮上最老的麵包店吃東西。

items.en: Lake Baikal is the world's deepest lake.
items.zh: 貝加爾湖是世界上最深的湖。

items.en: It's this year's biggest film.
items.zh: 那是今年最賣座的電影。

items.en: She's the company's youngest manager.
items.zh: 她是公司最年輕的經理。

items.en: That was last night's most exciting moment.
items.zh: 那是昨晚最刺激的時刻。

items.en: The school's best students won prizes.
items.zh: 學校最優秀的學生得了獎。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的句型

items.en: Is this your most comfortable chair?
items.zh: 這是你最舒服的椅子嗎？

items.en: What's your biggest problem at work?
items.zh: 你工作上最大的問題是什麼？

items.en: Our loudest neighbor plays the drums at night.
items.zh: 我們最吵的鄰居晚上打鼓。

items.en: Our closest neighbors live a mile away.
items.zh: 我們最近的鄰居住在一英里外。

items.en: Have you seen the band's newest video?
items.zh: 你看過那個樂團最新的 MV 嗎？

items.en: My best friend's oldest sister is a pilot.
items.zh: 我最好的朋友的大姊是機師。

items.en: I like this phone. Its best feature is the camera.
items.zh: 我喜歡這支手機，它最好的功能是相機。

items.en: Our hardest job this week is cleaning the garage.
items.zh: 我們這週最辛苦的工作是清理車庫。

items.en: Tell me about your happiest childhood memory.
items.zh: 跟我說說你童年最快樂的回憶。

title: We don't think our English is good enough.
translation: 我們覺得我們的英文不夠好。
name: enough 修飾形容詞
sentences: My room is big enough for a desk and a bed.
Is the soup hot enough, or should I heat it up?
Don't worry, your English is good enough for the job.
The bread is soft enough for Grandma.
Is the ladder long enough?
The rain stopped, and it was warm enough for a walk.
We don't think our English is good enough yet.
The coffee isn't warm enough. Can you heat it up?
The bed wasn't long enough for my tall brother.
The car isn't big enough for all of us.
My phone isn't fast enough for this game.
The hall wasn't quiet enough for the exam.
She's old enough to drive.
He isn't tall enough to reach the shelf.
The ice is thick enough to walk on.
Is the water clean enough to drink?
I wasn't fast enough to catch the bus.
Are you strong enough to carry this box?
Is the water warm enough for the kids?
The room is big enough for three beds.
This jacket isn't warm enough for winter.
The cake is big enough for everyone.
Is this dress nice enough for the wedding?
The table was long enough for twelve people.
The bananas look ripe enough to eat.
Do you feel well enough to go to school?
The plan seems good enough to me.
When it gets dark enough, we can see the stars.
The water didn't get hot enough for tea.
You don't look old enough to have a son in college!

examples.heading: ① 形容詞 + enough

items.en: My room is big enough for a desk and a bed.
items.zh: 我的房間夠大，放得下一張書桌和一張床。

items.en: Is the soup hot enough, or should I heat it up?
items.zh: 湯夠熱嗎？還是要我再熱一下？

items.en: Don't worry, your English is good enough for the job.
items.zh: 別擔心，你的英文夠應付這份工作。

items.en: The bread is soft enough for Grandma.
items.zh: 這個麵包夠軟，奶奶可以吃。

items.en: Is the ladder long enough?
items.zh: 梯子夠長嗎？

items.en: The rain stopped, and it was warm enough for a walk.
items.zh: 雨停了，天氣暖到可以去散步。

examples.heading: ② not + 形容詞 + enough

items.en: We don't think our English is good enough yet.
items.zh: 我們覺得我們的英文還不夠好。

items.en: The coffee isn't warm enough. Can you heat it up?
items.zh: 咖啡不夠熱，你可以幫我熱一下嗎？

items.en: The bed wasn't long enough for my tall brother.
items.zh: 那張床對我高個子的哥哥來說不夠長。

items.en: The car isn't big enough for all of us.
items.zh: 車子不夠大，我們全部坐不下。

items.en: My phone isn't fast enough for this game.
items.zh: 我的手機不夠快，跑不動這個遊戲。

items.en: The hall wasn't quiet enough for the exam.
items.zh: 那個大廳不夠安靜，沒辦法考試。

examples.heading: ③ 形容詞 + enough + to 不定詞

items.en: She's old enough to drive.
items.zh: 她已經到可以開車的年紀了。

items.en: He isn't tall enough to reach the shelf.
items.zh: 他不夠高，搆不到架子。

items.en: The ice is thick enough to walk on.
items.zh: 冰夠厚，可以在上面走。

items.en: Is the water clean enough to drink?
items.zh: 這水乾淨到可以喝嗎？

items.en: I wasn't fast enough to catch the bus.
items.zh: 我跑得不夠快，沒趕上公車。

items.en: Are you strong enough to carry this box?
items.zh: 你有力氣搬這個箱子嗎？

examples.heading: ④ 形容詞 + enough + for

items.en: Is the water warm enough for the kids?
items.zh: 水對孩子們來說夠暖嗎？

items.en: The room is big enough for three beds.
items.zh: 這個房間夠大，放得下三張床。

items.en: This jacket isn't warm enough for winter.
items.zh: 這件外套冬天穿不夠暖。

items.en: The cake is big enough for everyone.
items.zh: 蛋糕夠大，每個人都吃得到。

items.en: Is this dress nice enough for the wedding?
items.zh: 這件洋裝穿去婚禮夠正式嗎？

items.en: The table was long enough for twelve people.
items.zh: 那張桌子夠長，坐得下十二個人。

examples.heading: ⑤ look / feel / seem / get 後面

items.en: The bananas look ripe enough to eat.
items.zh: 香蕉看起來夠熟，可以吃了。

items.en: Do you feel well enough to go to school?
items.zh: 你覺得身體好到可以上學了嗎？

items.en: The plan seems good enough to me.
items.zh: 我覺得這個計畫夠好了。

items.en: When it gets dark enough, we can see the stars.
items.zh: 天色夠暗的時候，我們就看得到星星。

items.en: The water didn't get hot enough for tea.
items.zh: 水不夠熱，沒辦法泡茶。

items.en: You don't look old enough to have a son in college!
items.zh: 你看起來不像有兒子在讀大學的年紀！

title: I was lucky enough to take part in the race last November.
translation: 我很幸運，去年十一月參加了那場比賽。
name: 形容詞後的 enough 加不定詞
sentences: My daughter is old enough to walk to school alone.
He was brave enough to tell the truth.
The rope was strong enough to hold two people.
Is she tall enough to ride the roller coaster?
The room was warm enough to sleep without a blanket.
You're smart enough to solve this yourself.
Ann was quick enough to catch the cup before it fell.
Teenagers aren't always mature enough to choose a career.
My Spanish wasn't good enough to follow the film.
The ice isn't thick enough to skate on yet.
My grandmother isn't strong enough to climb the stairs.
The kids weren't patient enough to wait for dinner.
I'm not brave enough to try skydiving.
We were lucky enough to get tickets for the final.
I was lucky enough to visit Japan last spring.
She was lucky enough to find a flat near her office.
If you're lucky enough to see a whale, take a photo.
Only three people were lucky enough to win a prize.
Would you be kind enough to close the door?
A stranger was kind enough to show us the way.
My neighbor was kind enough to feed my cat last week.
Would you be kind enough to send me the details?
The teacher was kind enough to give us more time.
The test was easy enough for most students to finish in an hour.
The book is simple enough for children to read.
The bag is light enough for me to carry.
The water was shallow enough for the kids to play in.
Is the path wide enough for two bikes to pass?
The road wasn't safe enough for us to drive on at night.
The print isn't big enough for my dad to read.

examples.heading: ① 形容詞 + enough + to 不定詞

items.en: My daughter is old enough to walk to school alone.
items.zh: 我女兒已經大到可以自己走路上學了。

items.en: He was brave enough to tell the truth.
items.zh: 他有勇氣說出實話。

items.en: The rope was strong enough to hold two people.
items.zh: 那條繩子夠牢固，撐得住兩個人。

items.en: Is she tall enough to ride the roller coaster?
items.zh: 她夠高，可以坐雲霄飛車嗎？

items.en: The room was warm enough to sleep without a blanket.
items.zh: 房間夠暖，不蓋被子也能睡。

items.en: You're smart enough to solve this yourself.
items.zh: 你夠聰明，可以自己解決這個問題。

items.en: Ann was quick enough to catch the cup before it fell.
items.zh: Ann 反應夠快，在杯子掉下去之前接住了。

examples.heading: ② not + 形容詞 + enough + to 不定詞

items.en: Teenagers aren't always mature enough to choose a career.
items.zh: 青少年不一定成熟到可以自己選擇職業。

items.en: My Spanish wasn't good enough to follow the film.
items.zh: 我的西班牙文不夠好，看不懂那部電影。

items.en: The ice isn't thick enough to skate on yet.
items.zh: 冰還不夠厚，還不能在上面溜冰。

items.en: My grandmother isn't strong enough to climb the stairs.
items.zh: 我奶奶力氣不夠，爬不了樓梯。

items.en: The kids weren't patient enough to wait for dinner.
items.zh: 孩子們等不及晚餐。

items.en: I'm not brave enough to try skydiving.
items.zh: 我沒有勇氣去玩跳傘。

examples.heading: ③ lucky enough to

items.en: We were lucky enough to get tickets for the final.
items.zh: 我們很幸運，買到了決賽的票。

items.en: I was lucky enough to visit Japan last spring.
items.zh: 我很幸運，去年春天去了日本。

items.en: She was lucky enough to find a flat near her office.
items.zh: 她很幸運，在辦公室附近找到一間公寓。

items.en: If you're lucky enough to see a whale, take a photo.
items.zh: 如果你運氣好看到鯨魚，記得拍照。

items.en: Only three people were lucky enough to win a prize.
items.zh: 只有三個人幸運得獎。

examples.heading: ④ kind enough to

items.en: Would you be kind enough to close the door?
items.zh: 可以麻煩你把門關上嗎？

items.en: A stranger was kind enough to show us the way.
items.zh: 一個陌生人好心幫我們指路。

items.en: My neighbor was kind enough to feed my cat last week.
items.zh: 我的鄰居上禮拜好心幫我餵貓。

items.en: Would you be kind enough to send me the details?
items.zh: 可以麻煩你把詳細資料寄給我嗎？

items.en: The teacher was kind enough to give us more time.
items.zh: 老師好心多給了我們一些時間。

examples.heading: ⑤ 形容詞 + enough + for + 人 + to 不定詞

items.en: The test was easy enough for most students to finish in an hour.
items.zh: 考試夠簡單，大部分的學生一個小時就能寫完。

items.en: The book is simple enough for children to read.
items.zh: 這本書夠簡單，小孩也看得懂。

items.en: The bag is light enough for me to carry.
items.zh: 包包夠輕，我提得動。

items.en: The water was shallow enough for the kids to play in.
items.zh: 水夠淺，孩子們可以在裡面玩。

items.en: Is the path wide enough for two bikes to pass?
items.zh: 這條小路夠寬，兩台腳踏車可以錯身而過嗎？

items.en: The road wasn't safe enough for us to drive on at night.
items.zh: 那條路不夠安全，我們晚上不能開。

items.en: The print isn't big enough for my dad to read.
items.zh: 字印得不夠大，我爸爸看不清楚。

title: It's the biggest and oldest museum in Libya.
translation: 這是利比亞最大也最古老的博物館。

Cut the bread into the thinnest slices you can.
He was the thinnest boy in my class.
Our cat is the fattest cat on the street.
The fattest pig won a prize at the fair.

That was the wettest summer in years.

The day my dog died was the saddest day of my life.

items.zh: 大象是陸地上最大的動物。

items.zh: 澳洲最大的城市是哪一個？

items.en: This is the biggest pizza I've ever seen!
items.zh: 這是我看過最大的披薩！

items.en: Their biggest problem is money.
items.zh: 他們最大的問題是錢。

items.zh: 最大的那條魚大約一公尺長。

examples.heading: ② hottest

items.zh: 七月是這裡最熱的月份。

items.en: The news says tomorrow will be the hottest day so far.
items.zh: 新聞說明天會是到目前為止最熱的一天。

items.en: Be careful. That's the hottest pan.
items.zh: 小心，那是最燙的鍋子。

items.en: Kaohsiung is one of the hottest cities in Taiwan.
items.zh: 高雄是台灣最熱的城市之一。

items.en: Sit in the shade. This is the hottest spot in the garden.
items.zh: 坐在陰影下吧，這裡是花園裡最熱的地方。

examples.heading: ③ thinnest / fattest

items.en: This is the thinnest phone in the shop.
items.zh: 這是店裡最薄的手機。

items.en: Cut the bread into the thinnest slices you can.
items.zh: 把麵包切成你能切的最薄片。

items.en: He was the thinnest boy in my class.
items.zh: 他是我們班上最瘦的男生。

items.en: Our cat is the fattest cat on the street.
items.zh: 我們家的貓是這條街上最胖的貓。

items.en: The fattest pig won a prize at the fair.
items.zh: 最肥的那隻豬在市集上得了獎。

examples.heading: ④ wettest / saddest

items.en: November is the wettest month in Keelung.
items.zh: 十一月是基隆最多雨的月份。

items.en: That was the wettest summer in years.
items.zh: 那是好幾年來最多雨的夏天。

items.en: It's the saddest movie I've ever watched.
items.zh: 那是我看過最悲傷的電影。

items.en: The day my dog died was the saddest day of my life.
items.zh: 我的狗死掉的那天是我這輩子最難過的一天。

items.en: That was the saddest song on the album.
items.zh: 那是這張專輯裡最悲傷的歌。

examples.heading: ⑤ 兩個最高級和不同的句型

items.en: Rome has some of the biggest and oldest churches in Europe.
items.zh: 羅馬有一些歐洲最大也最古老的教堂。

items.en: This is the hottest and driest part of the country.
items.zh: 這是這個國家最熱也最乾的地區。

items.en: Who is the fittest player on the team?
items.zh: 隊上體能最好的球員是誰？

items.en: That's the reddest apple in the box.
items.zh: 那是箱子裡最紅的蘋果。

items.en: We sat in the hottest part of the stadium.
items.zh: 我們坐在體育場最熱的區域。

items.en: Is this the biggest size you have?
items.zh: 這是你們最大的尺寸嗎？

items.en: It was the wettest and coldest week of the trip.
items.zh: 那是這趟旅行最濕最冷的一週。

items.en: The fattest book on the shelf is a dictionary.
items.zh: 架子上最厚的書是一本字典。

items.en: This is the flattest road for cycling.
items.zh: 這是最平、最適合騎腳踏車的路。

title: It was the cheapest in this shop!
translation: 那是這家店裡最便宜的！
name: 單音節形容詞加 -est 的最高級
sentences: I only have fifty dollars. Which is the cheapest phone you sell?
I bought the shirt because it was the cheapest.
What's the cheapest way to get to the airport?
My grandfather is the oldest man in the village.
People say the oak by the gate is the oldest tree in the park.
Who's the oldest in your class?
My brother is the tallest in our family.
That's the tallest building in the city.
I'd like the smallest size, please.
Our flat is the smallest one on the floor.
The smallest dog in the park is the loudest.
The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
Monday felt like the longest day of the week.
That's the fastest train in the country.
Who is the fastest swimmer in your class?
Take the fastest road, not the prettiest.
Ann was the youngest at the party, so she went home first.
The youngest player on the team is fifteen.
Put the milk in the garage. It's the coldest place we have.
That was the hardest test this year.
We saw the most stars on the darkest night of the trip.
He's the kindest man I know.
Look at all these melons. Which one is the sweetest?
We tried all the cafés, and this one is the cheapest.
Of all the roads, the main road is the quickest.
Of our three cats, the grey one is the oldest and the laziest.
I washed all the towels. The blue one is the softest.
We looked at three beds, and this one is the longest.
I tried on five pairs of boots. These are the warmest.
All the boys are strong, but Bob is the strongest.

examples.heading: ① cheapest / oldest

items.en: I only have fifty dollars. Which is the cheapest phone you sell?
items.zh: 我只有五十塊，你們賣的最便宜的手機是哪一支？

items.en: I bought the shirt because it was the cheapest.
items.zh: 我買那件襯衫，因為它最便宜。

items.en: What's the cheapest way to get to the airport?
items.zh: 到機場最便宜的方法是什麼？

items.en: My grandfather is the oldest man in the village.
items.zh: 我爺爺是村子裡年紀最大的人。

items.en: People say the oak by the gate is the oldest tree in the park.
items.zh: 大家說門邊那棵橡樹是公園裡最老的樹。

items.en: Who's the oldest in your class?
items.zh: 你們班上誰年紀最大？

examples.heading: ② tallest / smallest

items.en: My brother is the tallest in our family.
items.zh: 我哥哥是我們家最高的。

items.en: That's the tallest building in the city.
items.zh: 那是這座城市最高的大樓。

items.en: I'd like the smallest size, please.
items.zh: 請給我最小的尺寸。

items.en: Our flat is the smallest one on the floor.
items.zh: 我們家是這層樓最小的一戶。

items.en: The smallest dog in the park is the loudest.
items.zh: 公園裡最小的那隻狗叫得最大聲。

examples.heading: ③ longest / fastest

items.en: The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
items.zh: 尼羅河是非洲最長的河。

items.en: Monday felt like the longest day of the week.
items.zh: 星期一感覺是一週裡最漫長的一天。

items.en: That's the fastest train in the country.
items.zh: 那是全國最快的火車。

items.en: Who is the fastest swimmer in your class?
items.zh: 你們班誰游得最快？

items.en: Take the fastest road, not the prettiest.
items.zh: 走最快的路，不要走最漂亮的那條。

examples.heading: ④ youngest / 其他

items.en: Ann was the youngest at the party, so she went home first.
items.zh: Ann 是派對上年紀最小的，所以她最先回家。

items.en: The youngest player on the team is fifteen.
items.zh: 隊上最年輕的球員十五歲。

items.en: Put the milk in the garage. It's the coldest place we have.
items.zh: 把牛奶放到車庫，那是我們家最冷的地方。

items.en: That was the hardest test this year.
items.zh: 那是今年最難的考試。

items.en: We saw the most stars on the darkest night of the trip.
items.zh: 我們在旅行中最黑的那一晚看到最多星星。

items.en: He's the kindest man I know.
items.zh: 他是我認識最好心的人。

examples.heading: ⑤ the + 形容詞-est，省略名詞

items.en: Look at all these melons. Which one is the sweetest?
items.zh: 你看這些瓜，哪一顆最甜？

items.en: We tried all the cafés, and this one is the cheapest.
items.zh: 我們每家咖啡店都試過了，這家最便宜。

items.en: Of all the roads, the main road is the quickest.
items.zh: 所有路裡面，大馬路最快。

items.en: Of our three cats, the grey one is the oldest and the laziest.
items.zh: 我們家三隻貓裡，灰色那隻年紀最大，也最懶。

items.en: I washed all the towels. The blue one is the softest.
items.zh: 我洗了所有毛巾，藍色那條最柔軟。

items.en: We looked at three beds, and this one is the longest.
items.zh: 我們看了三張床，這張最長。

items.en: I tried on five pairs of boots. These are the warmest.
items.zh: 我試穿了五雙靴子，這雙最保暖。

items.en: All the boys are strong, but Bob is the strongest.
items.zh: 男生們都很強壯，不過 Bob 最強壯。

title: The easiest way to get to my house is by subway.
translation: 到我家最簡單的方法是搭地鐵。
name: 字尾 -y 的雙音節形容詞加 -est
sentences: The easiest way to the museum is by bus.
That was the easiest test of the year.
What's the easiest dish to cook for a beginner?
Start with the easiest question first.
Walking is the easiest way to stay healthy.
My uncle is the funniest person at every family dinner.
That was the funniest part of the show.
It was the happiest day of my life.
Our dog is the happiest when we take him to the beach.
Who told the funniest story at dinner?
She looked the happiest of all the children.
Friday is the busiest night at the restaurant.
Avoid Main Station at eight. It's the busiest time of the morning.
December is our busiest month.
Give me the heaviest box. I'm strong.
The heaviest bag was full of books.
This is the heaviest rain we've had this year.
That's the prettiest dress in the window.
Spring is the prettiest season here.
What's the earliest flight to Tokyo?
The earliest bus leaves at six.
I'm the luckiest person in the world!
He was the luckiest player in the game.
That's the craziest idea I've ever heard.
After the party, the kitchen was the dirtiest I've ever seen it.
Who is the laziest student in the class?
This is the healthiest food on the menu.
It was the noisiest party on the street.
The tidiest room gets a prize.
Tuesday was the windiest day of the week.

examples.heading: ① easiest

items.en: The easiest way to the museum is by bus.
items.zh: 去博物館最簡單的方法是搭公車。

items.en: That was the easiest test of the year.
items.zh: 那是今年最簡單的考試。

items.en: What's the easiest dish to cook for a beginner?
items.zh: 對初學者來說，最容易煮的菜是什麼？

items.en: Start with the easiest question first.
items.zh: 先從最簡單的題目開始。

items.en: Walking is the easiest way to stay healthy.
items.zh: 走路是保持健康最簡單的方法。

examples.heading: ② funniest / happiest

items.en: My uncle is the funniest person at every family dinner.
items.zh: 每次家庭聚餐，我叔叔都是最好笑的人。

items.en: That was the funniest part of the show.
items.zh: 那是節目最好笑的部分。

items.en: It was the happiest day of my life.
items.zh: 那是我這輩子最快樂的一天。

items.en: Our dog is the happiest when we take him to the beach.
items.zh: 我們帶狗去海邊的時候，牠最開心。

items.en: Who told the funniest story at dinner?
items.zh: 晚餐時誰講的故事最好笑？

items.en: She looked the happiest of all the children.
items.zh: 她看起來是所有孩子裡最開心的。

examples.heading: ③ busiest / heaviest

items.en: Friday is the busiest night at the restaurant.
items.zh: 星期五是餐廳最忙的晚上。

items.en: Avoid Main Station at eight. It's the busiest time of the morning.
items.zh: 八點別去總站，那是早上最擠的時候。

items.en: December is our busiest month.
items.zh: 十二月是我們最忙的月份。

items.en: Give me the heaviest box. I'm strong.
items.zh: 把最重的箱子給我，我力氣大。

items.en: The heaviest bag was full of books.
items.zh: 最重的那個袋子裝滿了書。

items.en: This is the heaviest rain we've had this year.
items.zh: 這是今年下過最大的雨。

examples.heading: ④ prettiest / earliest / luckiest

items.en: That's the prettiest dress in the window.
items.zh: 那是櫥窗裡最漂亮的洋裝。

items.en: Spring is the prettiest season here.
items.zh: 春天是這裡最美的季節。

items.en: What's the earliest flight to Tokyo?
items.zh: 到東京最早的班機是幾點？

items.en: The earliest bus leaves at six.
items.zh: 最早的公車六點開。

items.en: I'm the luckiest person in the world!
items.zh: 我是世界上最幸運的人！

items.en: He was the luckiest player in the game.
items.zh: 他是比賽裡運氣最好的球員。

examples.heading: ⑤ 其他 -iest 形容詞

items.en: That's the craziest idea I've ever heard.
items.zh: 那是我聽過最瘋狂的點子。

items.en: After the party, the kitchen was the dirtiest I've ever seen it.
items.zh: 派對結束後，廚房髒到我從沒見過的程度。

items.en: Who is the laziest student in the class?
items.zh: 班上誰最懶？

items.en: This is the healthiest food on the menu.
items.zh: 這是菜單上最健康的食物。

items.en: It was the noisiest party on the street.
items.zh: 那是這條街上最吵的派對。

items.en: The tidiest room gets a prize.
items.zh: 最整齊的房間可以得獎。

items.en: Tuesday was the windiest day of the week.
items.zh: 星期二是這週風最大的一天。

title: I am absolutely sure that it will attract even more attention.
translation: 我非常確定這會吸引更多人的注意。
name: absolutely 等極度副詞修飾形容詞
sentences: The exam was extremely difficult, and nobody finished it.
It is extremely important to wear a helmet.
The roads are extremely busy before the holiday.
My grandmother is extremely proud of you.
When I lost my passport, the hotel staff were extremely helpful.
Is the water extremely cold in winter?
The new trains are incredibly fast.
Phones get incredibly hot when you play games.
Your sister is incredibly talented.
We booked early, so the plane tickets were incredibly cheap.
Moving house was an incredibly long day for all of us.
He's incredibly patient with the kids.
We climbed for three hours, and the view of the lake was absolutely amazing.
Can I have the recipe? Your curry is absolutely delicious.
It's absolutely freezing outside.
After the race, I was absolutely exhausted.
Thanks for the tickets. The show last night was absolutely fantastic.
Nobody had cleaned for weeks, and the kitchen was absolutely filthy.
I am absolutely sure that the plan will work.
You're absolutely right. We should leave earlier.
Before we leave, are you absolutely sure the oven is off?
What she said is absolutely true.
I'm absolutely certain I saw him at the station.
We need a totally new plan.
My new school is totally different from my old one.
Sorry, I was totally wrong about the time.
Finishing in one day is totally impossible.
I was totally lost in the old town.
The room was totally empty when we arrived.
Don't believe the rumor. It's totally untrue.

examples.heading: ① extremely + 形容詞

items.en: The exam was extremely difficult, and nobody finished it.
items.zh: 考試非常難，沒有人寫完。

items.en: It is extremely important to wear a helmet.
items.zh: 戴安全帽非常重要。

items.en: The roads are extremely busy before the holiday.
items.zh: 放假前路上的車非常多。

items.en: My grandmother is extremely proud of you.
items.zh: 我奶奶非常以你為榮。

items.en: When I lost my passport, the hotel staff were extremely helpful.
items.zh: 我護照弄丟的時候，飯店員工非常幫忙。

items.en: Is the water extremely cold in winter?
items.zh: 冬天的水非常冰嗎？

examples.heading: ② incredibly + 形容詞

items.en: The new trains are incredibly fast.
items.zh: 新的火車快得不得了。

items.en: Phones get incredibly hot when you play games.
items.zh: 玩遊戲的時候手機會變得非常燙。

items.en: Your sister is incredibly talented.
items.zh: 你妹妹非常有天分。

items.en: We booked early, so the plane tickets were incredibly cheap.
items.zh: 我們很早訂，所以機票便宜得不得了。

items.en: Moving house was an incredibly long day for all of us.
items.zh: 搬家那天對我們大家來說非常漫長。

items.en: He's incredibly patient with the kids.
items.zh: 他對孩子們非常有耐心。

examples.heading: ③ absolutely + 本身就很強的形容詞

items.en: We climbed for three hours, and the view of the lake was absolutely amazing.
items.zh: 我們爬了三個小時，湖的景色美極了。

items.en: Can I have the recipe? Your curry is absolutely delicious.
items.zh: 可以給我食譜嗎？你煮的咖哩好吃極了。

items.en: It's absolutely freezing outside.
items.zh: 外面冷死了。

items.en: After the race, I was absolutely exhausted.
items.zh: 比賽結束後，我累壞了。

items.en: Thanks for the tickets. The show last night was absolutely fantastic.
items.zh: 謝謝你的票，昨晚的表演精彩極了。

items.en: Nobody had cleaned for weeks, and the kitchen was absolutely filthy.
items.zh: 好幾個禮拜沒人打掃，廚房髒得要命。

examples.heading: ④ absolutely sure / certain / right / true

items.en: I am absolutely sure that the plan will work.
items.zh: 我非常確定這個計畫會成功。

items.en: You're absolutely right. We should leave earlier.
items.zh: 你說得完全正確，我們應該早點出發。

items.en: Before we leave, are you absolutely sure the oven is off?
items.zh: 出門前，你非常確定烤箱關了嗎？

items.en: What she said is absolutely true.
items.zh: 她說的話完全是真的。

items.en: I'm absolutely certain I saw him at the station.
items.zh: 我非常確定我在車站看到他。

examples.heading: ⑤ totally + 形容詞

items.en: We need a totally new plan.
items.zh: 我們需要一個全新的計畫。

items.en: My new school is totally different from my old one.
items.zh: 我的新學校跟以前的完全不一樣。

items.en: Sorry, I was totally wrong about the time.
items.zh: 抱歉，我完全搞錯時間了。

items.en: Finishing in one day is totally impossible.
items.zh: 一天內做完完全不可能。

items.en: I was totally lost in the old town.
items.zh: 我在舊城區完全迷路了。

items.en: The room was totally empty when we arrived.
items.zh: 我們到的時候，房間完全是空的。

items.en: Don't believe the rumor. It's totally untrue.
items.zh: 別相信那個謠言，那完全不是真的。

title: That's something that makes me angry!
translation: 這就是會讓我生氣的事！
name: 形容詞當 make 的受詞補語
sentences: Waiting in long lines makes me angry.
Long car trips make me sleepy.
Our old neighbour died last week. The news made my parents very sad.
Exams always make me nervous.
Her funny emails make me happy.
The smell of bread makes me hungry.
You always sleep with the light on. Does the dark make you afraid?
The hike up the hill made us hungry.
My dad only drinks one cup a day. Too much coffee makes him sick.
Nobody knew the writer before 2019. Winning the prize made her famous.
We played football at noon in July. The heat made everyone thirsty.
Don't drive after you take this. The medicine will make you sleepy.
My grandfather started with one small shop. Hard work made him rich.
We couldn't swim the next day. The storm made the river brown.
A little sugar makes the sauce sweet.
We painted my bedroom yellow. The new paint made the room bright.
Too much salt will make the soup salty.
We parked on the street all afternoon. The sun made the car really hot.
Our manager bought some plants for the office. They make it more pleasant.
I'm moving to another city, and I don't want to make you sad.
I just want to make my customers happy.
Grandma came to stay with us. We tried to make the spare room cozy for her.
Dad is tired after work. Try not to make him angry.
My cousin studies every night. She wants to make her parents proud.
You're singing in the kitchen. What makes you so happy today?
The ending of the film made me really emotional.
There was a loud bang outside last night. Did the noise make you nervous?
My brother and I travelled around Japan for a month. The trip has made us closer.
That song always makes me sleepy.
They're building a road from the city to our town. Will the new road make the town busier?

examples.heading: ① make + 人 + 感覺

items.en: Waiting in long lines makes me angry.
items.zh: 排長隊讓我很生氣。

items.en: Long car trips make me sleepy.
items.zh: 長途坐車讓我想睡。

items.en: Our old neighbour died last week. The news made my parents very sad.
items.zh: 我們以前的鄰居上星期過世了。這個消息讓我爸媽很難過。

items.en: Exams always make me nervous.
items.zh: 考試總是讓我很緊張。

items.en: Her funny emails make me happy.
items.zh: 她寫的好笑的電子郵件讓我很開心。

items.en: The smell of bread makes me hungry.
items.zh: 麵包的味道讓我肚子餓。

items.en: You always sleep with the light on. Does the dark make you afraid?
items.zh: 你睡覺總是開著燈。黑暗會讓你害怕嗎？

examples.heading: ② make + 人 + 狀態

items.en: The hike up the hill made us hungry.
items.zh: 爬上山讓我們肚子都餓了。

items.en: My dad only drinks one cup a day. Too much coffee makes him sick.
items.zh: 我爸一天只喝一杯。喝太多咖啡會讓他不舒服。

items.en: Nobody knew the writer before 2019. Winning the prize made her famous.
items.zh: 二〇一九年以前沒有人認識那位作家。得獎讓她出了名。

items.en: We played football at noon in July. The heat made everyone thirsty.
items.zh: 我們七月中午踢足球。天氣熱得大家都很口渴。

items.en: Don't drive after you take this. The medicine will make you sleepy.
items.zh: 吃了這個以後別開車。這個藥會讓你想睡。

items.en: My grandfather started with one small shop. Hard work made him rich.
items.zh: 我爺爺一開始只有一間小店。努力工作讓他變得很有錢。

examples.heading: ③ make + 東西 + 形容詞

items.en: We couldn't swim the next day. The storm made the river brown.
items.zh: 隔天我們不能游泳。暴風雨讓河水變成褐色。

items.en: A little sugar makes the sauce sweet.
items.zh: 加一點糖會讓醬汁變甜。

items.en: We painted my bedroom yellow. The new paint made the room bright.
items.zh: 我們把我的臥室漆成黃色。新的油漆讓房間變得很明亮。

items.en: Too much salt will make the soup salty.
items.zh: 放太多鹽會讓湯變得很鹹。

items.en: We parked on the street all afternoon. The sun made the car really hot.
items.zh: 我們整個下午把車停在街上。太陽把車子曬得很燙。

items.en: Our manager bought some plants for the office. They make it more pleasant.
items.zh: 我們經理買了一些植物放在辦公室。它們讓辦公室舒服多了。

examples.heading: ④ try to make / want to make

items.en: I'm moving to another city, and I don't want to make you sad.
items.zh: 我要搬到別的城市了，我不想讓你難過。

items.en: I just want to make my customers happy.
items.zh: 我只想讓我的客人開心。

items.en: Grandma came to stay with us. We tried to make the spare room cozy for her.
items.zh: 奶奶來我們家住。我們想把客房弄得溫馨一點給她住。

items.en: Dad is tired after work. Try not to make him angry.
items.zh: 爸爸下班以後很累。盡量別惹他生氣。

items.en: My cousin studies every night. She wants to make her parents proud.
items.zh: 我表妹每天晚上都在讀書。她想讓她爸媽以她為榮。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的時態和句型

items.en: You're singing in the kitchen. What makes you so happy today?
items.zh: 你在廚房裡唱歌。今天什麼事讓你這麼開心？

items.en: The ending of the film made me really emotional.
items.zh: 電影的結局讓我很感動。

items.en: There was a loud bang outside last night. Did the noise make you nervous?
items.zh: 昨天晚上外面有一聲巨響。那個聲音讓你緊張嗎？

items.en: My brother and I travelled around Japan for a month. The trip has made us closer.
items.zh: 我和我哥哥在日本旅行了一個月。這趟旅行讓我們更親近了。

items.en: That song always makes me sleepy.
items.zh: 那首歌總是讓我想睡。

items.en: They're building a road from the city to our town. Will the new road make the town busier?
items.zh: 他們在蓋一條從市區到我們鎮上的路。新的道路會讓鎮上更熱鬧嗎？

title: It was more expensive than the other clothes.
translation: 它比其他衣服貴。
name: more 加形容詞的比較級
sentences: This sofa is more comfortable than my bed.
Gold is more expensive than silver.
Math is more difficult than art for me.
History became more interesting with Mr. Lin.
Your health is more important than money.
The city is more beautiful at night.
Motorbikes are more dangerous than bikes.
The new phone is more expensive than I expected.
Is English more difficult than Japanese?
This exercise is more useful for beginners.
Leather seats feel more comfortable.
Today's lesson was more enjoyable.
You must be more careful.
She is more famous than her sister.
The meeting was more boring than usual.
I felt more tired after the trip.
My new job is more stressful.
Be more patient with your little brother.
Ski trips are more exciting than beach trips.
Ken looks more relaxed now.
I want a more interesting job.
The company hired a more careful driver.
She bought a more expensive bag.
Can you give me a more useful example?
They moved to a more beautiful area.
Tomorrow's game will be more important.
Was the hotel more comfortable than the last one?
Ann became more confident after the course.
Nothing is more important than your family.
The roads are more crowded on weekends.

examples.heading: ① 三個音節以上的形容詞

items.en: This sofa is more comfortable than my bed.
items.zh: 這張沙發比我的床舒服。

items.en: Gold is more expensive than silver.
items.zh: 黃金比銀貴。

items.en: Math is more difficult than art for me.
items.zh: 對我來說，數學比美術難。

items.en: History became more interesting with Mr. Lin.
items.zh: 林老師教的歷史變得比較有趣。

items.en: Your health is more important than money.
items.zh: 你的健康比錢重要。

items.en: The city is more beautiful at night.
items.zh: 這座城市晚上比較漂亮。

items.en: Motorbikes are more dangerous than bikes.
items.zh: 機車比腳踏車危險。

items.en: The new phone is more expensive than I expected.
items.zh: 新手機比我預期的貴。

items.en: Is English more difficult than Japanese?
items.zh: 英文比日文難嗎？

items.en: This exercise is more useful for beginners.
items.zh: 這個練習對初學者比較有用。

items.en: Leather seats feel more comfortable.
items.zh: 皮椅坐起來比較舒服。

items.en: Today's lesson was more enjoyable.
items.zh: 今天的課比較好玩。

examples.heading: ② -ful、-ous、-ing、-ed 的形容詞

items.en: You must be more careful.
items.zh: 你一定要更小心。

items.en: She is more famous than her sister.
items.zh: 她比她姊姊有名。

items.en: The meeting was more boring than usual.
items.zh: 會議比平常無聊。

items.en: I felt more tired after the trip.
items.zh: 旅行回來以後，我覺得更累了。

items.en: My new job is more stressful.
items.zh: 我的新工作壓力比較大。

items.en: Be more patient with your little brother.
items.zh: 對你弟弟要更有耐心。

items.en: Ski trips are more exciting than beach trips.
items.zh: 去滑雪比去海邊刺激。

items.en: Ken looks more relaxed now.
items.zh: Ken 現在看起來比較放鬆。

examples.heading: ③ more + 形容詞 + 名詞

items.en: I want a more interesting job.
items.zh: 我想要一份比較有趣的工作。

items.en: The company hired a more careful driver.
items.zh: 公司請了一個更小心的司機。

items.en: She bought a more expensive bag.
items.zh: 她買了一個比較貴的包包。

items.en: Can you give me a more useful example?
items.zh: 你可以給我一個比較有用的例子嗎？

items.en: They moved to a more beautiful area.
items.zh: 他們搬到一個比較漂亮的地區。

examples.heading: ④ 不同的時態和句型

items.en: Tomorrow's game will be more important.
items.zh: 明天的比賽會更重要。

items.en: Was the hotel more comfortable than the last one?
items.zh: 這家旅館比上一家舒服嗎？

items.en: Ann became more confident after the course.
items.zh: 上完課之後，Ann 變得比較有自信。

items.en: Nothing is more important than your family.
items.zh: 沒有什麼比你的家人更重要。

items.en: The roads are more crowded on weekends.
items.zh: 週末路上比較擁擠。

title: Please wear your oldest clothes.
translation: 請穿你最舊的衣服。
name: my、your 加最高級加名詞
sentences: I'm buying a bike for my youngest brother's birthday.
My oldest sister lives in London.
My youngest daughter starts school next week.
My eldest son is studying in Tainan this year.
My oldest friend is getting married.
We're painting today, so wear your oldest clothes.
Bring your warmest coat. It's snowing.
Put on your best shoes for the wedding.
Wear your most comfortable shoes for the hike.
Is this your newest phone?
Use your sharpest knife to cut the bread.
This is my best dress. I only wear it to weddings.
My oldest shoes have holes in them.
I keep my most important papers in this box.
My favorite cup is also my biggest.
My smallest bag fits in my pocket.
Math is my worst subject.
With two jobs, my biggest problem is finding time to sleep.
What's your biggest dream?
That was my hardest exam.
I got an A in art. It's always been my best subject.
What was your happiest moment this year?
His youngest son is a doctor.
Her best friend lives in Kaohsiung.
Our oldest car still works well.
Their biggest worry is the cost.
She wore her prettiest dress to the party.
They sold their oldest furniture.
Our smallest room is the office.
He gave away his newest toy.

examples.heading: ① my + 最高級 + 家人

items.en: I'm buying a bike for my youngest brother's birthday.
items.zh: 我要買一台腳踏車給我最小的弟弟當生日禮物。

items.en: My oldest sister lives in London.
items.zh: 我大姊住在倫敦。

items.en: My youngest daughter starts school next week.
items.zh: 我的小女兒下禮拜開始上學。

items.en: My eldest son is studying in Tainan this year.
items.zh: 我的大兒子今年在台南讀書。

items.en: My oldest friend is getting married.
items.zh: 我認識最久的朋友要結婚了。

examples.heading: ② your + 最高級 + 東西

items.en: We're painting today, so wear your oldest clothes.
items.zh: 我們今天要油漆，所以穿你最舊的衣服。

items.en: Bring your warmest coat. It's snowing.
items.zh: 帶你最保暖的外套，在下雪了。

items.en: Put on your best shoes for the wedding.
items.zh: 穿你最好的鞋去婚禮。

items.en: Wear your most comfortable shoes for the hike.
items.zh: 健行要穿你最舒服的鞋。

items.en: Is this your newest phone?
items.zh: 這是你最新的手機嗎？

items.en: Use your sharpest knife to cut the bread.
items.zh: 用你最利的刀切麵包。

examples.heading: ③ my + 最高級 + 東西

items.en: This is my best dress. I only wear it to weddings.
items.zh: 這是我最好的洋裝，我只穿去婚禮。

items.en: My oldest shoes have holes in them.
items.zh: 我最舊的鞋子有洞。

items.en: I keep my most important papers in this box.
items.zh: 我把最重要的文件放在這個盒子裡。

items.en: My favorite cup is also my biggest.
items.zh: 我最喜歡的杯子也是我最大的。

items.en: My smallest bag fits in my pocket.
items.zh: 我最小的包包放得進口袋。

examples.heading: ④ my / your + 最高級 + 事情

items.en: Math is my worst subject.
items.zh: 數學是我最差的科目。

items.en: With two jobs, my biggest problem is finding time to sleep.
items.zh: 做兩份工作，我最大的問題是找時間睡覺。

items.en: What's your biggest dream?
items.zh: 你最大的夢想是什麼？

items.en: That was my hardest exam.
items.zh: 那是我考過最難的考試。

items.en: I got an A in art. It's always been my best subject.
items.zh: 我美術拿了 A，美術一直是我最好的科目。

items.en: What was your happiest moment this year?
items.zh: 你今年最快樂的時刻是什麼時候？

examples.heading: ⑤ his / her / our / their + 最高級 + 名詞

items.en: His youngest son is a doctor.
items.zh: 他最小的兒子是醫生。

items.en: Her best friend lives in Kaohsiung.
items.zh: 她最好的朋友住在高雄。

items.en: Our oldest car still works well.
items.zh: 我們最舊的那輛車還很好開。

items.en: Their biggest worry is the cost.
items.zh: 他們最擔心的是費用。

items.en: She wore her prettiest dress to the party.
items.zh: 她穿了她最漂亮的洋裝去派對。

items.en: They sold their oldest furniture.
items.zh: 他們把最舊的家具賣掉了。

items.en: Our smallest room is the office.
items.zh: 我們最小的房間是書房。

items.en: He gave away his newest toy.
items.zh: 他把他最新的玩具送人了。

title: For people who can't afford a car, a bicycle is perhaps the cheapest way to travel in the city.
translation: 對買不起車的人來說，腳踏車大概是在市區移動最便宜的方式。
name: 最高級形容詞加名詞加不定詞
sentences: The bridge has a toll, and taxis cost a lot. Taking the ferry is the cheapest way to cross the bay.
The fastest way to reach the airport is the express train.
Our shop still writes every sale in a notebook. Using a computer is the easiest way to keep records.
I still type with two fingers. What's the fastest way to learn to type?
The simplest way to save money is to cook at home.
We've walked for half an hour already. Is this the shortest way to walk to the beach?
Don't carry your passport around the city. The safest place to keep it is the hotel safe.
Book your trip to Spain for the winter. The cheapest time to fly is in February.
The café is too noisy for me. The quietest place to study is the top floor of the library.
It's thirty-five degrees in the afternoon here. Early morning is the coolest time to go for a run.
The supermarket is a long way away. The nearest place to buy bread is the shop on the corner.
Storms come fast in the mountains. The most important thing to check before a hike is the weather.
Book a table at Rosa's for Saturday. It's the most popular place to eat in town.
I'm going to Osaka next week. What's the most useful word to learn in Japanese?
The bus stops right outside our house. Taking it is the most convenient way to get to school.
Come to our town in August. The most interesting time to visit is during the festival.
Let's go on Saturday morning instead. Friday afternoon is the worst time to drive into the city.
I loved my year in Spain. At the end, the hardest thing to do was say goodbye.
You won't get a seat at eight o'clock. Rush hour is the worst time to take the subway.
My Spanish course was fun. The hardest part to learn was the grammar.
Don't leave it under that tree. That's the worst place to park your car, because of the birds.
I want to send these books to my son in Canada. Which is the cheapest way to send a parcel?
The waves look big today. Where's the safest place to swim?
I've never grown anything before. Which is the easiest plant to grow on a balcony?
I don't like crowds. When's the quietest time to visit the museum?
For students, the library is the cheapest place to work.
When you're lost, the best thing to do is ask for help.
Please leave your room by eleven. That's the latest time to check out.
When a friend is sad, the kindest thing to do is listen.
The flowers come out in April. Spring is perhaps the best time to walk in the hills.

examples.heading: ① the + 形容詞-est + way to

items.en: The bridge has a toll, and taxis cost a lot. Taking the ferry is the cheapest way to cross the bay.
items.zh: 過橋要收費，計程車又很貴。搭渡輪是過海灣最便宜的方式。

items.en: The fastest way to reach the airport is the express train.
items.zh: 去機場最快的方法是搭快線列車。

items.en: Our shop still writes every sale in a notebook. Using a computer is the easiest way to keep records.
items.zh: 我們店裡還是把每筆交易寫在筆記本上。用電腦是記錄資料最簡單的方法。

items.en: I still type with two fingers. What's the fastest way to learn to type?
items.zh: 我打字還是用兩根手指。學打字最快的方法是什麼？

items.en: The simplest way to save money is to cook at home.
items.zh: 省錢最簡單的方法是在家煮飯。

items.en: We've walked for half an hour already. Is this the shortest way to walk to the beach?
items.zh: 我們已經走了半個小時。這是走去海邊最近的路嗎？

examples.heading: ② the + 形容詞-est + place / time to

items.en: Don't carry your passport around the city. The safest place to keep it is the hotel safe.
items.zh: 別帶著護照在市區走。放護照最安全的地方是飯店的保險箱。

items.en: Book your trip to Spain for the winter. The cheapest time to fly is in February.
items.zh: 你去西班牙的行程訂在冬天吧。二月是搭飛機最便宜的時候。

items.en: The café is too noisy for me. The quietest place to study is the top floor of the library.
items.zh: 咖啡館對我來說太吵了。讀書最安靜的地方是圖書館頂樓。

items.en: It's thirty-five degrees in the afternoon here. Early morning is the coolest time to go for a run.
items.zh: 這裡下午有三十五度。清晨是去跑步最涼快的時候。

items.en: The supermarket is a long way away. The nearest place to buy bread is the shop on the corner.
items.zh: 超市很遠。最近可以買麵包的地方是轉角那家店。

examples.heading: ③ the most + 形容詞 + 名詞 + to

items.en: Storms come fast in the mountains. The most important thing to check before a hike is the weather.
items.zh: 山上的暴風雨來得很快。爬山前最要緊的是先看天氣。

items.en: Book a table at Rosa's for Saturday. It's the most popular place to eat in town.
items.zh: 星期六去羅莎餐廳訂位吧。那是鎮上最熱門的吃飯地點。

items.en: I'm going to Osaka next week. What's the most useful word to learn in Japanese?
items.zh: 我下星期要去大阪。日文裡最值得學的字是哪一個？

items.en: The bus stops right outside our house. Taking it is the most convenient way to get to school.
items.zh: 公車就停在我們家外面。搭公車是上學最方便的方式。

items.en: Come to our town in August. The most interesting time to visit is during the festival.
items.zh: 八月來我們鎮上吧。節慶期間是最有意思的造訪時間。

examples.heading: ④ the worst / the hardest + 名詞 + to

items.en: Let's go on Saturday morning instead. Friday afternoon is the worst time to drive into the city.
items.zh: 我們改星期六早上去吧。星期五下午是開車進城最糟的時間。

items.en: I loved my year in Spain. At the end, the hardest thing to do was say goodbye.
items.zh: 我很愛在西班牙的那一年。到最後，最難做的事是說再見。

items.en: You won't get a seat at eight o'clock. Rush hour is the worst time to take the subway.
items.zh: 你八點鐘不會有位子坐。尖峰時間是搭地鐵最糟的時候。

items.en: My Spanish course was fun. The hardest part to learn was the grammar.
items.zh: 我的西班牙文課很好玩。最難學的部分是文法。

items.en: Don't leave it under that tree. That's the worst place to park your car, because of the birds.
items.zh: 別停在那棵樹下。那是停車最糟的地方，因為有鳥。

examples.heading: ⑤ 問句和不同的句型

items.en: I want to send these books to my son in Canada. Which is the cheapest way to send a parcel?
items.zh: 我想把這些書寄給我在加拿大的兒子。寄包裹最便宜的方法是哪一種？

items.en: The waves look big today. Where's the safest place to swim?
items.zh: 今天浪看起來很大。在哪裡游泳最安全？

items.en: I've never grown anything before. Which is the easiest plant to grow on a balcony?
items.zh: 我從來沒種過東西。在陽台上種哪一種植物最容易？

items.en: I don't like crowds. When's the quietest time to visit the museum?
items.zh: 我不喜歡人多。什麼時候去博物館人最少？

items.en: For students, the library is the cheapest place to work.
items.zh: 對學生來說，圖書館是最省錢的讀書地方。

items.en: When you're lost, the best thing to do is ask for help.
items.zh: 迷路的時候，最好的做法是找人幫忙。

items.en: Please leave your room by eleven. That's the latest time to check out.
items.zh: 請在十一點前離開房間。那是最晚的退房時間。

items.en: When a friend is sad, the kindest thing to do is listen.
items.zh: 朋友難過的時候，最體貼的做法是聽他說。

items.en: The flowers come out in April. Spring is perhaps the best time to walk in the hills.
items.zh: 花在四月開。春天大概是去山上散步最好的時候。

title: The house was full of people.
translation: 房子裡擠滿了人。
name: 形容詞加介系詞片語
sentences: Swimming is good for your back.
Fruit is good for you, so eat an apple.
Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
Is coffee bad for children?
Walking to school is good for the kids.
My sister is good at math.
Are you good at cooking?
Ken is good at tennis. He plays every weekend.
My grandpa is good at fixing bikes.
She's really good at drawing animals.
The bus was full of students this morning.
My bag is full of books today.
The fridge is full of food for the party.
The park was full of children on Sunday.
Your room is full of old toys.
My little brother is afraid of dogs.
Are you afraid of the dark?
I'm afraid of flying, so we're taking the train.
Ann is interested in old movies.
Are you interested in art?
My dad is interested in cooking Thai food.
Hurry up, or we'll be late for school.
Sorry I'm late for the meeting.
The nurses were very kind to my mother.
Be kind to your little sister.
Don't be late for dinner again.
The old man was kind to us when we got lost.
Was he late for work again?
Everyone at the hotel was kind to the children.
The bus didn't come, so I was late for my class.

examples.heading: ① good for / bad for

items.en: Swimming is good for your back.
items.zh: 游泳對你的背很好。

items.en: Fruit is good for you, so eat an apple.
items.zh: 水果對你有好處，吃顆蘋果吧。

items.en: Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
items.zh: 吃太多糖對你的牙齒不好。

items.en: Is coffee bad for children?
items.zh: 咖啡對小孩不好嗎？

items.en: Walking to school is good for the kids.
items.zh: 走路上學對孩子們有好處。

examples.heading: ② good at

items.en: My sister is good at math.
items.zh: 我姊姊數學很好。

items.en: Are you good at cooking?
items.zh: 你很會煮菜嗎？

items.en: Ken is good at tennis. He plays every weekend.
items.zh: Ken 很會打網球，他每個週末都打。

items.en: My grandpa is good at fixing bikes.
items.zh: 我爺爺很會修腳踏車。

items.en: She's really good at drawing animals.
items.zh: 她很會畫動物。

examples.heading: ③ full of

items.en: The bus was full of students this morning.
items.zh: 今天早上公車上都是學生。

items.en: My bag is full of books today.
items.zh: 我今天的包包裝滿了書。

items.en: The fridge is full of food for the party.
items.zh: 冰箱裡塞滿了派對要用的食物。

items.en: The park was full of children on Sunday.
items.zh: 星期天公園裡都是小孩。

items.en: Your room is full of old toys.
items.zh: 你的房間堆滿了舊玩具。

examples.heading: ④ afraid of / interested in

items.en: My little brother is afraid of dogs.
items.zh: 我弟弟怕狗。

items.en: Are you afraid of the dark?
items.zh: 你怕黑嗎？

items.en: I'm afraid of flying, so we're taking the train.
items.zh: 我怕坐飛機，所以我們要搭火車。

items.en: Ann is interested in old movies.
items.zh: Ann 對老電影有興趣。

items.en: Are you interested in art?
items.zh: 你對藝術有興趣嗎？

items.en: My dad is interested in cooking Thai food.
items.zh: 我爸爸對煮泰國菜有興趣。

examples.heading: ⑤ late for / kind to

items.en: Hurry up, or we'll be late for school.
items.zh: 快一點，不然我們上學會遲到。

items.en: Sorry I'm late for the meeting.
items.zh: 抱歉，我開會遲到了。

items.en: The nurses were very kind to my mother.
items.zh: 護理師們對我媽媽很好。

items.en: Be kind to your little sister.
items.zh: 對你妹妹好一點。

items.en: Don't be late for dinner again.
items.zh: 晚餐別再遲到了。

items.en: The old man was kind to us when we got lost.
items.zh: 我們迷路的時候，那位老先生對我們很好。

items.en: Was he late for work again?
items.zh: 他上班又遲到了嗎？

items.en: Everyone at the hotel was kind to the children.
items.zh: 飯店的每個人都對孩子們很好。

items.en: The bus didn't come, so I was late for my class.
items.zh: 公車沒來，所以我上課遲到了。

title: There is nothing interesting on TV.
translation: 電視上沒什麼好看的。

Sorry I'm late. Something terrible happened on the way home. A car hit a cyclist.
It's snowing, and I only have a thin jacket. I need something warm to wear.
We always go to the cinema. Let's do something different this weekend.
I called you three times, but you didn't answer. Is there something wrong with your phone?
She said something funny, and we all laughed.
Did the doctor say anything worrying about your knee?
The neighbours say someone broke into the garage. I didn't hear anything strange last night.
I just got home from football, Mum. Is there anything good to eat?
Your aunt's friends are coming for dinner. Don't say anything rude to the guests.
We didn't do anything special for New Year.
Dad put the paper down after two minutes. There's nothing interesting in the newspaper today.
The mechanic checked everything. There was nothing wrong with the car.
The kids were fine with the babysitter. Nothing bad happened, so don't worry.
Take this to the bank with you. Everything important is in this folder.
My mum moved to a smaller flat. She gave away everything old in her closet.
We need someone strong to move the piano.
I've just moved to this city. I want to meet someone new.
Look at all the photographers outside. Is there anyone famous at the party?
I left Tom's party at nine. No one interesting was there.
You can't reach the top shelf. Ask someone older for help.
Our cat always finds somewhere dark to hide.
I'm tired of the long, cold winters here. I want to live somewhere warm.
Is there anywhere cheap to eat near here?
The park benches are all wet. There's nowhere dry to sit after the rain.
We haven't been anywhere exciting this year.
The children can open that drawer. Put the medicine somewhere safe.
It's our anniversary tonight. Let's find somewhere nice for dinner.
My aunt goes to Spain every year. This time she wanted to go somewhere new for her holiday.
There's nowhere quiet to study in this house.

examples.heading: ① something + 形容詞

items.en: My sister got her first salary. She bought something expensive for our mother.
items.zh: 我姊姊領了第一份薪水。她買了很貴的東西給我們媽媽。

items.en: Sorry I'm late. Something terrible happened on the way home. A car hit a cyclist.
items.zh: 抱歉我晚到了。回家的路上發生了一件很可怕的事。一輛車撞到一個騎腳踏車的人。

items.en: It's snowing, and I only have a thin jacket. I need something warm to wear.
items.zh: 下雪了，我只有一件薄外套。我需要一件保暖的衣服穿。

items.en: We always go to the cinema. Let's do something different this weekend.
items.zh: 我們每次都去看電影。這個週末我們做點不一樣的事吧。

items.en: I called you three times, but you didn't answer. Is there something wrong with your phone?
items.zh: 我打給你三次，你都沒接。你的手機有什麼問題嗎？

items.en: She said something funny, and we all laughed.
items.zh: 她說了一句好笑的話，我們全都笑了。

examples.heading: ② anything + 形容詞

items.en: Did the doctor say anything worrying about your knee?
items.zh: 醫生有說你的膝蓋有什麼令人擔心的地方嗎？

items.en: The neighbours say someone broke into the garage. I didn't hear anything strange last night.
items.zh: 鄰居說有人闖進了車庫。我昨晚沒聽到什麼奇怪的聲音。

items.en: I just got home from football, Mum. Is there anything good to eat?
items.zh: 媽，我剛踢完足球回家。有什麼好吃的嗎？

items.en: Your aunt's friends are coming for dinner. Don't say anything rude to the guests.
items.zh: 你阿姨的朋友要來吃晚餐。別對客人說沒禮貌的話。

items.en: We didn't do anything special for New Year.
items.zh: 我們過年沒做什麼特別的事。

examples.heading: ③ nothing / everything + 形容詞

items.en: Dad put the paper down after two minutes. There's nothing interesting in the newspaper today.
items.zh: 爸爸看了兩分鐘就把報紙放下。今天報紙上沒什麼有趣的新聞。

items.en: The mechanic checked everything. There was nothing wrong with the car.
items.zh: 修車師傅全部檢查過了。車子沒什麼問題。

items.en: The kids were fine with the babysitter. Nothing bad happened, so don't worry.
items.zh: 孩子們跟保母在一起很好。沒發生什麼壞事，別擔心。

items.en: Take this to the bank with you. Everything important is in this folder.
items.zh: 帶這個去銀行。所有重要的東西都在這個資料夾裡。

items.en: My mum moved to a smaller flat. She gave away everything old in her closet.
items.zh: 我媽搬到一間比較小的公寓。她把衣櫃裡所有舊的東西都送人了。

examples.heading: ④ someone / anyone / no one + 形容詞

items.en: We need someone strong to move the piano.
items.zh: 我們需要一個力氣大的人來搬鋼琴。

items.en: I've just moved to this city. I want to meet someone new.
items.zh: 我剛搬到這個城市。我想認識新朋友。

items.en: Look at all the photographers outside. Is there anyone famous at the party?
items.zh: 你看外面那些攝影師。派對上有什麼名人嗎？

items.en: I left Tom's party at nine. No one interesting was there.
items.zh: 我九點就離開湯姆的派對了。那裡沒有什麼有趣的人。

items.en: You can't reach the top shelf. Ask someone older for help.
items.zh: 你搆不到最上面那一層。找一個年紀比較大的人幫忙。

examples.heading: ⑤ somewhere / anywhere / nowhere + 形容詞

items.en: Our cat always finds somewhere dark to hide.
items.zh: 我們的貓總是找個暗暗的地方躲起來。

items.en: I'm tired of the long, cold winters here. I want to live somewhere warm.
items.zh: 我受夠了這裡又長又冷的冬天。我想住在溫暖的地方。

items.en: Is there anywhere cheap to eat near here?
items.zh: 這附近有便宜的地方吃飯嗎？

items.en: The park benches are all wet. There's nowhere dry to sit after the rain.
items.zh: 公園的長椅都是濕的。雨後沒有乾的地方可以坐。

items.en: We haven't been anywhere exciting this year.
items.zh: 我們今年沒去過什麼刺激的地方。

items.en: The children can open that drawer. Put the medicine somewhere safe.
items.zh: 孩子們打得開那個抽屜。把藥放在安全的地方。

items.en: It's our anniversary tonight. Let's find somewhere nice for dinner.
items.zh: 今天晚上是我們的結婚紀念日。我們找個好地方吃晚餐吧。

items.en: My aunt goes to Spain every year. This time she wanted to go somewhere new for her holiday.
items.zh: 我阿姨每年都去西班牙。這次她放假想去一個沒去過的地方。

items.en: There's nowhere quiet to study in this house.
items.zh: 這間房子裡沒有安靜的地方可以讀書。

title: I personally think going to a large school is quite a good idea.
translation: 我個人覺得去讀大型學校是個滿好的主意。
name: quite a 加形容詞
sentences: Let's drive. The lake is quite a long way from here.
In summer, starting work early is quite a good idea.
That's quite a difficult situation you're in.
She has quite a big family. There are six kids.
It was quite a hot day, so we went to the pool.
He's quite a good cook for a ten-year-old.
My brother drives quite a fast car.
It's quite an interesting book about bees.
We live in quite an old house near the river.
That was quite an easy test.
It was quite an expensive dinner, but the food was great.
She gave quite an unusual answer.
They're quite nice people.
We had quite good weather last week.
You can find quite cheap furniture at the market on Sundays.
The Lins next door have been quite friendly neighbors to us.
My parents give me quite good advice.
These are quite old photos of my grandmother.
I've been waiting for quite a long time.
I've been thinking about your letter for quite a long time.
We haven't seen Ken for quite a long time.
She knows quite a lot about cars.
It took quite a long time to fix the machine.
We spent quite a lot on the holiday.
Is it quite a long drive to your parents' house?
Thanks, everyone. That was quite a useful meeting.
That's quite a nice jacket. Where did you get it?
Quite a big crowd came to the concert.
You have quite a good memory.
It's going to be quite a busy week.

examples.heading: ① quite a + 形容詞 + 名詞

items.en: Let's drive. The lake is quite a long way from here.
items.zh: 開車吧，湖離這裡滿遠的。

items.en: In summer, starting work early is quite a good idea.
items.zh: 夏天提早開始工作是個滿好的主意。

items.en: That's quite a difficult situation you're in.
items.zh: 你現在的處境相當棘手。

items.en: She has quite a big family. There are six kids.
items.zh: 她家人口滿多的，有六個小孩。

items.en: It was quite a hot day, so we went to the pool.
items.zh: 那天滿熱的，所以我們去游泳池。

items.en: He's quite a good cook for a ten-year-old.
items.zh: 以十歲小孩來說，他算很會煮菜了。

items.en: My brother drives quite a fast car.
items.zh: 我哥哥開的車滿快的。

examples.heading: ② quite an + 形容詞 + 名詞

items.en: It's quite an interesting book about bees.
items.zh: 那是一本跟蜜蜂有關、相當有趣的書。

items.en: We live in quite an old house near the river.
items.zh: 我們住在河邊一棟相當老的房子。

items.en: That was quite an easy test.
items.zh: 那次考試還算簡單。

items.en: It was quite an expensive dinner, but the food was great.
items.zh: 那頓晚餐相當貴，不過菜很好吃。

items.en: She gave quite an unusual answer.
items.zh: 她給了一個相當特別的答案。

examples.heading: ③ quite + 形容詞 + 複數 / 不可數名詞

items.en: They're quite nice people.
items.zh: 他們是滿好的人。

items.en: We had quite good weather last week.
items.zh: 我們上禮拜天氣還算不錯。

items.en: You can find quite cheap furniture at the market on Sundays.
items.zh: 星期天的市集可以買到滿便宜的家具。

items.en: The Lins next door have been quite friendly neighbors to us.
items.zh: 隔壁的林家一直是對我們相當友善的鄰居。

items.en: My parents give me quite good advice.
items.zh: 我爸媽給我的建議還滿好的。

items.en: These are quite old photos of my grandmother.
items.zh: 這些是我奶奶滿久以前的照片。

examples.heading: ④ quite a long time / quite a lot

items.en: I've been waiting for quite a long time.
items.zh: 我已經等了滿久了。

items.en: I've been thinking about your letter for quite a long time.
items.zh: 我想你那封信想了滿久。

items.en: We haven't seen Ken for quite a long time.
items.zh: 我們滿久沒見到 Ken 了。

items.en: She knows quite a lot about cars.
items.zh: 她對車子懂得滿多的。

items.en: It took quite a long time to fix the machine.
items.zh: 修那台機器花了滿久的時間。

items.en: We spent quite a lot on the holiday.
items.zh: 這趟假期我們花了滿多錢的。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的句型

items.en: Is it quite a long drive to your parents' house?
items.zh: 開車到你爸媽家滿遠的嗎？

items.en: Thanks, everyone. That was quite a useful meeting.
items.zh: 謝謝大家，這次會議還滿有用的。

items.en: That's quite a nice jacket. Where did you get it?
items.zh: 那件夾克還滿好看的，你在哪裡買的？

items.en: Quite a big crowd came to the concert.
items.zh: 滿多人來看那場演唱會。

items.en: You have quite a good memory.
items.zh: 你記性滿好的。

items.en: It's going to be quite a busy week.
items.zh: 這個禮拜會滿忙的。

title: I must confess that I'm rather a poor player.
translation: 我得承認，我實在玩得不太好。
name: rather a 加形容詞
sentences: My parents live rather a long way from the station.
That's rather a big problem for a small company.
I'm afraid I'm rather a slow reader.
It was rather a strange thing to say at a wedding.
Sorry, I've had rather a busy morning.
The bride's father gave rather a short speech at dinner.
We had rather a bad start to the holiday.
It was rather an odd request.
He drives rather an old car for a rich man.
Sailing is rather an expensive hobby for a student.
It was rather an awkward moment for everyone.
She asked rather an unusual question.
The last part of the exam had a rather difficult question about verbs.
We stayed in a rather old hotel by the sea.
He's a rather quiet person.
We had a rather cold winter in Taipei last year.
She made a rather surprising decision.
They live in a rather small flat in the city.
They were rather difficult questions.
The campsite had rather poor facilities.
They're rather expensive shoes for a child.
The hotel served rather plain food.
These are rather old photos, so the colors are faded.
He gave us rather strange directions.
I must admit it was rather a disappointing result.
I'm afraid this is rather a serious matter.
The report took rather a long time to finish.
It has been rather a difficult year for the company.
I have rather a large number of emails to answer.
That was rather a generous offer.

examples.heading: ① rather a + 形容詞 + 名詞

items.en: My parents live rather a long way from the station.
items.zh: 我爸媽住的地方離車站相當遠。

items.en: That's rather a big problem for a small company.
items.zh: 對一間小公司來說，這是個相當大的問題。

items.en: I'm afraid I'm rather a slow reader.
items.zh: 恐怕我看書看得相當慢。

items.en: It was rather a strange thing to say at a wedding.
items.zh: 在婚禮上說那種話相當奇怪。

items.en: Sorry, I've had rather a busy morning.
items.zh: 抱歉，我今天早上相當忙。

items.en: The bride's father gave rather a short speech at dinner.
items.zh: 新娘的爸爸在晚宴上的致詞相當短。

items.en: We had rather a bad start to the holiday.
items.zh: 我們的假期一開始就相當不順。

examples.heading: ② rather an + 形容詞 + 名詞

items.en: It was rather an odd request.
items.zh: 那是一個相當奇怪的要求。

items.en: He drives rather an old car for a rich man.
items.zh: 以有錢人來說，他開的車相當舊。

items.en: Sailing is rather an expensive hobby for a student.
items.zh: 對學生來說，帆船是相當花錢的嗜好。

items.en: It was rather an awkward moment for everyone.
items.zh: 那一刻大家都相當尷尬。

items.en: She asked rather an unusual question.
items.zh: 她問了一個相當特別的問題。

examples.heading: ③ a rather + 形容詞 + 名詞

items.en: The last part of the exam had a rather difficult question about verbs.
items.zh: 考試的最後一部分有一題關於動詞的題目相當難。

items.en: We stayed in a rather old hotel by the sea.
items.zh: 我們住在海邊一家相當老舊的旅館。

items.en: He's a rather quiet person.
items.zh: 他是個相當安靜的人。

items.en: We had a rather cold winter in Taipei last year.
items.zh: 去年台北的冬天相當冷。

items.en: She made a rather surprising decision.
items.zh: 她做了一個相當出人意料的決定。

items.en: They live in a rather small flat in the city.
items.zh: 他們住在城裡一間相當小的公寓。

examples.heading: ④ rather + 形容詞 + 複數 / 不可數名詞

items.en: They were rather difficult questions.
items.zh: 那些題目相當難。

items.en: The campsite had rather poor facilities.
items.zh: 那個露營區的設施相當簡陋。

items.en: They're rather expensive shoes for a child.
items.zh: 以小孩子穿的來說，那雙鞋相當貴。

items.en: The hotel served rather plain food.
items.zh: 那家旅館的菜相當清淡。

items.en: These are rather old photos, so the colors are faded.
items.zh: 這些照片相當舊了，所以顏色都褪了。

items.en: He gave us rather strange directions.
items.zh: 他給我們的指路說明相當奇怪。

examples.heading: ⑤ 正式的說法

items.en: I must admit it was rather a disappointing result.
items.zh: 我得承認，這個結果相當令人失望。

items.en: I'm afraid this is rather a serious matter.
items.zh: 恐怕這是相當嚴重的事。

items.en: The report took rather a long time to finish.
items.zh: 那份報告花了相當久的時間才完成。

items.en: It has been rather a difficult year for the company.
items.zh: 對公司來說，這一年相當艱難。

items.en: I have rather a large number of emails to answer.
items.zh: 我有相當多封電子郵件要回。

items.en: That was rather a generous offer.
items.zh: 那是一個相當大方的提議。

title: I always watch the latest music videos.

items.zh: 離飯店最近的海灘是哪一個？

sentences: The sea is warmer than the pool.

Ann is stronger than he is.
