items.zh: 開始下雨了，所以我們進到屋裡。

items.en: Your umbrella is inside, by the door.
items.zh: 你的雨傘在屋裡，門旁邊。

items.en: Our dog sleeps outside in summer.
items.zh: 我們的狗夏天睡在外面。

examples.heading: ④ upstairs、downstairs

items.en: My bedroom is upstairs.
items.zh: 我的房間在樓上。

items.en: Grandma can't walk upstairs anymore.
items.zh: 奶奶已經沒辦法走上樓了。

items.en: Someone is knocking on the door downstairs.
items.zh: 樓下有人在敲門。

items.en: Can you take these towels upstairs?
items.zh: 你可以把這些毛巾拿上樓嗎？

items.en: Breakfast is ready, so come downstairs.
items.zh: 早餐好了，下樓來吧。

examples.heading: ⑤ abroad、nearby、everywhere

items.en: My uncle spent ten years teaching English abroad.
items.zh: 我叔叔在國外教了十年英文。

items.en: My grandparents live nearby, so they visit us every weekend.
items.zh: 我爺爺奶奶住在附近，所以每個週末都會來看我們。

items.en: I looked for my glasses everywhere.
items.zh: 我到處找我的眼鏡。

items.en: My parents have never travelled abroad.
items.zh: 我爸媽從來沒出過國。

items.en: We found a nice little hotel nearby.
items.zh: 我們在附近找到一間不錯的小旅館。

examples.heading: ⑥ 受詞 + 地點副詞

items.en: I met my husband there.
items.zh: 我是在那裡認識我先生的。

items.en: Can you bring your guitar here on Saturday?
items.zh: 你星期六可以把吉他帶來這裡嗎？

items.en: Could you carry the shopping bags upstairs for me?
items.zh: 你可以幫我把購物袋提上樓嗎？

examples.heading: ⑦ 地點副詞 + 時間

items.en: I'll see you there at half past seven.
items.zh: 我們七點半那裡見。

items.en: We're going abroad next month.
items.zh: 我們下個月要出國。

items.en: My brother came home late last night.
items.zh: 我哥昨晚很晚才回家。

items.en: Let's have lunch outside today.
items.zh: 我們今天在外面吃午餐吧。

title: For a long time, many politicians have been able to work almost exclusively for their own interests.
translation: 很長一段時間以來，很多政客幾乎都只為自己的利益做事。
name: 前後有修飾語的副詞片語
sentences: The company makes furniture almost exclusively for hotels.
The charity relies almost exclusively on donations from the public.
My grandfather listens nearly exclusively to jazz from the 1950s.
The research focused almost exclusively on young adults.
The architect designed the building almost exclusively for elderly residents.
Two research teams carried out the studies completely independently of each other.
The judges reach their decisions entirely independently of the government.
By the age of ten, most children can study quite independently of their parents.
The app works completely independently of the internet.
The two inventors developed the idea entirely independently of one another.
The hospital runs the new wing quite separately from the main building.
Our town collects glass completely separately from other rubbish.
The police interviewed the children entirely separately from their parents.
We need to deal with these two issues quite separately from each other.
Boys and girls often react very differently to the same situation.
The second film ends rather differently from the book.
My brother thinks quite differently from the rest of the family.
Young people today spend their money very differently from their parents.
Prices in the capital have developed rather differently to those in the north.
The new model behaves remarkably similarly to the old one.
The twins dress very similarly to each other.
The disease spreads quite similarly to the common cold.
In the test, the cheap battery performed surprisingly similarly to the expensive one.
The staff acted entirely consistently with the company's rules.
The government spent the money completely consistently with its promises.
The law applies to everyone, completely regardless of age.
The prize is given to the best student, quite regardless of background.
It was so completely in harmony with the sun and the sea that I decided to buy it.
The committee made the decision far too quickly for anyone to object.
She sings so differently from her mother that nobody believes they're related.

examples.heading: ① almost、nearly + exclusively + 介系詞片語

items.en: The company makes furniture almost exclusively for hotels.
items.zh: 這家公司做的家具幾乎都是賣給旅館的。

items.en: The charity relies almost exclusively on donations from the public.
items.zh: 這個慈善團體幾乎完全仰賴民眾的捐款。

items.en: My grandfather listens nearly exclusively to jazz from the 1950s.
items.zh: 我爺爺幾乎只聽 1950 年代的爵士樂。

items.en: The research focused almost exclusively on young adults.
items.zh: 這項研究幾乎只針對年輕人。

items.en: The architect designed the building almost exclusively for elderly residents.
items.zh: 建築師幾乎是專為年長住戶設計這棟大樓的。

examples.heading: ② completely、entirely + independently of

items.en: Two research teams carried out the studies completely independently of each other.
items.zh: 兩個研究團隊完全各自獨立進行這兩項研究。

items.en: The judges reach their decisions entirely independently of the government.
items.zh: 法官完全不受政府影響，自行做出判決。

items.en: By the age of ten, most children can study quite independently of their parents.
items.zh: 到了十歲，大部分孩子都能相當程度地不靠父母自己讀書。

items.en: The app works completely independently of the internet.
items.zh: 這個應用程式完全不需要網路就能運作。

items.en: The two inventors developed the idea entirely independently of one another.
items.zh: 兩位發明家完全各自想出了這個點子。

examples.heading: ③ quite、completely、entirely + separately from

items.en: The hospital runs the new wing quite separately from the main building.
items.zh: 醫院把新的側樓和主建築分開管理。

items.en: Our town collects glass completely separately from other rubbish.
items.zh: 我們鎮上把玻璃和其他垃圾完全分開回收。

items.en: The police interviewed the children entirely separately from their parents.
items.zh: 警方在父母完全不在場的情況下訪談孩子們。

items.en: We need to deal with these two issues quite separately from each other.
items.zh: 我們得把這兩個問題分開處理。

examples.heading: ④ very、rather、quite + differently from、to

items.en: Boys and girls often react very differently to the same situation.
items.zh: 男孩和女孩面對同樣的情況，反應常常很不一樣。

items.en: The second film ends rather differently from the book.
items.zh: 第二部電影的結局和原著相當不同。

items.en: My brother thinks quite differently from the rest of the family.
items.zh: 我哥的想法和家裡其他人很不一樣。

items.en: Young people today spend their money very differently from their parents.
items.zh: 現在的年輕人花錢的方式跟他們的父母很不一樣。

items.en: Prices in the capital have developed rather differently to those in the north.
items.zh: 首都的房價走勢跟北部相當不同。

examples.heading: ⑤ remarkably、very、quite、surprisingly + similarly to

items.en: The new model behaves remarkably similarly to the old one.
items.zh: 新型號的表現和舊型號非常相似。

items.en: The twins dress very similarly to each other.
items.zh: 那對雙胞胎穿得很像。

items.en: The disease spreads quite similarly to the common cold.
items.zh: 這種病傳播的方式和普通感冒很像。

items.en: In the test, the cheap battery performed surprisingly similarly to the expensive one.
items.zh: 測試中，便宜的電池表現出乎意料地和貴的很接近。

examples.heading: ⑥ entirely、completely、quite + consistently with、regardless of

items.en: The staff acted entirely consistently with the company's rules.
items.zh: 員工的行為完全符合公司的規定。

items.en: The government spent the money completely consistently with its promises.
items.zh: 政府花這筆錢的方式和它的承諾完全一致。

items.en: The law applies to everyone, completely regardless of age.
items.zh: 這條法律適用於每個人，完全不分年齡。

items.en: The prize is given to the best student, quite regardless of background.
items.zh: 這個獎頒給最優秀的學生，完全不看家庭背景。

examples.heading: ⑦ so、far too + 副詞 + 介系詞片語

items.en: It was so completely in harmony with the sun and the sea that I decided to buy it.
items.zh: 它和陽光、大海是那麼地和諧，我當場決定買下來。

items.en: The committee made the decision far too quickly for anyone to object.
items.zh: 委員會做決定做得太快，誰都來不及反對。

items.en: She sings so differently from her mother that nobody believes they're related.
items.zh: 她唱歌的方式和她媽媽差太多了，沒人相信她們是母女。

title: I really love walking.
translation: 我真的很愛散步。
name: really 放在主詞和動詞之間
sentences: My little brother really loves dinosaurs.
We really enjoyed our walk along the river.
I really hate getting up early on Mondays.
Our students really like the new library.
Grandpa really enjoys his garden in spring.
I really need a new phone.
The kids really want a puppy for Christmas.
We really hope you can come to the wedding.
My dad really needs a holiday.
I really want to learn to swim this summer.
I would really like to visit Japan one day.
You should really try the fish here.
I can really see the difference now.
Everyone at the office will really miss Helen.
She has really changed since last year.
I don't really care about football.
My parents don't really understand computers.
He doesn't really talk much in class.
We didn't really enjoy the trip because of the rain.
I don't really know your cousin.
I really don't feel like going out tonight.
She really doesn't like waiting in queues.
You really don't need to bring anything.
We really don't have time for lunch today.
My cat really doesn't like the vet.
Do you really live next to the station?
Does Tom really speak four languages?
Did she really eat the whole pizza?
Do you really think it will snow tomorrow?
Do they really want to move to the countryside?

examples.heading: ① really + like、love、enjoy、hate

items.en: My little brother really loves dinosaurs.
items.zh: 我弟弟超愛恐龍。

items.en: We really enjoyed our walk along the river.
items.zh: 我們沿著河邊散步，走得很開心。

items.en: I really hate getting up early on Mondays.
items.zh: 我真的很討厭星期一早起。

items.en: Our students really like the new library.
items.zh: 我們的學生很喜歡新的圖書館。

items.en: Grandpa really enjoys his garden in spring.
items.zh: 爺爺春天很喜歡待在他的花園裡。

examples.heading: ② really + want、need、hope

items.en: I really need a new phone.
items.zh: 我真的需要一支新手機。

items.en: The kids really want a puppy for Christmas.
items.zh: 孩子們很想要一隻小狗當聖誕禮物。

items.en: We really hope you can come to the wedding.
items.zh: 我們很希望你能來參加婚禮。

items.en: My dad really needs a holiday.
items.zh: 我爸真的需要放個假。

items.en: I really want to learn to swim this summer.
items.zh: 我今年夏天很想學游泳。

examples.heading: ③ 助動詞 + really + 動詞

items.en: I would really like to visit Japan one day.
items.zh: 我很想有一天去日本玩。

items.en: You should really try the fish here.
items.zh: 你真的該試試這裡的魚。

items.en: I can really see the difference now.
items.zh: 我現在真的看得出差別了。

items.en: Everyone at the office will really miss Helen.
items.zh: 辦公室的大家都會很想念 Helen。

items.en: She has really changed since last year.
items.zh: 她從去年到現在變了很多。

examples.heading: ④ don't really + 動詞

items.en: I don't really care about football.
items.zh: 我不太在乎足球。

items.en: My parents don't really understand computers.
items.zh: 我爸媽不太懂電腦。

items.en: He doesn't really talk much in class.
items.zh: 他上課不太說話。

items.en: We didn't really enjoy the trip because of the rain.
items.zh: 因為下雨，那趟旅行我們玩得不太開心。

items.en: I don't really know your cousin.
items.zh: 我跟你表哥不太熟。

examples.heading: ⑤ really don't + 動詞

items.en: I really don't feel like going out tonight.
items.zh: 我今晚真的很不想出門。

items.en: She really doesn't like waiting in queues.
items.zh: 她真的很不喜歡排隊。

items.en: You really don't need to bring anything.
items.zh: 你真的什麼都不用帶。

items.en: We really don't have time for lunch today.
items.zh: 我們今天真的沒時間吃午餐。

items.en: My cat really doesn't like the vet.
items.zh: 我的貓真的很討厭獸醫。

examples.heading: ⑥ 疑問句

items.en: Do you really live next to the station?
items.zh: 你真的住在車站旁邊嗎？

items.en: Does Tom really speak four languages?
items.zh: Tom 真的會說四種語言嗎？

items.en: Did she really eat the whole pizza?
items.zh: 她真的把整個披薩吃完了嗎？

items.en: Do you really think it will snow tomorrow?
items.zh: 你真的覺得明天會下雪嗎？

items.en: Do they really want to move to the countryside?
items.zh: 他們真的想搬到鄉下嗎？

title: First, I bought a pair of shoes, and then I bought a dress.
translation: 我先買了一雙鞋子，然後又買了一件洋裝。
name: 句首的句子副詞
sentences: First, wash your hands. Then you can help me with the salad.
First we went to the beach, and then we had ice cream.
We waited for two hours. Finally, the doctor called my name.
First, I want to thank my parents for their help.
Fill in the form. Then give it to the woman at the desk.
I looked for my keys everywhere. Finally, I found them in my coat.
Thanks for the cake. Actually, I'm not very hungry right now.
Everyone thinks Sam is shy. Actually, he talks a lot at home.
I said I'd come at six. Actually, can we meet at seven?
The test looked difficult. Actually, it was quite easy.
You don't need to bring anything. Actually, we need a few more chairs.
My aunt planned a big garden party. Unfortunately, only six people came.
Unfortunately, the concert tickets were too expensive for us.
I'd love to help. Unfortunately, I'm working on Saturday.
Unfortunately, we missed the last bus home.
The hotel was nice. Unfortunately, the beach was very dirty.
I left my wallet in the taxi. Luckily, the driver brought it back.
Luckily, I had an umbrella in my bag.
The car broke down. Luckily, we were near a garage.
Luckily, the shop still had my size.
You're my best friend. Of course I'll come to your wedding.
Of course, you can stay with us when you're in Rome.
It's your birthday, so of course you can choose the restaurant.
Of course, the children were very excited about the snow.
My brother wanted to be a pilot. Actually, he's a teacher now.
I called you three times. Unfortunately, your phone was off.
We got lost on the way. Finally, a farmer showed us the road.
Our flight was late. Then we lost our suitcase.
My phone fell in the water. Luckily, it still works.
I'll be home late tonight. Of course, you can start dinner without me.

examples.heading: ① first、then、finally

items.en: First, wash your hands. Then you can help me with the salad.
items.zh: 先洗手，然後你可以幫我弄沙拉。

items.en: First we went to the beach, and then we had ice cream.
items.zh: 我們先去了海邊，然後吃了冰淇淋。

items.en: We waited for two hours. Finally, the doctor called my name.
items.zh: 我們等了兩個小時，最後醫生終於叫到我的名字。

items.en: First, I want to thank my parents for their help.
items.zh: 首先，我要謝謝我爸媽的幫忙。

items.en: Fill in the form. Then give it to the woman at the desk.
items.zh: 把表格填好，然後交給櫃台的小姐。

items.en: I looked for my keys everywhere. Finally, I found them in my coat.
items.zh: 我到處找鑰匙，最後在外套裡找到了。

examples.heading: ② actually

items.en: Thanks for the cake. Actually, I'm not very hungry right now.
items.zh: 謝謝你的蛋糕。其實我現在不太餓。

items.en: Everyone thinks Sam is shy. Actually, he talks a lot at home.
items.zh: 大家都以為 Sam 很害羞。其實他在家話很多。

items.en: I said I'd come at six. Actually, can we meet at seven?
items.zh: 我說過我六點會到。其實我們可以改七點見面嗎？

items.en: The test looked difficult. Actually, it was quite easy.
items.zh: 那個考試看起來很難，其實滿簡單的。

items.en: You don't need to bring anything. Actually, we need a few more chairs.
items.zh: 你什麼都不用帶。其實我們還需要幾張椅子。

examples.heading: ③ unfortunately

items.en: My aunt planned a big garden party. Unfortunately, only six people came.
items.zh: 我阿姨辦了一場盛大的花園派對，可惜只來了六個人。

items.en: Unfortunately, the concert tickets were too expensive for us.
items.zh: 可惜音樂會的票對我們來說太貴了。

items.en: I'd love to help. Unfortunately, I'm working on Saturday.
items.zh: 我很想幫忙。可惜我星期六要上班。

items.en: Unfortunately, we missed the last bus home.
items.zh: 可惜我們錯過了回家的末班公車。

items.en: The hotel was nice. Unfortunately, the beach was very dirty.
items.zh: 旅館很好。可惜海灘很髒。

examples.heading: ④ luckily

items.en: I left my wallet in the taxi. Luckily, the driver brought it back.
items.zh: 我把錢包忘在計程車上，幸好司機送回來了。

items.en: Luckily, I had an umbrella in my bag.
items.zh: 幸好我包包裡有一把傘。

items.en: The car broke down. Luckily, we were near a garage.
items.zh: 車子拋錨了，幸好我們就在修車廠附近。

items.en: Luckily, the shop still had my size.
items.zh: 幸好店裡還有我的尺寸。

examples.heading: ⑤ of course

items.en: You're my best friend. Of course I'll come to your wedding.
items.zh: 你是我最好的朋友，我當然會去你的婚禮。

items.en: Of course, you can stay with us when you're in Rome.
items.zh: 你來羅馬的時候，當然可以住我們家。

items.en: It's your birthday, so of course you can choose the restaurant.
items.zh: 今天是你生日，餐廳當然由你選。

items.en: Of course, the children were very excited about the snow.
items.zh: 孩子們看到下雪當然很興奮。

examples.heading: ⑥ 句子副詞連接前一句

items.en: My brother wanted to be a pilot. Actually, he's a teacher now.
items.zh: 我哥哥本來想當飛行員。其實他現在是老師。

items.en: I called you three times. Unfortunately, your phone was off.
items.zh: 我打了三次電話給你，可惜你關機了。

items.en: We got lost on the way. Finally, a farmer showed us the road.
items.zh: 我們在路上迷路了。最後一個農夫幫我們指了路。

items.en: Our flight was late. Then we lost our suitcase.
items.zh: 我們的班機誤點了，然後行李箱又不見了。

items.en: My phone fell in the water. Luckily, it still works.
items.zh: 我的手機掉到水裡，幸好還能用。

items.en: I'll be home late tonight. Of course, you can start dinner without me.
items.zh: 我今晚會晚回家。你們當然可以先吃晚餐，不用等我。

title: Yesterday I went shopping and bought some clothes.
translation: 昨天我去逛街，買了一些衣服。
name: 時間副詞和順序副詞修飾子句
sentences: Yesterday we cleaned the whole house.
Today I have three classes.
Last week my sister started a new job.
Tomorrow we're going to the zoo.
Last year, we moved to a bigger flat.
This morning I missed the bus and walked to school.
I saw your brother yesterday.
We have a maths test today.
She'll call you tomorrow.
They got married last month.
My parents bought a car last week.
My uncle often sends us photos from his trips.
He always forgets his keys.
I've just finished my essay.
They've already left.
She is often late for class.
I usually walk my dog after dinner.
Yesterday I got up late and missed breakfast.
Last night we went out and had a pizza.
On Sunday my family visited my aunt and stayed for lunch.
Every morning she makes coffee and reads the news.
First I washed the car, then I cut the grass.
We watched a film. After that, we went to bed.
First you mix the eggs and sugar, then you add the flour.
She did her homework. After that, she called her friends.
First we went to the market, and then we cooked dinner together.
Yesterday we went to the beach first, and then we had lunch.
Last weekend I painted my room. After that, I bought a new lamp.
This afternoon I'll go to the bank, and then I'll meet you.
Last summer we visited Rome first. Then we went to Venice.

examples.heading: ① 句首的時間副詞

items.en: Yesterday we cleaned the whole house.
items.zh: 昨天我們把整間房子打掃了一遍。

items.en: Today I have three classes.
items.zh: 我今天有三堂課。

items.en: Last week my sister started a new job.
items.zh: 上禮拜我姊姊開始做新工作。

items.en: Tomorrow we're going to the zoo.
items.zh: 明天我們要去動物園。

items.en: Last year, we moved to a bigger flat.
items.zh: 去年我們搬到比較大的公寓。

items.en: This morning I missed the bus and walked to school.
items.zh: 今天早上我錯過公車，走路去學校。

examples.heading: ② 句尾的時間副詞

items.en: I saw your brother yesterday.
items.zh: 我昨天看到你哥哥。

items.en: We have a maths test today.
items.zh: 我們今天有數學考試。

items.en: She'll call you tomorrow.
items.zh: 她明天會打給你。

items.en: They got married last month.
items.zh: 他們上個月結婚了。

items.en: My parents bought a car last week.
items.zh: 我爸媽上禮拜買了一輛車。

examples.heading: ③ 句中的時間副詞

items.en: My uncle often sends us photos from his trips.
items.zh: 我叔叔常傳他旅行的照片給我們。

items.en: He always forgets his keys.
items.zh: 他總是忘記帶鑰匙。

items.en: I've just finished my essay.
items.zh: 我剛寫完報告。

items.en: They've already left.
items.zh: 他們已經走了。

items.en: She is often late for class.
items.zh: 她上課常遲到。

items.en: I usually walk my dog after dinner.
items.zh: 我通常晚餐後遛狗。

examples.heading: ④ 時間副詞修飾兩個動詞

items.en: Yesterday I got up late and missed breakfast.
items.zh: 昨天我起得晚，沒吃到早餐。

items.en: Last night we went out and had a pizza.
items.zh: 昨晚我們出去吃了披薩。

items.en: On Sunday my family visited my aunt and stayed for lunch.
items.zh: 星期天我們全家去看我阿姨，留下來吃午餐。

items.en: Every morning she makes coffee and reads the news.
items.zh: 她每天早上泡咖啡、看新聞。

examples.heading: ⑤ first、then、after that

items.en: First I washed the car, then I cut the grass.
items.zh: 我先洗車，然後割草。

items.en: We watched a film. After that, we went to bed.
items.zh: 我們看了一部電影。之後就去睡了。

items.en: First you mix the eggs and sugar, then you add the flour.
items.zh: 你先把蛋和糖拌在一起，然後加麵粉。

items.en: She did her homework. After that, she called her friends.
items.zh: 她寫完功課。之後打電話給她的朋友。

items.en: First we went to the market, and then we cooked dinner together.
items.zh: 我們先去市場，然後一起煮晚餐。

examples.heading: ⑥ 時間副詞和順序副詞一起用

items.en: Yesterday we went to the beach first, and then we had lunch.
items.zh: 昨天我們先去海邊，然後吃午餐。

items.en: Last weekend I painted my room. After that, I bought a new lamp.
items.zh: 上個週末我油漆了我的房間。之後買了一盞新燈。

items.en: This afternoon I'll go to the bank, and then I'll meet you.
items.zh: 今天下午我會先去銀行，然後跟你碰面。

items.en: Last summer we visited Rome first. Then we went to Venice.
items.zh: 去年夏天我們先去羅馬。然後去威尼斯。

title: We can meet tomorrow.
translation: 我們可以明天見面。
name: 時間副詞放在句尾
sentences: My cousin is flying back to Canada tomorrow.
There's a football match on TV tonight.
I finished the whole book yesterday.
Can you pick up the kids from school today?
The new supermarket opens tomorrow.
Mum is making lasagne tonight.
I'm busy at the moment, so I'll text you later.
The plumber said he would be here soon.
Please turn off your phones now.
Dinner will be ready soon.
We can talk about the holiday later.
My sister lives in Manchester now.
The train arrived ten minutes late.
I want to go to bed early tonight.
Sorry, I'm going to be a bit late.
Our neighbours always get up early.
He worked late every night last week.
I failed my driving test, but I'm taking it again in May.
I lost my umbrella again.
We'd love to visit your town again.
Let's try the new Thai restaurant again next month.
The printer isn't working again.
I'll send you the photos tomorrow.
She cleaned her bedroom yesterday.
Don't forget to water the plants tonight.
We watched a scary film yesterday.
My parents are coming to my school tomorrow.
I was at the dentist's yesterday.
Let's meet at the café later.
My brother got home from the party really late.
We're going to the cinema tonight.

examples.heading: ① today、tomorrow、yesterday、tonight

items.en: My cousin is flying back to Canada tomorrow.
items.zh: 我表哥明天要飛回加拿大。

items.en: There's a football match on TV tonight.
items.zh: 今晚電視上有足球比賽。

items.en: I finished the whole book yesterday.
items.zh: 我昨天把整本書看完了。

items.en: Can you pick up the kids from school today?
items.zh: 你今天可以去學校接孩子嗎？

items.en: The new supermarket opens tomorrow.
items.zh: 新的超市明天開幕。

items.en: Mum is making lasagne tonight.
items.zh: 媽媽今晚要做千層麵。

examples.heading: ② now、soon、later

items.en: I'm busy at the moment, so I'll text you later.
items.zh: 我現在在忙，晚點再傳訊息給你。

items.en: The plumber said he would be here soon.
items.zh: 水電工說他很快就會到。

items.en: Please turn off your phones now.
items.zh: 現在請把手機關機。

items.en: Dinner will be ready soon.
items.zh: 晚餐快好了。

items.en: We can talk about the holiday later.
items.zh: 我們晚點再討論假期的事。

items.en: My sister lives in Manchester now.
items.zh: 我姊姊現在住在曼徹斯特。

examples.heading: ③ early、late

items.en: The train arrived ten minutes late.
items.zh: 火車晚了十分鐘到。

items.en: I want to go to bed early tonight.
items.zh: 我今晚想早點睡。

items.en: Sorry, I'm going to be a bit late.
items.zh: 抱歉，我會晚一點到。

items.en: Our neighbours always get up early.
items.zh: 我們的鄰居都很早起床。

items.en: He worked late every night last week.
items.zh: 他上禮拜每天晚上都工作到很晚。

examples.heading: ④ again

items.en: I failed my driving test, but I'm taking it again in May.
items.zh: 我駕照考試沒過，不過五月要再考一次。

items.en: I lost my umbrella again.
items.zh: 我又把雨傘弄丟了。

items.en: We'd love to visit your town again.
items.zh: 我們很想再去你們那裡玩。

items.en: Let's try the new Thai restaurant again next month.
items.zh: 我們下個月再去那家新的泰式餐廳吧。

items.en: The printer isn't working again.
items.zh: 印表機又壞了。

examples.heading: ⑤ 受詞 + 時間副詞

items.en: I'll send you the photos tomorrow.
items.zh: 我明天把照片傳給你。

items.en: She cleaned her bedroom yesterday.
items.zh: 她昨天打掃了她的房間。

items.en: Don't forget to water the plants tonight.
items.zh: 今晚別忘了給植物澆水。

items.en: We watched a scary film yesterday.
items.zh: 我們昨天看了一部恐怖片。

examples.heading: ⑥ 地點 + 時間副詞

items.en: My parents are coming to my school tomorrow.
items.zh: 我爸媽明天要來我學校。

items.en: I was at the dentist's yesterday.
items.zh: 我昨天去看牙醫了。

items.en: Let's meet at the café later.
items.zh: 我們晚點在咖啡店碰面吧。

items.en: My brother got home from the party really late.
items.zh: 我哥哥參加完派對，很晚才回到家。

items.en: We're going to the cinema tonight.
items.zh: 我們今晚要去看電影。

title: Luckily enough, we have a garden where we can cook over an open fire.
translation: 幸好我們有個花園，可以在那裡生火煮東西。
name: 副詞後加 enough 加強語氣
sentences: Luckily enough, the restaurant still had one table free.
Luckily enough, my neighbour had a spare key.
Luckily enough, the weather stayed dry for the whole festival.
Luckily enough, nobody was in the car when the tree fell.
Luckily enough, I'd saved a copy of the report on my laptop.
Surprisingly enough, the cheapest wine tasted the best.
Surprisingly enough, my grandfather loves video games.
Surprisingly enough, the train arrived exactly on time.
The children, surprisingly enough, ate all their vegetables.
Surprisingly enough, very few people applied for the job.
Sadly enough, I wasn't able to find any job offers.
Sadly enough, the old theatre is going to be knocked down.
Sadly enough, many of these animals are now in danger.
Sadly enough, the band split up before their second album.
Strangely enough, I've never been to the beach near my house.
Oddly enough, the shop was empty on a Saturday afternoon.
The dog, strangely enough, didn't bark at the stranger.
Oddly enough, I felt more relaxed during the exam than before it.
Strangely enough, we both chose the same dress for the party.
Funnily enough, I met my wife on a train.
Funnily enough, my brother and I have the same birthday.
Funnily enough, I was just about to call you.
Funnily enough, the person sitting next to me was from my hometown.
Interestingly enough, the word "robot" comes from Czech.
Interestingly enough, women in the survey slept less than men.
Interestingly enough, sales went up during the rainy months.
The book, interestingly enough, was written in only three weeks.
My sister, luckily enough, found her passport in the taxi.
The meeting, sadly enough, ended without any decision.
Our old car, funnily enough, never broke down once.

examples.heading: ① luckily enough

items.en: Luckily enough, the restaurant still had one table free.
items.zh: 很幸運的是，那家餐廳還有一張空桌。

items.en: Luckily enough, my neighbour had a spare key.
items.zh: 很幸運的是，我鄰居有一把備用鑰匙。

items.en: Luckily enough, the weather stayed dry for the whole festival.
items.zh: 很幸運的是，整個音樂節期間都沒下雨。

items.en: Luckily enough, nobody was in the car when the tree fell.
items.zh: 很幸運的是，樹倒下來的時候車裡沒人。

items.en: Luckily enough, I'd saved a copy of the report on my laptop.
items.zh: 很幸運的是，我在筆電裡存了一份報告。

examples.heading: ② surprisingly enough

items.en: Surprisingly enough, the cheapest wine tasted the best.
items.zh: 出乎意料的是，最便宜的酒最好喝。

items.en: Surprisingly enough, my grandfather loves video games.
items.zh: 出乎意料的是，我爺爺很愛打電動。

items.en: Surprisingly enough, the train arrived exactly on time.
items.zh: 出乎意料的是，火車準時到站了。

items.en: The children, surprisingly enough, ate all their vegetables.
items.zh: 出乎意料的是，孩子們把蔬菜全吃光了。

items.en: Surprisingly enough, very few people applied for the job.
items.zh: 出乎意料的是，應徵這份工作的人很少。

examples.heading: ③ sadly enough

items.en: Sadly enough, I wasn't able to find any job offers.
items.zh: 可惜的是，我沒找到任何工作機會。

items.en: Sadly enough, the old theatre is going to be knocked down.
items.zh: 令人難過的是，那間老劇院要被拆掉了。

items.en: Sadly enough, many of these animals are now in danger.
items.zh: 令人難過的是，這些動物很多現在都瀕臨絕種。

items.en: Sadly enough, the band split up before their second album.
items.zh: 可惜的是，那個樂團在出第二張專輯前就解散了。

examples.heading: ④ strangely enough、oddly enough

items.en: Strangely enough, I've never been to the beach near my house.
items.zh: 說也奇怪，我從來沒去過我家附近的海灘。

items.en: Oddly enough, the shop was empty on a Saturday afternoon.
items.zh: 說也奇怪，星期六下午店裡竟然沒人。

items.en: The dog, strangely enough, didn't bark at the stranger.
items.zh: 說也奇怪，那隻狗沒有對陌生人叫。

items.en: Oddly enough, I felt more relaxed during the exam than before it.
items.zh: 說也奇怪，我考試的時候反而比考前放鬆。

items.en: Strangely enough, we both chose the same dress for the party.
items.zh: 說也奇怪，我們兩個為派對挑了同一件洋裝。

examples.heading: ⑤ funnily enough

items.en: Funnily enough, I met my wife on a train.
items.zh: 說來也巧，我是在火車上認識我太太的。

items.en: Funnily enough, my brother and I have the same birthday.
items.zh: 說來也巧，我和我哥同一天生日。

items.en: Funnily enough, I was just about to call you.
items.zh: 說來也巧，我正要打給你。

items.en: Funnily enough, the person sitting next to me was from my hometown.
items.zh: 說來也巧，坐在我旁邊的人跟我同鄉。

examples.heading: ⑥ interestingly enough

items.en: Interestingly enough, the word "robot" comes from Czech.
items.zh: 有意思的是，robot 這個字來自捷克文。

items.en: Interestingly enough, women in the survey slept less than men.
items.zh: 有意思的是，調查中的女性睡得比男性少。

items.en: Interestingly enough, sales went up during the rainy months.
items.zh: 有意思的是，下雨的那幾個月銷售量反而上升了。

items.en: The book, interestingly enough, was written in only three weeks.
items.zh: 有意思的是，這本書只花了三個禮拜就寫完了。

examples.heading: ⑦ 插在主詞和動詞中間

items.en: My sister, luckily enough, found her passport in the taxi.
items.zh: 很幸運的是，我姊姊在計程車上找到了她的護照。

items.en: The meeting, sadly enough, ended without any decision.
items.zh: 可惜的是，會議最後沒有做出任何決定。

items.en: Our old car, funnily enough, never broke down once.
items.zh: 說來好笑，我們那輛舊車一次都沒壞過。

title: Luckily for you, I kept notes on everything we did.
translation: 算你運氣好，我把我們做過的每件事都記下來了。
name: 副詞後接介系詞片語表示強調
sentences: Luckily for me, my sister lent me her car.
Fortunately for the passengers, the pilot landed the plane safely.
Luckily for the team, their best player recovered in time.
Fortunately for us, the hotel had one room left.
Luckily for the children, school was closed because of the snow.
Unfortunately for Tom, the exam was on the one topic he hadn't studied.
Sadly for the fans, the concert was cancelled at the last minute.
Unfortunately for the company, the new product failed.
Sadly for my grandmother, she couldn't travel to the wedding.
Unfortunately for the tourists, the museum was closed for repairs.
Conveniently for us, the station is right next to the hotel.
Conveniently for parents, the school has a free car park.
Conveniently for the staff, the canteen stays open until eight.
Conveniently for me, the meeting was moved to Friday.
Especially in winter, the roads here can be dangerous.
Prices went up sharply, particularly during the last three months.
The city is very crowded, especially at weekends.
Particularly in the early mornings, the park is very peaceful.
Sales fell, especially between January and March.
Especially in big cities, rents have become very high.
The disease is common, particularly in tropical countries.
Many shops have closed, especially in the town centre.
Particularly in rural areas, buses are not very frequent.
English is widely spoken, especially in tourist areas.
Probably in the next few years, most cars will be electric.
Probably by the end of the month, the bridge will be finished.
Probably in about two weeks, you'll get the results.
Probably after the summer, we'll move to a bigger flat.
The rain, luckily for us, stopped before the wedding.
The ferry, unfortunately for the passengers, left six hours late.

examples.heading: ① luckily for、fortunately for

items.en: Luckily for me, my sister lent me her car.
items.zh: 算我運氣好，我姊姊把她的車借給我。

items.en: Fortunately for the passengers, the pilot landed the plane safely.
items.zh: 對乘客來說很幸運，機長讓飛機平安降落。

items.en: Luckily for the team, their best player recovered in time.
items.zh: 對球隊來說很幸運，他們最好的球員及時康復了。

items.en: Fortunately for us, the hotel had one room left.
items.zh: 我們很幸運，那間旅館還剩一間房。

items.en: Luckily for the children, school was closed because of the snow.
items.zh: 孩子們很幸運，學校因為下雪停課了。

examples.heading: ② unfortunately for、sadly for

items.en: Unfortunately for Tom, the exam was on the one topic he hadn't studied.
items.zh: 對 Tom 來說很不幸，考試考的正是他唯一沒讀的那個主題。

items.en: Sadly for the fans, the concert was cancelled at the last minute.
items.zh: 對歌迷來說很遺憾，演唱會在最後一刻取消了。

items.en: Unfortunately for the company, the new product failed.
items.zh: 對那家公司來說很不幸，新產品失敗了。

items.en: Sadly for my grandmother, she couldn't travel to the wedding.
items.zh: 對我奶奶來說很遺憾，她沒辦法去參加婚禮。

items.en: Unfortunately for the tourists, the museum was closed for repairs.
items.zh: 對遊客來說很不巧，博物館正在整修，沒有開放。

examples.heading: ③ conveniently for

items.en: Conveniently for us, the station is right next to the hotel.
items.zh: 對我們來說很方便，車站就在旅館旁邊。

items.en: Conveniently for parents, the school has a free car park.
items.zh: 對家長來說很方便，學校有免費的停車場。

items.en: Conveniently for the staff, the canteen stays open until eight.
items.zh: 對員工來說很方便，員工餐廳開到八點。

items.en: Conveniently for me, the meeting was moved to Friday.
items.zh: 對我來說剛好方便，會議改到星期五了。

examples.heading: ④ especially、particularly + 時間片語

items.en: Especially in winter, the roads here can be dangerous.
items.zh: 特別是冬天，這裡的路可能很危險。

items.en: Prices went up sharply, particularly during the last three months.
items.zh: 價格大幅上漲，特別是最近三個月。

items.en: The city is very crowded, especially at weekends.
items.zh: 這座城市很擠，特別是週末。

items.en: Particularly in the early mornings, the park is very peaceful.
items.zh: 特別是清晨，公園非常寧靜。

items.en: Sales fell, especially between January and March.
items.zh: 銷售量下滑，特別是一月到三月之間。

examples.heading: ⑤ especially、particularly + 地點片語

items.en: Especially in big cities, rents have become very high.
items.zh: 特別是在大城市，房租變得非常高。

items.en: The disease is common, particularly in tropical countries.
items.zh: 這種病很常見，特別是在熱帶國家。

items.en: Many shops have closed, especially in the town centre.
items.zh: 很多商店都關了，特別是在市中心。

items.en: Particularly in rural areas, buses are not very frequent.
items.zh: 特別是在鄉下地區，公車班次不多。

items.en: English is widely spoken, especially in tourist areas.
items.zh: 英語在很多地方都通，特別是在觀光區。

examples.heading: ⑥ probably + 介系詞片語

items.en: Probably in the next few years, most cars will be electric.
items.zh: 大概在未來幾年內，大部分的車都會是電動車。

items.en: Probably by the end of the month, the bridge will be finished.
items.zh: 大概到月底，這座橋就會完工。

items.en: Probably in about two weeks, you'll get the results.
items.zh: 大概再過兩個禮拜左右，你就會拿到結果。

items.en: Probably after the summer, we'll move to a bigger flat.
items.zh: 大概過了夏天，我們就會搬到大一點的公寓。

examples.heading: ⑦ 片語放在句中

items.en: The rain, luckily for us, stopped before the wedding.
items.zh: 對我們來說很幸運，雨在婚禮前停了。

items.en: The ferry, unfortunately for the passengers, left six hours late.
items.zh: 對乘客來說很不幸，渡輪晚了六個小時才開。

title: Never have I seen such a realistic and impressive film before.
translation: 我從來沒看過這麼逼真、這麼令人印象深刻的電影。
name: 句首 never 的倒裝句
sentences: Never have I met such a kind and generous person.
Never have I felt so welcome in a foreign country.
Never have I heard such a beautiful voice.
Never have we had so much rain in one month.
Never has the city looked so beautiful.
Never have I been so embarrassed in my whole life.
Never had I seen so many people in one place.
Never had she travelled alone before that trip.
Never had I worked so hard for an exam.
Never had they experienced such cold weather.
Never had I imagined that the job would be so stressful.
Never did I expect to see him again.
Never did we think the hotel would be so crowded.
Never did she complain about her difficult job.
Never did I believe that I could run a marathon.
Never did my grandfather miss a football match on TV.
Never did I dream that I would win the competition.
Never will I forget the day my daughter was born.
Never will I stay in that hotel again.
Never will I lend him money again.
Never will we forget your kindness.
Never will I trust that airline again after what happened.
Never could I live in such a noisy city.
Never would I lie to my best friend.
Never could we afford a house in this part of town.
Never would she leave her children alone at home.
Never do I feel as relaxed as I do by the sea.
Never does my brother say thank you.
Never had I spoken in front of so many people before.
Never have I tasted such fresh fish before.
Never had the team won a championship before.

examples.heading: ① Never have I + 過去分詞

items.en: Never have I met such a kind and generous person.
items.zh: 我從來沒遇過這麼善良、這麼大方的人。

items.en: Never have I felt so welcome in a foreign country.
items.zh: 我在國外從來沒有這麼受歡迎的感覺。

items.en: Never have I heard such a beautiful voice.
items.zh: 我從來沒聽過這麼美的聲音。

items.en: Never have we had so much rain in one month.
items.zh: 我們從來沒有一個月下過這麼多雨。

items.en: Never has the city looked so beautiful.
items.zh: 這座城市從來沒有這麼美過。

items.en: Never have I been so embarrassed in my whole life.
items.zh: 我這輩子從來沒有這麼丟臉過。

examples.heading: ② Never had I + 過去分詞

items.en: Never had I seen so many people in one place.
items.zh: 我從來沒在同一個地方看過這麼多人。

items.en: Never had she travelled alone before that trip.
items.zh: 在那趟旅行之前，她從來沒有自己一個人旅行過。

items.en: Never had I worked so hard for an exam.
items.zh: 我從來沒有為一場考試這麼用功過。

items.en: Never had they experienced such cold weather.
items.zh: 他們從來沒碰過這麼冷的天氣。

items.en: Never had I imagined that the job would be so stressful.
items.zh: 我從來沒想到那份工作壓力會這麼大。

examples.heading: ③ Never did I + 原形動詞

items.en: Never did I expect to see him again.
items.zh: 我從沒想過會再見到他。

items.en: Never did we think the hotel would be so crowded.
items.zh: 我們從沒想過旅館會這麼擠。

items.en: Never did she complain about her difficult job.
items.zh: 她從來沒有抱怨過她辛苦的工作。

items.en: Never did I believe that I could run a marathon.
items.zh: 我從來不相信自己能跑完馬拉松。

items.en: Never did my grandfather miss a football match on TV.
items.zh: 我爺爺從來沒錯過電視上的任何一場足球賽。

items.en: Never did I dream that I would win the competition.
items.zh: 我做夢也沒想到我會贏得比賽。

examples.heading: ④ Never will I + 原形動詞

items.en: Never will I forget the day my daughter was born.
items.zh: 我永遠不會忘記我女兒出生的那一天。

items.en: Never will I stay in that hotel again.
items.zh: 我再也不會住那間旅館了。

items.en: Never will I lend him money again.
items.zh: 我再也不會借錢給他了。

items.en: Never will we forget your kindness.
items.zh: 我們永遠不會忘記你的好意。

items.en: Never will I trust that airline again after what happened.
items.zh: 發生那件事以後，我再也不會相信那家航空公司了。

examples.heading: ⑤ Never could I、Never would I + 原形動詞

items.en: Never could I live in such a noisy city.
items.zh: 我絕對沒辦法住在這麼吵的城市。

items.en: Never would I lie to my best friend.
items.zh: 我絕對不會對我最好的朋友說謊。

items.en: Never could we afford a house in this part of town.
items.zh: 我們絕對買不起這一區的房子。

items.en: Never would she leave her children alone at home.
items.zh: 她絕對不會把孩子單獨留在家裡。

examples.heading: ⑥ Never do I + 原形動詞

items.en: Never do I feel as relaxed as I do by the sea.
items.zh: 我從來沒有像在海邊時那麼放鬆。

items.en: Never does my brother say thank you.
items.zh: 我弟弟從來不說謝謝。

examples.heading: ⑦ Never + 助動詞 + 主詞 + 主要動詞 + before

items.en: Never had I spoken in front of so many people before.
items.zh: 我以前從來沒在這麼多人面前說過話。

items.en: Never have I tasted such fresh fish before.
items.zh: 我以前從來沒吃過這麼新鮮的魚。

items.en: Never had the team won a championship before.
items.zh: 這支隊伍以前從來沒拿過冠軍。

title: Piggy theoretically has all the necessary character traits and skills to be an effective leader.
translation: 照理說，Piggy 具備當一個好領袖所需的一切性格特質和能力。
name: 句中副詞表示保留態度
sentences: Anyone can theoretically apply for the job, but most applicants have a degree.
The bridge should theoretically last for a hundred years.
The tickets are theoretically available online, but the website keeps crashing.
We could theoretically finish the project by Friday.
Members theoretically have the right to vote on every decision.
The medicine theoretically works for adults and children.
A tomato is technically a fruit.
The company technically broke no laws, but many customers felt cheated.
I'm technically on leave until Monday.
The shop technically opens at nine, but the staff rarely arrive before half past.
The car is technically still mine, but my son drives it every day.
Students are technically not allowed to use phones in class.
The hotel officially has four stars, but the rooms are quite basic.
The two companies have officially merged, but they still use different names.
My grandfather is officially retired, but he still helps at the farm.
The road is officially closed, yet cars use it every day.
The library officially closes at eight, but the staff let us stay later.
The meeting was officially about the budget.
He ostensibly went to Paris to study art, but he spent most of his time in cafés.
The new fee is ostensibly for maintenance.
The minister ostensibly resigned for health reasons.
The visit was ostensibly a friendly one, but both sides wanted something.
The changes were ostensibly made to help small businesses.
Their second album is arguably better than their first.
The internet has arguably changed the way we think.
This is arguably the most important decision of his career.
The town's old market is arguably its main attraction.
Climate change is arguably the biggest challenge we face.
The service is officially free, but you have to pay for parking.
The flat technically has two bedrooms, but the second one is tiny.
Everyone could theoretically win, but the favourite usually does.

examples.heading: ① theoretically

items.en: Anyone can theoretically apply for the job, but most applicants have a degree.
items.zh: 照理說任何人都能應徵這份工作，不過大部分應徵者都有學位。

items.en: The bridge should theoretically last for a hundred years.
items.zh: 照理說這座橋應該能用一百年。

items.en: The tickets are theoretically available online, but the website keeps crashing.
items.zh: 票照理說可以在網路上買，可是網站一直當掉。

items.en: We could theoretically finish the project by Friday.
items.zh: 照理說我們可以在星期五前完成這個專案。

items.en: Members theoretically have the right to vote on every decision.
items.zh: 照理說會員對每一項決定都有投票權。

items.en: The medicine theoretically works for adults and children.
items.zh: 照理說這種藥對大人和小孩都有效。

examples.heading: ② technically

items.en: A tomato is technically a fruit.
items.zh: 嚴格來說，番茄是水果。

items.en: The company technically broke no laws, but many customers felt cheated.
items.zh: 嚴格來說這家公司沒有違法，不過很多顧客覺得被騙了。

items.en: I'm technically on leave until Monday.
items.zh: 嚴格來說，我休假到星期一。

items.en: The shop technically opens at nine, but the staff rarely arrive before half past.
items.zh: 嚴格來說那家店九點開門，不過店員很少九點半前到。

items.en: The car is technically still mine, but my son drives it every day.
items.zh: 這輛車嚴格來說還是我的，不過每天都是我兒子在開。

items.en: Students are technically not allowed to use phones in class.
items.zh: 嚴格來說，學生上課不准用手機。

examples.heading: ③ officially

items.en: The hotel officially has four stars, but the rooms are quite basic.
items.zh: 那間旅館名義上是四星級，不過房間很簡陋。

items.en: The two companies have officially merged, but they still use different names.
items.zh: 這兩家公司名義上已經合併了，不過還是用不同的名字。

items.en: My grandfather is officially retired, but he still helps at the farm.
items.zh: 我爺爺名義上退休了，不過他還是會去農場幫忙。

items.en: The road is officially closed, yet cars use it every day.
items.zh: 這條路照規定是封閉的，可是每天都有車在走。

items.en: The library officially closes at eight, but the staff let us stay later.
items.zh: 圖書館照規定八點關門，不過館員讓我們待晚一點。

items.en: The meeting was officially about the budget.
items.zh: 這場會議名義上是討論預算。

examples.heading: ④ ostensibly

items.en: He ostensibly went to Paris to study art, but he spent most of his time in cafés.
items.zh: 他表面上是去巴黎學藝術，可是大部分時間都待在咖啡館。

items.en: The new fee is ostensibly for maintenance.
items.zh: 新收的費用表面上是為了維修。

items.en: The minister ostensibly resigned for health reasons.
items.zh: 那位部長表面上是因為健康因素辭職。

items.en: The visit was ostensibly a friendly one, but both sides wanted something.
items.zh: 這次訪問表面上很友好，不過雙方都各有所圖。

items.en: The changes were ostensibly made to help small businesses.
items.zh: 這些改變表面上是為了幫助小型企業。

examples.heading: ⑤ arguably

items.en: Their second album is arguably better than their first.
items.zh: 他們的第二張專輯可以說比第一張好。

items.en: The internet has arguably changed the way we think.
items.zh: 網路可以說改變了我們思考的方式。

items.en: This is arguably the most important decision of his career.
items.zh: 這可以說是他職業生涯中最重要的決定。

items.en: The town's old market is arguably its main attraction.
items.zh: 鎮上的老市場可以說是那裡最吸引人的地方。

items.en: Climate change is arguably the biggest challenge we face.
items.zh: 氣候變遷可以說是我們面對的最大挑戰。

examples.heading: ⑥ 保留態度副詞 + but + 實際的情況

items.en: The service is officially free, but you have to pay for parking.
items.zh: 這項服務名義上免費，不過停車要付錢。

items.en: The flat technically has two bedrooms, but the second one is tiny.
items.zh: 嚴格來說這間公寓有兩間臥室，不過第二間非常小。

items.en: Everyone could theoretically win, but the favourite usually does.
items.zh: 照理說每個人都可能贏，不過通常是熱門人選贏。

title: Luckily, I arrived in time.
translation: 幸好我及時趕到了。
name: 修飾整個句子的態度副詞
sentences: Fortunately, nobody was hurt in the accident.
Sadly, our neighbours are moving to Leeds.
Surprisingly, the exam was quite easy.
Honestly, I don't remember her name.
Hopefully, the swelling will go down by Monday.
Unfortunately, the museum is closed on Mondays.
Frankly, the film was too long.
Luckily, my phone was still in my bag.
The lift, unfortunately, was out of order.
My grandmother, surprisingly, loves video games.
The hotel, luckily, had one room left.
Our teacher, sadly, is leaving at the end of term.
I wanted to go, but, unfortunately, I had to work.
We got lost, and, surprisingly, we found a great café.
It rained all day, so, obviously, we stayed in.
The tickets were expensive, but, luckily, my uncle paid.
He clearly forgot about our meeting.
You're obviously tired. Go to bed.
The kids were clearly bored.
He unfortunately missed the start of the film.
Obviously, you can't park here.
Clearly, someone has been in my room.
Sadly, the dog didn't survive.
Frankly, your essay needs a lot more work.
Fortunately, the bank was still open.
Surprisingly, my cousin passed his driving test first time.
Hopefully, the heating engineer can come on Friday.
Honestly, the soup needs more salt.
Unfortunately, the printer doesn't work.
Luckily, the train wasn't full.
Honestly, do you like my new haircut?
Seriously, are you moving to Canada?

examples.heading: ① 態度副詞放在句首

items.en: Fortunately, nobody was hurt in the accident.
items.zh: 幸好那場車禍沒有人受傷。

items.en: Sadly, our neighbours are moving to Leeds.
items.zh: 可惜我們的鄰居要搬去里茲了。

items.en: Surprisingly, the exam was quite easy.
items.zh: 沒想到考試還滿簡單的。

items.en: Honestly, I don't remember her name.
items.zh: 老實說，我不記得她的名字。

items.en: Hopefully, the swelling will go down by Monday.
items.zh: 希望星期一前能消腫。

items.en: Unfortunately, the museum is closed on Mondays.
items.zh: 可惜博物館星期一休館。

items.en: Frankly, the film was too long.
items.zh: 坦白說，那部電影太長了。

items.en: Luckily, my phone was still in my bag.
items.zh: 幸好我的手機還在包包裡。

examples.heading: ② 態度副詞放在主詞後面

items.en: The lift, unfortunately, was out of order.
items.zh: 不巧電梯故障了。

items.en: My grandmother, surprisingly, loves video games.
items.zh: 沒想到我奶奶很愛打電玩。

items.en: The hotel, luckily, had one room left.
items.zh: 幸好那家飯店還剩一間房。

items.en: Our teacher, sadly, is leaving at the end of term.
items.zh: 可惜我們老師這學期結束就要走了。

examples.heading: ③ 態度副詞放在連接詞後面

items.en: I wanted to go, but, unfortunately, I had to work.
items.zh: 我很想去，可是不巧我得上班。

items.en: We got lost, and, surprisingly, we found a great café.
items.zh: 我們迷路了，結果沒想到找到一間很棒的咖啡館。

items.en: It rained all day, so, obviously, we stayed in.
items.zh: 下了一整天雨，所以我們當然待在家裡。

items.en: The tickets were expensive, but, luckily, my uncle paid.
items.zh: 票很貴，不過幸好我叔叔出錢。

examples.heading: ④ 態度副詞放在動詞前面或 be 後面

items.en: He clearly forgot about our meeting.
items.zh: 他顯然忘了我們有約。

items.en: You're obviously tired. Go to bed.
items.zh: 你顯然累了，去睡吧。

items.en: The kids were clearly bored.
items.zh: 孩子們顯然很無聊。

items.en: He unfortunately missed the start of the film.
items.zh: 他不巧錯過了電影的開頭。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的看法

items.en: Obviously, you can't park here.
items.zh: 這裡當然不能停車。

items.en: Clearly, someone has been in my room.
items.zh: 顯然有人進過我的房間。

items.en: Sadly, the dog didn't survive.
items.zh: 可惜那隻狗沒活下來。

items.en: Frankly, your essay needs a lot more work.
items.zh: 坦白說，你的報告還要大改。

items.en: Fortunately, the bank was still open.
items.zh: 幸好銀行還開著。

items.en: Surprisingly, my cousin passed his driving test first time.
items.zh: 沒想到我表哥第一次考駕照就過了。

items.en: Hopefully, the heating engineer can come on Friday.
items.zh: 希望修暖氣的師傅星期五能來。

items.en: Honestly, the soup needs more salt.
items.zh: 老實說，這湯要再加點鹽。

examples.heading: ⑥ 疑問句和否定句

items.en: Unfortunately, the printer doesn't work.
items.zh: 不巧印表機壞了。

items.en: Luckily, the train wasn't full.
items.zh: 幸好火車上人不多。

items.en: Honestly, do you like my new haircut?
items.zh: 說真的，你喜歡我的新髮型嗎？

items.en: Seriously, are you moving to Canada?
items.zh: 說真的，你要搬去加拿大？

title: My teacher is very good.
translation: 我的老師很好。
name: very 當程度副詞修飾形容詞
sentences: My home is very warm in winter.
Our neighbours are very friendly.
The bread is very fresh.
This question is very difficult.
Her parents were very angry.
The weather was very bad yesterday.
Are you very busy this week?
The kitchen isn't very big.
Rome is a very beautiful city.
I have a very important question.
That was a very interesting lesson.
She wears very bright colours.
We had a very quick lunch.
He lives in a very quiet street.
They sell very cheap clothes.
The cake smells very good.
Your sister looks very pretty in that dress.
I felt very sad when he left.
The music sounds very loud from here.
It got very dark outside.
The view from the top was absolutely amazing.
Their new house is absolutely huge.
After the long walk, we were absolutely starving.
The hotel staff were absolutely brilliant.
His jokes are really funny.
I'm really sorry about your cat.
This soup is really delicious.
The shoes were really cheap.
Is your town very old?
"Was the exam difficult?" "Yes, very difficult."
"Are you tired?" "Not very."
Do you live in a very big house?

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + be + very + 形容詞

items.en: My home is very warm in winter.
items.zh: 我家冬天很暖和。

items.en: Our neighbours are very friendly.
items.zh: 我們的鄰居很友善。

items.en: The bread is very fresh.
items.zh: 這個麵包很新鮮。

items.en: This question is very difficult.
items.zh: 這個問題很難。

items.en: Her parents were very angry.
items.zh: 她的爸媽很生氣。

items.en: The weather was very bad yesterday.
items.zh: 昨天天氣很差。

items.en: Are you very busy this week?
items.zh: 你這禮拜很忙嗎？

items.en: The kitchen isn't very big.
items.zh: 廚房不太大。

examples.heading: ② very + 形容詞 + 名詞

items.en: Rome is a very beautiful city.
items.zh: 羅馬是個很美的城市。

items.en: I have a very important question.
items.zh: 我有一個很重要的問題。

items.en: That was a very interesting lesson.
items.zh: 那是一堂很有意思的課。

items.en: She wears very bright colours.
items.zh: 她穿很鮮豔的顏色。

items.en: We had a very quick lunch.
items.zh: 我們很快地吃了午餐。

items.en: He lives in a very quiet street.
items.zh: 他住在一條很安靜的街上。

items.en: They sell very cheap clothes.
items.zh: 他們賣很便宜的衣服。

examples.heading: ③ 連綴動詞 + very + 形容詞

items.en: The cake smells very good.
items.zh: 蛋糕聞起來很香。

items.en: Your sister looks very pretty in that dress.
items.zh: 你姊姊穿那件洋裝很漂亮。

items.en: I felt very sad when he left.
items.zh: 他離開的時候我很難過。

items.en: The music sounds very loud from here.
items.zh: 從這裡聽，音樂很大聲。

items.en: It got very dark outside.
items.zh: 外面天色變得很暗。

examples.heading: ④ absolutely + 表示程度最高的形容詞

items.en: The view from the top was absolutely amazing.
items.zh: 從頂端看出去的景色美極了。

items.en: Their new house is absolutely huge.
items.zh: 他們的新房子大得不得了。

items.en: After the long walk, we were absolutely starving.
items.zh: 走了那麼久，我們都餓死了。

items.en: The hotel staff were absolutely brilliant.
items.zh: 飯店的員工棒極了。

examples.heading: ⑤ really + 形容詞

items.en: His jokes are really funny.
items.zh: 他的笑話真的很好笑。

items.en: I'm really sorry about your cat.
items.zh: 你的貓的事，我真的很遺憾。

items.en: This soup is really delicious.
items.zh: 這碗湯真的很好喝。

items.en: The shoes were really cheap.
items.zh: 那雙鞋真的很便宜。

examples.heading: ⑥ 疑問句和回答

items.en: Is your town very old?
items.zh: 你住的城鎮很古老嗎？

items.en: "Was the exam difficult?" "Yes, very difficult."
items.zh: 考試難嗎？難，很難。

items.en: "Are you tired?" "Not very."
items.zh: 你累嗎？不太累。

items.en: Do you live in a very big house?
items.zh: 你住的房子很大嗎？

title: I like my job very much.
translation: 我很喜歡我的工作。
name: very 修飾時間副詞和程度副詞
sentences: We enjoyed our holiday in Spain very much.
My little sister wants a pet rabbit very much.
Thank you very much for your help.
I appreciate your kind letter very much.
Our whole family enjoyed the boat trip around the island very much.
Do you miss your family very much?
The film starts very soon. Let's go in.
I'll write to you again very soon.
My cousin is coming to visit very soon.
The shop is closing very soon.
We have to leave very soon.
My parents don't go out for dinner very often.
Do you go to the cinema very often?
Our neighbours have barbecues in the garden very often.
It doesn't snow here very often.
We play tennis very often in summer.
I get up very early on Mondays.
The farmers start work very early.
We arrived at the airport very early.
My baby sister wakes up very early.
My dad works very late on Fridays.
The train arrived very late last night.
Don't stay up very late. You have school tomorrow.
We had dinner very late because of the traffic.
She often goes to bed very late.
My son doesn't enjoy swimming lessons very much.
Do you see your grandparents very often?
Did you get home very late last night?
They don't visit us very often.
We didn't stay very late at the party.

examples.heading: ① very much

items.en: We enjoyed our holiday in Spain very much.
items.zh: 我們在西班牙的假期玩得很開心。

items.en: My little sister wants a pet rabbit very much.
items.zh: 我妹妹非常想要養一隻兔子。

items.en: Thank you very much for your help.
items.zh: 非常謝謝你的幫忙。

items.en: I appreciate your kind letter very much.
items.zh: 我非常感謝你那封貼心的信。

items.en: Our whole family enjoyed the boat trip around the island very much.
items.zh: 我們全家都很喜歡那趟環島的坐船之旅。

items.en: Do you miss your family very much?
items.zh: 你很想念你的家人嗎？

examples.heading: ② very soon

items.en: The film starts very soon. Let's go in.
items.zh: 電影馬上就要開始了，我們進去吧。

items.en: I'll write to you again very soon.
items.zh: 我很快會再寫信給你。

items.en: My cousin is coming to visit very soon.
items.zh: 我表姊很快就要來拜訪了。

items.en: The shop is closing very soon.
items.zh: 那家店馬上就要關門了。

items.en: We have to leave very soon.
items.zh: 我們很快就得走了。

examples.heading: ③ very often

items.en: My parents don't go out for dinner very often.
items.zh: 我爸媽不常出去吃晚餐。

items.en: Do you go to the cinema very often?
items.zh: 你常去看電影嗎？

items.en: Our neighbours have barbecues in the garden very often.
items.zh: 我們的鄰居很常在院子裡烤肉。

items.en: It doesn't snow here very often.
items.zh: 這裡不常下雪。

items.en: We play tennis very often in summer.
items.zh: 我們夏天很常打網球。

examples.heading: ④ very early

items.en: I get up very early on Mondays.
items.zh: 我星期一起得很早。

items.en: The farmers start work very early.
items.zh: 農夫很早就開始工作。

items.en: We arrived at the airport very early.
items.zh: 我們很早就到機場了。

items.en: My baby sister wakes up very early.
items.zh: 我妹妹很早就醒了。

examples.heading: ⑤ very late

items.en: My dad works very late on Fridays.
items.zh: 我爸星期五工作到很晚。

items.en: The train arrived very late last night.
items.zh: 火車昨晚很晚才到。

items.en: Don't stay up very late. You have school tomorrow.
items.zh: 別熬到很晚，你明天要上學。

items.en: We had dinner very late because of the traffic.
items.zh: 因為塞車，我們很晚才吃晚餐。

items.en: She often goes to bed very late.
items.zh: 她常常很晚才睡。

examples.heading: ⑥ 否定句和疑問句

items.en: My son doesn't enjoy swimming lessons very much.
items.zh: 我兒子不太喜歡上游泳課。

items.en: Do you see your grandparents very often?
items.zh: 你常去看你爺爺奶奶嗎？

items.en: Did you get home very late last night?
items.zh: 你昨晚很晚才到家嗎？

items.en: They don't visit us very often.
items.zh: 他們不常來看我們。

items.en: We didn't stay very late at the party.
items.zh: 我們沒有在派對待到很晚。

title: I hope you get well very soon.
translation: 我希望你很快就好起來。

sentences: The bus will be here very soon.
We need an answer very soon.

Write back very soon!
The rain will stop very soon.

My lessons start very early on Tuesdays.
The baby woke up very early today.
Do you always go to bed very early?
They left the party very early.
The plane arrived very late.
He often works very late.
We stayed up very late last night.
Don't come home very late, OK?
The shops are open very late on Thursdays.
I don't see my grandparents very often.
It rains very often here in spring.
Do you go swimming very often?
My sister very often borrows my clothes.
We don't eat meat very often.

They opened a new café very recently.

I have to get up really early tomorrow.
The film finished really late.
See you really soon!
My brother texts me really often.

examples.heading: ① very soon

items.en: The bus will be here very soon.
items.zh: 公車很快就到了。

items.en: We need an answer very soon.
items.zh: 我們很快就需要答覆。

items.en: Dinner's nearly ready. We'll eat very soon.
items.zh: 晚餐快好了。我們很快就開飯。

items.en: My cousin is getting married very soon.
items.zh: 我表姊很快就要結婚了。

items.en: Write back very soon!
items.zh: 早點回信喔！

items.en: The rain will stop very soon.
items.zh: 雨很快就會停了。

examples.heading: ② very early

items.en: The sun comes up very early in summer.
items.zh: 夏天太陽很早就出來了。

items.en: My lessons start very early on Tuesdays.
items.zh: 我星期二的課很早就開始。

items.en: The baby woke up very early today.
items.zh: 寶寶今天很早就醒了。

items.en: Do you always go to bed very early?
items.zh: 你都很早就睡嗎？

items.en: They left the party very early.
items.zh: 他們很早就離開派對了。

examples.heading: ③ very late

items.en: The plane arrived very late.
items.zh: 飛機很晚才到。

items.en: He often works very late.
items.zh: 他常常工作到很晚。

items.en: We stayed up very late last night.
items.zh: 我們昨晚熬夜到很晚。

items.en: Don't come home very late, OK?
items.zh: 別太晚回家，好嗎？

items.en: The shops are open very late on Thursdays.
items.zh: 商店星期四開到很晚。

examples.heading: ④ very often

items.en: I don't see my grandparents very often.
items.zh: 我不常見到我祖父母。

items.en: It rains very often here in spring.
items.zh: 這裡春天很常下雨。

items.en: Do you go swimming very often?
items.zh: 你常去游泳嗎？

items.en: My sister very often borrows my clothes.
items.zh: 我妹妹很常借我的衣服。

items.en: We don't eat meat very often.
items.zh: 我們不常吃肉。

examples.heading: ⑤ very recently

items.en: I moved to this town very recently.
items.zh: 我最近才搬到這個鎮上。

items.en: They opened a new café very recently.
items.zh: 他們最近才開了一家新的咖啡館。

items.en: She has very recently changed jobs.
items.zh: 她最近才換了工作。

items.en: The school has very recently bought new computers.
items.zh: 學校最近才買了新電腦。

items.en: I've very recently started learning the guitar.
items.zh: 我最近才開始學吉他。

examples.heading: ⑥ really + 時間副詞

items.en: I have to get up really early tomorrow.
items.zh: 我明天得很早起床。

items.en: The film finished really late.
items.zh: 電影很晚才結束。

items.en: See you really soon!
items.zh: 很快就會見到你！

items.en: My brother texts me really often.
items.zh: 我哥哥很常傳訊息給我。

title: Maybe we can walk there because it's not far from my house.
translation: 也許我們可以走過去，因為那裡離我家不遠。
name: maybe、perhaps 表示確定程度
sentences: Maybe she missed the bus.
Maybe he doesn't know about the meeting.
Maybe they're on holiday.
Maybe I'll buy a new phone next month.
Maybe I wrote down the wrong number.
Maybe the dog is hungry.
Perhaps you're right.
Perhaps the train is late.
Perhaps she forgot my birthday.
Perhaps they didn't hear the phone.
Perhaps it's in the other drawer.
Perhaps I'll see you there.
It's perhaps the best café in town.
She was perhaps a little tired.
We could perhaps take a taxi.
You perhaps know my brother.
Maybe we should leave now.
Maybe you could ask your teacher.
Perhaps you'd like a cup of tea.
Perhaps we can try again tomorrow.
Maybe we can go to the cinema on Saturday.
"Will you be home for dinner?" "Maybe not."
"Is she angry with me?" "Perhaps."
"Are we going to the beach tomorrow?" "Maybe, if it's sunny."
"Can you help me on Sunday?" "Perhaps. I'll call you."
Maybe he isn't coming.
Perhaps she doesn't like fish.
Maybe they won't sell the house.
Shall we wait a bit? Maybe she's still on her way.
Perhaps it isn't a good idea.
Why don't you call him? Maybe he's at home.

examples.heading: ① Maybe + 子句

items.en: Maybe she missed the bus.
items.zh: 她可能錯過公車了。

items.en: Maybe he doesn't know about the meeting.
items.zh: 也許他不知道開會的事。

items.en: Maybe they're on holiday.
items.zh: 他們也許在度假。

items.en: Maybe I'll buy a new phone next month.
items.zh: 也許我下個月會買一支新手機。

items.en: Maybe I wrote down the wrong number.
items.zh: 也許我把號碼抄錯了。

items.en: Maybe the dog is hungry.
items.zh: 也許狗餓了。

examples.heading: ② Perhaps + 子句

items.en: Perhaps you're right.
items.zh: 也許你說得對。

items.en: Perhaps the train is late.
items.zh: 火車也許誤點了。

items.en: Perhaps she forgot my birthday.
items.zh: 她也許忘了我的生日。

items.en: Perhaps they didn't hear the phone.
items.zh: 他們也許沒聽到電話響。

items.en: Perhaps it's in the other drawer.
items.zh: 也許在另一個抽屜裡。

items.en: Perhaps I'll see you there.
items.zh: 也許我會在那裡見到你。

examples.heading: ③ perhaps 放在句中

items.en: It's perhaps the best café in town.
items.zh: 這也許是城裡最好的咖啡館。

items.en: She was perhaps a little tired.
items.zh: 她也許有點累。

items.en: We could perhaps take a taxi.
items.zh: 我們也許可以搭計程車。

items.en: You perhaps know my brother.
items.zh: 你也許認識我哥哥。

examples.heading: ④ 用 maybe、perhaps 提建議

items.en: Maybe we should leave now.
items.zh: 也許我們現在該走了。

items.en: Maybe you could ask your teacher.
items.zh: 也許你可以問你的老師。

items.en: Perhaps you'd like a cup of tea.
items.zh: 也許你想喝杯茶。

items.en: Perhaps we can try again tomorrow.
items.zh: 也許我們明天可以再試一次。

items.en: Maybe we can go to the cinema on Saturday.
items.zh: 也許我們星期六可以去看電影。

examples.heading: ⑤ 回答問題

items.en: "Will you be home for dinner?" "Maybe not."
items.zh: 你會回家吃晚餐嗎？可能不會。

items.en: "Is she angry with me?" "Perhaps."
items.zh: 她在生我的氣嗎？也許吧。

items.en: "Are we going to the beach tomorrow?" "Maybe, if it's sunny."
items.zh: 我們明天要去海邊嗎？也許吧，如果天氣好的話。

items.en: "Can you help me on Sunday?" "Perhaps. I'll call you."
items.zh: 你星期天可以幫我嗎？也許吧。我再打給你。

examples.heading: ⑥ 否定句和對話

items.en: Maybe he isn't coming.
items.zh: 也許他不來了。

items.en: Perhaps she doesn't like fish.
items.zh: 她也許不喜歡吃魚。

items.en: Maybe they won't sell the house.
items.zh: 也許他們不會賣房子。

items.en: Shall we wait a bit? Maybe she's still on her way.
items.zh: 我們要不要再等一下？也許她還在路上。

items.en: Perhaps it isn't a good idea.
items.zh: 這也許不是個好主意。

items.en: Why don't you call him? Maybe he's at home.
items.zh: 你何不打給他？也許他在家。

title: It will probably be on TV next month!
translation: 它下個月大概會在電視上播！
name: 表示確定程度的副詞（probably、certainly）
sentences: The shop will probably close early on Christmas Eve.
We'll probably move house next year.
He's probably at the gym.
Your keys are probably in your other bag.
They probably took the wrong road.
I'll probably see you at the weekend.
She probably won't remember me.
It probably isn't true.
My parents probably don't know about the party.
I probably won't finish before six.
I'll definitely be at your sister's concert on Saturday.
This is definitely the creamiest ice cream I've ever tasted.
With three dogs, we definitely need a bigger car for camping trips.
She definitely said three o'clock.
That was definitely a mistake.
If I were you, I'd certainly say no.
The new manager is certainly very busy.
It's certainly colder today than it was last week.
They will certainly win the match.
You certainly know a lot about cars.
Because of the snow, the train from Leeds will possibly be late.
He's possibly the funniest uncle in our whole family.
We could possibly meet on Friday.
It's possibly the most important decision of my life.
"Can I borrow your pen?" "Certainly."
"Are you coming to the wedding?" "Definitely!"
"Will they be late?" "Probably."
"Is she going to say yes?" "Possibly."
"Do you want to go camping?" "Definitely not."
"Will it snow tomorrow?" "Probably not."
"Are you going to tell him?" "Certainly not!"

examples.heading: ① probably

items.en: The shop will probably close early on Christmas Eve.
items.zh: 那家店平安夜大概會提早關門。

items.en: We'll probably move house next year.
items.zh: 我們明年大概會搬家。

items.en: He's probably at the gym.
items.zh: 他大概在健身房。

items.en: Your keys are probably in your other bag.
items.zh: 你的鑰匙大概在你另一個包包裡。

items.en: They probably took the wrong road.
items.zh: 他們大概走錯路了。

items.en: I'll probably see you at the weekend.
items.zh: 我週末大概會見到你。

examples.heading: ② probably + 否定

items.en: She probably won't remember me.
items.zh: 她大概不會記得我。

items.en: It probably isn't true.
items.zh: 那大概不是真的。

items.en: My parents probably don't know about the party.
items.zh: 我爸媽大概不知道派對的事。

items.en: I probably won't finish before six.
items.zh: 我大概六點前做不完。

examples.heading: ③ definitely

items.en: I'll definitely be at your sister's concert on Saturday.
items.zh: 你姊姊星期六的音樂會我一定會到。

items.en: This is definitely the creamiest ice cream I've ever tasted.
items.zh: 這絕對是我吃過最濃郁的冰淇淋。

items.en: With three dogs, we definitely need a bigger car for camping trips.
items.zh: 有三隻狗，我們去露營絕對需要一輛大一點的車。

items.en: She definitely said three o'clock.
items.zh: 她確實說的是三點。

items.en: That was definitely a mistake.
items.zh: 那絕對是個錯誤。

examples.heading: ④ certainly

items.en: If I were you, I'd certainly say no.
items.zh: 如果我是你，我一定會拒絕。

items.en: The new manager is certainly very busy.
items.zh: 新經理確實很忙。

items.en: It's certainly colder today than it was last week.
items.zh: 今天確實比上星期冷。

items.en: They will certainly win the match.
items.zh: 他們一定會贏得比賽。

items.en: You certainly know a lot about cars.
items.zh: 你確實很懂車。

examples.heading: ⑤ possibly

items.en: Because of the snow, the train from Leeds will possibly be late.
items.zh: 因為下雪，從里茲來的火車可能會誤點。

items.en: He's possibly the funniest uncle in our whole family.
items.zh: 他可能是我們全家最好笑的叔叔。

items.en: We could possibly meet on Friday.
items.zh: 我們也許可以星期五碰面。

items.en: It's possibly the most important decision of my life.
items.zh: 這可能是我人生中最重要的決定。

examples.heading: ⑥ 單獨回答問題

items.en: "Can I borrow your pen?" "Certainly."
items.zh: 我可以借你的筆嗎？當然可以。

items.en: "Are you coming to the wedding?" "Definitely!"
items.zh: 你會來婚禮嗎？一定會！

items.en: "Will they be late?" "Probably."
items.zh: 他們會遲到嗎？大概會。

items.en: "Is she going to say yes?" "Possibly."
items.zh: 她會答應嗎？有可能。

examples.heading: ⑦ definitely not、probably not

items.en: "Do you want to go camping?" "Definitely not."
items.zh: 你想去露營嗎？絕對不要。

items.en: "Will it snow tomorrow?" "Probably not."
items.zh: 明天會下雪嗎？大概不會。

items.en: "Are you going to tell him?" "Certainly not!"
items.zh: 你要告訴他嗎？當然不要！

title: It was undoubtedly an unforgettable experience.
translation: 那無疑是一次難忘的經驗。
name: 表示確定程度的副詞（較多種）
sentences: She is undoubtedly the best teacher in the school.
The new road will undoubtedly reduce traffic.
Undoubtedly, the internet has changed the way we work.
He has undoubtedly made some mistakes.
Television is undeniably a useful way to keep informed.
The hotel is undeniably expensive, but the service is excellent.
It was undeniably a difficult year for the company.
Social media has undeniably changed how teenagers talk to each other.
I absolutely love this song.
My grandmother absolutely refuses to use a mobile phone.
We absolutely must finish this today.
"Can I bring a friend?" "Absolutely!"
The bus is late. Presumably there's a lot of traffic.
Presumably your sister told you about the change of plan.
The lights are off, so presumably they've gone to bed.
He'll presumably want to bring his wife.
She is arguably the greatest tennis player of all time.
This is arguably the most beautiful city in Europe.
The book is arguably his best work.
Arguably, the first film was better than the second.
The project could conceivably take two years.
He might conceivably change his mind.
Conceivably, the shop could open on Sundays too.
The storm could conceivably reach the coast by tomorrow.
The plan will undoubtedly save the company money.
These results are undeniably important for future research.
Presumably, the report will be ready by Friday.
This is arguably the most serious problem we face.
The answer is presumably not in this book.
He presumably didn't get my message.
This is undoubtedly not the end of the story.

examples.heading: ① undoubtedly

items.en: She is undoubtedly the best teacher in the school.
items.zh: 她無疑是學校裡最好的老師。

items.en: The new road will undoubtedly reduce traffic.
items.zh: 新的道路無疑會減少車流。

items.en: Undoubtedly, the internet has changed the way we work.
items.zh: 毫無疑問，網路改變了我們工作的方式。

items.en: He has undoubtedly made some mistakes.
items.zh: 他無疑犯了一些錯。

examples.heading: ② undeniably

items.en: Television is undeniably a useful way to keep informed.
items.zh: 電視無可否認是獲得資訊的實用方式。

items.en: The hotel is undeniably expensive, but the service is excellent.
items.zh: 那家飯店確實很貴，可是服務很好。

items.en: It was undeniably a difficult year for the company.
items.zh: 對那家公司來說，那無可否認是艱難的一年。

items.en: Social media has undeniably changed how teenagers talk to each other.
items.zh: 社群媒體無可否認地改變了青少年彼此交談的方式。

examples.heading: ③ absolutely

items.en: I absolutely love this song.
items.zh: 我超愛這首歌。

items.en: My grandmother absolutely refuses to use a mobile phone.
items.zh: 我奶奶堅決不肯用手機。

items.en: We absolutely must finish this today.
items.zh: 我們今天絕對要做完這個。

items.en: "Can I bring a friend?" "Absolutely!"
items.zh: 我可以帶一個朋友嗎？當然可以！

examples.heading: ④ presumably

items.en: The bus is late. Presumably there's a lot of traffic.
items.zh: 公車遲到了。想必路上很塞。

items.en: Presumably your sister told you about the change of plan.
items.zh: 想必你姊姊跟你說了計畫改變的事。

items.en: The lights are off, so presumably they've gone to bed.
items.zh: 燈都關了，想必他們已經睡了。

items.en: He'll presumably want to bring his wife.
items.zh: 他想必會想帶他太太一起來。

examples.heading: ⑤ arguably

items.en: She is arguably the greatest tennis player of all time.
items.zh: 她可以說是史上最偉大的網球選手。

items.en: This is arguably the most beautiful city in Europe.
items.zh: 這可以說是歐洲最美的城市。

items.en: The book is arguably his best work.
items.zh: 這本書可以說是他最好的作品。

items.en: Arguably, the first film was better than the second.
items.zh: 可以說第一部電影比第二部好。

examples.heading: ⑥ conceivably

items.en: The project could conceivably take two years.
items.zh: 這個專案有可能要花兩年。

items.en: He might conceivably change his mind.
items.zh: 他有可能會改變主意。

items.en: Conceivably, the shop could open on Sundays too.
items.zh: 那家店有可能星期天也開。

items.en: The storm could conceivably reach the coast by tomorrow.
items.zh: 暴風雨有可能明天就會抵達海岸。

examples.heading: ⑦ 在正式的文字裡

items.en: The plan will undoubtedly save the company money.
items.zh: 這個計畫無疑會替公司省錢。

items.en: These results are undeniably important for future research.
items.zh: 這些結果對未來的研究無可否認地很重要。

items.en: Presumably, the report will be ready by Friday.
items.zh: 報告想必星期五前會完成。

items.en: This is arguably the most serious problem we face.
items.zh: 這可以說是我們面臨的最嚴重的問題。

examples.heading: ⑧ 否定句

items.en: The answer is presumably not in this book.
items.zh: 答案想必不在這本書裡。

items.en: He presumably didn't get my message.
items.zh: 他想必沒收到我的訊息。

items.en: This is undoubtedly not the end of the story.
items.zh: 這無疑不是故事的結局。

title: I am not keen on football, so I think it is really really boring.
translation: 我不太喜歡足球，所以我覺得足球真的真的很無聊。
name: really really 加強語氣
sentences: The view from our balcony was really really beautiful.
I'm really really tired today.
Your cake is really really good!
My maths homework is really really difficult this week.
It's really really cold outside.
That was a really really long day.
I really really want to go to the concert.
She really really loves her new puppy.
We really really need a holiday.
I really really hope you can come.
He really really hates getting up early.
My kids really really enjoyed the water park.
Thanks for the present. I really really like it!
Sorry I'm late. The traffic was really really bad.
"Do you want to come?" "Yes, I really really do!"
I really really miss you.
Mum, please! I really really want this jacket.
You look really really happy in this photo.
Do you really really think so?
Are you really really sure?
Was it really really your idea?
Do you really really need another pair of shoes?
My grandmother is very very old.
The film was very very sad.
The new teacher is very very strict.
The shop was very very busy on Saturday.
I was really really hungry, so I ate two sandwiches.
We left early because the party was really really boring.
The room was really really small, so we asked for another one.
I really really wanted to win, so I trained every day.

examples.heading: ① really really + 形容詞

items.en: The view from our balcony was really really beautiful.
items.zh: 從我們陽台看出去的景色真的真的很美。

items.en: I'm really really tired today.
items.zh: 我今天真的真的很累。

items.en: Your cake is really really good!
items.zh: 你的蛋糕真的真的很好吃！

items.en: My maths homework is really really difficult this week.
items.zh: 我這禮拜的數學功課真的真的很難。

items.en: It's really really cold outside.
items.zh: 外面真的真的很冷。

items.en: That was a really really long day.
items.zh: 今天真的真的好漫長。

examples.heading: ② really really + 一般動詞

items.en: I really really want to go to the concert.
items.zh: 我真的真的很想去那場演唱會。

items.en: She really really loves her new puppy.
items.zh: 她真的真的很愛她的新小狗。

items.en: We really really need a holiday.
items.zh: 我們真的真的需要放個假。

items.en: I really really hope you can come.
items.zh: 我真的真的希望你能來。

items.en: He really really hates getting up early.
items.zh: 他真的真的很討厭早起。

items.en: My kids really really enjoyed the water park.
items.zh: 我的孩子真的真的很喜歡那座水上樂園。

examples.heading: ③ 在訊息和對話裡

items.en: Thanks for the present. I really really like it!
items.zh: 謝謝你的禮物。我真的真的很喜歡！

items.en: Sorry I'm late. The traffic was really really bad.
items.zh: 抱歉我遲到了。路上真的真的很塞。

items.en: "Do you want to come?" "Yes, I really really do!"
items.zh: 你要來嗎？要，我真的真的很想去！

items.en: I really really miss you.
items.zh: 我真的真的好想你。

items.en: Mum, please! I really really want this jacket.
items.zh: 媽，拜託！我真的真的很想要這件外套。

items.en: You look really really happy in this photo.
items.zh: 你在這張照片裡看起來真的真的很開心。

examples.heading: ④ 疑問句

items.en: Do you really really think so?
items.zh: 你真的真的這麼認為嗎？

items.en: Are you really really sure?
items.zh: 你真的真的確定嗎？

items.en: Was it really really your idea?
items.zh: 那真的真的是你的主意嗎？

items.en: Do you really really need another pair of shoes?
items.zh: 你真的真的還需要再買一雙鞋嗎？

examples.heading: ⑤ very very

items.en: My grandmother is very very old.
items.zh: 我奶奶年紀非常非常大了。

items.en: The film was very very sad.
items.zh: 那部電影非常非常讓人難過。

items.en: The new teacher is very very strict.
items.zh: 新老師非常非常嚴格。

items.en: The shop was very very busy on Saturday.
items.zh: 那家店星期六非常非常忙。

examples.heading: ⑥ 和 so、because 一起用

items.en: I was really really hungry, so I ate two sandwiches.
items.zh: 我真的真的很餓，所以吃了兩個三明治。

items.en: We left early because the party was really really boring.
items.zh: 我們提早走了，因為派對真的真的很無聊。

items.en: The room was really really small, so we asked for another one.
items.zh: 房間真的真的很小，所以我們要求換一間。

items.en: I really really wanted to win, so I trained every day.
items.zh: 我真的真的很想贏，所以每天都在練習。

title: The weather was too hot.
translation: 天氣太熱了。
name: so、quite、too 修飾形容詞
sentences: I went to the night market. It was so busy.
Your baby is so cute!
The view from the hotel was so beautiful.
I'm so happy for you.
This sofa is so comfortable.
Why are you so angry?
The exam wasn't so difficult.
It was quite expensive. It cost a hundred pounds.
The film was quite good.
My new school is quite big.
The hotel was quite close to the beach.
I'm quite tired, so I'll go to bed early.
Her English is quite good now.
It's quite a long way to the station.
He's quite a good singer.
We had quite a nice time.
This coffee is too hot. I can't drink it yet.
These shoes are too small for me.
The music is too loud!
It's too late to call him now.
The test was too long, and I didn't finish it.
Is the bag too heavy for you?
My room was too dark, so I bought a new lamp.
You look so tired.
The new manager seems quite friendly.
I feel too sick to go to school.
The room looked quite small in the photo.
He seems so different now.
The soup was so salty that I couldn't eat it.
She was too young to drive.
The street was so noisy that we closed the window.
The box was too heavy to lift.

examples.heading: ① so + 形容詞

items.en: I went to the night market. It was so busy.
items.zh: 我去了夜市。人超多的。

items.en: Your baby is so cute!
items.zh: 你的寶寶好可愛！

items.en: The view from the hotel was so beautiful.
items.zh: 飯店看出去的風景好美。

items.en: I'm so happy for you.
items.zh: 我真替你高興。

items.en: This sofa is so comfortable.
items.zh: 這張沙發好舒服。

items.en: Why are you so angry?
items.zh: 你為什麼那麼生氣？

items.en: The exam wasn't so difficult.
items.zh: 考試沒有那麼難。

examples.heading: ② quite + 形容詞

items.en: It was quite expensive. It cost a hundred pounds.
items.zh: 那個滿貴的。花了一百英鎊。

items.en: The film was quite good.
items.zh: 那部電影還滿好看的。

items.en: My new school is quite big.
items.zh: 我的新學校滿大的。

items.en: The hotel was quite close to the beach.
items.zh: 那家飯店離海灘滿近的。

items.en: I'm quite tired, so I'll go to bed early.
items.zh: 我滿累的，所以我會早點睡。

items.en: Her English is quite good now.
items.zh: 她的英文現在還滿好的。

examples.heading: ③ quite a + 形容詞 + 名詞

items.en: It's quite a long way to the station.
items.zh: 到車站的路滿遠的。

items.en: He's quite a good singer.
items.zh: 他唱歌滿好聽的。

items.en: We had quite a nice time.
items.zh: 我們玩得滿愉快的。

examples.heading: ④ too + 形容詞

items.en: This coffee is too hot. I can't drink it yet.
items.zh: 這咖啡太燙了。我還不能喝。

items.en: These shoes are too small for me.
items.zh: 這雙鞋我穿太小了。

items.en: The music is too loud!
items.zh: 音樂太大聲了！

items.en: It's too late to call him now.
items.zh: 現在打給他太晚了。

items.en: The test was too long, and I didn't finish it.
items.zh: 考試太長了，我沒寫完。

items.en: Is the bag too heavy for you?
items.zh: 這個包包對你來說太重嗎？

items.en: My room was too dark, so I bought a new lamp.
items.zh: 我的房間太暗了，所以我買了一盞新燈。

examples.heading: ⑤ look / feel / seem + so / quite / too + 形容詞

items.en: You look so tired.
items.zh: 你看起來好累。

items.en: The new manager seems quite friendly.
items.zh: 新經理看起來滿友善的。

items.en: I feel too sick to go to school.
items.zh: 我不舒服到沒辦法上學。

items.en: The room looked quite small in the photo.
items.zh: 照片裡的房間看起來滿小的。

items.en: He seems so different now.
items.zh: 他現在好像變了好多。

examples.heading: ⑥ so ... that、too ... to

items.en: The soup was so salty that I couldn't eat it.
items.zh: 湯鹹到我喝不下去。

items.en: She was too young to drive.
items.zh: 她年紀太小，不能開車。

items.en: The street was so noisy that we closed the window.
items.zh: 街上吵到我們把窗戶關起來。

items.en: The box was too heavy to lift.
items.zh: 箱子太重了，搬不起來。

title: It is extremely important that the project is finished before September.
translation: 這個專案一定要在九月之前完成，這非常重要。
name: 副詞修飾形容詞表示程度（較多種副詞）
sentences: The instructions were extremely clear.
Our new neighbours are extremely helpful.
Flights to Rome were incredibly cheap last spring.
She's incredibly talented.
It's extremely unlikely that he'll agree.
It's highly likely that prices will rise again.
She's a highly qualified engineer.
Our accountant is highly organised and never misses a deadline.
The company has been highly successful.
We are deeply grateful for your support.
Her speech at the wedding was deeply moving.
His parents were deeply worried about him.
I'm deeply sorry about what happened.
The two sisters are completely different.
The map on the website is totally wrong about the bus times.
I'm not entirely sure what he meant.
The building looks completely new.
That kind of behaviour is totally unacceptable.
The decision is entirely yours.
My grandmother's apple pie was absolutely delicious.
The nurses were absolutely exhausted after the night shift.
The weather on our holiday was absolutely terrible.
It's absolutely impossible to finish by Monday.
Your garden looks absolutely gorgeous.
The water in the lake was really cold.
It's really freezing in here.
I'm really tired after work.
I'm really exhausted after the trip.
The new rules aren't completely fair.
I'm not completely happy with the result.
The plan isn't entirely clear to me.

examples.heading: ① extremely、incredibly + 可分級形容詞

items.en: The instructions were extremely clear.
items.zh: 說明寫得非常清楚。

items.en: Our new neighbours are extremely helpful.
items.zh: 我們的新鄰居非常樂於助人。

items.en: Flights to Rome were incredibly cheap last spring.
items.zh: 去年春天飛羅馬的機票便宜得不得了。

items.en: She's incredibly talented.
items.zh: 她非常有天分。

items.en: It's extremely unlikely that he'll agree.
items.zh: 他極不可能同意。

examples.heading: ② highly

items.en: It's highly likely that prices will rise again.
items.zh: 價格很可能會再上漲。

items.en: She's a highly qualified engineer.
items.zh: 她是一位資歷很高的工程師。
