items.en: How I long to sleep in my own bed again!
items.zh: 我好想再睡在自己的床上！

items.en: How I long to see the mountains again!
items.zh: 我好想再看到那些山！

items.en: How I wish I could go with you!
items.zh: 我多希望能跟你一起去！

items.en: How I wish it were summer!
items.zh: 我多希望現在是夏天！

items.en: How she longed to go home!
items.zh: 她好想回家！

examples.heading: ④ How + 主詞 + 副詞 + 動詞

items.en: How I often dreamed of flying when I was a child!
items.zh: 我小時候常常好想飛！

items.en: How I sometimes wish I lived in the country!
items.zh: 我有時候好希望自己住在鄉下！

items.en: How we always laughed at his jokes!
items.zh: 我們總是被他的笑話逗得好樂！

items.en: How I still remember that day!
items.zh: 我到現在還好清楚記得那一天！

examples.heading: ⑤ How much ...! 和不同的句型

items.en: How much I love this city!
items.zh: 我好愛這座城市！

items.en: How much we enjoyed our stay!
items.zh: 我們住得好開心！

items.en: Look at you, Ken! How you've grown since last summer!
items.zh: 你看看你，Ken！從去年夏天到現在，你長高好多！

items.en: Ten years since we met! How the years have flown!
items.zh: 我們認識十年了！這些年過得好快！

items.en: How the town has changed!
items.zh: 這個小鎮變了好多！

items.en: How they laughed when they heard the news!
items.zh: 他們聽到那個消息時，笑得好開心！

items.en: How I wanted to tell her the truth!
items.zh: 我好想告訴她實話！

items.en: How we cried at the end of the film!
items.zh: 電影結束時我們哭得好慘！

items.en: How the children enjoyed the snow!
items.zh: 孩子們玩雪玩得好開心！

items.en: How I hope you'll come back soon!
items.zh: 我好希望你很快就回來！

items.en: How I envy you!
items.zh: 我好羨慕你！

title: If you agree, we can go shopping after the film.
translation: 如果你同意，我們看完電影可以去逛街。
name: 現在簡單式的 if 子句
sentences: If you come early, we'll have time for a coffee.
If the weather is nice, we'll go for a walk by the river.
If you want to pass the exam, you'll have to study very hard.
If I see Paul, I'll give him your message.
If you're tired, I'll drive.
If we leave now, we'll be there by nine.
I'll lend you my bike if yours is broken.
If you're free tomorrow, we can play tennis.
If you need a dictionary, you can use mine.
If the film finishes early, we can get a pizza.
If the shop is open, we can buy some milk on the way.
If you finish your homework, you can watch TV.
You can sleep in my room if your sister comes.
If we get up early, we can see the sunrise.
If you buy me a present, please make it a book.
If you visit London, go to the Science Museum.
If you need more chairs, take them from the kitchen.
If you have time, phone your grandmother.
Wake me up if I fall asleep.
If you go out, lock the door.
If Anna wants to come, she can sit next to me.
If it snows, the children will build a snowman.
If my brother passes his driving test, he'll buy a car.
If the restaurant is full, we'll go somewhere else.
If Dad gets home early, he cooks dinner.
If the train leaves on time, it arrives at ten.
If you don't hurry, we'll miss the opening song.
If she doesn't answer, leave a message.
If you don't understand, I can explain again.
If it doesn't stop raining, we'll stay in.
I'll be sad if you don't come to my party.
If you don't like the colour, you can change it.

examples.heading: ① will 說結果

items.en: If you come early, we'll have time for a coffee.
items.zh: 如果你早點來，我們就有時間喝杯咖啡。

items.en: If the weather is nice, we'll go for a walk by the river.
items.zh: 如果天氣好，我們會去河邊散步。

items.en: If you want to pass the exam, you'll have to study very hard.
items.zh: 如果你想通過考試，就得非常用功。

items.en: If I see Paul, I'll give him your message.
items.zh: 如果我見到 Paul，會把你的話轉告他。

items.en: If you're tired, I'll drive.
items.zh: 如果你累了，我來開車。

items.en: If we leave now, we'll be there by nine.
items.zh: 如果我們現在出發，九點前就會到。

items.en: I'll lend you my bike if yours is broken.
items.zh: 如果你的腳踏車壞了，我借你我的。

examples.heading: ② can 說可以做的事

items.en: If you're free tomorrow, we can play tennis.
items.zh: 如果你明天有空，我們可以打網球。

items.en: If you need a dictionary, you can use mine.
items.zh: 如果你需要字典，可以用我的。

items.en: If the film finishes early, we can get a pizza.
items.zh: 如果電影提早結束，我們可以去吃披薩。

items.en: If the shop is open, we can buy some milk on the way.
items.zh: 如果店有開，我們可以順路買牛奶。

items.en: If you finish your homework, you can watch TV.
items.zh: 如果你寫完功課，就可以看電視。

items.en: You can sleep in my room if your sister comes.
items.zh: 如果你姊姊來，你可以睡我房間。

items.en: If we get up early, we can see the sunrise.
items.zh: 如果我們早起，就可以看日出。

examples.heading: ③ 祈使句說要對方做的事

items.en: If you buy me a present, please make it a book.
items.zh: 如果你要送我禮物，請送書。

items.en: If you visit London, go to the Science Museum.
items.zh: 如果你去倫敦，去科學博物館看看。

items.en: If you need more chairs, take them from the kitchen.
items.zh: 如果你需要更多椅子，就去廚房拿。

items.en: If you have time, phone your grandmother.
items.zh: 如果你有時間，打電話給你奶奶。

items.en: Wake me up if I fall asleep.
items.zh: 如果我睡著了，叫醒我。

items.en: If you go out, lock the door.
items.zh: 如果你出門，記得鎖門。

examples.heading: ④ 動詞加 -s 的條件

items.en: If Anna wants to come, she can sit next to me.
items.zh: 如果 Anna 想來，她可以坐我旁邊。

items.en: If it snows, the children will build a snowman.
items.zh: 如果下雪，孩子們會堆雪人。

items.en: If my brother passes his driving test, he'll buy a car.
items.zh: 如果我哥考過駕照，他會買車。

items.en: If the restaurant is full, we'll go somewhere else.
items.zh: 如果餐廳客滿，我們就去別家。

items.en: If Dad gets home early, he cooks dinner.
items.zh: 如果爸爸早回家，他會煮晚餐。

items.en: If the train leaves on time, it arrives at ten.
items.zh: 如果火車準時開，十點就會到。

examples.heading: ⑤ don't 和 doesn't

items.en: If you don't hurry, we'll miss the opening song.
items.zh: 如果你不快一點，我們會錯過開場的歌。

items.en: If she doesn't answer, leave a message.
items.zh: 如果她沒接，就留言。

items.en: If you don't understand, I can explain again.
items.zh: 如果你不懂，我可以再解釋一次。

items.en: If it doesn't stop raining, we'll stay in.
items.zh: 如果雨一直不停，我們就待在家。

items.en: I'll be sad if you don't come to my party.
items.zh: 如果你不來我的派對，我會很難過。

items.en: If you don't like the colour, you can change it.
items.zh: 如果你不喜歡這個顏色，可以換。

title: Do you still remember my best friend?
translation: 你還記得我最好的朋友嗎？
name: 疑問句中的句中副詞
sentences: You've lived in Taipei for a month. Have you ever been to the night market in Shilin?
I bought a big fish at the market. Have you ever cooked a whole fish by yourself?
My uncle needs help with the apples this autumn. Has your brother ever worked on a farm?
You work at the concert hall. Have you ever shaken hands with a famous singer?
The manager asked about the two new cleaners. Have they ever been late for work?
We're going camping by the sea. Have you ever slept in a tent on the beach?
You always have a book in your hand. What kind of books do you usually read?
Your office is only ten minutes away. Do you usually go there on foot?
You look very fit. How often do you usually go to the gym?
You never cook at the end of the week. Do you often eat out on Fridays?
I saw her jogging at six this morning. Does your sister always get up so early?
You look tired every morning. What time do you normally go to bed?
I found this old photo of us in the sand. Do you still remember our first trip to the beach?
I want to send you a wedding invitation. Do you still live on Park Road?
I need some advice about a loan. Does Ken still work at the bank?
I used to buy sweets at the corner shop as a child. Do they still sell those old sweets?
I saw you at the stop an hour ago. Are you still waiting for the bus?
The party has only just started. Do you really want to leave now?
Our teacher said the exam is cancelled? Did she really say that?
It's Mum's birthday dinner. Have you already booked the restaurant for Friday?
Has the film already started? I can hear music.
Tom says we should sell the car. Do you really think he's right?
Your flat is next to the railway. Can you always hear the trains from it?
I'm so sorry I missed your wedding. Will you ever forgive me?
The meeting started twenty minutes ago. Why do you always arrive late?
You sent back the broken phone in March. Did you ever get your money back from that shop?
There's no car park at your office. Where do you usually park?
You look busy on Saturdays. Do you sometimes work at weekends?
You love Italian food and the language. Have you ever thought about moving abroad?
We're thinking of buying a house by the water. Does the river often flood after heavy rain?

examples.heading: ① Have you ever + 過去分詞?

items.en: You've lived in Taipei for a month. Have you ever been to the night market in Shilin?
items.zh: 你在台北住了一個月。你去過士林夜市嗎？

items.en: I bought a big fish at the market. Have you ever cooked a whole fish by yourself?
items.zh: 我在市場買了一條大魚。你自己煮過一整條魚嗎？

items.en: My uncle needs help with the apples this autumn. Has your brother ever worked on a farm?
items.zh: 我叔叔今年秋天需要人手採蘋果。你哥哥在農場工作過嗎？

items.en: You work at the concert hall. Have you ever shaken hands with a famous singer?
items.zh: 你在音樂廳工作。你跟有名的歌手握過手嗎？

items.en: The manager asked about the two new cleaners. Have they ever been late for work?
items.zh: 經理問起那兩個新來的清潔人員。他們上班遲到過嗎？

items.en: We're going camping by the sea. Have you ever slept in a tent on the beach?
items.zh: 我們要去海邊露營。你在海灘上睡過帳篷嗎？

examples.heading: ② Do you usually / often + 原形動詞?

items.en: You always have a book in your hand. What kind of books do you usually read?
items.zh: 你手上總是拿著一本書。你通常讀哪一類的書？

items.en: Your office is only ten minutes away. Do you usually go there on foot?
items.zh: 你的辦公室只要十分鐘。你通常走路去嗎？

items.en: You look very fit. How often do you usually go to the gym?
items.zh: 你身材看起來很好。你通常多久去一次健身房？

items.en: You never cook at the end of the week. Do you often eat out on Fridays?
items.zh: 你週末前從來不煮飯。你星期五常出去吃嗎？

items.en: I saw her jogging at six this morning. Does your sister always get up so early?
items.zh: 我今天早上六點看到她在慢跑。你姊姊總是這麼早起嗎？

items.en: You look tired every morning. What time do you normally go to bed?
items.zh: 你每天早上看起來都很累。你平常幾點睡？

examples.heading: ③ Do you still + 原形動詞?

items.en: I found this old photo of us in the sand. Do you still remember our first trip to the beach?
items.zh: 我找到這張我們在沙灘上的舊照片。你還記得我們第一次去海邊嗎？

items.en: I want to send you a wedding invitation. Do you still live on Park Road?
items.zh: 我想寄喜帖給你。你還住在公園路嗎？

items.en: I need some advice about a loan. Does Ken still work at the bank?
items.zh: 我需要一些貸款的建議。Ken 還在銀行上班嗎？

items.en: I used to buy sweets at the corner shop as a child. Do they still sell those old sweets?
items.zh: 我小時候常在轉角的店買糖果。他們還有賣那種懷舊糖果嗎？

items.en: I saw you at the stop an hour ago. Are you still waiting for the bus?
items.zh: 我一個小時前看到你在公車站。你還在等公車嗎？

examples.heading: ④ Do you really / Have you already ...?

items.en: The party has only just started. Do you really want to leave now?
items.zh: 派對才剛開始。你真的現在就想走嗎？

items.en: Our teacher said the exam is cancelled? Did she really say that?
items.zh: 我們老師說考試取消了？她真的那樣說嗎？

items.en: It's Mum's birthday dinner. Have you already booked the restaurant for Friday?
items.zh: 那是媽媽的生日晚餐。你已經訂好星期五的餐廳了嗎？

items.en: Has the film already started? I can hear music.
items.zh: 電影已經開始了嗎？我聽到音樂了。

items.en: Tom says we should sell the car. Do you really think he's right?
items.zh: 湯姆說我們應該把車賣了。你真的覺得他是對的嗎？

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的助動詞和句型

items.en: Your flat is next to the railway. Can you always hear the trains from it?
items.zh: 你的公寓在鐵路旁邊。你在公寓裡總是聽得到火車的聲音嗎？

items.en: I'm so sorry I missed your wedding. Will you ever forgive me?
items.zh: 很抱歉我錯過了你的婚禮。你會原諒我嗎？

items.en: The meeting started twenty minutes ago. Why do you always arrive late?
items.zh: 會議二十分鐘前就開始了。你為什麼總是遲到？

items.en: You sent back the broken phone in March. Did you ever get your money back from that shop?
items.zh: 你三月把壞掉的手機寄回去。你後來有從那家店拿回你的錢嗎？

items.en: There's no car park at your office. Where do you usually park?
items.zh: 你辦公室沒有停車場。你通常把車停在哪裡？

items.en: You look busy on Saturdays. Do you sometimes work at weekends?
items.zh: 你星期六看起來很忙。你週末有時候要上班嗎？

items.en: You love Italian food and the language. Have you ever thought about moving abroad?
items.zh: 你很愛義大利菜和義大利文。你想過搬到國外嗎？

items.en: We're thinking of buying a house by the water. Does the river often flood after heavy rain?
items.zh: 我們在考慮買一間水邊的房子。大雨過後那條河常淹水嗎？

title: It smelled like roses.
translation: 那聞起來像玫瑰花。
name: 連綴動詞加 like 或 similar to
sentences: People say I look like a pop star in this jacket.
We're on the fiftieth floor. From up here, the cars look like ants.
You look like a real chef in that apron.
My son had a window seat on his first flight. From the plane, the houses looked like toys.
It's round and silver, with lights all around it. The new library looks like a spaceship.
A car tyre exploded outside our house. The noise sounded like a gunshot.
I bought this at the market in Sicily. This soap smells like lemons.
I didn't put any sugar in it, but this tea tastes like honey.
So we leave early and miss the traffic? Your plan sounds like a good idea.
Grandma has been baking all morning. The kitchen smells like fresh bread.
The vegetarian burger tasted like real meat.
Up there, I felt like a bird.
I slept for ten hours on our first night. The hotel bed felt like a cloud.
Is it really only two years? It seems like a long time since we met.
The boss was away, and we left work early every day. That week felt like a holiday.
We matched pictures and words on a tablet. The test seemed like a game.
Your idea is similar to one I had last week.
It's warm and wet in Hong Kong in April. The weather here is similar to Taipei's in spring.
Both use a lot of rice and soup. Japanese food is similar to Korean food in some ways.
I still answer customers' emails all day. My new job is similar to my old one.
It's green and has big soft cushions. Our new sofa is similar to the one at your parents' house.
The teacher thinks I wrote this note. Does this look like my handwriting?
Take the train and rent bikes there? It doesn't sound like a bad plan.
I saw a girl with your smile at the station. Your sister looks similar to you.
I've never tried durian. What does it taste like?
My first flat had no air conditioning. The room felt like a sauna in summer.
My dad hums along to the new hit. That song sounds similar to an old one from the eighties.
I can read some Italian already. Is Spanish similar to Italian?
Bring the washing in. It smells like rain.
I thought Mr Lee answered the phone, but it was his son. His voice sounds like his father's.

examples.heading: ① look like + 名詞

items.en: People say I look like a pop star in this jacket.
items.zh: 大家說我穿這件夾克看起來像流行歌手。

items.en: We're on the fiftieth floor. From up here, the cars look like ants.
items.zh: 我們在五十樓。從這上面看，車子看起來像螞蟻。

items.en: You look like a real chef in that apron.
items.zh: 你穿那件圍裙看起來像個真正的廚師。

items.en: My son had a window seat on his first flight. From the plane, the houses looked like toys.
items.zh: 我兒子第一次搭飛機坐靠窗的位子。從飛機上看，房子看起來像玩具。

items.en: It's round and silver, with lights all around it. The new library looks like a spaceship.
items.zh: 它是圓的、銀色的，四周都是燈。新的圖書館看起來像太空船。

examples.heading: ② sound / smell / taste like + 名詞

items.en: A car tyre exploded outside our house. The noise sounded like a gunshot.
items.zh: 我們家外面有一個車胎爆了。那個聲音聽起來像槍聲。

items.en: I bought this at the market in Sicily. This soap smells like lemons.
items.zh: 我在西西里的市場買了這個。這塊肥皂聞起來像檸檬。

items.en: I didn't put any sugar in it, but this tea tastes like honey.
items.zh: 我沒加糖，可是這茶喝起來像蜂蜜。

items.en: So we leave early and miss the traffic? Your plan sounds like a good idea.
items.zh: 所以我們早點出發，避開車潮？你的計畫聽起來是個好主意。

items.en: Grandma has been baking all morning. The kitchen smells like fresh bread.
items.zh: 奶奶整個早上都在烤東西。廚房聞起來像剛烤好的麵包。

items.en: The vegetarian burger tasted like real meat.
items.zh: 那個素漢堡吃起來像真的肉。

examples.heading: ③ feel / seem like + 名詞

items.en: Up there, I felt like a bird.
items.zh: 在上面，我覺得自己像一隻鳥。

items.en: I slept for ten hours on our first night. The hotel bed felt like a cloud.
items.zh: 我們第一晚我睡了十個小時。飯店的床躺起來像雲一樣。

items.en: Is it really only two years? It seems like a long time since we met.
items.zh: 真的才兩年嗎？我們好像很久沒見了。

items.en: The boss was away, and we left work early every day. That week felt like a holiday.
items.zh: 老闆不在，我們每天都提早下班。那個禮拜感覺像放假一樣。

items.en: We matched pictures and words on a tablet. The test seemed like a game.
items.zh: 我們在平板上把圖片和單字配對。那次考試感覺像遊戲一樣。

examples.heading: ④ be similar to + 名詞

items.en: Your idea is similar to one I had last week.
items.zh: 你的點子跟我上禮拜想到的很像。

items.en: It's warm and wet in Hong Kong in April. The weather here is similar to Taipei's in spring.
items.zh: 香港四月又暖又濕。這裡的天氣跟台北春天的差不多。

items.en: Both use a lot of rice and soup. Japanese food is similar to Korean food in some ways.
items.zh: 兩種都常用米飯和湯。日本菜在某些方面跟韓國菜很像。

items.en: I still answer customers' emails all day. My new job is similar to my old one.
items.zh: 我還是整天回客人的電子郵件。我的新工作跟舊的差不多。

items.en: It's green and has big soft cushions. Our new sofa is similar to the one at your parents' house.
items.zh: 它是綠色的，有大大軟軟的靠墊。我們的新沙發跟你爸媽家那張很像。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的句型

items.en: The teacher thinks I wrote this note. Does this look like my handwriting?
items.zh: 老師以為這張紙條是我寫的。這看起來像我的字嗎？

items.en: Take the train and rent bikes there? It doesn't sound like a bad plan.
items.zh: 搭火車去，在那裡租腳踏車？聽起來不像個壞主意。

items.en: I saw a girl with your smile at the station. Your sister looks similar to you.
items.zh: 我在車站看到一個笑起來跟你一樣的女孩。你妹妹長得跟你很像。

items.en: I've never tried durian. What does it taste like?
items.zh: 我從來沒吃過榴槤。吃起來像什麼？

items.en: My first flat had no air conditioning. The room felt like a sauna in summer.
items.zh: 我的第一間公寓沒有冷氣。夏天這個房間熱得像三溫暖。

items.en: My dad hums along to the new hit. That song sounds similar to an old one from the eighties.
items.zh: 我爸爸跟著那首新歌哼。那首歌聽起來跟一首八〇年代的老歌很像。

items.en: I can read some Italian already. Is Spanish similar to Italian?
items.zh: 我已經看得懂一些義大利文。西班牙文跟義大利文很像嗎？

items.en: Bring the washing in. It smells like rain.
items.zh: 把晾的衣服收進來。聞起來像要下雨了。

items.en: I thought Mr Lee answered the phone, but it was his son. His voice sounds like his father's.
items.zh: 我以為是李先生接的電話，可是那是他兒子。他的聲音聽起來像他爸爸的。

title: I like English lessons, but I don't like physics.
translation: 我喜歡英文課，但我不喜歡物理。
name: 對等子句（兩個主要子句）
sentences: I love my new school and my teachers are kind.
My father is a doctor and my mother is a teacher.
Here is my school day. I get up at seven and I have breakfast at half past seven.
Our house is never quiet. We have a dog and we have two cats.
Ken plays the guitar and his sister sings.
We can't buy milk today. It's Sunday and the shops are closed.
I like cooking, but I don't like washing up.
On Saturdays I play tennis, but I often stay home on Sundays.
I don't want to move. My flat is old, but the rent is cheap.
Look at the red coat in the window. I want to buy that coat, but it costs too much.
My little sister is six. She can swim, but she can't ride a bike.
We ate at a small café near the station. The food was cheap, but it was very good.
The museum is two kilometres away. We can take the bus or we can walk.
Tell me when your train arrives. You can call me or you can send a text.
I don't know which jacket to wear. Is it cold outside or is it warm?
I can't come to your house on Thursday. I'll come on Friday or I'll come on Saturday.
Come in and sit down. Do you want tea or do you want coffee?
On Sundays, we sleep late, we have a big breakfast and we go for a walk.
My weekdays are always the same. I go to school, I do my homework and I play football.
Everyone helps at home. My mother cooks, my father cleans and I wash the dishes.
We had a great day at the beach. We swam, we played games and we ate ice cream.
It's raining, so we can't go to the park. You can read, you can draw or you can watch a film.
Let's go to the beach now. It rained yesterday, but today it's sunny.
I had football practice after school. I was tired, but I finished my homework.
Last Sunday was very hot. We went to the lake and we had a great time.
The doctor's secretary has your results. She will call you or she will send an email.
We didn't see each other much in those years. I lived in Tainan and my brother lived in Taipei.
My brother played games all week. He didn't study, but he passed the test.
I worked for ten hours today. I'm hungry and I'm tired.
We watched a film about the moon last night. It was long, but it was very interesting.

examples.heading: ① and

items.en: I love my new school and my teachers are kind.
items.zh: 我喜歡我的新學校，老師也很和善。

items.en: My father is a doctor and my mother is a teacher.
items.zh: 我爸爸是醫生，我媽媽是老師。

items.en: Here is my school day. I get up at seven and I have breakfast at half past seven.
items.zh: 這是我上學的一天。我七點起床，七點半吃早餐。

items.en: Our house is never quiet. We have a dog and we have two cats.
items.zh: 我們家從來都不安靜。我們養了一隻狗，還養了兩隻貓。

items.en: Ken plays the guitar and his sister sings.
items.zh: Ken 彈吉他，他妹妹唱歌。

items.en: We can't buy milk today. It's Sunday and the shops are closed.
items.zh: 我們今天買不到牛奶。今天是星期天，店都沒開。

examples.heading: ② but

items.en: I like cooking, but I don't like washing up.
items.zh: 我喜歡煮飯，但我不喜歡洗碗。

items.en: On Saturdays I play tennis, but I often stay home on Sundays.
items.zh: 星期六我會打網球，但星期天我常常待在家。

items.en: I don't want to move. My flat is old, but the rent is cheap.
items.zh: 我不想搬家。我的公寓很舊，但是房租很便宜。

items.en: Look at the red coat in the window. I want to buy that coat, but it costs too much.
items.zh: 你看櫥窗裡那件紅外套。我想買那件外套，但是太貴了。

items.en: My little sister is six. She can swim, but she can't ride a bike.
items.zh: 我妹妹六歲。她會游泳，但是不會騎腳踏車。

items.en: We ate at a small café near the station. The food was cheap, but it was very good.
items.zh: 我們在車站附近一家小咖啡館吃飯。食物很便宜，但是很好吃。

examples.heading: ③ or

items.en: The museum is two kilometres away. We can take the bus or we can walk.
items.zh: 博物館在兩公里外。我們可以搭公車，或是走路。

items.en: Tell me when your train arrives. You can call me or you can send a text.
items.zh: 你的火車到的時候告訴我。你可以打給我，或是傳簡訊。

items.en: I don't know which jacket to wear. Is it cold outside or is it warm?
items.zh: 我不知道要穿哪件外套。外面冷還是暖和？

items.en: I can't come to your house on Thursday. I'll come on Friday or I'll come on Saturday.
items.zh: 我星期四沒辦法去你家。我會星期五來，或是星期六來。

items.en: Come in and sit down. Do you want tea or do you want coffee?
items.zh: 進來坐。你要喝茶還是喝咖啡？

examples.heading: ④ 三個以上的子句

items.en: On Sundays, we sleep late, we have a big breakfast and we go for a walk.
items.zh: 星期天我們會睡晚一點、吃頓豐盛的早餐，然後去散步。

items.en: My weekdays are always the same. I go to school, I do my homework and I play football.
items.zh: 我平日每天都一樣。我上學、寫作業，然後踢足球。

items.en: Everyone helps at home. My mother cooks, my father cleans and I wash the dishes.
items.zh: 家裡每個人都會幫忙。我媽媽煮飯，我爸爸打掃，我洗碗。

items.en: We had a great day at the beach. We swam, we played games and we ate ice cream.
items.zh: 我們在海邊玩了很開心的一天。我們游泳、玩遊戲，還吃了冰淇淋。

items.en: It's raining, so we can't go to the park. You can read, you can draw or you can watch a film.
items.zh: 下雨了，所以我們不能去公園。你可以看書、畫畫，或是看電影。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的時態

items.en: Let's go to the beach now. It rained yesterday, but today it's sunny.
items.zh: 我們現在去海邊吧。昨天下雨，但是今天出太陽。

items.en: I had football practice after school. I was tired, but I finished my homework.
items.zh: 我放學後有足球練習。我很累，但我寫完作業了。

items.en: Last Sunday was very hot. We went to the lake and we had a great time.
items.zh: 上星期天很熱。我們去了湖邊，玩得很開心。

items.en: The doctor's secretary has your results. She will call you or she will send an email.
items.zh: 醫生的秘書有你的檢查結果。她會打給你，或是寄電子郵件。

items.en: We didn't see each other much in those years. I lived in Tainan and my brother lived in Taipei.
items.zh: 那幾年我們不常見面。我住在台南，我哥哥住在台北。

items.en: My brother played games all week. He didn't study, but he passed the test.
items.zh: 我哥哥整個星期都在打電動。他沒讀書，但考試及格了。

items.en: I worked for ten hours today. I'm hungry and I'm tired.
items.zh: 我今天工作了十個小時。我又餓又累。

items.en: We watched a film about the moon last night. It was long, but it was very interesting.
items.zh: 我們昨天晚上看了一部關於月球的電影。它很長，但是很有趣。

title: I don't have children.
translation: 我沒有小孩。
name: 一般動詞的否定直述句
sentences: I grew up alone with my parents. I don't have any brothers or sisters.
I don't enjoy long car trips. I get carsick.
Sorry, I don't speak Italian very well.
We don't own a car, so we cycle everywhere.
You're looking for the Smiths? They don't live here anymore.
Send the photos by post. My grandparents don't use the internet.
Don't order the curry for my uncle. He doesn't eat spicy food.
My sister is always in a hurry. She doesn't eat breakfast on weekdays.
Can you drive Ken home? He doesn't have a car.
Go now if you want a loaf. The bakery doesn't sell bread after six.
Our dog is very friendly. She doesn't bark at strangers.
Can I borrow yours? This pen doesn't work.
Someone broke into our garage last night. We didn't hear the alarm.
The neighbors were noisy, so I didn't get much sleep.
I left a message for my sister at noon. She didn't call me back.
Our school team played well, but they didn't win the game.
My son played games all evening. He didn't finish his homework.
The shop assistant offered to carry my bags. I don't need help, thanks.
My grandmother walks everywhere. She doesn't drive.
The landlord has strict rules. We don't keep any pets in our flat.
We met only once, at a wedding. Ann doesn't remember my name.
It's nine o'clock, and they're still playing. The kids don't want to go to bed.
It's only half past eight. I don't think the shop is open yet.
The party goes on until midnight. It doesn't matter if you're late.
Can you help me? I don't understand the second page of this form.
My brother doesn't play football, but he likes watching it.
The café is never full on Mondays. We don't need to book a table.
Dad is very pale this morning. He doesn't look well today.
I didn't hear my alarm this morning, so I was late.
The bill is three hundred dollars for two coffees? That doesn't sound right.

examples.heading: ① I / we / they + don't

items.en: I grew up alone with my parents. I don't have any brothers or sisters.
items.zh: 我跟爸媽一起長大。我沒有兄弟姊妹。

items.en: I don't enjoy long car trips. I get carsick.
items.zh: 我不喜歡長途坐車，我會暈車。

items.en: Sorry, I don't speak Italian very well.
items.zh: 抱歉，我的義大利文說得不太好。

items.en: We don't own a car, so we cycle everywhere.
items.zh: 我們沒有車，所以到哪裡都騎腳踏車。

items.en: You're looking for the Smiths? They don't live here anymore.
items.zh: 你在找史密斯一家？他們已經不住這裡了。

items.en: Send the photos by post. My grandparents don't use the internet.
items.zh: 照片用郵寄的。我爺爺奶奶不上網。

examples.heading: ② he / she / it + doesn't

items.en: Don't order the curry for my uncle. He doesn't eat spicy food.
items.zh: 別幫我叔叔點咖哩。他不吃辣。

items.en: My sister is always in a hurry. She doesn't eat breakfast on weekdays.
items.zh: 我姊姊總是很趕。她平日不吃早餐。

items.en: Can you drive Ken home? He doesn't have a car.
items.zh: 你可以載 Ken 回家嗎？他沒有車。

items.en: Go now if you want a loaf. The bakery doesn't sell bread after six.
items.zh: 你要買麵包就現在去。那家麵包店六點以後就不賣麵包了。

items.en: Our dog is very friendly. She doesn't bark at strangers.
items.zh: 我們家的狗很友善。她不會對陌生人叫。

items.en: Can I borrow yours? This pen doesn't work.
items.zh: 可以借你的嗎？這支筆寫不出來。

examples.heading: ③ didn't + 原形動詞

items.en: Someone broke into our garage last night. We didn't hear the alarm.
items.zh: 昨天晚上有人闖進我們的車庫。我們沒聽到警報聲。

items.en: The neighbors were noisy, so I didn't get much sleep.
items.zh: 鄰居很吵，所以我沒怎麼睡。

items.en: I left a message for my sister at noon. She didn't call me back.
items.zh: 我中午留言給我姊姊。她沒有回我電話。

items.en: Our school team played well, but they didn't win the game.
items.zh: 我們學校的球隊打得很好，可是他們沒贏比賽。

items.en: My son played games all evening. He didn't finish his homework.
items.zh: 我兒子整個晚上都在打電動。他沒寫完作業。

examples.heading: ④ don't / doesn't + 動詞 + 受詞

items.en: The shop assistant offered to carry my bags. I don't need help, thanks.
items.zh: 店員說要幫我提袋子。我不需要幫忙，謝謝。

items.en: My grandmother walks everywhere. She doesn't drive.
items.zh: 我奶奶去哪裡都走路。她不開車。

items.en: The landlord has strict rules. We don't keep any pets in our flat.
items.zh: 房東的規定很嚴。我們的公寓沒養寵物。

items.en: We met only once, at a wedding. Ann doesn't remember my name.
items.zh: 我們只在一場婚禮上見過一次。Ann 不記得我的名字。

items.en: It's nine o'clock, and they're still playing. The kids don't want to go to bed.
items.zh: 已經九點了，他們還在玩。孩子們不想去睡覺。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的句型

items.en: It's only half past eight. I don't think the shop is open yet.
items.zh: 才八點半。我覺得那家店還沒開。

items.en: The party goes on until midnight. It doesn't matter if you're late.
items.zh: 派對會到半夜。你遲到也沒關係。

items.en: Can you help me? I don't understand the second page of this form.
items.zh: 你可以幫我嗎？我看不懂這張表格的第二頁。

items.en: My brother doesn't play football, but he likes watching it.
items.zh: 我哥哥不踢足球，但他喜歡看。

items.en: The café is never full on Mondays. We don't need to book a table.
items.zh: 那家咖啡館星期一從來不會客滿。我們不用訂位。

items.en: Dad is very pale this morning. He doesn't look well today.
items.zh: 爸爸今天早上臉色很蒼白。他今天看起來不太舒服。

items.en: I didn't hear my alarm this morning, so I was late.
items.zh: 我今天早上沒聽到鬧鐘，所以遲到了。

items.en: The bill is three hundred dollars for two coffees? That doesn't sound right.
items.zh: 兩杯咖啡的帳單要三百塊？那聽起來不太對。

title: I can't wait to see you.
translation: 我等不及要見你了。
name: 情態動詞加 not 的否定直述句
sentences: Sorry, I've got work, so I can't join you for lunch on Saturday.
Speak up a little. Grandpa can't hear you from there.
The sign says we can't leave bikes in front of the gate.
The car park is huge, and I can't remember where we parked.
My brother can't ride a bike, so he walks to school.
We can't wait to try your new restaurant.
I'm sorry you couldn't come to the wedding.
When I lived abroad, I couldn't call my family every day.
A tall man sat in front of us, so we couldn't see the screen.
The dog next door barked all night, and my sister couldn't fall asleep.
I couldn't open the jar, so I asked my dad.
It's warm in July, so you won't need your winter boots.
Once you try this cake, you won't want any other.
Don't worry. I won't say a word to your parents.
The car won't start, so we'll take the bus.
Dinner took an hour last night. My son wouldn't eat his vegetables.
The doctor says Dad shouldn't eat so much salt.
The new director is coming today. We shouldn't be late for the meeting.
The electrician is still working on the light. You mustn't touch the wires.
Passengers mustn't stand near the doors while the train is moving.
If you've had a glass of wine, you shouldn't drive home.
Thank you, but I cannot accept such an expensive gift.
We still have to drive the long way round. The new bridge won't open until next spring.
Ten dollars for a coffee? You can't be serious!
My dad saw his old school friend on TV. He couldn't believe his eyes.
You want to quit your job by email? I wouldn't do that if I were you.
Bring some cash to the market. The shop can't take credit cards.
Don't wait up for us. We won't be home until late.
The exam is easy. You shouldn't lose sleep over it.
Can I use your computer tonight? My old laptop won't connect to the Wi-Fi.

examples.heading: ① can't + 原形動詞

items.en: Sorry, I've got work, so I can't join you for lunch on Saturday.
items.zh: 抱歉，我要上班，所以星期六不能跟你們吃午餐。

items.en: Speak up a little. Grandpa can't hear you from there.
items.zh: 大聲一點，爺爺在那裡聽不到你說話。

items.en: The sign says we can't leave bikes in front of the gate.
items.zh: 牌子上說不能把腳踏車停在大門前面。

items.en: The car park is huge, and I can't remember where we parked.
items.zh: 停車場好大，我記不得我們把車停在哪裡了。

items.en: My brother can't ride a bike, so he walks to school.
items.zh: 我弟弟不會騎腳踏車，所以都走路上學。

items.en: We can't wait to try your new restaurant.
items.zh: 我們等不及要去你的新餐廳吃了。

examples.heading: ② couldn't + 原形動詞

items.en: I'm sorry you couldn't come to the wedding.
items.zh: 很遺憾你沒辦法來婚禮。

items.en: When I lived abroad, I couldn't call my family every day.
items.zh: 我住在國外的時候，沒辦法每天打電話給家人。

items.en: A tall man sat in front of us, so we couldn't see the screen.
items.zh: 一個高個子坐在我們前面，所以我們看不到螢幕。

items.en: The dog next door barked all night, and my sister couldn't fall asleep.
items.zh: 隔壁的狗叫了一整晚，我姊姊睡不著。

items.en: I couldn't open the jar, so I asked my dad.
items.zh: 我打不開那個罐子，所以請我爸爸幫忙。

examples.heading: ③ won't / wouldn't + 原形動詞

items.en: It's warm in July, so you won't need your winter boots.
items.zh: 七月很暖和，所以你不需要冬天的靴子。

items.en: Once you try this cake, you won't want any other.
items.zh: 你一旦吃過這個蛋糕，就不會想吃別的了。

items.en: Don't worry. I won't say a word to your parents.
items.zh: 別擔心，我不會跟你爸媽說一個字。

items.en: The car won't start, so we'll take the bus.
items.zh: 車子發不動，所以我們搭公車吧。

items.en: Dinner took an hour last night. My son wouldn't eat his vegetables.
items.zh: 昨天晚餐吃了一個小時。我兒子就是不肯吃蔬菜。

examples.heading: ④ shouldn't / mustn't + 原形動詞

items.en: The doctor says Dad shouldn't eat so much salt.
items.zh: 醫生說爸爸不應該吃那麼多鹽。

items.en: The new director is coming today. We shouldn't be late for the meeting.
items.zh: 新主任今天要來。我們開會不應該遲到。

items.en: The electrician is still working on the light. You mustn't touch the wires.
items.zh: 電工還在修那盞燈。你絕對不可以碰那些電線。

items.en: Passengers mustn't stand near the doors while the train is moving.
items.zh: 火車行駛時，乘客絕對不可以站在車門附近。

items.en: If you've had a glass of wine, you shouldn't drive home.
items.zh: 如果你喝了一杯酒，就不應該開車回家。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的句型

items.en: Thank you, but I cannot accept such an expensive gift.
items.zh: 謝謝你，可是我不能收這麼貴的禮物。

items.en: We still have to drive the long way round. The new bridge won't open until next spring.
items.zh: 我們還是得開車繞遠路。新橋要到明年春天才會通車。

items.en: Ten dollars for a coffee? You can't be serious!
items.zh: 一杯咖啡十塊錢？你不是說真的吧！

items.en: My dad saw his old school friend on TV. He couldn't believe his eyes.
items.zh: 我爸爸在電視上看到他的老同學。他簡直不敢相信自己的眼睛。

items.en: You want to quit your job by email? I wouldn't do that if I were you.
items.zh: 你想用電子郵件辭職？如果我是你，我不會那樣做。

items.en: Bring some cash to the market. The shop can't take credit cards.
items.zh: 去市場帶點現金。那家店不能刷信用卡。

items.en: Don't wait up for us. We won't be home until late.
items.zh: 別等我們。我們會很晚才到家。

items.en: The exam is easy. You shouldn't lose sleep over it.
items.zh: 考試很簡單，你不必為它睡不著。

items.en: Can I use your computer tonight? My old laptop won't connect to the Wi-Fi.
items.zh: 我今天晚上可以用你的電腦嗎？我的舊筆電連不上 Wi-Fi。

title: This place isn't big.
translation: 這個地方不大。
name: be 動詞的否定直述句
sentences: Our kitchen isn't very big, but it's bright.
The bathwater isn't warm. Is the heater broken?
You can park outside our house. Our street isn't busy at night.
Don't worry about Friday. The test isn't difficult if you study.
I only have one book and my lunch. My bag isn't heavy today.
Let's wait in the café. The sofa in the hotel lobby isn't very comfortable.
Buy bread on Saturday. The shops aren't open on Sunday morning.
My parents aren't teachers. They're nurses.
Someone left their trainers by the door. These shoes aren't mine.
Don't pick them now. The apples aren't ripe yet.
Can the taxi wait five minutes? We aren't ready to leave.
Ask Anna, please. I'm not sure about the time of the meeting.
No cake for me, thanks. I'm not a fan of chocolate.
A man fell over in the street. I'm not a doctor, but I can help.
I'm not very good with computers, so please help me.
I'm not from here. I'm from Tainan.
Sorry, she's at the gym. My sister is not at home right now.
I've looked everywhere. The keys aren't in my bag.
Can I take a message? Mr. Lee isn't in the office today.
You can walk there in five minutes. The post office isn't far from the station.
The kids aren't at school today. It's a holiday.
The singer had a cold. The concert last night wasn't very good.
I called the front desk this morning. The towels in our room weren't dry.
The broken window wasn't my fault. The ball hit it.
I got a seat by the window. The train wasn't crowded on Sunday.
Ask someone else about the fight. We weren't at the party last night.
It isn't cold today, so leave your coat at home.
Swimming after a big meal isn't a good idea.
My phone isn't new. It's three years old.
He's not angry. He's just tired.

examples.heading: ① isn't + 形容詞

items.en: Our kitchen isn't very big, but it's bright.
items.zh: 我們的廚房不太大，不過很明亮。

items.en: The bathwater isn't warm. Is the heater broken?
items.zh: 洗澡水不熱，熱水器壞了嗎？

items.en: You can park outside our house. Our street isn't busy at night.
items.zh: 你可以把車停在我們家外面。我們這條街晚上車不多。

items.en: Don't worry about Friday. The test isn't difficult if you study.
items.zh: 別擔心星期五。如果有讀書，考試就不難。

items.en: I only have one book and my lunch. My bag isn't heavy today.
items.zh: 我只帶了一本書和午餐。我的包包今天不重。

items.en: Let's wait in the café. The sofa in the hotel lobby isn't very comfortable.
items.zh: 我們去咖啡廳等吧。飯店大廳的沙發不太舒服。

examples.heading: ② aren't + 形容詞 / 名詞

items.en: Buy bread on Saturday. The shops aren't open on Sunday morning.
items.zh: 星期六就買麵包。商店星期天早上沒開。

items.en: My parents aren't teachers. They're nurses.
items.zh: 我爸媽不是老師，他們是護理師。

items.en: Someone left their trainers by the door. These shoes aren't mine.
items.zh: 有人把運動鞋留在門邊。這雙鞋不是我的。

items.en: Don't pick them now. The apples aren't ripe yet.
items.zh: 現在別摘。蘋果還沒熟。

items.en: Can the taxi wait five minutes? We aren't ready to leave.
items.zh: 計程車可以等五分鐘嗎？我們還沒準備好出發。

examples.heading: ③ I'm not + 形容詞 / 名詞

items.en: Ask Anna, please. I'm not sure about the time of the meeting.
items.zh: 請問安娜。我不確定開會的時間。

items.en: No cake for me, thanks. I'm not a fan of chocolate.
items.zh: 我不用蛋糕，謝謝，我不太喜歡巧克力。

items.en: A man fell over in the street. I'm not a doctor, but I can help.
items.zh: 一個男人在街上跌倒了。我不是醫生，但我可以幫忙。

items.en: I'm not very good with computers, so please help me.
items.zh: 我不太會用電腦，所以請幫幫我。

items.en: I'm not from here. I'm from Tainan.
items.zh: 我不是這裡人，我是台南人。

examples.heading: ④ be + not + 地方

items.en: Sorry, she's at the gym. My sister is not at home right now.
items.zh: 抱歉，她在健身房。我姊姊現在不在家。

items.en: I've looked everywhere. The keys aren't in my bag.
items.zh: 我到處都找過了。鑰匙不在我的包包裡。

items.en: Can I take a message? Mr. Lee isn't in the office today.
items.zh: 要我幫你留話嗎？李先生今天不在辦公室。

items.en: You can walk there in five minutes. The post office isn't far from the station.
items.zh: 你走五分鐘就到了。郵局離車站不遠。

items.en: The kids aren't at school today. It's a holiday.
items.zh: 孩子們今天不在學校，今天放假。

examples.heading: ⑤ wasn't / weren't 和不同的句型

items.en: The singer had a cold. The concert last night wasn't very good.
items.zh: 那個歌手感冒了。昨晚的演唱會不怎麼好。

items.en: I called the front desk this morning. The towels in our room weren't dry.
items.zh: 我今天早上打電話到櫃台。我們房間的毛巾不是乾的。

items.en: The broken window wasn't my fault. The ball hit it.
items.zh: 窗戶破了不是我的錯，是球打到的。

items.en: I got a seat by the window. The train wasn't crowded on Sunday.
items.zh: 我坐到了靠窗的位子。星期天的火車不擠。

items.en: Ask someone else about the fight. We weren't at the party last night.
items.zh: 打架的事去問別人吧。我們昨晚沒去派對。

items.en: It isn't cold today, so leave your coat at home.
items.zh: 今天不冷，所以外套留在家吧。

items.en: Swimming after a big meal isn't a good idea.
items.zh: 吃飽飯就去游泳不是個好主意。

items.en: My phone isn't new. It's three years old.
items.zh: 我的手機不是新的，已經用三年了。

items.en: He's not angry. He's just tired.
items.zh: 他沒生氣，他只是累了。

title: I haven't eaten Italian food for a long time.
translation: 我很久沒吃義大利菜了。
name: 助動詞 have 的否定直述句
sentences: I haven't driven a car since my accident.
We've visited Korea twice. We haven't been to Japan yet.
I haven't finished my homework, so I can't go out.
We asked the hotel about a late check-out. They haven't called us back.
Yes, let's order a pizza! I haven't had pizza for months.
I want to make an album for my parents. You haven't sent me the photos from the wedding.
My sister hasn't paid me back for the concert ticket.
He finished university in June. My brother hasn't found a job yet.
The garden is so dry. It hasn't rained since June.
I wrote to Ken about the trip on Monday. He hasn't answered my email.
We're waiting for Grandma to arrive. My son hasn't opened his presents yet.
Can you go to the shop? We haven't got any milk left for the tea.
We haven't got a garage, so we park on the street.
My girlfriend has three sisters. She hasn't got any brothers.
Sorry, my bus is here. I haven't got time to talk now.
I grow my tomatoes on the balcony. My flat hasn't got a garden.
My grandparents hadn't got a phone when I was a child.
We hadn't eaten all day, so we were very hungry.
My husband's family lives in Canada. I hadn't met his parents until the wedding.
Thanks for telling me about Grandpa. I hadn't heard the news when you called.
Many people stood at the meeting. The school hadn't got enough chairs for everyone.
I've worked late every night. I haven't been to the gym this week.
We've only been together for a month. My parents haven't met my new boyfriend.
No TV yet! The kids haven't cleaned their room.
My dad has two jobs now. He hasn't got much free time these days.
The party is tomorrow, and I haven't bought a present yet.
Ann moved to Berlin in the spring. We haven't heard from her since May.
The bus hasn't come, and we've waited for twenty minutes.
Tom left the party an hour ago. I haven't got a clue where he is.
We're taking him to the doctor. Grandpa hasn't felt like eating since Monday.

examples.heading: ① haven't + 過去分詞

items.en: I haven't driven a car since my accident.
items.zh: 我出車禍之後就沒開過車。

items.en: We've visited Korea twice. We haven't been to Japan yet.
items.zh: 我們去過韓國兩次。我們還沒去過日本。

items.en: I haven't finished my homework, so I can't go out.
items.zh: 我還沒寫完作業，所以不能出去。

items.en: We asked the hotel about a late check-out. They haven't called us back.
items.zh: 我們問飯店能不能晚一點退房。他們還沒回我們電話。

items.en: Yes, let's order a pizza! I haven't had pizza for months.
items.zh: 好啊，我們叫披薩吧！我好幾個月沒吃披薩了。

items.en: I want to make an album for my parents. You haven't sent me the photos from the wedding.
items.zh: 我想幫我爸媽做一本相簿。你還沒把婚禮的照片傳給我。

examples.heading: ② hasn't + 過去分詞

items.en: My sister hasn't paid me back for the concert ticket.
items.zh: 我姊姊還沒把演唱會的票錢還我。

items.en: He finished university in June. My brother hasn't found a job yet.
items.zh: 他六月大學畢業。我哥哥還沒找到工作。

items.en: The garden is so dry. It hasn't rained since June.
items.zh: 花園好乾，從六月到現在都沒下雨。

items.en: I wrote to Ken about the trip on Monday. He hasn't answered my email.
items.zh: 我星期一寫信跟 Ken 說旅行的事。他還沒回我的電子郵件。

items.en: We're waiting for Grandma to arrive. My son hasn't opened his presents yet.
items.zh: 我們在等奶奶到。我兒子還沒拆禮物。

examples.heading: ③ haven't got / hasn't got

items.en: Can you go to the shop? We haven't got any milk left for the tea.
items.zh: 你可以去一下商店嗎？我們沒有牛奶可以加在茶裡了。

items.en: We haven't got a garage, so we park on the street.
items.zh: 我們沒有車庫，所以把車停在街上。

items.en: My girlfriend has three sisters. She hasn't got any brothers.
items.zh: 我女朋友有三個姊妹。她沒有兄弟。

items.en: Sorry, my bus is here. I haven't got time to talk now.
items.zh: 抱歉，我的公車來了。我現在沒時間講話。

items.en: I grow my tomatoes on the balcony. My flat hasn't got a garden.
items.zh: 我在陽台種番茄。我的公寓沒有花園。

examples.heading: ④ hadn't + 過去分詞 / hadn't got

items.en: My grandparents hadn't got a phone when I was a child.
items.zh: 我小時候，我爺爺奶奶家沒有電話。

items.en: We hadn't eaten all day, so we were very hungry.
items.zh: 我們一整天沒吃東西，所以很餓。

items.en: My husband's family lives in Canada. I hadn't met his parents until the wedding.
items.zh: 我先生的家人住在加拿大。婚禮之前我沒見過他爸媽。

items.en: Thanks for telling me about Grandpa. I hadn't heard the news when you called.
items.zh: 謝謝你告訴我爺爺的事。你打來的時候，我還沒聽說那個消息。

items.en: Many people stood at the meeting. The school hadn't got enough chairs for everyone.
items.zh: 很多人站著開會。學校那時的椅子不夠大家坐。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的句型

items.en: I've worked late every night. I haven't been to the gym this week.
items.zh: 我每天晚上都加班。我這個禮拜沒去健身房。

items.en: We've only been together for a month. My parents haven't met my new boyfriend.
items.zh: 我們才在一起一個月。我爸媽還沒見過我的新男朋友。

items.en: No TV yet! The kids haven't cleaned their room.
items.zh: 還不能看電視！孩子們還沒打掃房間。

items.en: My dad has two jobs now. He hasn't got much free time these days.
items.zh: 我爸爸現在有兩份工作。他最近沒什麼空。

items.en: The party is tomorrow, and I haven't bought a present yet.
items.zh: 派對就在明天，我還沒買禮物。

items.en: Ann moved to Berlin in the spring. We haven't heard from her since May.
items.zh: Ann 春天搬去柏林。我們從五月以後就沒有她的消息了。

items.en: The bus hasn't come, and we've waited for twenty minutes.
items.zh: 公車還沒來，我們已經等了二十分鐘了。

items.en: Tom left the party an hour ago. I haven't got a clue where he is.
items.zh: 湯姆一個小時前離開派對。我完全不知道他在哪裡。

items.en: We're taking him to the doctor. Grandpa hasn't felt like eating since Monday.
items.zh: 我們要帶他去看醫生。爺爺從星期一起就沒胃口。

title: Don't you like pizza?
translation: 你不喜歡披薩嗎？
name: 否定疑問句
sentences: Don't you like spicy food? I made a mild curry too.
Don't you recognize me? I used to live next door.
Doesn't she speak French? She lived in Paris.
Everyone else is eating. Don't you want a slice of birthday cake?
All the stalls are closed tonight. Doesn't the night market open on Mondays?
Look at that blue sky. Isn't it a beautiful day?
Aren't you hungry? You haven't eaten all day.
Look at the man in the red cap. Isn't that your brother over there?
You're travelling alone across Africa. Aren't your parents worried about you?
We finally reached the top of the hill. Isn't the view amazing from here?
It's nearly midnight, and the kids are asleep on the sofa. Isn't it time to go home?
I passed my driving test. Didn't I tell you?
The guard came to my car window. Didn't you see the "No Parking" sign by the gate?
The receptionist can't find your booking. Didn't the hotel send you a confirmation email?
Your face looks familiar. Didn't we sit next to each other on the flight to Tokyo?
Why are you studying on Friday night? Didn't the teacher say the test was on Monday?
It's two in the morning. Can't you get to sleep?
Haven't you packed your suitcase yet? We leave at six.
I've made a big pot of soup. Won't you stay for dinner?
I'm trying to study. Can't you turn the music down a bit?
I remember that fountain. Haven't we been here before?
A: Didn't you get my message? B: No, I didn't. My phone was off.
A: Aren't you cold? B: No, I'm fine.
We walked out of the cinema smiling. Wasn't the film great?
I think I saw you in the crowd on Saturday. Weren't you at the concert too?
It's ten o'clock on a Monday. Shouldn't you be at work?
You're an hour late. Couldn't you find a parking space?
Taste it, Mum. Doesn't this soup need more salt?
I saw a cake in the shop and thought of you. Isn't your birthday next week?
He came on Monday and Tuesday. Hasn't the plumber fixed the shower yet?

examples.heading: ① Don't / Doesn't + 主詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: Don't you like spicy food? I made a mild curry too.
items.zh: 你不喜歡吃辣嗎？我也煮了不辣的咖哩。

items.en: Don't you recognize me? I used to live next door.
items.zh: 你認不出我嗎？我以前住你隔壁。

items.en: Doesn't she speak French? She lived in Paris.
items.zh: 她不會說法文嗎？她在巴黎住過。

items.en: Everyone else is eating. Don't you want a slice of birthday cake?
items.zh: 其他人都在吃。你不想吃一片生日蛋糕嗎？

items.en: All the stalls are closed tonight. Doesn't the night market open on Mondays?
items.zh: 今晚所有的攤子都沒開。夜市星期一不開嗎？

examples.heading: ② Isn't / Aren't + 主詞 ...

items.en: Look at that blue sky. Isn't it a beautiful day?
items.zh: 你看那片藍天。今天天氣不是很好嗎？

items.en: Aren't you hungry? You haven't eaten all day.
items.zh: 你不餓嗎？你一整天都沒吃東西。

items.en: Look at the man in the red cap. Isn't that your brother over there?
items.zh: 你看那個戴紅帽子的男人。那邊那個不是你哥哥嗎？

items.en: You're travelling alone across Africa. Aren't your parents worried about you?
items.zh: 你一個人在非洲旅行。你爸媽不擔心你嗎？

items.en: We finally reached the top of the hill. Isn't the view amazing from here?
items.zh: 我們終於到了山頂。從這裡看出去的景色不是很棒嗎？

items.en: It's nearly midnight, and the kids are asleep on the sofa. Isn't it time to go home?
items.zh: 快半夜了，孩子們都在沙發上睡著了。不是該回家了嗎？

examples.heading: ③ Didn't + 主詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: I passed my driving test. Didn't I tell you?
items.zh: 我考過駕照了，我沒跟你說嗎？

items.en: The guard came to my car window. Didn't you see the "No Parking" sign by the gate?
items.zh: 警衛走到我的車窗旁邊。你沒看到大門旁邊禁止停車的牌子嗎？

items.en: The receptionist can't find your booking. Didn't the hotel send you a confirmation email?
items.zh: 櫃台人員找不到你的訂房。飯店沒寄確認信給你嗎？

items.en: Your face looks familiar. Didn't we sit next to each other on the flight to Tokyo?
items.zh: 你看起來很面熟。我們不是在飛東京的班機上坐隔壁嗎？

items.en: Why are you studying on Friday night? Didn't the teacher say the test was on Monday?
items.zh: 你為什麼星期五晚上在讀書？老師不是說考試在星期一嗎？

examples.heading: ④ Can't / Haven't / Won't + 主詞 ...

items.en: It's two in the morning. Can't you get to sleep?
items.zh: 已經凌晨兩點了，你睡不著嗎？

items.en: Haven't you packed your suitcase yet? We leave at six.
items.zh: 你還沒打包行李嗎？我們六點就要出發了。

items.en: I've made a big pot of soup. Won't you stay for dinner?
items.zh: 我煮了一大鍋湯。你不留下來吃晚餐嗎？

items.en: I'm trying to study. Can't you turn the music down a bit?
items.zh: 我在讀書。你不能把音樂關小聲一點嗎？

items.en: I remember that fountain. Haven't we been here before?
items.zh: 我記得那座噴泉。我們以前不是來過這裡嗎？

examples.heading: ⑤ 回答和不同的句型

items.en: A: Didn't you get my message? B: No, I didn't. My phone was off.
items.zh: A：你沒收到我的訊息嗎？B：沒有，我的手機關機了。

items.en: A: Aren't you cold? B: No, I'm fine.
items.zh: A：你不冷嗎？B：不冷，我還好。

items.en: We walked out of the cinema smiling. Wasn't the film great?
items.zh: 我們笑著走出電影院。那部電影不是很好看嗎？

items.en: I think I saw you in the crowd on Saturday. Weren't you at the concert too?
items.zh: 我好像星期六在人群裡看到你。你不是也有去演唱會嗎？

items.en: It's ten o'clock on a Monday. Shouldn't you be at work?
items.zh: 今天星期一，現在十點。你不是應該在上班嗎？

items.en: You're an hour late. Couldn't you find a parking space?
items.zh: 你晚了一個小時。你找不到停車位嗎？

items.en: Taste it, Mum. Doesn't this soup need more salt?
items.zh: 媽，你嚐嚐。這湯不用再加點鹽嗎？

items.en: I saw a cake in the shop and thought of you. Isn't your birthday next week?
items.zh: 我在店裡看到一個蛋糕就想到你。你的生日不是下禮拜嗎？

items.en: He came on Monday and Tuesday. Hasn't the plumber fixed the shower yet?
items.zh: 他星期一和星期二都來了。水電工還沒修好淋浴間嗎？

title: Why don't you ever listen to me?
translation: 你為什麼從來都不聽我說話？
name: 否定疑問句中的副詞位置
sentences: Someone could walk in at night. Why don't you ever lock the back door?
She asks about you every week. Why don't you ever call your grandmother?
My brother eats and goes straight to his room. Why doesn't he ever help with the dishes?
I've called the hotel five times today. Why don't they ever answer the phone?
It's been in your wardrobe for a year. Why don't you ever wear that dress?
I've waited twenty minutes again. Why doesn't the bus ever come on time?
She's on the radio every day. Haven't you ever heard of this singer?
You look nervous at the gate. Haven't you ever been on a plane?
My friend from Spain is coming to dinner. Hasn't she ever tried sushi?
You've lived in this town all your life. Haven't you ever wanted to live abroad?
The kids from Singapore are running around in the garden. Haven't they ever seen snow?
You're surprised by the price of the flat? Hasn't rent always been expensive in the city?
Why is everyone talking about the new factory? Hasn't this town always been quiet?
Why are you going to the supermarket? Don't you always buy your bread at the corner bakery?
Let's eat at your place this weekend. Doesn't your father always cook on Sundays?
Of course you can stay with us. Haven't our families always been close?
You want to buy a sofa? Don't you still live with your parents?
Ask Lisa about the medicine. Doesn't she still work at the hospital?
You're going out without an umbrella? Isn't it still raining?
You're laughing with Tom again. Aren't you still angry with him?
Your parents need to get to the airport. Don't they still have that old car?
You're free on Friday evening? Don't you usually go swimming on Fridays?
You're walking to work today. Don't you normally take the bus?
You broke her cup. Can't you just say sorry?
We missed the start of the film again. Why can't you ever be on time?
You left the party at nine. Why didn't you even say goodbye?
The wedding is in a month. Haven't you already sent the invitations?
You live alone on that farm. Don't you sometimes feel lonely?
We stay home every Saturday night. Why don't we ever go out anymore?
Pack your boots for the trip. Doesn't it often snow there in January?

examples.heading: ① Why don't you ever ...?

items.en: Someone could walk in at night. Why don't you ever lock the back door?
items.zh: 晚上可能會有人走進來。你為什麼從來都不鎖後門？

items.en: She asks about you every week. Why don't you ever call your grandmother?
items.zh: 她每個星期都問起你。你為什麼從來都不打給你奶奶？

items.en: My brother eats and goes straight to his room. Why doesn't he ever help with the dishes?
items.zh: 我哥哥吃完就直接回房間。他為什麼從來都不幫忙洗碗？

items.en: I've called the hotel five times today. Why don't they ever answer the phone?
items.zh: 我今天打給飯店五次了。他們為什麼從來都不接電話？

items.en: It's been in your wardrobe for a year. Why don't you ever wear that dress?
items.zh: 它在你的衣櫃裡掛了一年。你為什麼從來都不穿那件洋裝？

items.en: I've waited twenty minutes again. Why doesn't the bus ever come on time?
items.zh: 我又等了二十分鐘。公車為什麼從來都不準時？

examples.heading: ② Haven't you ever ...?

items.en: She's on the radio every day. Haven't you ever heard of this singer?
items.zh: 她每天都在廣播上。你從沒聽過這個歌手嗎？

items.en: You look nervous at the gate. Haven't you ever been on a plane?
items.zh: 你在登機門看起來很緊張。你從沒搭過飛機嗎？

items.en: My friend from Spain is coming to dinner. Hasn't she ever tried sushi?
items.zh: 我西班牙的朋友要來吃晚餐。她從沒吃過壽司嗎？

items.en: You've lived in this town all your life. Haven't you ever wanted to live abroad?
items.zh: 你一輩子都住在這個鎮上。你從沒想過要住在國外嗎？

items.en: The kids from Singapore are running around in the garden. Haven't they ever seen snow?
items.zh: 從新加坡來的孩子們在花園裡跑來跑去。他們從沒看過雪嗎？

examples.heading: ③ Hasn't it always ...? / Don't you always ...?

items.en: You're surprised by the price of the flat? Hasn't rent always been expensive in the city?
items.zh: 你對那間公寓的價錢很驚訝？城市的房租不是一直都很貴嗎？

items.en: Why is everyone talking about the new factory? Hasn't this town always been quiet?
items.zh: 為什麼大家都在談新工廠的事？這個小鎮不是一直都很安靜嗎？

items.en: Why are you going to the supermarket? Don't you always buy your bread at the corner bakery?
items.zh: 你為什麼要去超市？你不是都在轉角那家麵包店買麵包嗎？

items.en: Let's eat at your place this weekend. Doesn't your father always cook on Sundays?
items.zh: 這個週末我們去你家吃吧。你爸爸不是每個星期天都會下廚嗎？

items.en: Of course you can stay with us. Haven't our families always been close?
items.zh: 你當然可以住我們家。我們兩家不是一直都很親近嗎？

examples.heading: ④ Don't you still ...? / Isn't it still ...?

items.en: You want to buy a sofa? Don't you still live with your parents?
items.zh: 你想買沙發？你不是還跟你爸媽住嗎？

items.en: Ask Lisa about the medicine. Doesn't she still work at the hospital?
items.zh: 藥的事問麗莎吧。她不是還在醫院上班嗎？

items.en: You're going out without an umbrella? Isn't it still raining?
items.zh: 你不帶傘就要出門？不是還在下雨嗎？

items.en: You're laughing with Tom again. Aren't you still angry with him?
items.zh: 你又跟湯姆有說有笑了。你不是還在生他的氣嗎？

items.en: Your parents need to get to the airport. Don't they still have that old car?
items.zh: 你爸媽要去機場。他們不是還有那輛舊車嗎？

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的副詞和句型

items.en: You're free on Friday evening? Don't you usually go swimming on Fridays?
items.zh: 你星期五晚上有空？你星期五不是通常會去游泳嗎？

items.en: You're walking to work today. Don't you normally take the bus?
items.zh: 你今天走路上班。你不是通常搭公車嗎？

items.en: You broke her cup. Can't you just say sorry?
items.zh: 你打破了她的杯子。你就不能說聲對不起嗎？

items.en: We missed the start of the film again. Why can't you ever be on time?
items.zh: 我們又錯過了電影開頭。你為什麼從來都不能準時？

items.en: You left the party at nine. Why didn't you even say goodbye?
items.zh: 你九點就離開派對。你為什麼連再見都沒說？

items.en: The wedding is in a month. Haven't you already sent the invitations?
items.zh: 婚禮再一個月就到了。你不是已經寄出邀請函了嗎？

items.en: You live alone on that farm. Don't you sometimes feel lonely?
items.zh: 你一個人住在那個農場。你有時候不會覺得孤單嗎？

items.en: We stay home every Saturday night. Why don't we ever go out anymore?
items.zh: 我們每個星期六晚上都待在家。我們為什麼都不再出去了？

items.en: Pack your boots for the trip. Doesn't it often snow there in January?
items.zh: 旅行帶上你的靴子。那裡一月不是常下雪嗎？

title: Why didn't you come with me?
translation: 你為什麼沒跟我一起去？
name: 否定 wh- 疑問句
sentences: We waited for you at the station on Sunday. Why didn't you come to the beach with us?
The report is due tomorrow, and now you tell me? Why didn't you mention the problem earlier?
I sent her a long message on Monday. Why didn't your sister reply to it?
Everyone from our class was there except Ken. Why didn't they invite him to the party?
You're soaking wet! Why didn't you wait for the rain to stop?
We pressed the button, but the bus went past. Why didn't the driver let us off?
You're always hungry by ten. Why don't you eat breakfast in the morning?
He takes two buses to work every day. Why doesn't your brother drive?
The zoo trip is tomorrow. Why don't the kids want to go?
I changed the bulb this morning. Why doesn't this light work?
I've written to you five times this month. Why don't you ever answer my emails?
It's a sunny afternoon. Why don't we rent bikes and ride around the lake?
He has a big van. Why don't you ask your cousin to help you move?
Why don't we eat outside? It's a lovely day.
You look exhausted. Why don't you take a day off?
The office is too noisy to talk. Why don't we meet at the café instead?
Why couldn't you come on Saturday? We missed you.
All my friends are going, Mum. Why can't I go to the party?
I filled it with petrol yesterday. Why won't the car start?
I rang three times. Why can't Grandpa hear the doorbell?
We told Tom the ice was thin. Why wouldn't he listen to us?
I count only twenty-eight books on my desk. Who didn't hand in their homework?
You gave it only two stars. What didn't you like about the hotel?
You ran out of time in the test. Which questions didn't you answer?
The teacher called about Lucy. Why isn't she at school today?
It's freezing outside. Why aren't you wearing a coat?
They sent it two weeks ago. Why hasn't the parcel arrived yet?
We got a red letter today. Why haven't you paid the electricity bill yet?
We drove there at ten on a Tuesday. Why wasn't the shop open?
The boss asked about you this morning. Why weren't you at the meeting?

examples.heading: ① Why didn't + 主詞 + 原形動詞（問原因）

items.en: We waited for you at the station on Sunday. Why didn't you come to the beach with us?
items.zh: 我們星期天在車站等你。你為什麼沒跟我們一起去海邊？

items.en: The report is due tomorrow, and now you tell me? Why didn't you mention the problem earlier?
items.zh: 報告明天就要交，你現在才跟我說？你為什麼沒早點提這個問題？

items.en: I sent her a long message on Monday. Why didn't your sister reply to it?
items.zh: 我星期一傳了一則很長的訊息給她。你姊姊為什麼沒回？

items.en: Everyone from our class was there except Ken. Why didn't they invite him to the party?
items.zh: 我們班除了 Ken 每個人都在。他們為什麼沒邀請他來派對？

items.en: You're soaking wet! Why didn't you wait for the rain to stop?
items.zh: 你全身都濕透了！你為什麼沒等雨停？

items.en: We pressed the button, but the bus went past. Why didn't the driver let us off?
items.zh: 我們按了鈴，可是公車開過去了。司機為什麼沒讓我們下車？

examples.heading: ② Why don't / doesn't + 主詞 + 原形動詞（問原因）

items.en: You're always hungry by ten. Why don't you eat breakfast in the morning?
items.zh: 你總是十點就餓了。你早上為什麼不吃早餐？

items.en: He takes two buses to work every day. Why doesn't your brother drive?
items.zh: 他每天搭兩班公車上班。你哥哥為什麼不開車？

items.en: The zoo trip is tomorrow. Why don't the kids want to go?
items.zh: 去動物園是明天。孩子們為什麼不想去？

items.en: I changed the bulb this morning. Why doesn't this light work?
items.zh: 我今天早上換了燈泡。這盞燈為什麼不亮？

items.en: I've written to you five times this month. Why don't you ever answer my emails?
items.zh: 我這個月寫了五次信給你。你為什麼從來都不回我的電子郵件？

examples.heading: ③ Why don't we / you ...?（建議）

items.en: It's a sunny afternoon. Why don't we rent bikes and ride around the lake?
items.zh: 今天下午天氣很好。我們何不租腳踏車環湖騎一圈？

items.en: He has a big van. Why don't you ask your cousin to help you move?
items.zh: 他有一台大廂型車。你何不找你表哥幫你搬家？

items.en: Why don't we eat outside? It's a lovely day.
items.zh: 我們何不在外面吃？天氣很好。

items.en: You look exhausted. Why don't you take a day off?
items.zh: 你看起來累壞了。你何不請一天假？

items.en: The office is too noisy to talk. Why don't we meet at the café instead?
items.zh: 辦公室太吵了，不好談。我們何不改在咖啡店見面？

examples.heading: ④ Why can't / couldn't / won't + 主詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: Why couldn't you come on Saturday? We missed you.
items.zh: 你星期六為什麼不能來？我們很想你。

items.en: All my friends are going, Mum. Why can't I go to the party?
items.zh: 媽，我所有的朋友都要去。我為什麼不能去派對？

items.en: I filled it with petrol yesterday. Why won't the car start?
items.zh: 我昨天才加滿油。車子為什麼發不動？

items.en: I rang three times. Why can't Grandpa hear the doorbell?
items.zh: 我按了三次。爺爺為什麼聽不到門鈴？

items.en: We told Tom the ice was thin. Why wouldn't he listen to us?
items.zh: 我們跟湯姆說冰很薄。他為什麼就是不聽我們的？

examples.heading: ⑤ Who / What / Which + 否定 和不同的句型

items.en: I count only twenty-eight books on my desk. Who didn't hand in their homework?
items.zh: 我桌上只有二十八本。誰沒交作業？

items.en: You gave it only two stars. What didn't you like about the hotel?
items.zh: 你只給了兩顆星。那家飯店你哪裡不喜歡？

items.en: You ran out of time in the test. Which questions didn't you answer?
items.zh: 你考試時間不夠。你哪幾題沒回答？

items.en: The teacher called about Lucy. Why isn't she at school today?
items.zh: 老師打電話來問露西的事。她今天為什麼沒去上學？

items.en: It's freezing outside. Why aren't you wearing a coat?
items.zh: 外面冷死了。你為什麼沒穿外套？

items.en: They sent it two weeks ago. Why hasn't the parcel arrived yet?
items.zh: 他們兩個星期前就寄了。包裹為什麼還沒到？

items.en: We got a red letter today. Why haven't you paid the electricity bill yet?
items.zh: 我們今天收到一封催繳信。你為什麼還沒繳電費？

items.en: We drove there at ten on a Tuesday. Why wasn't the shop open?
items.zh: 我們星期二十點開車去。那家店為什麼沒開？

items.en: The boss asked about you this morning. Why weren't you at the meeting?
items.zh: 老闆今天早上問起你。你為什麼沒來開會？

title: Thanks for your letter, which I received a few days ago.
translation: 謝謝你的來信，我幾天前收到了。
name: which 當受詞的非限定關係子句
sentences: I'm still reading your email, which I got this morning.
We had dinner at the new Thai place, which Jenny found online.
He finally returned my umbrella, which he borrowed in March.
I've lost my blue scarf, which my aunt knitted for me.
They live in a tiny flat, which they rent from a friend.
Try some of this jam, which my neighbor makes every summer.
The blue sofa, which we bought last year, is already falling apart.
My first car, which I drove for ten years, was a tiny red Fiat.
The photos, which Tom took at the wedding, came out really well.
Her speech, which she wrote the night before, made everyone cry.
This recipe, which I found in an old cookbook, is really easy.
The old piano, which nobody plays anymore, takes up half the room.
The report, which the manager asked for on Monday, still isn't ready.
The hotel, which we had paid for in advance, was closed when we arrived.
We're watching that new series, which everyone at work keeps talking about.
I finally found my passport, which I'd been looking for all week.
She didn't get the job, which she had applied for twice.
You can borrow my bike, which I hardly ever use.
She's wearing the necklace, which her husband gave her for their anniversary.
We'll take the early train, which my boss has already booked for us.
I'm sending you the file, which you needed for the meeting.
I gave her my old guitar, which I never play anymore.
He's selling his motorbike, which he's owned since college.
We sold the house in Taichung, which we couldn't afford anymore.
I specified the size in my order, which the shop ignored completely.
My thrifty brother still uses the phone, which our parents gave him ten years ago.
The quilt on my bed, which my great-grandmother sewed, is over eighty years old.
My grandfather's watch, which I take everywhere with me, stopped yesterday.
The cake, which Lucy baked for the party, disappeared in ten minutes.
Here's your wallet, which you left in my car last night.

examples.heading: ① 子句在句尾

items.en: I'm still reading your email, which I got this morning.
items.zh: 我還在看你的電子郵件，那是我今天早上收到的。

items.en: We had dinner at the new Thai place, which Jenny found online.
items.zh: 我們在那家新開的泰國餐廳吃晚餐，那是 Jenny 在網路上找到的。

items.en: He finally returned my umbrella, which he borrowed in March.
items.zh: 他終於還我傘了，那是他三月借走的。

items.en: I've lost my blue scarf, which my aunt knitted for me.
items.zh: 我弄丟了我的藍色圍巾，那是我阿姨幫我織的。

items.en: They live in a tiny flat, which they rent from a friend.
items.zh: 他們住在一間很小的公寓，那是跟朋友租的。

items.en: Try some of this jam, which my neighbor makes every summer.
items.zh: 吃點這個果醬，那是我鄰居每年夏天做的。

examples.heading: ② 子句在句子中間

items.en: The blue sofa, which we bought last year, is already falling apart.
items.zh: 那張藍色沙發是我們去年買的，已經快壞了。

items.en: My first car, which I drove for ten years, was a tiny red Fiat.
items.zh: 我的第一輛車開了十年，是一輛紅色的小 Fiat。

items.en: The photos, which Tom took at the wedding, came out really well.
items.zh: 那些照片是 Tom 在婚禮上拍的，拍得很好。

items.en: Her speech, which she wrote the night before, made everyone cry.
items.zh: 她的演講稿是前一晚寫的，讓大家都哭了。

items.en: This recipe, which I found in an old cookbook, is really easy.
items.zh: 這個食譜是我在一本舊食譜書裡找到的，很簡單。

items.en: The old piano, which nobody plays anymore, takes up half the room.
items.zh: 那台舊鋼琴已經沒人彈了，佔了半個房間。

examples.heading: ③ 子句動詞後面接介系詞

items.en: The report, which the manager asked for on Monday, still isn't ready.
items.zh: 那份報告是經理星期一要的，到現在還沒好。

items.en: The hotel, which we had paid for in advance, was closed when we arrived.
items.zh: 那家飯店我們已經先付了錢，結果我們到的時候它關門了。

items.en: We're watching that new series, which everyone at work keeps talking about.
items.zh: 我們在看那部新影集，公司裡大家一直在討論。

items.en: I finally found my passport, which I'd been looking for all week.
items.zh: 我終於找到我的護照了，我找了一整個星期。

items.en: She didn't get the job, which she had applied for twice.
items.zh: 她沒得到那份工作，那份工作她申請過兩次。

examples.heading: ④ 不同的時態和人稱

items.en: You can borrow my bike, which I hardly ever use.
items.zh: 你可以借我的腳踏車，我幾乎不騎。

items.en: She's wearing the necklace, which her husband gave her for their anniversary.
items.zh: 她戴著那條項鍊，那是她先生在結婚紀念日送她的。

items.en: We'll take the early train, which my boss has already booked for us.
items.zh: 我們會搭早班火車，我老闆已經幫我們訂好了。

items.en: I'm sending you the file, which you needed for the meeting.
items.zh: 我把檔案寄給你，那是你開會要用的。

items.en: I gave her my old guitar, which I never play anymore.
items.zh: 我把我的舊吉他給了她，我已經不彈了。

items.en: He's selling his motorbike, which he's owned since college.
items.zh: 他要賣掉他的機車，那台車他從大學就有了。

examples.heading: ⑤ 更多的情境

items.en: We sold the house in Taichung, which we couldn't afford anymore.
items.zh: 我們把台中的房子賣了，我們已經負擔不起了。

items.en: I specified the size in my order, which the shop ignored completely.
items.zh: 我在訂單裡寫明了尺寸，店家卻完全沒理會。

items.en: My thrifty brother still uses the phone, which our parents gave him ten years ago.
items.zh: 我那個節儉的哥哥還在用那支手機，那是爸媽十年前送他的。

items.en: The quilt on my bed, which my great-grandmother sewed, is over eighty years old.
items.zh: 我床上的被子是我曾祖母縫的，已經八十多年了。

items.en: My grandfather's watch, which I take everywhere with me, stopped yesterday.
items.zh: 我爺爺的錶我到哪裡都帶著，昨天停了。

items.en: The cake, which Lucy baked for the party, disappeared in ten minutes.
items.zh: 那個蛋糕是 Lucy 為派對烤的，十分鐘就被吃光了。

items.en: Here's your wallet, which you left in my car last night.
items.zh: 這是你的皮夾，你昨晚把它留在我車上。

title: It was my old classmate Tom, who I hadn't seen for ages!
translation: 原來是我的老同學 Tom，我好久沒見到他了！
name: who 當受詞的非限定關係子句
sentences: At the station I saw Lucy, who I hadn't met since high school.
We stayed with my aunt, who we visit every summer.
I've just had an email from Kevin, who I worked with in Tokyo.
Last night I phoned my grandfather, who I don't call often enough.
She's bringing her boyfriend, who none of us have met yet.
They hired Ms. Huang, who the manager had recommended.
Our neighbor, who we hardly ever see, left a cake at our door.
My piano teacher, who I adored as a child, still lives in the same house.
The new coach, who the players really respect, has changed everything.
Ana, who I share a flat with, is learning Chinese.
Mr. Kuo, who we all called "the Professor," retired last month.
My older brother, who I always argued with, is now my best friend.
I ran into Peter, who I used to go to school with.
We had dinner with the Changs, who we stayed with in Kaohsiung.
That's Rosa, who I sat next to at the conference.
Our host, who we'd heard so much about, met us at the airport.
The nurse, who I spoke to on the phone, was really helpful.
The author, whom we invited to speak, sent a short reply.
Dr. Ho, whom the hospital appointed in May, starts on Monday.
The applicants, whom we interviewed yesterday, will hear from us by Friday.
Mr. Lai, whom I contacted last week, has not replied.
Have you met Joe, who my sister is going to marry?
I'm going to visit Mrs. Tsai, who I'll miss a lot when she moves.
We're inviting Ben, who everyone likes.
My little sister, who I'm babysitting tonight, refuses to go to bed.
My best friend, who I've known for twenty years, has always been there for me.
The zealous young reporter, who the mayor had refused to see, waited outside all day.
Our old landlord, who we never really liked, is selling the building.
I finally reconciled with my father, who I hadn't spoken to in two years.
Tell Ken, who you'll see before me, that the meeting is cancelled.

examples.heading: ① 子句在句尾

items.en: At the station I saw Lucy, who I hadn't met since high school.
items.zh: 我在車站看到 Lucy，我高中以後就沒見過她了。

items.en: We stayed with my aunt, who we visit every summer.
items.zh: 我們住在我阿姨家，我們每年夏天都會去看她。

items.en: I've just had an email from Kevin, who I worked with in Tokyo.
items.zh: 我剛收到 Kevin 的電子郵件，我在東京的時候跟他一起工作。

items.en: Last night I phoned my grandfather, who I don't call often enough.
items.zh: 我昨晚打電話給我爺爺，我太少打給他了。

items.en: She's bringing her boyfriend, who none of us have met yet.
items.zh: 她要帶她男朋友來，我們都還沒見過他。

items.en: They hired Ms. Huang, who the manager had recommended.
items.zh: 他們雇用了黃小姐，她是經理推薦的。

examples.heading: ② 子句在句子中間

items.en: Our neighbor, who we hardly ever see, left a cake at our door.
items.zh: 我們很少見到的鄰居在我們門口放了一個蛋糕。

items.en: My piano teacher, who I adored as a child, still lives in the same house.
items.zh: 我小時候很喜歡的鋼琴老師還住在同一棟房子裡。

items.en: The new coach, who the players really respect, has changed everything.
items.zh: 新教練很受球員尊敬，他改變了一切。

items.en: Ana, who I share a flat with, is learning Chinese.
items.zh: Ana 在學中文，我跟她合租一間公寓。

items.en: Mr. Kuo, who we all called "the Professor," retired last month.
items.zh: 郭先生上個月退休了，我們都叫他教授。

items.en: My older brother, who I always argued with, is now my best friend.
items.zh: 我以前老是跟我哥哥吵架，現在他是我最好的朋友。

examples.heading: ③ 子句動詞後面接介系詞

items.en: I ran into Peter, who I used to go to school with.
items.zh: 我遇到 Peter，我以前跟他同校。

items.en: We had dinner with the Changs, who we stayed with in Kaohsiung.
items.zh: 我們跟張家吃了晚餐，我們在高雄的時候住在他們家。

items.en: That's Rosa, who I sat next to at the conference.
items.zh: 那就是 Rosa，我在研討會上坐在她旁邊。

items.en: Our host, who we'd heard so much about, met us at the airport.
items.zh: 我們的房東到機場接我們，我們聽說過他很多事。

items.en: The nurse, who I spoke to on the phone, was really helpful.
items.zh: 那個護理師真的幫了很大的忙，我在電話上跟她說過話。

examples.heading: ④ whom（正式）

items.en: The author, whom we invited to speak, sent a short reply.
items.zh: 那位作者寄來了簡短的回覆，我們邀請過他來演講。

items.en: Dr. Ho, whom the hospital appointed in May, starts on Monday.
items.zh: 何醫師星期一開始上班，醫院是五月聘她的。

items.en: The applicants, whom we interviewed yesterday, will hear from us by Friday.
items.zh: 我們昨天面試的應徵者星期五之前會收到我們的通知。

items.en: Mr. Lai, whom I contacted last week, has not replied.
items.zh: 賴先生還沒回覆，我上禮拜聯絡過他。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的時態和情境

items.en: Have you met Joe, who my sister is going to marry?
items.zh: 你見過 Joe 嗎？我姊姊要嫁給他。

items.en: I'm going to visit Mrs. Tsai, who I'll miss a lot when she moves.
items.zh: 我要去看蔡太太，她搬走以後我會很想她。

items.en: We're inviting Ben, who everyone likes.
items.zh: 我們要邀請 Ben，大家都喜歡他。

items.en: My little sister, who I'm babysitting tonight, refuses to go to bed.
items.zh: 我今晚幫忙照顧的妹妹不肯上床睡覺。

items.en: My best friend, who I've known for twenty years, has always been there for me.
items.zh: 我最好的朋友一直都在我身邊，我認識他二十年了。

items.en: The zealous young reporter, who the mayor had refused to see, waited outside all day.
items.zh: 那個熱血的年輕記者在外面等了一整天，市長拒絕見他。

items.en: Our old landlord, who we never really liked, is selling the building.
items.zh: 我們的舊房東要把大樓賣掉了，我們一直都不太喜歡他。

items.en: I finally reconciled with my father, who I hadn't spoken to in two years.
items.zh: 我終於跟我爸爸和好了，我兩年沒跟他說話了。

items.en: Tell Ken, who you'll see before me, that the meeting is cancelled.
items.zh: 你會比我先見到 Ken，跟他說會議取消了。

title: I've been to Cardiff, which is the capital city of Wales.
translation: 我去過卡地夫，那是威爾斯的首都。
name: which 當主詞的非限定關係子句

I got it at the corner shop, which is open until midnight.
We stayed at the Grand Hotel, which is near the station.
I live in Tainan, which is in the south of Taiwan.
We visited the old castle, which stands on a hill.
They had lunch at Ann's café, which opens at eleven.
I bought three T-shirts, which were on sale.
My new phone, which was a gift, takes great photos.
We watched the cooking show, which was on at nine.
She gave me a book, which made me cry.
Our car, which is ten years old, still runs well.
The museum, which opened last year, is free on Sundays.
My bike, which has a basket, is in the garage.
The festival, which happens every May, brings many tourists.
The bridge, which is very old, is closed to cars.
Our school, which has 2,000 students, is the biggest in town.
My flat is on the top floor, which gives me a great view.
He didn't call me, which was strange.
It rained all week, which made us sad.
She passed the exam, which surprised everyone.
The train was late, which meant we missed the show.
We tried a café and a bakery, which were both excellent.
I'll take the 8:15 train, which gets in at ten.
The soup, which had too much salt, went in the bin.
My old laptop, which still works, is now my son's.
The test, which lasted three hours, was very hard.
We went to the night market, which was very crowded.
I lost my umbrella, which was a present from my aunt.

The new park, which has a lake, is great for kids.

examples.heading: ① 地方, + which ...

items.en: We spent a week in Hualien, which is on the east coast.
items.zh: 我們在花蓮待了一個禮拜，花蓮在東海岸。

items.en: I got it at the corner shop, which is open until midnight.
items.zh: 我在轉角那家店買的，那家店開到半夜。

items.en: We stayed at the Grand Hotel, which is near the station.
items.zh: 我們住在 Grand Hotel，那家飯店在車站附近。

items.en: I live in Tainan, which is in the south of Taiwan.
items.zh: 我住在台南，台南在台灣南部。

items.en: We visited the old castle, which stands on a hill.
items.zh: 我們參觀了那座老城堡，它在一座山丘上。

items.en: They had lunch at Ann's café, which opens at eleven.
items.zh: 他們在 Ann 的咖啡店吃午餐，那家店十一點開門。

examples.heading: ② 東西, + which ...

items.en: I bought three T-shirts, which were on sale.
items.zh: 我買了三件 T 恤，都在特價。

items.en: My new phone, which was a gift, takes great photos.
items.zh: 我的新手機是別人送的，拍照很好看。

items.en: We watched the cooking show, which was on at nine.
items.zh: 我們看了那個烹飪節目，節目九點播。

items.en: She gave me a book, which made me cry.
items.zh: 她送我一本書，那本書讓我哭了。

items.en: Our car, which is ten years old, still runs well.
items.zh: 我們的車已經十年了，還是很好開。

examples.heading: ③ which 在句子中間

items.en: The museum, which opened last year, is free on Sundays.
items.zh: 那間博物館去年開幕，星期天免費。

items.en: My bike, which has a basket, is in the garage.
items.zh: 我的腳踏車有籃子，放在車庫裡。

items.en: The festival, which happens every May, brings many tourists.
items.zh: 那個節慶每年五月舉辦，吸引很多觀光客。

items.en: The bridge, which is very old, is closed to cars.
items.zh: 那座橋很老，禁止汽車通行。

items.en: Our school, which has 2,000 students, is the biggest in town.
items.zh: 我們學校有兩千名學生，是鎮上最大的學校。

examples.heading: ④ which 指前面整件事

items.en: My flat is on the top floor, which gives me a great view.
items.zh: 我的公寓在頂樓，讓我有很棒的視野。

items.en: He didn't call me, which was strange.
items.zh: 他沒打給我，這很奇怪。

items.en: It rained all week, which made us sad.
items.zh: 整個禮拜都在下雨，讓我們很難過。

items.en: She passed the exam, which surprised everyone.
items.zh: 她考試及格了，讓大家都很驚訝。

items.en: The train was late, which meant we missed the show.
items.zh: 火車誤點了，所以我們錯過了表演。

examples.heading: ⑤ 不同的時態和句型

items.en: We tried a café and a bakery, which were both excellent.
items.zh: 我們去了一家咖啡店和一家麵包店，兩家都很棒。

items.en: I'll take the 8:15 train, which gets in at ten.
items.zh: 我會搭八點十五分的火車，十點到。

items.en: The soup, which had too much salt, went in the bin.
items.zh: 那碗湯太鹹了，倒進垃圾桶。

items.en: My old laptop, which still works, is now my son's.
items.zh: 我的舊筆電還能用，現在給我兒子用了。

items.en: The test, which lasted three hours, was very hard.
items.zh: 考試考了三個小時，非常難。

items.en: We went to the night market, which was very crowded.
items.zh: 我們去了夜市，人非常多。

items.en: I lost my umbrella, which was a present from my aunt.
items.zh: 我弄丟了我的傘，那是我阿姨送的禮物。

items.en: The concert, which starts at eight, will finish late.
items.zh: 演唱會八點開始，會很晚結束。

items.en: The new park, which has a lake, is great for kids.
items.zh: 新的公園有一座湖，很適合小孩。

title: I went to the game with my brother, who is also interested in sports.
translation: 我跟我哥哥去看比賽，他也對運動很有興趣。
name: who 當主詞的非限定關係子句
sentences: I'm going to the concert with Mia, who loves this band.
We visited Ann, who lives near the beach.
Ken, who works at the bank, helped me with the form.
I asked Mr. Lin, who teaches math at our school.
Lucy, who speaks three languages, works as a tour guide.
I went hiking with my cousin, who knows the mountains well.
My parents, who are on holiday in Bali, sent us a postcard.
This is my aunt, who lives in Tainan.
My grandmother, who is ninety, still walks every day.
I stayed with my uncle, who has a farm in the south.
My sister, who studies law, wants to work in Taipei.
My brother, who is a doctor, lives in London.
Our teacher, who is very kind, gave us extra time.
Mrs. Chen, who runs the bakery downstairs, gave us free bread.
The doctor, who was very young, explained everything clearly.
My best friend, who moved to Canada, sends me letters.
I had lunch with my boss, who paid for everything.
We met the singer, who was very friendly.
I called my dad, who was at work.
The prize went to Ann, who worked really hard.
I spoke to the manager, who said sorry.
My grandfather, who died last year, loved gardening.
I'll ask my cousin, who knows a lot about cars.
My friends, who had never been to Taipei, loved the night market.
The children, who were tired, fell asleep in the car.
I'm meeting Tom, who just got back from Spain.
My mother, who can't swim, stayed on the beach.
We thanked the driver, who had waited for us.
Ann's husband, who is a chef, cooked dinner for us.
I wrote to my old teacher, who still remembers me.

examples.heading: ① 名字, + who ...

items.en: I'm going to the concert with Mia, who loves this band.
items.zh: 我要跟 Mia 去看演唱會，她很愛這個樂團。

items.en: We visited Ann, who lives near the beach.
items.zh: 我們去拜訪 Ann，她住在海邊附近。

items.en: Ken, who works at the bank, helped me with the form.
items.zh: Ken 在銀行上班，他幫我填了表格。

items.en: I asked Mr. Lin, who teaches math at our school.
items.zh: 我問了林老師，他在我們學校教數學。

items.en: Lucy, who speaks three languages, works as a tour guide.
items.zh: Lucy 會說三種語言，她當導遊。

examples.heading: ② my + 家人, + who ...

items.en: I went hiking with my cousin, who knows the mountains well.
items.zh: 我跟我表哥去爬山，他對那些山很熟。

items.en: My parents, who are on holiday in Bali, sent us a postcard.
items.zh: 我爸媽在峇里島度假，他們寄了一張明信片給我們。

items.en: This is my aunt, who lives in Tainan.
items.zh: 這是我阿姨，她住在台南。

items.en: My grandmother, who is ninety, still walks every day.
items.zh: 我奶奶九十歲了，還是每天散步。

items.en: I stayed with my uncle, who has a farm in the south.
items.zh: 我住在我叔叔家，他在南部有一座農場。

items.en: My sister, who studies law, wants to work in Taipei.
items.zh: 我姊姊讀法律，她想在台北工作。

examples.heading: ③ 子句在句子中間

items.en: My brother, who is a doctor, lives in London.
items.zh: 我哥哥是醫生，他住在倫敦。

items.en: Our teacher, who is very kind, gave us extra time.
items.zh: 我們的老師人很好，多給了我們一些時間。

items.en: Mrs. Chen, who runs the bakery downstairs, gave us free bread.
items.zh: 陳太太在樓下開麵包店，她送了我們免費的麵包。

items.en: The doctor, who was very young, explained everything clearly.
items.zh: 那位醫生很年輕，把一切都解釋得很清楚。

items.en: My best friend, who moved to Canada, sends me letters.
items.zh: 我最好的朋友搬到加拿大了，常寄信給我。

examples.heading: ④ 子句在句尾

items.en: I had lunch with my boss, who paid for everything.
items.zh: 我跟我老闆吃午餐，老闆全部都付了。

items.en: We met the singer, who was very friendly.
items.zh: 我們見到了那位歌手，人很友善。

items.en: I called my dad, who was at work.
items.zh: 我打給我爸爸，他當時在上班。
