sentences: Young drivers are likely to have more accidents.
The new shopping centre is likely to attract many visitors.
Children who sleep well are likely to do better at school.
The meeting was likely to go on for hours.
After the bad harvest, the price of bread is likely to go up.
It's my first interview, so I'm bound to feel nervous.
With our new marketing plan, we are sure to increase our profit.
The team is certain to win if their best player is fit.
If you leave the window open, the cat is bound to get out.
The film was sure to be popular with teenagers.
A car like that is bound to be expensive to repair.
She's certain to get the job. She's the best candidate.
I am due to start my new job on Monday 4 June.
The plane is due to land at half past six.
The baby is due to arrive in March.
The new library was due to open last year, but it's still not ready.
The band is due to play in our town next month.
The results are due to come out on Friday.
You're meant to take this medicine after meals.
The museum is meant to be very good.
We were meant to meet at ten, but I was late.
This bag isn't meant to carry heavy things.
The party was meant to be a surprise.
What am I meant to do with all these papers?
From 1st June, all staff will be obliged to use identity cards.
I was obliged to spend the evening listening to a very boring speaker.
Drivers are obliged to stop at a red light.
We were obliged to cancel the trip because of the storm.
You are not obliged to buy anything from the shop.
The company was obliged to pay back the money.
Tenants will be obliged to give two months' notice.

examples.heading: ① be likely to + 原形動詞

items.en: Young drivers are likely to have more accidents.
items.zh: 年輕駕駛往往比較容易出車禍。

items.en: The new shopping centre is likely to attract many visitors.
items.zh: 新的購物中心很可能會吸引很多遊客。

items.en: Children who sleep well are likely to do better at school.
items.zh: 睡得好的孩子在學校往往表現比較好。

items.en: The meeting was likely to go on for hours.
items.zh: 會議很可能會開好幾個小時。

items.en: After the bad harvest, the price of bread is likely to go up.
items.zh: 收成不好之後，麵包的價格很可能會上漲。

examples.heading: ② be bound to / be sure to / be certain to + 原形動詞

items.en: It's my first interview, so I'm bound to feel nervous.
items.zh: 這是我第一次面試，所以我一定會緊張。

items.en: With our new marketing plan, we are sure to increase our profit.
items.zh: 有了新的行銷計畫，我們一定會增加利潤。

items.en: The team is certain to win if their best player is fit.
items.zh: 如果最好的球員身體沒問題，這支隊伍一定會贏。

items.en: If you leave the window open, the cat is bound to get out.
items.zh: 如果你開著窗，貓一定會跑出去。

items.en: The film was sure to be popular with teenagers.
items.zh: 那部電影一定會受青少年歡迎。

items.en: A car like that is bound to be expensive to repair.
items.zh: 那種車修起來一定很貴。

items.en: She's certain to get the job. She's the best candidate.
items.zh: 她一定會得到那份工作，她是最好的人選。

examples.heading: ③ be due to + 原形動詞

items.en: I am due to start my new job on Monday 4 June.
items.zh: 我預定六月四日星期一開始新工作。

items.en: The plane is due to land at half past six.
items.zh: 飛機預定六點半降落。

items.en: The baby is due to arrive in March.
items.zh: 寶寶預產期在三月。

items.en: The new library was due to open last year, but it's still not ready.
items.zh: 新圖書館原本預定去年開幕，可是到現在還沒好。

items.en: The band is due to play in our town next month.
items.zh: 樂團預定下個月在我們鎮上表演。

items.en: The results are due to come out on Friday.
items.zh: 結果預定星期五公布。

examples.heading: ④ be meant to + 原形動詞

items.en: You're meant to take this medicine after meals.
items.zh: 這種藥應該飯後吃。

items.en: The museum is meant to be very good.
items.zh: 那間博物館聽說很棒。

items.en: We were meant to meet at ten, but I was late.
items.zh: 我們原本應該十點見面，可是我遲到了。

items.en: This bag isn't meant to carry heavy things.
items.zh: 這個袋子不是用來裝重的東西。

items.en: The party was meant to be a surprise.
items.zh: 這個派對原本應該是個驚喜。

items.en: What am I meant to do with all these papers?
items.zh: 這些文件我應該怎麼處理？

examples.heading: ⑤ be obliged to + 原形動詞

items.en: From 1st June, all staff will be obliged to use identity cards.
items.zh: 從六月一日起，所有員工都必須使用識別證。

items.en: I was obliged to spend the evening listening to a very boring speaker.
items.zh: 我不得不花一整晚聽一個很無聊的講者說話。

items.en: Drivers are obliged to stop at a red light.
items.zh: 駕駛遇到紅燈必須停車。

items.en: We were obliged to cancel the trip because of the storm.
items.zh: 因為暴風雨，我們不得不取消旅行。

items.en: You are not obliged to buy anything from the shop.
items.zh: 你不一定要在店裡買東西。

items.en: The company was obliged to pay back the money.
items.zh: 那家公司必須把錢還回去。

items.en: Tenants will be obliged to give two months' notice.
items.zh: 房客必須提前兩個月通知。

title: I'm sure I can beat you at chess.
translation: 我很確定下西洋棋我贏得了你。
name: I'm sure 加子句
sentences: I'm sure we will find something to do at the weekend.
I'm sure you'll pass your driving test.
I'm sure she knows the answer.
I'm sure it'll be a great party.
I'm sure I left my keys on the table.
I'm sure your parents will understand.
I'm sure the shop opens at nine.
I'm sure he can fix your bike.
I'm sure we've met before.
I'm sure the train will be on time.
I'm sure the museum is free on the first Sunday of the month.
I'm sure I can finish the work by Friday.
I'm sure that you will love the new flat.
I'm sure that the children will enjoy the zoo.
I'm sure that my sister can help you.
I'm sure that this is the right road.
I'm sure that we'll win next time.
I'm sure that the hotel has free wifi.
My mum is sure that I'll get the job.
We're sure the weather will be good tomorrow.
Tom is sure he saw a fox in the garden.
They're sure the film starts at eight.
The teacher is sure everyone will do well.
Are you sure you locked the door?
I'm not sure what I want to do after school.
I'm not sure if I can come to your party.
I'm not sure where she lives.
I'm not sure when the bus leaves.
I'm not sure who's coming tonight.
I'm not sure how much the tickets cost.
I'm not sure what I want to do, but I'm sure we'll find something.

examples.heading: ① I'm sure + 子句

items.en: I'm sure we will find something to do at the weekend.
items.zh: 我確定週末我們會找到事情做。

items.en: I'm sure you'll pass your driving test.
items.zh: 我確定你會通過駕照考試。

items.en: I'm sure she knows the answer.
items.zh: 我確定她知道答案。

items.en: I'm sure it'll be a great party.
items.zh: 我確定那會是一場很棒的派對。

items.en: I'm sure I left my keys on the table.
items.zh: 我確定我把鑰匙放在桌上。

items.en: I'm sure your parents will understand.
items.zh: 我確定你爸媽會理解。

items.en: I'm sure the shop opens at nine.
items.zh: 我確定那家店九點開門。

items.en: I'm sure he can fix your bike.
items.zh: 我確定他修得好你的腳踏車。

items.en: I'm sure we've met before.
items.zh: 我確定我們以前見過。

items.en: I'm sure the train will be on time.
items.zh: 我確定火車會準時。

items.en: I'm sure the museum is free on the first Sunday of the month.
items.zh: 我確定博物館每個月第一個星期天免費。

items.en: I'm sure I can finish the work by Friday.
items.zh: 我確定我星期五之前做得完。

examples.heading: ② I'm sure that + 子句

items.en: I'm sure that you will love the new flat.
items.zh: 我確定你會愛上新公寓。

items.en: I'm sure that the children will enjoy the zoo.
items.zh: 我確定孩子們會喜歡動物園。

items.en: I'm sure that my sister can help you.
items.zh: 我確定我姊可以幫你。

items.en: I'm sure that this is the right road.
items.zh: 我確定這是對的路。

items.en: I'm sure that we'll win next time.
items.zh: 我確定我們下次會贏。

items.en: I'm sure that the hotel has free wifi.
items.zh: 我確定那家飯店有免費無線網路。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + is / are + sure + 子句

items.en: My mum is sure that I'll get the job.
items.zh: 我媽確定我會得到那份工作。

items.en: We're sure the weather will be good tomorrow.
items.zh: 我們確定明天天氣會很好。

items.en: Tom is sure he saw a fox in the garden.
items.zh: Tom 確定他在花園裡看到一隻狐狸。

items.en: They're sure the film starts at eight.
items.zh: 他們確定電影八點開始。

items.en: The teacher is sure everyone will do well.
items.zh: 老師確定大家都會考得好。

items.en: Are you sure you locked the door?
items.zh: 你確定你鎖門了嗎？

examples.heading: ④ I'm not sure + what / if / where + 子句

items.en: I'm not sure what I want to do after school.
items.zh: 我不確定畢業後我想做什麼。

items.en: I'm not sure if I can come to your party.
items.zh: 我不確定能不能來你的派對。

items.en: I'm not sure where she lives.
items.zh: 我不確定她住在哪裡。

items.en: I'm not sure when the bus leaves.
items.zh: 我不確定公車什麼時候開。

items.en: I'm not sure who's coming tonight.
items.zh: 我不確定今晚誰會來。

items.en: I'm not sure how much the tickets cost.
items.zh: 我不確定票要多少錢。

items.en: I'm not sure what I want to do, but I'm sure we'll find something.
items.zh: 我不確定我想做什麼，不過我確定我們會找到事情做。

title: Maybe we could visit that park you told me about.
translation: 它也許在廚房的桌子底下。
name: maybe、perhaps 放在子句前面
sentences: When you come next month, maybe we could visit that park you told me about, or play at your house.
It's going to rain all weekend. Maybe we could watch some old films at my place.
You don't understand the maths homework? Maybe your older cousin could explain it.
Maybe we could have a picnic if the weather is nice.
Maybe you could stay with us for a few days.
Maybe we could meet halfway, in the town centre.
I've looked everywhere for the remote control. Perhaps it's in the kitchen under the table.
Anna is never this late. Perhaps the trains are running slowly because of the snow.
Perhaps the shop is closed for the holiday.
He hasn't replied all day. Perhaps his phone has run out of battery.
We've been driving for an hour and there's no sign of the village. Perhaps the map is wrong.
Perhaps it will stop raining by the afternoon.
I think I left my phone at your house, maybe in your kitchen.
We could meet on Friday, maybe at six.
I'll buy her a present, maybe a book.
For our holiday we want a sunny place, maybe the south of Spain.
He's about forty, maybe older.
I'll send you the photos soon, maybe this weekend.
I want to buy new trousers and, perhaps, a T-shirt.
We'll need some bread and, perhaps, some cheese.
The trip will take three days, perhaps four.
There were about fifty people at the party, perhaps more.
I'll invite Anna and, perhaps, her brother.
We could paint the room white or, perhaps, light blue.
There's a big club in town. There you can dance, eat, drink and maybe meet new friends.
At the beach you can swim, and perhaps you'll see some dolphins.
In the old town you can walk around, and maybe you'll find a nice café.
At the market you can buy fresh fruit, and perhaps try some local cheese.
In the park you can relax, and maybe have a picnic by the lake.
At the festival you can hear great music, and perhaps meet the bands.
In the mountains you can walk for hours, and maybe see some wild goats.

examples.heading: ① Maybe + 主詞 + could + 原形動詞：提議

items.en: When you come next month, maybe we could visit that park you told me about, or play at your house.
items.zh: 你下個月來的時候，也許我們可以去你跟我說的那座公園，或在你家玩。

items.en: It's going to rain all weekend. Maybe we could watch some old films at my place.
items.zh: 整個週末都會下雨。也許我們可以在我家看幾部老電影。

items.en: You don't understand the maths homework? Maybe your older cousin could explain it.
items.zh: 你不懂數學功課？也許你表哥可以解釋給你聽。

items.en: Maybe we could have a picnic if the weather is nice.
items.zh: 如果天氣好，也許我們可以去野餐。

items.en: Maybe you could stay with us for a few days.
items.zh: 也許你可以來我們家住幾天。

items.en: Maybe we could meet halfway, in the town centre.
items.zh: 也許我們可以在中間碰面，在市中心。

examples.heading: ② Perhaps + 子句：猜測

items.en: I've looked everywhere for the remote control. Perhaps it's in the kitchen under the table.
items.zh: 我到處找遙控器。也許它在廚房的桌子底下。

items.en: Anna is never this late. Perhaps the trains are running slowly because of the snow.
items.zh: 安娜從來不會這麼晚到。也許火車因為下雪開得很慢。

items.en: Perhaps the shop is closed for the holiday.
items.zh: 也許那家店放假沒開。

items.en: He hasn't replied all day. Perhaps his phone has run out of battery.
items.zh: 他一整天都沒回。也許他的手機沒電了。

items.en: We've been driving for an hour and there's no sign of the village. Perhaps the map is wrong.
items.zh: 我們開了一個小時，都沒看到那個村子。也許地圖錯了。

items.en: Perhaps it will stop raining by the afternoon.
items.zh: 也許下午雨就會停。

examples.heading: ③ …, maybe + 片語：省略的子句

items.en: I think I left my phone at your house, maybe in your kitchen.
items.zh: 我想我把手機留在你家了，也許在你的廚房。

items.en: We could meet on Friday, maybe at six.
items.zh: 我們可以星期五見面，也許六點。

items.en: I'll buy her a present, maybe a book.
items.zh: 我會買個禮物給她，也許一本書。

items.en: For our holiday we want a sunny place, maybe the south of Spain.
items.zh: 我們度假想去一個陽光充足的地方，也許西班牙南部。

items.en: He's about forty, maybe older.
items.zh: 他大概四十歲，也許更老。

items.en: I'll send you the photos soon, maybe this weekend.
items.zh: 我很快會把照片寄給你，也許這個週末。

examples.heading: ④ …, perhaps + 名詞：補充一個可能

items.en: I want to buy new trousers and, perhaps, a T-shirt.
items.zh: 我想買一條新褲子，也許再買一件T恤。

items.en: We'll need some bread and, perhaps, some cheese.
items.zh: 我們需要一些麵包，也許還要一些起司。

items.en: The trip will take three days, perhaps four.
items.zh: 這趟旅行要三天，也許四天。

items.en: There were about fifty people at the party, perhaps more.
items.zh: 派對上大概有五十個人，也許更多。

items.en: I'll invite Anna and, perhaps, her brother.
items.zh: 我會邀請安娜，也許還有她哥哥。

items.en: We could paint the room white or, perhaps, light blue.
items.zh: 我們可以把房間漆成白色，或者也許淺藍色。

examples.heading: ⑤ Maybe / Perhaps + 子句：描述一個地方能做的事

items.en: There's a big club in town. There you can dance, eat, drink and maybe meet new friends.
items.zh: 城裡有一家很大的俱樂部。在那裡你可以跳舞、吃東西、喝飲料，也許還能認識新朋友。

items.en: At the beach you can swim, and perhaps you'll see some dolphins.
items.zh: 在海灘你可以游泳，也許還會看到海豚。

items.en: In the old town you can walk around, and maybe you'll find a nice café.
items.zh: 在舊城區你可以四處走走，也許會找到一家不錯的咖啡館。

items.en: At the market you can buy fresh fruit, and perhaps try some local cheese.
items.zh: 在市場你可以買新鮮水果，也許還可以嚐嚐當地的起司。

items.en: In the park you can relax, and maybe have a picnic by the lake.
items.zh: 在公園你可以放鬆，也許在湖邊野餐。

items.en: At the festival you can hear great music, and perhaps meet the bands.
items.zh: 在節慶上你可以聽到很棒的音樂，也許還能見到樂團。

items.en: In the mountains you can walk for hours, and maybe see some wild goats.
items.zh: 在山上你可以走好幾個小時，也許還會看到野山羊。

title: They will certainly have a banquet that day, and you oughtn't miss it for the world!
translation: 你說什麼都不該錯過！
name: 不加 to 的 oughtn't 加動詞
sentences: There will certainly be a banquet that day, and you oughtn't miss it for the world!
You're in Sydney for New Year? The fireworks start at midnight. You oughtn't miss them.
Mum was very upset last year. You oughtn't forget her birthday again.
Everything in the bookshop is half price, and the sale ends tomorrow. You oughtn't miss it.
We're flying to Spain at six in the morning. You oughtn't forget to bring your passport.
It's the last concert of the tour, and it's in our town. You oughtn't miss it.
You've studied every day for a month. You oughtn't worry so much about the exam.
You keep waking up with a stomach ache. You oughtn't eat so late at night.
You've been awake since five this morning. You oughtn't drive when you're this tired.
You can't pay your rent this month. You oughtn't spend all your money on clothes.
Three bikes were stolen on our street last week. You oughtn't leave yours outside without a lock.
That story about the moon isn't true. You oughtn't believe everything you read online.
I've already had two slices. I oughtn't eat any more cake, but it's so good.
We oughtn't stay out too late. We have school tomorrow.
I oughtn't say this, but I don't like Sara's new haircut.
Half the vegetables in our fridge go in the bin every week. We oughtn't waste so much food.
My friends lost their jobs this year. I oughtn't complain. My job is quite good.
Our gas bill was huge last month. We oughtn't keep the heating on when nobody's at home.
You're at the office until ten every night. You oughtn't to work so hard.
The report says children watch four hours of TV a day. Children oughtn't to watch so much.
Tom shouted at his mum in the supermarket. He oughtn't to speak to her like that.
The river floods every few winters. They oughtn't to build houses so close to it.
The park has no lights after nine. Lucy oughtn't to walk home alone at night.
The guests are already at the door. We oughtn't to keep them waiting.
The shirt was ten pounds and the postage was eight. The shop oughtn't charge so much for delivery.
My boss shouts at us every day. He oughtn't treat his staff so badly.
Hundreds of people use the library every week. The council oughtn't close it.
Our neighbours' visitors block our drive every weekend. They oughtn't park in front of our gate.
The cars go very fast on this street. The children oughtn't play so near the road.
Emma isn't sure about the job in London. She oughtn't take it if she doesn't want it.
Bus fares went up in January and again in June. The bus company oughtn't raise them again.

examples.heading: ① You oughtn't + miss / forget：不該錯過

items.en: There will certainly be a banquet that day, and you oughtn't miss it for the world!
items.zh: 那天一定會辦一場盛宴，你無論如何都不該錯過！

items.en: You're in Sydney for New Year? The fireworks start at midnight. You oughtn't miss them.
items.zh: 你新年在雪梨？煙火半夜開始。你不該錯過。

items.en: Mum was very upset last year. You oughtn't forget her birthday again.
items.zh: 媽媽去年很難過。你不該再忘記她的生日。

items.en: Everything in the bookshop is half price, and the sale ends tomorrow. You oughtn't miss it.
items.zh: 書店全部半價，特價明天結束。你不該錯過。

items.en: We're flying to Spain at six in the morning. You oughtn't forget to bring your passport.
items.zh: 我們早上六點要飛西班牙。你不該忘記帶護照。

items.en: It's the last concert of the tour, and it's in our town. You oughtn't miss it.
items.zh: 這是巡迴演唱的最後一場，而且就在我們鎮上。你不該錯過。

examples.heading: ② You oughtn't + 原形動詞：給建議

items.en: You've studied every day for a month. You oughtn't worry so much about the exam.
items.zh: 你一個月來每天都在讀書。你不該那麼擔心考試。

items.en: You keep waking up with a stomach ache. You oughtn't eat so late at night.
items.zh: 你一直肚子痛醒。你不該那麼晚還吃東西。

items.en: You've been awake since five this morning. You oughtn't drive when you're this tired.
items.zh: 你從今天早上五點就醒著。你這麼累的時候不該開車。

items.en: You can't pay your rent this month. You oughtn't spend all your money on clothes.
items.zh: 你這個月付不出房租。你不該把錢都花在衣服上。

items.en: Three bikes were stolen on our street last week. You oughtn't leave yours outside without a lock.
items.zh: 上星期我們這條街有三台腳踏車被偷。你不該把你的腳踏車放在外面不上鎖。

items.en: That story about the moon isn't true. You oughtn't believe everything you read online.
items.zh: 那個關於月亮的故事不是真的。你不該相信你在網路上讀到的每一件事。

examples.heading: ③ I / We oughtn't + 原形動詞：說自己

items.en: I've already had two slices. I oughtn't eat any more cake, but it's so good.
items.zh: 我已經吃了兩片了。我不該再吃蛋糕了，可是它太好吃了。

items.en: We oughtn't stay out too late. We have school tomorrow.
items.zh: 我們不該在外面待太晚。我們明天要上學。

items.en: I oughtn't say this, but I don't like Sara's new haircut.
items.zh: 我不該這麼說，可是我不喜歡 Sara 的新髮型。

items.en: Half the vegetables in our fridge go in the bin every week. We oughtn't waste so much food.
items.zh: 我們冰箱裡一半的蔬菜每週都被丟掉。我們不該浪費這麼多食物。

items.en: My friends lost their jobs this year. I oughtn't complain. My job is quite good.
items.zh: 我朋友今年都失業了。我不該抱怨。我的工作還不錯。

items.en: Our gas bill was huge last month. We oughtn't keep the heating on when nobody's at home.
items.zh: 我們上個月的瓦斯費很高。沒人在家的時候，我們不該開著暖氣。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + oughtn't to + 原形動詞：保留 to

items.en: You're at the office until ten every night. You oughtn't to work so hard.
items.zh: 你每天晚上都在辦公室待到十點。你不該這麼拚命工作。

items.en: The report says children watch four hours of TV a day. Children oughtn't to watch so much.
items.zh: 報告說孩子一天看四個小時的電視。孩子們不該看這麼多。

items.en: Tom shouted at his mum in the supermarket. He oughtn't to speak to her like that.
items.zh: Tom 在超市對他媽媽大吼。他不該那樣跟她說話。

items.en: The river floods every few winters. They oughtn't to build houses so close to it.
items.zh: 那條河每隔幾個冬天就淹水。他們不該把房子蓋得離河這麼近。

items.en: The park has no lights after nine. Lucy oughtn't to walk home alone at night.
items.zh: 公園九點以後沒有燈。Lucy 晚上不該一個人走路回家。

items.en: The guests are already at the door. We oughtn't to keep them waiting.
items.zh: 客人已經到門口了。我們不該讓他們等。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + oughtn't + 原形動詞：說別人或機構

items.en: The shirt was ten pounds and the postage was eight. The shop oughtn't charge so much for delivery.
items.zh: 襯衫十英鎊，運費卻要八英鎊。那家店的運費不該收這麼貴。

items.en: My boss shouts at us every day. He oughtn't treat his staff so badly.
items.zh: 我老闆每天都對我們大吼。他不該這樣虧待他的員工。

items.en: Hundreds of people use the library every week. The council oughtn't close it.
items.zh: 每週有好幾百人用圖書館。市議會不該關閉它。

items.en: Our neighbours' visitors block our drive every weekend. They oughtn't park in front of our gate.
items.zh: 我們鄰居的客人每個週末都擋住我們的車道。他們不該把車停在我們大門前。

items.en: The cars go very fast on this street. The children oughtn't play so near the road.
items.zh: 這條街的車開得很快。孩子們不該在離馬路這麼近的地方玩。

items.en: Emma isn't sure about the job in London. She oughtn't take it if she doesn't want it.
items.zh: Emma 對倫敦的工作不確定。如果她不想要，她不該接受。

items.en: Bus fares went up in January and again in June. The bus company oughtn't raise them again.
items.zh: 公車票價一月漲過，六月又漲了。公車公司不該再漲價。

title: You must! It's amazing!
translation: 我現在照顧她，是因為我非這麼做不可。
name: must 後省略動詞
sentences: "I haven't been to the new museum." "You must! The dinosaurs are amazing!"
"Have you tried the ice cream shop on the corner?" "Not yet." "You must!"
"I've never been to the night market." "Oh, you must!"
"I might read her new book." "You must! It's her best one."
"Should I join the drama club?" "You must! It's so much fun."
"I've never heard this band live." "You must! They're brilliant."
Right now, I take care of my grandmother because I must!
I work at weekends because I must, not because I want to.
She gets up at five because she must.
I'm learning German because I must. My new job is in Berlin.
We're selling the house because we must. The bank wants its money.
He takes the bus because he must. He can't drive.
"Do I really have to wear a uniform?" "Yes, you must."
"Must we finish the whole book?" "Yes, we must."
"Should I tell my boss?" "Yes, I think you must."
"Do we need to book a table?" "Yes, we must. It's Saturday."
"Must I sign here?" "Yes, you must."
"Do I have to take this medicine every day?" "Yes, you must."
I don't want to leave, but I must.
She didn't want to tell him, but she knew she must.
We don't want to cancel the trip, but we must.
I hate going to the dentist, but I must.
He doesn't want to sell his bike, but he must.
They don't want to move, but they must.
"Can I bring my dog?" "If you must."
If you must smoke, please go outside.
"I want to watch the football tonight." "Well, if you must."
If you must leave early, tell the teacher.
"Can I have another biscuit?" "Oh, if you must."
If you must use your phone, do it in the hall.
"I need to borrow your car." "If you must, but be careful."

examples.heading: ① You must!：熱情地推薦

items.en: "I haven't been to the new museum." "You must! The dinosaurs are amazing!"
items.zh: 我還沒去過新的博物館。你一定要去！恐龍很棒！

items.en: "Have you tried the ice cream shop on the corner?" "Not yet." "You must!"
items.zh: 你吃過轉角那家冰淇淋店嗎？還沒。你一定要去吃！

items.en: "I've never been to the night market." "Oh, you must!"
items.zh: 我從來沒去過夜市。噢，你一定要去！

items.en: "I might read her new book." "You must! It's her best one."
items.zh: 我可能會讀她的新書。你一定要讀！那是她最好的一本。

items.en: "Should I join the drama club?" "You must! It's so much fun."
items.zh: 我該加入戲劇社嗎？你一定要加入！超好玩的。

items.en: "I've never heard this band live." "You must! They're brilliant."
items.zh: 我從來沒聽過這個樂團的現場演出。你一定要去聽！他們太棒了。

examples.heading: ② because + 主詞 + must：說不得不做

items.en: Right now, I take care of my grandmother because I must!
items.zh: 現在我照顧我奶奶，因為我非照顧不可！

items.en: I work at weekends because I must, not because I want to.
items.zh: 我週末工作是因為不得不，不是因為我想要。

items.en: She gets up at five because she must.
items.zh: 她五點起床是因為不得不。

items.en: I'm learning German because I must. My new job is in Berlin.
items.zh: 我在學德文是因為不得不。我的新工作在柏林。

items.en: We're selling the house because we must. The bank wants its money.
items.zh: 我們要賣房子，因為不得不。銀行要收回貸款。

items.en: He takes the bus because he must. He can't drive.
items.zh: 他搭公車是因為不得不。他不會開車。

examples.heading: ③ Yes, 主詞 + must.：回答問題

items.en: "Do I really have to wear a uniform?" "Yes, you must."
items.zh: 我真的一定要穿制服嗎？對，你一定要穿。

items.en: "Must we finish the whole book?" "Yes, we must."
items.zh: 我們一定要讀完整本書嗎？對，一定要。

items.en: "Should I tell my boss?" "Yes, I think you must."
items.zh: 我該告訴老闆嗎？對，我想你一定要說。

items.en: "Do we need to book a table?" "Yes, we must. It's Saturday."
items.zh: 我們需要訂位嗎？對，一定要。今天是星期六。

items.en: "Must I sign here?" "Yes, you must."
items.zh: 我一定要簽在這裡嗎？對，一定要。

items.en: "Do I have to take this medicine every day?" "Yes, you must."
items.zh: 我每天都一定要吃這個藥嗎？對，一定要吃。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + don't want to, but + 主詞 + must

items.en: I don't want to leave, but I must.
items.zh: 我不想走，可是我必須走。

items.en: She didn't want to tell him, but she knew she must.
items.zh: 她不想告訴他，可是她知道她必須說。

items.en: We don't want to cancel the trip, but we must.
items.zh: 我們不想取消旅行，可是我們必須取消。

items.en: I hate going to the dentist, but I must.
items.zh: 我很討厭去看牙醫，可是我必須去。

items.en: He doesn't want to sell his bike, but he must.
items.zh: 他不想賣他的腳踏車，可是他必須賣。

items.en: They don't want to move, but they must.
items.zh: 他們不想搬家，可是他們必須搬。

examples.heading: ⑤ If you must, + 句子：勉強同意

items.en: "Can I bring my dog?" "If you must."
items.zh: 我可以帶我的狗來嗎？如果你一定要的話。

items.en: If you must smoke, please go outside.
items.zh: 如果你一定要抽菸，請到外面去。

items.en: "I want to watch the football tonight." "Well, if you must."
items.zh: 我今天晚上想看足球。好吧，如果你一定要的話。

items.en: If you must leave early, tell the teacher.
items.zh: 如果你一定要提早走，告訴老師。

items.en: "Can I have another biscuit?" "Oh, if you must."
items.zh: 我可以再吃一塊餅乾嗎？噢，如果你一定要的話。

items.en: If you must use your phone, do it in the hall.
items.zh: 如果你一定要用手機，到走廊去用。

items.en: "I need to borrow your car." "If you must, but be careful."
items.zh: 我需要借你的車。如果你一定要的話，可是要小心。

title: Must go now.
translation: 我得走了。
name: 省略主詞的 must
sentences: My train is here. Must go now. Speak soon!
That's all my news. Must dash, the bus is coming.
Must run. The shop closes at five.
Must go, my lesson starts in five minutes.
Sorry this is short. Must get back to work.
Must stop writing now. It's very late.
Must remember to buy milk on the way home.
Must call the dentist tomorrow.
Must finish this essay before Friday.
Must tidy my room before Mum gets home.
Must try that new café next week.
Must get some sleep. Big day tomorrow.
Your grandmother is in hospital? Must be really difficult for you.
Three exams in one day? Must be exhausting.
Must be hard living so far from your family.
You lost your phone? Must be so annoying.
Must be lonely in that big house on your own.
Moving to a new school? Must be a bit scary.
You're going to Australia? Must be exciting!
Must be nice to have the whole summer off.
Your new flat has a garden? Must be lovely.
Must be great to see your old friends again.
A new baby brother? Must be fun!
Must be wonderful to wake up by the sea.
Someone's at the door. Must be the postman.
Look at all those people. Must be a concert tonight.
Must be your sister on the phone. She always calls at this time.
That smell? Must be the bakery next door.
Must be a mistake. I didn't order this.
Who's that singing? Must be our neighbour's daughter.
Must be the wind. There's nobody outside.

examples.heading: ① Must + go / dash / run：信件和訊息的結尾

items.en: My train is here. Must go now. Speak soon!
items.zh: 我的火車來了。我得走了。再聊！

items.en: That's all my news. Must dash, the bus is coming.
items.zh: 我的消息就這些。我得趕快走了，公車來了。

items.en: Must run. The shop closes at five.
items.zh: 我得走了。那家店五點關門。

items.en: Must go, my lesson starts in five minutes.
items.zh: 我得走了，我的課五分鐘後開始。

items.en: Sorry this is short. Must get back to work.
items.zh: 抱歉寫得很短。我得回去工作了。

items.en: Must stop writing now. It's very late.
items.zh: 我得停筆了。已經很晚了。

examples.heading: ② Must + 原形動詞：提醒自己

items.en: Must remember to buy milk on the way home.
items.zh: 回家的路上要記得買牛奶。

items.en: Must call the dentist tomorrow.
items.zh: 明天一定要打電話給牙醫。

items.en: Must finish this essay before Friday.
items.zh: 星期五前一定要寫完這篇作文。

items.en: Must tidy my room before Mum gets home.
items.zh: 媽媽回家前一定要整理房間。

items.en: Must try that new café next week.
items.zh: 下星期一定要去試試那家新咖啡館。

items.en: Must get some sleep. Big day tomorrow.
items.zh: 一定要睡一下。明天是重要的日子。

examples.heading: ③ Must be + 形容詞：同情對方

items.en: Your grandmother is in hospital? Must be really difficult for you.
items.zh: 你奶奶住院了？這對你來說一定很難。

items.en: Three exams in one day? Must be exhausting.
items.zh: 一天考三科？一定累死了。

items.en: Must be hard living so far from your family.
items.zh: 住得離家人那麼遠一定很辛苦。

items.en: You lost your phone? Must be so annoying.
items.zh: 你的手機掉了？一定很煩吧。

items.en: Must be lonely in that big house on your own.
items.zh: 一個人住在那麼大的房子裡一定很寂寞。

items.en: Moving to a new school? Must be a bit scary.
items.zh: 要轉學？一定有點可怕吧。

examples.heading: ④ Must be + 形容詞：說好事

items.en: You're going to Australia? Must be exciting!
items.zh: 你要去澳洲？一定很興奮吧！

items.en: Must be nice to have the whole summer off.
items.zh: 整個夏天都放假一定很棒。

items.en: Your new flat has a garden? Must be lovely.
items.zh: 你的新公寓有花園？一定很漂亮。

items.en: Must be great to see your old friends again.
items.zh: 再見到老朋友一定很棒。

items.en: A new baby brother? Must be fun!
items.zh: 有了一個小弟弟？一定很好玩！

items.en: Must be wonderful to wake up by the sea.
items.zh: 在海邊醒來一定很美好。

examples.heading: ⑤ Must be + 名詞：猜是什麼

items.en: Someone's at the door. Must be the postman.
items.zh: 有人在門口。一定是郵差。

items.en: Look at all those people. Must be a concert tonight.
items.zh: 你看那麼多人。今天晚上一定有音樂會。

items.en: Must be your sister on the phone. She always calls at this time.
items.zh: 電話一定是你姊姊打的。她總是在這個時間打來。

items.en: That smell? Must be the bakery next door.
items.zh: 那個味道？一定是隔壁的麵包店。

items.en: Must be a mistake. I didn't order this.
items.zh: 一定是弄錯了。我沒點這個。

items.en: Who's that singing? Must be our neighbour's daughter.
items.zh: 誰在唱歌？一定是我們鄰居的女兒。

items.en: Must be the wind. There's nobody outside.
items.zh: 一定是風。外面沒有人。

title: Must have fallen out of a car.
translation: 一定是從車上掉出來的。
name: 省略主詞的 must have 加過去分詞
sentences: He picked up the old wallet by the busy road. Must have fallen out of a car, he thought.
She found the cake tin open and only crumbs inside. Must have been the children.
The window was open and the papers were on the floor. Must have been the wind.
He saw the wet footprints on the stairs. Must have come in from the garden.
She heard the front door close. Must have been her brother going out.
The lights in the house were all off. Must have gone to bed early.
Sorry I didn't answer. Must have fallen asleep on the sofa.
Can't find my glasses. Must have left them at work.
Must have eaten something bad. I feel terrible.
This physics book is so hard. Must have read that page three times without understanding it.
Must have walked ten miles today. My feet hurt.
The ticket isn't in my pocket. Must have dropped it on the bus.
"Where's Tom?" "Must have gone home."
She looks really happy. Must have passed her exam.
He's not answering. Must have switched his phone off.
They're very late. Must have got lost.
The baby has stopped crying. Must have found her teddy.
He knows all the answers. Must have seen the test before.
"We waited three hours." "Must have been boring."
"I met the Queen once." "Really? Must have been amazing!"
Someone left flowers on the step. Must have been Mrs Green.
"The power was off all night." "Must have been cold."
Loud music all night next door. Must have been a party.
"I climbed to the top." "Must have been hard work."
Tuesday. Must have slept for ten hours. Feel much better.
Got home at midnight. Must have missed the last bus by a minute.
Garden looks green again. Must have rained while we were away.
Back door unlocked this morning. Must have forgotten to lock it last night.
Ten emails from the boss. Must have been something urgent.
Car covered in snow. Must have snowed all night.
Fridge empty again. Must have been the boys after football.

examples.heading: ① Must have + 過去分詞：故事裡人物的想法

items.en: He picked up the old wallet by the busy road. Must have fallen out of a car, he thought.
items.zh: 他在車很多的路邊撿起那個舊皮夾。他想，一定是從車上掉出來的。

items.en: She found the cake tin open and only crumbs inside. Must have been the children.
items.zh: 她發現蛋糕盒開著，裡面只剩碎屑。一定是孩子們吃的。

items.en: The window was open and the papers were on the floor. Must have been the wind.
items.zh: 窗戶開著，紙張掉在地上。一定是風吹的。

items.en: He saw the wet footprints on the stairs. Must have come in from the garden.
items.zh: 他看到樓梯上濕濕的腳印。一定是從花園進來的。

items.en: She heard the front door close. Must have been her brother going out.
items.zh: 她聽到前門關上的聲音。一定是她哥哥出去了。

items.en: The lights in the house were all off. Must have gone to bed early.
items.zh: 屋子裡的燈全都關了。一定是早早上床睡了。

examples.heading: ② Must have + 過去分詞：說自己的事

items.en: Sorry I didn't answer. Must have fallen asleep on the sofa.
items.zh: 抱歉我沒接電話。我一定是在沙發上睡著了。

items.en: Can't find my glasses. Must have left them at work.
items.zh: 找不到我的眼鏡。一定是留在公司了。

items.en: Must have eaten something bad. I feel terrible.
items.zh: 一定是吃了不乾淨的東西。我覺得很不舒服。

items.en: This physics book is so hard. Must have read that page three times without understanding it.
items.zh: 這本物理書好難。那一頁我一定讀了三遍還看不懂。

items.en: Must have walked ten miles today. My feet hurt.
items.zh: 我今天一定走了十英里。我的腳好痛。

items.en: The ticket isn't in my pocket. Must have dropped it on the bus.
items.zh: 票不在我的口袋裡。一定是掉在公車上了。

examples.heading: ③ Must have + 過去分詞：說別人的事

items.en: "Where's Tom?" "Must have gone home."
items.zh: Tom 在哪裡？一定是回家了。

items.en: She looks really happy. Must have passed her exam.
items.zh: 她看起來好高興。一定是考試過了。

items.en: He's not answering. Must have switched his phone off.
items.zh: 他沒接電話。一定是把手機關了。

items.en: They're very late. Must have got lost.
items.zh: 他們遲到好久了。一定是迷路了。

items.en: The baby has stopped crying. Must have found her teddy.
items.zh: 寶寶不哭了。一定是找到她的泰迪熊了。

items.en: He knows all the answers. Must have seen the test before.
items.zh: 他知道所有的答案。一定是之前看過考卷。

examples.heading: ④ Must have been + 形容詞或名詞

items.en: "We waited three hours." "Must have been boring."
items.zh: 我們等了三個小時。一定很無聊。

items.en: "I met the Queen once." "Really? Must have been amazing!"
items.zh: 我見過女王一次。真的嗎？一定很棒！

items.en: Someone left flowers on the step. Must have been Mrs Green.
items.zh: 有人在台階上留了花。一定是 Green 太太。

items.en: "The power was off all night." "Must have been cold."
items.zh: 整晚都停電。一定很冷。

items.en: Loud music all night next door. Must have been a party.
items.zh: 隔壁整晚都在放很大聲的音樂。一定是在開派對。

items.en: "I climbed to the top." "Must have been hard work."
items.zh: 我爬到山頂了。一定很辛苦。

examples.heading: ⑤ Must have + 過去分詞：日記和便條

items.en: Tuesday. Must have slept for ten hours. Feel much better.
items.zh: 星期二。我一定睡了十個小時。覺得好多了。

items.en: Got home at midnight. Must have missed the last bus by a minute.
items.zh: 半夜才到家。一定是差一分鐘沒趕上最後一班公車。

items.en: Garden looks green again. Must have rained while we were away.
items.zh: 花園又變綠了。我們不在的時候一定下過雨。

items.en: Back door unlocked this morning. Must have forgotten to lock it last night.
items.zh: 今天早上後門沒鎖。昨晚一定是忘了鎖。

items.en: Ten emails from the boss. Must have been something urgent.
items.zh: 老闆寄了十封電子郵件。一定是有急事。

items.en: Car covered in snow. Must have snowed all night.
items.zh: 車子被雪蓋住了。一定下了一整夜的雪。

items.en: Fridge empty again. Must have been the boys after football.
items.zh: 冰箱又空了。一定是兒子們踢完球回來吃的。

title: Some students would not get as much specialised help as they ought to.
translation: 有些學生得到的專業協助，會比他們應該得到的少。
name: ought to 後面省略動詞
sentences: With forty pupils in a class, some students would not get as much specialised help as they ought to.
My jeans feel tight again. I don't go to the gym as often as I ought to.
My son's English teacher is worried. He doesn't read as much as he ought to.
Our bins are full of plastic every week. We don't recycle as much as we ought to.
The children are up until eleven playing games. They don't sleep as much as they ought to.
My grandparents live two hours away. I don't visit them as often as I ought to.
I get headaches in the afternoon. I don't drink much water, but I ought to.
My sister rides her bike to school every day. She doesn't wear a helmet, but she ought to.
Our neighbours spend everything they earn. They don't save any money, but they ought to.
Grandma cooks for Uncle Bill every Sunday. He never says thank you, but he ought to.
Everyone in my family leaves at different times. We don't eat breakfast together, but we ought to.
Mum works full time. My brother doesn't help with the cooking, but he ought to.
"A boy in my class took my phone. Should I tell my teacher?" "Yes, I think you ought to."
"That Italian place is always busy on Saturdays. Do you think we should book?" "Yes, we ought to."
"Amy broke Jo's favourite mug. Should she apologise?" "I think she ought to."
"I've had this cough for three weeks. Should I go to the doctor?" "Yes, you really ought to."
"Their cousin is in town on the day of the party. Should they invite her?" "I suppose they ought to."
"Dad hasn't heard from me for a month. Do you think I should call him?" "Yes, you ought to."
You know more about the project than me, but I'll speak at the meeting if you think I ought to.
The shop gave you twenty pounds too much? Take the money back if you think you ought to.
You know who broke Leo's bike. Tell him the truth if you feel you ought to.
Grandma seems lonely tonight. We'll stay longer if you think we ought to.
The weather looks bad for Saturday. Change the plan if you think we ought to.
There's a man in a car outside the school every day. Phone the police if you think you ought to.
My brother buys new trainers every month. He spends more than he ought to.
I have biscuits with every cup of tea. I eat more sugar than I ought to.
My mum is a nurse and often works twelve-hour shifts. She works longer hours than she ought to.
My cousins have a TV in every room. They watch more TV than they ought to.
Our accountant checked our forms. Every year we pay more tax than we ought to.
It's the summer holidays, so the kids stay up later than they ought to.
I can't put it down, even at dinner. I check my phone more often than I ought to.

examples.heading: ① as + 主詞 + ought to：比較實際和應該

items.en: With forty pupils in a class, some students would not get as much specialised help as they ought to.
items.zh: 一班四十個學生，有些學生就得不到他們應該得到的專門協助。

items.en: My jeans feel tight again. I don't go to the gym as often as I ought to.
items.zh: 我的牛仔褲又變緊了。我上健身房沒有我應該的那麼常。

items.en: My son's English teacher is worried. He doesn't read as much as he ought to.
items.zh: 我兒子的英文老師很擔心。他讀的書沒有他應該讀的那麼多。

items.en: Our bins are full of plastic every week. We don't recycle as much as we ought to.
items.zh: 我們的垃圾桶每週都裝滿塑膠。我們回收的沒有我們應該回收的那麼多。

items.en: The children are up until eleven playing games. They don't sleep as much as they ought to.
items.zh: 孩子們打電動打到十一點。他們睡得沒有他們應該睡的那麼多。

items.en: My grandparents live two hours away. I don't visit them as often as I ought to.
items.zh: 我爺爺奶奶住在兩個小時車程外。我去看他們沒有我應該的那麼常。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + don't + 動詞, but + 主詞 + ought to

items.en: I get headaches in the afternoon. I don't drink much water, but I ought to.
items.zh: 我下午常頭痛。我不常喝水，可是我應該多喝。

items.en: My sister rides her bike to school every day. She doesn't wear a helmet, but she ought to.
items.zh: 我妹妹每天騎腳踏車上學。她沒戴安全帽，可是她應該戴。

items.en: Our neighbours spend everything they earn. They don't save any money, but they ought to.
items.zh: 我們的鄰居賺多少花多少。他們都不存錢，可是他們應該存。

items.en: Grandma cooks for Uncle Bill every Sunday. He never says thank you, but he ought to.
items.zh: 奶奶每個星期天都煮飯給 Bill 叔叔吃。他從來不說謝謝，可是他應該說。

items.en: Everyone in my family leaves at different times. We don't eat breakfast together, but we ought to.
items.zh: 我家每個人出門的時間都不一樣。我們不一起吃早餐，可是我們應該一起吃。

items.en: Mum works full time. My brother doesn't help with the cooking, but he ought to.
items.zh: 媽媽做全職工作。我哥哥不幫忙煮飯，可是他應該幫忙。

examples.heading: ③ "Should + 主詞 + …？" "Yes, 主詞 + ought to."：回答

items.en: "A boy in my class took my phone. Should I tell my teacher?" "Yes, I think you ought to."
items.zh: 我班上一個男生拿了我的手機。我該告訴我的老師嗎？對，我想你應該說。

items.en: "That Italian place is always busy on Saturdays. Do you think we should book?" "Yes, we ought to."
items.zh: 那家義大利餐廳星期六總是客滿。你覺得我們應該訂位嗎？對，我們應該訂。

items.en: "Amy broke Jo's favourite mug. Should she apologise?" "I think she ought to."
items.zh: Amy 打破了 Jo 最喜歡的杯子。她應該道歉嗎？我想她應該。

items.en: "I've had this cough for three weeks. Should I go to the doctor?" "Yes, you really ought to."
items.zh: 我咳了三個星期了。我該去看醫生嗎？對，你真的應該去。

items.en: "Their cousin is in town on the day of the party. Should they invite her?" "I suppose they ought to."
items.zh: 派對那天他們的表妹剛好在城裡。他們應該邀請她嗎？我想他們應該邀請。

items.en: "Dad hasn't heard from me for a month. Do you think I should call him?" "Yes, you ought to."
items.zh: 爸爸一個月沒有我的消息了。你覺得我應該打給他嗎？對，你應該打。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + 動詞 + … + if + 主詞 + ought to

items.en: You know more about the project than me, but I'll speak at the meeting if you think I ought to.
items.zh: 你比我了解這個專案，可是如果你覺得我應該在會議上發言，我就發言。

items.en: The shop gave you twenty pounds too much? Take the money back if you think you ought to.
items.zh: 店家多找了你二十英鎊？如果你覺得應該還錢，就還吧。

items.en: You know who broke Leo's bike. Tell him the truth if you feel you ought to.
items.zh: 你知道是誰弄壞了 Leo 的腳踏車。如果你覺得應該告訴他真相，就說吧。

items.en: Grandma seems lonely tonight. We'll stay longer if you think we ought to.
items.zh: 奶奶今晚好像很寂寞。如果你覺得我們應該多待一會，我們就多待。

items.en: The weather looks bad for Saturday. Change the plan if you think we ought to.
items.zh: 星期六的天氣看起來很糟。如果你覺得我們應該改計畫，就改吧。

items.en: There's a man in a car outside the school every day. Phone the police if you think you ought to.
items.zh: 每天都有個男人坐在學校外面的車裡。如果你覺得應該報警，就打電話吧。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + 動詞 + more / less than + 主詞 + ought to

items.en: My brother buys new trainers every month. He spends more than he ought to.
items.zh: 我哥哥每個月都買新球鞋。他花的錢比他應該花的多。

items.en: I have biscuits with every cup of tea. I eat more sugar than I ought to.
items.zh: 我每喝一杯茶就配餅乾。我吃的糖比我應該吃的多。

items.en: My mum is a nurse and often works twelve-hour shifts. She works longer hours than she ought to.
items.zh: 我媽媽是護理師，常常一班工作十二個小時。她工作的時間比她應該工作的長。

items.en: My cousins have a TV in every room. They watch more TV than they ought to.
items.zh: 我表弟妹每個房間都有電視。他們看的電視比他們應該看的多。

items.en: Our accountant checked our forms. Every year we pay more tax than we ought to.
items.zh: 我們的會計師檢查了我們的表格。我們每年繳的稅都比我們應該繳的多。

items.en: It's the summer holidays, so the kids stay up later than they ought to.
items.zh: 現在是暑假，所以孩子們熬夜熬得比他們應該的晚。

items.en: I can't put it down, even at dinner. I check my phone more often than I ought to.
items.zh: 我連吃晚餐都放不下手機。我看手機看得比我應該的還常。

title: Have you ever checked your blood pressure? I think you should.
translation: 他想再跟她見面，但他知道自己不應該。
name: should 後面省略動詞
sentences: You get headaches every day. Have you ever checked your blood pressure? I think you should.
Have you told your parents about the new job? I think you should.
Have you ever tried yoga? I think you should. It helps with back pain.
Have you read the contract carefully? I really think you should.
Have you booked your flight yet? I think you should. Prices are rising.
Have you ever been to the dentist about that tooth? I think you should.
John spent the day thinking. He wanted to answer her letter and meet her again, but he knew that he shouldn't.
She wanted to eat the last biscuit, but she knew she shouldn't.
He wanted to look at her diary, but he knew he shouldn't.
I wanted to buy the expensive coat, but I knew I shouldn't.
They wanted to swim in the lake, but they knew they shouldn't.
We wanted to stay out all night, but we knew we shouldn't.
"Should I call the doctor?" "Yes, you should. You've had a fever for three days."
"Should we invite your cousins?" "Yes, we should. They invited us last year."
"Should I apologise to her?" "I think you should."
"Should we take the early train?" "Yes, we should, if we want seats."
"Should she take the job?" "I think she should."
"Should I bring a present?" "Yes, you should. It's her birthday."
"Should I drive home?" "No, you shouldn't. You're too tired."
"Should we tell Dad?" "No, we shouldn't. Not yet."
"Should I lend him the money?" "I don't think you should."
"Should we go swimming?" "No, we shouldn't. There's a storm coming."
"Should I eat this old yoghurt?" "No, you shouldn't!"
"Should they sell the farm?" "I don't think they should."
I don't exercise much, but I know I should.
He doesn't wear a helmet, but he should.
She smokes, but she knows she shouldn't.
We don't visit Grandma often, but we should.
He talks on the phone while driving, but he shouldn't.
I don't save much money, but I should.
They leave the lights on all night, but they shouldn't.

examples.heading: ① 問句 + I think you should.：建議對方去做

items.en: You get headaches every day. Have you ever checked your blood pressure? I think you should.
items.zh: 你每天都頭痛。你有沒有量過血壓？我想你應該量一下。

items.en: Have you told your parents about the new job? I think you should.
items.zh: 你有沒有把新工作的事告訴你爸媽？我想你應該說。

items.en: Have you ever tried yoga? I think you should. It helps with back pain.
items.zh: 你試過瑜伽嗎？我想你應該試試。它對背痛有幫助。

items.en: Have you read the contract carefully? I really think you should.
items.zh: 你有沒有仔細讀合約？我真的覺得你應該讀。

items.en: Have you booked your flight yet? I think you should. Prices are rising.
items.zh: 你訂機票了嗎？我想你應該訂了。價格在上漲。

items.en: Have you ever been to the dentist about that tooth? I think you should.
items.zh: 你有沒有為那顆牙去看過牙醫？我想你應該去。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + wanted to …, but + 主詞 + knew + 主詞 + shouldn't.

items.en: John spent the day thinking. He wanted to answer her letter and meet her again, but he knew that he shouldn't.
items.zh: 約翰想了一整天。他想回她的信，再跟她見面，可是他知道他不應該。

items.en: She wanted to eat the last biscuit, but she knew she shouldn't.
items.zh: 她想吃最後一塊餅乾，可是她知道她不應該。

items.en: He wanted to look at her diary, but he knew he shouldn't.
items.zh: 他想看她的日記，可是他知道他不應該。

items.en: I wanted to buy the expensive coat, but I knew I shouldn't.
items.zh: 我想買那件很貴的外套，可是我知道我不應該。

items.en: They wanted to swim in the lake, but they knew they shouldn't.
items.zh: 他們想在湖裡游泳，可是他們知道他們不應該。

items.en: We wanted to stay out all night, but we knew we shouldn't.
items.zh: 我們想整晚待在外面，可是我們知道我們不應該。

examples.heading: ③ "Should + 主詞 + …？" "Yes, 主詞 + should."

items.en: "Should I call the doctor?" "Yes, you should. You've had a fever for three days."
items.zh: 我該打電話給醫生嗎？對，你應該打。你已經發燒三天了。

items.en: "Should we invite your cousins?" "Yes, we should. They invited us last year."
items.zh: 我們該邀請你的表親嗎？對，我們應該邀。他們去年邀請過我們。

items.en: "Should I apologise to her?" "I think you should."
items.zh: 我該跟她道歉嗎？我想你應該。

items.en: "Should we take the early train?" "Yes, we should, if we want seats."
items.zh: 我們該搭早班火車嗎？對，如果我們想要有位子的話。

items.en: "Should she take the job?" "I think she should."
items.zh: 她該接受那份工作嗎？我想她應該接受。

items.en: "Should I bring a present?" "Yes, you should. It's her birthday."
items.zh: 我該帶禮物嗎？對，你應該帶。今天是她生日。

examples.heading: ④ "Should + 主詞 + …？" "No, 主詞 + shouldn't."

items.en: "Should I drive home?" "No, you shouldn't. You're too tired."
items.zh: 我該開車回家嗎？不，你不應該。你太累了。

items.en: "Should we tell Dad?" "No, we shouldn't. Not yet."
items.zh: 我們該告訴爸爸嗎？不，我們不應該。還不要。

items.en: "Should I lend him the money?" "I don't think you should."
items.zh: 我該借他錢嗎？我覺得你不應該。

items.en: "Should we go swimming?" "No, we shouldn't. There's a storm coming."
items.zh: 我們該去游泳嗎？不，我們不應該。暴風雨要來了。

items.en: "Should I eat this old yoghurt?" "No, you shouldn't!"
items.zh: 我該吃這個過期的優格嗎？不，你不應該吃！

items.en: "Should they sell the farm?" "I don't think they should."
items.zh: 他們該賣掉農場嗎？我覺得他們不應該。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + 動詞 + …, but + 主詞 + should / shouldn't.

items.en: I don't exercise much, but I know I should.
items.zh: 我不常運動，可是我知道我應該運動。

items.en: He doesn't wear a helmet, but he should.
items.zh: 他沒戴安全帽，可是他應該戴。

items.en: She smokes, but she knows she shouldn't.
items.zh: 她抽菸，可是她知道她不應該。

items.en: We don't visit Grandma often, but we should.
items.zh: 我們不常去看奶奶，可是我們應該去。

items.en: He talks on the phone while driving, but he shouldn't.
items.zh: 他開車的時候講電話，可是他不應該。

items.en: I don't save much money, but I should.
items.zh: 我存的錢不多，可是我應該多存。

items.en: They leave the lights on all night, but they shouldn't.
items.zh: 他們整晚都開著燈，可是他們不應該。

title: She doesn't travel as much as she used to.
translation: 她現在不像以前那麼常旅行了。
name: used to 後面省略動詞
sentences: My grandmother's knees are bad now. She doesn't travel as much as she used to.
I don't eat as much chocolate as I used to.
My dad doesn't work as hard as he used to.
We don't go out as much as we used to since the baby was born.
He doesn't play the guitar as much as he used to.
Now that I work from home, I don't spend as much money on lunch as I used to.
I must admit that the band sounded quite a lot better than they used to.
Since the new coach arrived, our team plays much better than it used to.
My little brother reads much faster than he used to.
The trains to London run more often than they used to.
She speaks French better than she used to.
Bread costs more than it used to.
We don't see our cousins as often as we used to.
I don't go swimming as often as I used to.
She doesn't call her mother as often as she used to.
They don't come to our parties as often as they used to.
My grandfather doesn't go fishing as often as he used to.
We don't eat out as often as we used to.
I don't smoke any more, but I used to.
She doesn't live here now, but she used to.
We don't have a dog now, but we used to.
He doesn't play rugby any more, but he used to.
They don't sell newspapers any more, but they used to.
I don't believe in ghosts, but I used to.
"Do you play the piano?" "Not now, but I used to."
"Does your brother still live in Paris?" "No, but he used to."
"Do you ride a motorbike?" "Not any more, but I used to."
"Do you know Mr Davies?" "Not really, but my mum used to."
"Does she still sing in the choir?" "No, but she used to."
"Do you go skiing?" "Not these days, but we used to."
"Do you collect anything?" "Not now, but I used to."

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + don't / doesn't + 動詞 + as much as + 主詞 + used to

items.en: My grandmother's knees are bad now. She doesn't travel as much as she used to.
items.zh: 我奶奶的膝蓋現在不好。她旅行沒有以前那麼多了。

items.en: I don't eat as much chocolate as I used to.
items.zh: 我吃巧克力沒有以前那麼多了。

items.en: My dad doesn't work as hard as he used to.
items.zh: 我爸爸工作沒有以前那麼辛苦了。

items.en: We don't go out as much as we used to since the baby was born.
items.zh: 寶寶出生以後，我們出門沒有以前那麼多了。

items.en: He doesn't play the guitar as much as he used to.
items.zh: 他彈吉他沒有以前那麼多了。

items.en: Now that I work from home, I don't spend as much money on lunch as I used to.
items.zh: 我現在在家工作，午餐花的錢沒有以前那麼多了。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + 動詞 + 比較級 + than + 主詞 + used to

items.en: I must admit that the band sounded quite a lot better than they used to.
items.zh: 我必須承認，那個樂團聽起來比以前好多了。

items.en: Since the new coach arrived, our team plays much better than it used to.
items.zh: 新教練來了以後，我們隊踢得比以前好多了。

items.en: My little brother reads much faster than he used to.
items.zh: 我弟弟讀得比以前快多了。

items.en: The trains to London run more often than they used to.
items.zh: 往倫敦的火車班次比以前多。

items.en: She speaks French better than she used to.
items.zh: 她的法文說得比以前好。

items.en: Bread costs more than it used to.
items.zh: 麵包比以前貴。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + don't / doesn't + 動詞 + as often as + 主詞 + used to

items.en: We don't see our cousins as often as we used to.
items.zh: 我們見到表親的次數沒有以前那麼多了。

items.en: I don't go swimming as often as I used to.
items.zh: 我去游泳的次數沒有以前那麼多了。

items.en: She doesn't call her mother as often as she used to.
items.zh: 她打電話給她媽媽沒有以前那麼常了。

items.en: They don't come to our parties as often as they used to.
items.zh: 他們來我們派對的次數沒有以前那麼多了。

items.en: My grandfather doesn't go fishing as often as he used to.
items.zh: 我爺爺去釣魚沒有以前那麼常了。

items.en: We don't eat out as often as we used to.
items.zh: 我們出去吃飯沒有以前那麼常了。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + don't / doesn't + 動詞 + any more, but + 主詞 + used to

items.en: I don't smoke any more, but I used to.
items.zh: 我現在不抽菸了，可是我以前抽。

items.en: She doesn't live here now, but she used to.
items.zh: 她現在不住這裡，可是她以前住過。

items.en: We don't have a dog now, but we used to.
items.zh: 我們現在沒有養狗，可是以前有。

items.en: He doesn't play rugby any more, but he used to.
items.zh: 他現在不打橄欖球了，可是他以前打。

items.en: They don't sell newspapers any more, but they used to.
items.zh: 他們現在不賣報紙了，可是以前有賣。

items.en: I don't believe in ghosts, but I used to.
items.zh: 我現在不相信鬼，可是我以前相信。

examples.heading: ⑤ "Do you …？" "Not now, but I used to."：回答問題

items.en: "Do you play the piano?" "Not now, but I used to."
items.zh: 你彈鋼琴嗎？現在不彈了，可是我以前彈。

items.en: "Does your brother still live in Paris?" "No, but he used to."
items.zh: 你哥哥還住在巴黎嗎？沒有，可是他以前住過。

items.en: "Do you ride a motorbike?" "Not any more, but I used to."
items.zh: 你騎摩托車嗎？現在不騎了，可是我以前騎。

items.en: "Do you know Mr Davies?" "Not really, but my mum used to."
items.zh: 你認識戴維斯先生嗎？不算認識，可是我媽媽以前認識。

items.en: "Does she still sing in the choir?" "No, but she used to."
items.zh: 她還在合唱團唱歌嗎？沒有，可是她以前有。

items.en: "Do you go skiing?" "Not these days, but we used to."
items.zh: 你們去滑雪嗎？最近沒有，可是我們以前會去。

items.en: "Do you collect anything?" "Not now, but I used to."
items.zh: 你有收集什麼東西嗎？現在沒有，可是我以前有。

title: I'm sorry to have to change the time of our meeting next Tuesday.
translation: 我得去買新窗簾了。
name: 不定詞形式的 have to
sentences: The cat has torn the curtains again. I'm going to have to buy new ones.
The car is making a strange noise. We're going to have to take it to the garage.
If the rain doesn't stop, they're going to have to cancel the match.
My phone is broken, so I'm going to have to use my old one.
She's going to have to work late every day this week.
We're going to have to leave before the end of the concert.
You're going to have to speak louder. I can't hear you.
I'm sorry to have to remind you about the rent.
I'm sorry to have to tell you that the flight is full.
We're sorry to have to cancel your order.
I'm sorry to have to leave so early.
I'm sorry to have to ask you for more money.
We're sorry to have to close the pool for repairs.
My family and my friends both mean a lot to me. I'd hate to have to choose between them.
I'd hate to have to sell my grandmother's ring.
I hate to have to say no to my friends.
She'd hate to have to move away from her family.
I'd hate to have to wear a suit every day.
We'd hate to have to start the project again.
Please be on time. I don't want to have to wait for you again.
I don't like to have to ask my parents for money.
He didn't expect to have to pay for the drinks.
Nobody wants to have to work on their birthday.
I don't want to have to explain everything twice.
She didn't expect to have to stay in hospital for a week.
We may have to wait for the next train.
You might have to show your ID at the door.
If the price goes up, we'll have to find a cheaper hotel.
They may have to sell the house.
I might have to miss the party on Saturday.
She'll have to learn to drive if she moves to the country.

examples.heading: ① going to have to + 原形動詞：將來必須

items.en: The cat has torn the curtains again. I'm going to have to buy new ones.
items.zh: 貓又把窗簾抓破了。我得買新的了。

items.en: The car is making a strange noise. We're going to have to take it to the garage.
items.zh: 車子發出奇怪的聲音。我們得把它送去修車廠了。

items.en: If the rain doesn't stop, they're going to have to cancel the match.
items.zh: 如果雨不停，他們就得取消比賽。

items.en: My phone is broken, so I'm going to have to use my old one.
items.zh: 我的手機壞了，所以我得用舊的了。

items.en: She's going to have to work late every day this week.
items.zh: 她這個星期得每天加班。

items.en: We're going to have to leave before the end of the concert.
items.zh: 我們得在音樂會結束前離開。

items.en: You're going to have to speak louder. I can't hear you.
items.zh: 你得大聲一點。我聽不到你。

examples.heading: ② sorry to have to + 原形動詞：很抱歉必須

items.en: I'm sorry to have to remind you about the rent.
items.zh: 很抱歉我必須提醒你房租的事。

items.en: I'm sorry to have to tell you that the flight is full.
items.zh: 很抱歉我必須告訴你，班機客滿了。

items.en: We're sorry to have to cancel your order.
items.zh: 很抱歉我們必須取消你的訂單。

items.en: I'm sorry to have to leave so early.
items.zh: 很抱歉我必須這麼早離開。

items.en: I'm sorry to have to ask you for more money.
items.zh: 很抱歉我必須跟你要更多錢。

items.en: We're sorry to have to close the pool for repairs.
items.zh: 很抱歉我們必須關閉游泳池進行修理。

examples.heading: ③ hate to have to + 原形動詞：真不想得

items.en: My family and my friends both mean a lot to me. I'd hate to have to choose between them.
items.zh: 我的家人和朋友對我都很重要。我真不想得在他們之間做選擇。

items.en: I'd hate to have to sell my grandmother's ring.
items.zh: 我真不想得賣掉我奶奶的戒指。

items.en: I hate to have to say no to my friends.
items.zh: 我真不想得拒絕我的朋友。

items.en: She'd hate to have to move away from her family.
items.zh: 她真不想得搬到離家人很遠的地方。

items.en: I'd hate to have to wear a suit every day.
items.zh: 我真不想得每天穿西裝。

items.en: We'd hate to have to start the project again.
items.zh: 我們真不想得重新開始這個專案。

examples.heading: ④ want / like / expect + to have to + 原形動詞

items.en: Please be on time. I don't want to have to wait for you again.
items.zh: 請準時。我不想又得等你。

items.en: I don't like to have to ask my parents for money.
items.zh: 我不喜歡得跟父母要錢。

items.en: He didn't expect to have to pay for the drinks.
items.zh: 他沒想到必須付飲料的錢。

items.en: Nobody wants to have to work on their birthday.
items.zh: 沒有人想在生日那天還得工作。

items.en: I don't want to have to explain everything twice.
items.zh: 我不想得把每件事解釋兩次。

items.en: She didn't expect to have to stay in hospital for a week.
items.zh: 她沒想到必須住院一個星期。

examples.heading: ⑤ may / might / will + have to：情態動詞後面的 have to

items.en: We may have to wait for the next train.
items.zh: 我們也許必須等下一班火車。

items.en: You might have to show your ID at the door.
items.zh: 你也許必須在門口出示身分證。

items.en: If the price goes up, we'll have to find a cheaper hotel.
items.zh: 如果價錢上漲，我們必須找便宜一點的飯店。

items.en: They may have to sell the house.
items.zh: 他們也許必須賣掉房子。

items.en: I might have to miss the party on Saturday.
items.zh: 我也許必須錯過星期六的派對。

items.en: She'll have to learn to drive if she moves to the country.
items.zh: 如果她搬到鄉下，她必須學開車。

title: Not only must you study really hard during university, but you must also keep studying afterwards.
translation: 你不但讀大學的時候要非常用功，畢業以後也要繼續學習。
name: 否定詞放在句首後 must 倒裝
sentences: Graduates, not only must you study really hard at university, but you must also keep studying afterwards.
The manager told the staff meeting that sales had fallen again. Not only must we cut costs, but we must also find new customers.
Rents in our city have doubled in ten years. Not only must the city build more houses, but it must also improve public transport.
The new coach spoke to the team before the season. Not only must players be fit, but they must also work as a team.
The parenting book makes one point clearly. Not only must parents set rules, but they must also follow them.
The editor gave us one final instruction. Not only must the report be accurate, but it must also be clear.
Education is necessary and useful to all of us, and never must it be called a waste of time.
The mayor spoke at the memorial on Sunday. Never must we forget the people who died in the war.
The swimming instructor repeated the first rule to the parents. Never must you leave a child alone near water.
The hotel manager spoke to the new staff. Never must we treat our guests with anything less than respect.
Our professor of medicine ended her lecture with one rule. Never must a doctor lie to a patient.
The bank sent all its customers a warning. Never must you give your bank details to a stranger.
We mustn't judge a leader only by results. Nor must we overlook their human qualities.
The council is discussing a new bridge over the river. We mustn't ignore the cost of building it. Nor must we forget the risks of doing nothing.
The exam rules are strict. Students mustn't copy each other's work. Nor must they use their phones in the exam.
The workers wrote to the new owners. The company must not raise prices. Nor must it cut jobs.
Our school's results were poor this year, the head said. We must not blame the children. Nor must we blame their teachers.
The castle has new rules for tourists. Visitors must not feed the birds. Nor must they climb on the walls.
The sign on the washing machine in the factory says: "On no account must you open this door while the machine is running."
The new IT rules came out today. Under no circumstances must staff share their passwords.
The camp leader told the helpers that the river was deep and fast. On no account must the children go near it alone.
The driving teacher warned us on the first day. Under no circumstances must you drive without insurance.
The nurse wrote a note above Mr Brown's bed. On no account must the patient eat before the operation.
The sign at the entrance to the national park says: "Under no circumstances must visitors feed the bears."
In my essay I describe the perfect teacher. Not only must a good teacher be patient, but he or she must also be fair.
The chef explained her rules to the new cooks. Not only must the food be fresh, but it must also look good.
In my review I explain what I look for in a hotel. Not only must it be clean, but it must also be quiet.
The town is choosing a plan for the new playground. Not only must the plan be cheap, but it must also be safe.
Our designers know what customers want. Not only must a website be fast, but it must also be easy to use.
The city wants a new bridge over the river. Not only must the bridge be strong, but it must also be beautiful.
The article asks what makes a good leader. Not only must a leader be clever, but he or she must also be honest.

examples.heading: ① Not only must + 主詞 + 原形動詞, but …

items.en: Graduates, not only must you study really hard at university, but you must also keep studying afterwards.
items.zh: 各位畢業生，你們不只在大學時要非常用功，畢業以後也一定要繼續學習。

items.en: The manager told the staff meeting that sales had fallen again. Not only must we cut costs, but we must also find new customers.
items.zh: 經理在員工會議上說銷售又下滑了。我們不只必須減少開支，也必須找到新顧客。

items.en: Rents in our city have doubled in ten years. Not only must the city build more houses, but it must also improve public transport.
items.zh: 我們城市的房租十年漲了一倍。這個城市不只必須蓋更多房子，也必須改善大眾運輸。

items.en: The new coach spoke to the team before the season. Not only must players be fit, but they must also work as a team.
items.zh: 新教練在球季開始前對球隊講話。球員不只必須體能好，也必須團隊合作。

items.en: The parenting book makes one point clearly. Not only must parents set rules, but they must also follow them.
items.zh: 那本教養書把一個重點講得很清楚。父母不只必須訂規矩，自己也必須遵守。

items.en: The editor gave us one final instruction. Not only must the report be accurate, but it must also be clear.
items.zh: 編輯給了我們最後一個指示。這份報告不只必須準確，也必須清楚。

examples.heading: ② Never must + 主詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: Education is necessary and useful to all of us, and never must it be called a waste of time.
items.zh: 教育對我們所有人都必要而且有用，絕對不可以把它說成浪費時間。（被動）

items.en: The mayor spoke at the memorial on Sunday. Never must we forget the people who died in the war.
items.zh: 市長星期天在紀念碑前致詞。我們絕對不可以忘記在戰爭中死去的人。

items.en: The swimming instructor repeated the first rule to the parents. Never must you leave a child alone near water.
items.zh: 游泳教練對家長再說一次第一條規定。你絕對不可以把孩子單獨留在水邊。

items.en: The hotel manager spoke to the new staff. Never must we treat our guests with anything less than respect.
items.zh: 飯店經理對新員工講話。我們對客人絕對不可以有一點不尊重。

items.en: Our professor of medicine ended her lecture with one rule. Never must a doctor lie to a patient.
items.zh: 我們的醫學教授用一條規則結束她的課。醫生絕對不可以對病人說謊。

items.en: The bank sent all its customers a warning. Never must you give your bank details to a stranger.
items.zh: 銀行寄了一封警告給所有客戶。你絕對不可以把銀行資料給陌生人。

examples.heading: ③ Nor must + 主詞 + 原形動詞：再加上一件不可以做的事

items.en: We mustn't judge a leader only by results. Nor must we overlook their human qualities.
items.zh: 我們不可以只用成績評斷一個領導者。我們也不可以忽略他們人性的特質。

items.en: The council is discussing a new bridge over the river. We mustn't ignore the cost of building it. Nor must we forget the risks of doing nothing.
items.zh: 議會在討論河上的新橋。我們不可以忽略建橋的成本。我們也不可以忘記什麼都不做的風險。

items.en: The exam rules are strict. Students mustn't copy each other's work. Nor must they use their phones in the exam.
items.zh: 考試規定很嚴格。學生不可以抄彼此的作業。考試時也不可以用手機。

items.en: The workers wrote to the new owners. The company must not raise prices. Nor must it cut jobs.
items.zh: 員工寫信給新老闆。公司不可以漲價。也不可以裁員。

items.en: Our school's results were poor this year, the head said. We must not blame the children. Nor must we blame their teachers.
items.zh: 校長說我們學校今年的成績很差。我們不可以責怪孩子。也不可以責怪他們的老師。

items.en: The castle has new rules for tourists. Visitors must not feed the birds. Nor must they climb on the walls.
items.zh: 城堡有給遊客的新規定。參觀者不可以餵鳥。也不可以爬牆。

examples.heading: ④ On no account / Under no circumstances + must + 主詞 + 原形動詞：嚴格的禁止

items.en: The sign on the washing machine in the factory says: "On no account must you open this door while the machine is running."
items.zh: 工廠洗衣機上的牌子寫著：機器運轉的時候，你絕對不可以打開這扇門。

items.en: The new IT rules came out today. Under no circumstances must staff share their passwords.
items.zh: 新的資訊規定今天公布了。員工在任何情況下都不可以分享密碼。

items.en: The camp leader told the helpers that the river was deep and fast. On no account must the children go near it alone.
items.zh: 營隊領隊告訴幫手，那條河又深又急。孩子們絕對不可以自己靠近河邊。

items.en: The driving teacher warned us on the first day. Under no circumstances must you drive without insurance.
items.zh: 駕訓教練第一天就警告我們。你在任何情況下都不可以沒有保險就開車。

items.en: The nurse wrote a note above Mr Brown's bed. On no account must the patient eat before the operation.
items.zh: 護理師在 Brown 先生的床頭寫了一張字條。病人手術前絕對不可以吃東西。

items.en: The sign at the entrance to the national park says: "Under no circumstances must visitors feed the bears."
items.zh: 國家公園入口的牌子寫著：參觀者在任何情況下都不可以餵熊。

examples.heading: ⑤ Not only must + 主詞 + be + 形容詞, but …：寫作的強調

items.en: In my essay I describe the perfect teacher. Not only must a good teacher be patient, but he or she must also be fair.
items.zh: 我在作文裡描寫理想的老師。好老師不只必須有耐心，也必須公平。

items.en: The chef explained her rules to the new cooks. Not only must the food be fresh, but it must also look good.
items.zh: 主廚對新廚師說明她的規則。食物不只必須新鮮，看起來也必須好看。

items.en: In my review I explain what I look for in a hotel. Not only must it be clean, but it must also be quiet.
items.zh: 我在評論裡說明我對飯店的要求。它不只必須乾淨，也必須安靜。

items.en: The town is choosing a plan for the new playground. Not only must the plan be cheap, but it must also be safe.
items.zh: 鎮上正在選新遊樂場的計畫。這個計畫不只必須便宜，也必須安全。

items.en: Our designers know what customers want. Not only must a website be fast, but it must also be easy to use.
items.zh: 我們的設計師知道顧客要什麼。網站不只必須快，也必須好用。

items.en: The city wants a new bridge over the river. Not only must the bridge be strong, but it must also be beautiful.
items.zh: 這個城市想在河上蓋一座新橋。這座橋不只必須堅固，也必須美觀。

items.en: The article asks what makes a good leader. Not only must a leader be clever, but he or she must also be honest.
items.zh: 那篇文章問什麼是好的領導者。領導者不只必須聰明，也必須誠實。

title: It's impossible for me to meet with you at six o'clock.
translation: 我六點不可能跟你見面。
name: it is 加形容詞加 for 受詞加不定詞
sentences: If you have to choose between two schools, I think it's important for you to know what they're like.

It's necessary for all visitors to sign in at reception.
It's important for children to play outside.
It's essential for the players to warm up before the match.
It's important for us to stay together in the crowd.
It was necessary for him to work at weekends.
It's important for parents to know their children's friends.
It's impossible for me to finish this by tomorrow.
Is it possible for you to come a bit earlier?
It was impossible for them to hear the speaker at the back.
It's possible for students to borrow laptops from the library.
It's impossible for my grandmother to climb those stairs.
It wasn't possible for us to get a table at that restaurant.
It's impossible for one person to do all this work.
It's easy for young children to learn languages.
It's difficult for me to get up early in winter.
It was hard for her to leave her home town.
It's not easy for him to talk about his feelings.
It's difficult for tourists to find this little café.
It was easy for us to find the hotel.
It's hard for my dad to read small print.
It's difficult for small shops to compete with supermarkets.
It's good for you to get some fresh air.
It's dangerous for children to play near the road.
It's bad for your eyes to read in the dark.
It's unusual for her to be late.
It's useful for travellers to carry some cash.
It's healthy for dogs to walk every day.
It's normal for teenagers to sleep late at the weekend.

examples.heading: ① It is + important / essential / necessary + for + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: If you have to choose between two schools, I think it's important for you to know what they're like.
items.zh: 如果你要在兩間學校之間選一間，我覺得你要先了解它們是什麼樣子，這很重要。

items.en: It is important for everyone to attend this meeting.
items.zh: 每個人都要出席這次會議，這很重要。

items.en: It's essential for me to go to the lesson, because I can't study physics by myself.
items.zh: 我一定要去上課，因為我沒辦法自己讀物理。

items.en: It's necessary for all visitors to sign in at reception.
items.zh: 所有訪客都必須在櫃台登記。

items.en: It's important for children to play outside.
items.zh: 小孩到戶外玩很重要。

items.en: It's essential for the players to warm up before the match.
items.zh: 球員比賽前一定要熱身。

items.en: It's important for us to stay together in the crowd.
items.zh: 在人群中我們要待在一起，這很重要。

items.en: It was necessary for him to work at weekends.
items.zh: 他週末必須上班。

items.en: It's important for parents to know their children's friends.
items.zh: 父母認識孩子的朋友很重要。

examples.heading: ② It is + possible / impossible + for + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: It's impossible for me to finish this by tomorrow.
items.zh: 我不可能明天之前做完這個。

items.en: Is it possible for you to come a bit earlier?
items.zh: 你有可能早一點來嗎？

items.en: It was impossible for them to hear the speaker at the back.
items.zh: 他們在後面根本聽不到講者說話。

items.en: It's possible for students to borrow laptops from the library.
items.zh: 學生可以向圖書館借筆電。

items.en: It's impossible for my grandmother to climb those stairs.
items.zh: 我奶奶不可能爬那些樓梯。

items.en: It wasn't possible for us to get a table at that restaurant.
items.zh: 我們在那家餐廳訂不到位子。

items.en: It's impossible for one person to do all this work.
items.zh: 一個人不可能做完這些工作。

examples.heading: ③ It is + easy / difficult / hard + for + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: It's easy for young children to learn languages.
items.zh: 小孩學語言很容易。

items.en: It's difficult for me to get up early in winter.
items.zh: 冬天我很難早起。

items.en: It was hard for her to leave her home town.
items.zh: 她很難離開她的家鄉。

items.en: It's not easy for him to talk about his feelings.
items.zh: 他很難說出自己的感受。

items.en: It's difficult for tourists to find this little café.
items.zh: 觀光客很難找到這家小咖啡店。

items.en: It was easy for us to find the hotel.
items.zh: 我們很容易就找到飯店了。

items.en: It's hard for my dad to read small print.
items.zh: 我爸很難看清楚小字。

items.en: It's difficult for small shops to compete with supermarkets.
items.zh: 小商店很難跟超市競爭。

examples.heading: ④ It is + good / bad / dangerous 和其他形容詞 + for + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: It's good for you to get some fresh air.
items.zh: 呼吸一點新鮮空氣對你有好處。

items.en: It's dangerous for children to play near the road.
items.zh: 小孩在馬路附近玩很危險。

items.en: It's bad for your eyes to read in the dark.
items.zh: 在暗處看書對眼睛不好。

items.en: It's unusual for her to be late.
items.zh: 她很少遲到。

items.en: It's useful for travellers to carry some cash.
items.zh: 旅行的人帶一點現金很有用。

items.en: It's healthy for dogs to walk every day.
items.zh: 狗每天散步很健康。

items.en: It's normal for teenagers to sleep late at the weekend.
items.zh: 青少年週末睡得晚很正常。

title: It's important that you eat healthy food.
translation: 你要吃健康的食物，這很重要。

examples.heading: ① It's important that + you + 動詞

items.en: It's important that you take breaks and don't work all the time.
items.zh: 你要休息，不要一直工作，這很重要。

items.en: It's important that you drink enough water in hot weather.
items.zh: 天氣熱的時候要喝足夠的水，這很重要。

items.en: It's important that you arrive on time for the interview.
items.zh: 面試要準時到，這很重要。

items.en: It's important that you tell your teacher about the problem.
items.zh: 你要把這個問題告訴老師，這很重要。

items.en: It's important that you wear a helmet on your bike.
items.zh: 騎腳踏車要戴安全帽，這很重要。

items.zh: 先讀說明很重要。
