It is possible that children learn more from games than from books.
It is possible that the train is delayed.
It's possible that we'll have to change our plans.
It is possible that the museum will close for a year.
It is possible that the company made a mistake.
It seems likely that the shop will close soon.
It seems possible that robots will do many of our jobs.
It seems likely that the bad weather will continue into next week.
It seems possible that the two problems are connected.
It seems likely that the minister will resign.
It seems possible that we misunderstood each other.
It seems likely that the twins will go to different schools.
It does not seem possible that prices will fall soon.
It doesn't seem likely that he will change his mind.
It is not likely that the factory will reopen.
It doesn't seem possible that she is already forty.
It is not possible that everyone will agree.
It does not seem likely that the plan will succeed.
It isn't likely that we'll see snow this winter.
It doesn't seem possible that the work can be done in a week.

examples.heading: ① It is likely / probable + that + 子句

items.en: It is likely that regular exercise will improve your sleep.
items.zh: 規律運動很可能會改善你的睡眠。

items.en: It is likely that more people will work from home in the future.
items.zh: 將來很可能會有更多人在家工作。

items.en: It is probable that the price of food will continue to rise.
items.zh: 食物的價格很可能會繼續上漲。

items.en: It's likely that the new law will reduce pollution.
items.zh: 新法律很可能會減少污染。

items.en: It is likely that most students will choose the easier course.
items.zh: 大部分的學生很可能會選比較簡單的課。

items.en: It is probable that the meeting will run late.
items.zh: 會議很可能會延後結束。

items.en: It's likely that she has already heard the news.
items.zh: 她很可能已經聽說了這個消息。

items.en: It is likely that the team will need more money.
items.zh: 這個團隊很可能需要更多錢。

examples.heading: ② It is possible + that + 子句

items.en: It is possible that the storm will reach the coast tonight.
items.zh: 暴風雨今晚有可能會到達海岸。

items.en: It is possible that the results are wrong.
items.zh: 結果有可能是錯的。

items.en: It's possible that he forgot about the appointment.
items.zh: 他有可能忘了約會。

items.en: It is possible that children learn more from games than from books.
items.zh: 小孩從遊戲學到的有可能比從書上學到的多。

items.en: It is possible that the train is delayed.
items.zh: 火車有可能誤點了。（被動）

items.en: It's possible that we'll have to change our plans.
items.zh: 我們有可能得改變計畫。

items.en: It is possible that the museum will close for a year.
items.zh: 博物館有可能會關閉一年。

items.en: It is possible that the company made a mistake.
items.zh: 那家公司有可能犯了錯。

examples.heading: ③ It seems + likely / possible + that + 子句

items.en: It seems likely that the shop will close soon.
items.zh: 那家店看起來很可能很快就會關門。

items.en: It seems possible that robots will do many of our jobs.
items.zh: 機器人看起來有可能會做我們很多工作。

items.en: It seems likely that the bad weather will continue into next week.
items.zh: 壞天氣看起來很可能會持續到下星期。

items.en: It seems possible that the two problems are connected.
items.zh: 這兩個問題看起來有可能有關。

items.en: It seems likely that the minister will resign.
items.zh: 部長看起來很可能會辭職。

items.en: It seems possible that we misunderstood each other.
items.zh: 我們看起來有可能誤會了彼此。

items.en: It seems likely that the twins will go to different schools.
items.zh: 雙胞胎看起來很可能會念不同的學校。

examples.heading: ④ 否定：It does not seem / is not + possible / likely + that + 子句

items.en: It does not seem possible that prices will fall soon.
items.zh: 物價似乎不可能很快下跌。

items.en: It doesn't seem likely that he will change his mind.
items.zh: 他似乎不太可能改變主意。

items.en: It is not likely that the factory will reopen.
items.zh: 工廠不太可能重新開工。

items.en: It doesn't seem possible that she is already forty.
items.zh: 她似乎不可能已經四十歲了。

items.en: It is not possible that everyone will agree.
items.zh: 不可能每個人都同意。

items.en: It does not seem likely that the plan will succeed.
items.zh: 這個計畫似乎不太可能成功。

items.en: It isn't likely that we'll see snow this winter.
items.zh: 今年冬天不太可能看到雪。

items.en: It doesn't seem possible that the work can be done in a week.
items.zh: 這項工作似乎不可能在一個星期內完成。（被動）

title: It is clear that we can't live without computers today.
translation: 很顯然，現在的我們已經離不開電腦了。
name: it 加連綴動詞加形容詞表示強調
sentences: Computers make our lives easier, but it is clear that we should never depend on machines.
It is obvious that the team played better in the second half.
It's clear that the town needs more parking spaces.
It is obvious that the students worked hard on this project.
It's clear that young people use their phones too much.
It is obvious the café has a new owner.
It's clear that the old system doesn't work any more.
It is obvious that everyone enjoyed the party.
It seems obvious that this oil comes from the petrol station.
It seems clear that the plan will cost too much.
It seems obvious that the two men know each other.
It seems clear that nobody read the instructions.
It seems obvious that we need a bigger room.
It seems clear that he was telling the truth.
It is crucial that we test the software before the launch.
It is essential that you know the advantages of our new product.
It is vital that everyone leaves the building quickly.
It's essential that the patient rests for a week.
It is crucial that we finish the report by Monday.
It is vital that you keep the receipt.
It's crucial that the children feel safe at school.
It is essential that all staff wear their badges.
It is surprising that so few people came to the meeting.
It is worrying that the river is getting dirtier.
It is interesting that both writers grew up in the same town.
It's amazing that the old car still runs.
It is unfortunate that the museum is closed on Mondays.
It's remarkable that she learned Chinese in two years.
It is significant that sales fell after the price rise.
It is disappointing that the hotel cancelled our booking.
It's odd the dog didn't bark.

examples.heading: ① It is + clear / obvious + that + 子句：引出結論

items.en: Computers make our lives easier, but it is clear that we should never depend on machines.
items.zh: 電腦讓我們的生活更方便，可是很顯然，我們絕不該依賴機器。

items.en: It is obvious that the team played better in the second half.
items.zh: 很明顯，這支隊伍下半場踢得比較好。

items.en: It's clear that the town needs more parking spaces.
items.zh: 很顯然，這個鎮需要更多停車位。

items.en: It is obvious that the students worked hard on this project.
items.zh: 很明顯，學生們在這個專案上很努力。

items.en: It's clear that young people use their phones too much.
items.zh: 很顯然，年輕人用手機用得太多了。

items.en: It is obvious the café has a new owner.
items.zh: 很明顯，那家咖啡店換老闆了。

items.en: It's clear that the old system doesn't work any more.
items.zh: 很顯然，舊的制度已經行不通了。

items.en: It is obvious that everyone enjoyed the party.
items.zh: 很明顯，大家都很喜歡這場派對。

examples.heading: ② It seems + clear / obvious + that + 子句

items.en: It seems obvious that this oil comes from the petrol station.
items.zh: 很明顯，這些油是從加油站來的。

items.en: It seems clear that the plan will cost too much.
items.zh: 看起來很清楚，這個計畫會花太多錢。

items.en: It seems obvious that the two men know each other.
items.zh: 看起來很明顯，那兩個男人互相認識。

items.en: It seems clear that nobody read the instructions.
items.zh: 看起來很清楚，沒有人讀過說明。

items.en: It seems obvious that we need a bigger room.
items.zh: 看起來很明顯，我們需要更大的房間。

items.en: It seems clear that he was telling the truth.
items.zh: 看起來很清楚，他說的是實話。

examples.heading: ③ It is + essential / crucial / vital + that + 子句：強調要求

items.en: It is crucial that we test the software before the launch.
items.zh: 上市前我們一定要先測試軟體。

items.en: It is essential that you know the advantages of our new product.
items.zh: 你一定要了解我們新產品的優點。

items.en: It is vital that everyone leaves the building quickly.
items.zh: 每個人都要迅速離開大樓，這極為重要。

items.en: It's essential that the patient rests for a week.
items.zh: 病人一定要休息一個星期。

items.en: It is crucial that we finish the report by Monday.
items.zh: 我們一定要在星期一前完成報告。

items.en: It is vital that you keep the receipt.
items.zh: 你一定要保留收據。

items.en: It's crucial that the children feel safe at school.
items.zh: 孩子們在學校覺得安全，這極為重要。

items.en: It is essential that all staff wear their badges.
items.zh: 所有員工都一定要戴識別證。

examples.heading: ④ It is + 其他形容詞 + that + 子句：強調

items.en: It is surprising that so few people came to the meeting.
items.zh: 令人意外的是，來開會的人這麼少。

items.en: It is worrying that the river is getting dirtier.
items.zh: 令人擔心的是，河水越來越髒。

items.en: It is interesting that both writers grew up in the same town.
items.zh: 有趣的是，兩位作家都在同一個小鎮長大。

items.en: It's amazing that the old car still runs.
items.zh: 令人驚訝的是，那台老車還能開。

items.en: It is unfortunate that the museum is closed on Mondays.
items.zh: 可惜的是，博物館星期一不開放。

items.en: It's remarkable that she learned Chinese in two years.
items.zh: 了不起的是，她兩年就學會了中文。

items.en: It is significant that sales fell after the price rise.
items.zh: 值得注意的是，漲價後銷售量下降了。

items.en: It is disappointing that the hotel cancelled our booking.
items.zh: 令人失望的是，飯店取消了我們的訂房。

items.en: It's odd the dog didn't bark.
items.zh: 奇怪的是，那隻狗沒有叫。

title: I may as well see the other things.
translation: 反正你也該知道了。
name: may as well 表示最合理的做法
sentences: The museum ticket includes the gardens, so I may as well see them.
We're already in town, so we may as well do the shopping.
You've come all this way, so you may as well stay for dinner.
The car is dirty anyway, so I may as well drive through the mud.
I'm up now, so I may as well make breakfast.
We've got the paint out, so we may as well do the kitchen too.
The last bus has gone. We may as well walk home.
Nobody else wants the last piece of cake, so I may as well eat it.
The shop is closed today. We may as well go back tomorrow.
It's raining too hard to play tennis. We may as well watch a film.
There's nothing on TV. I may as well go to bed early.
The train is an hour late, so we may as well get a coffee.
The meeting won't start for twenty minutes. You may as well sit down.
You may as well throw those old shoes away. Nobody will wear them.
You may as well take the bigger size. It's the same price.
You may as well ask her. The worst she can say is no.
If you're going to the post office, you may as well post my letter too.
You may as well keep the book. I've already read it.
After a long silence, she said, "You may as well know. I'm ill."
You may as well know the truth. I've lost my job.
I may as well tell you now. We're moving to Canada.
Everyone will find out soon, so we may as well tell them today.
You may as well hear it from me. The project has been cancelled.
I may as well admit it. I forgot your birthday.
If the weather is this bad, I may as well stay at home and read.
There's only one wall left, so we may as well finish the job now.
He may as well apply for the job. He's got nothing to lose.
Since the tickets are free, we may as well go.
The phone is broken. I may as well buy a new one.
The kids are already wet, so they may as well jump in the pool.
We've missed the first half, so we may as well wait for the next show.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + may as well + 原形動詞：已經在這裡，乾脆做

items.en: The museum ticket includes the gardens, so I may as well see them.
items.zh: 博物館的門票包含花園，我乾脆也去看一看。

items.en: We're already in town, so we may as well do the shopping.
items.zh: 我們已經在市區了，乾脆把東西買一買。

items.en: You've come all this way, so you may as well stay for dinner.
items.zh: 你大老遠來了，乾脆留下來吃晚餐吧。

items.en: The car is dirty anyway, so I may as well drive through the mud.
items.zh: 車子反正已經髒了，我乾脆直接開過泥巴路。

items.en: I'm up now, so I may as well make breakfast.
items.zh: 我已經起床了，乾脆做早餐吧。

items.en: We've got the paint out, so we may as well do the kitchen too.
items.zh: 油漆都拿出來了，我們乾脆把廚房也漆一漆。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + may as well + 原形動詞：沒有更好的選擇

items.en: The last bus has gone. We may as well walk home.
items.zh: 最後一班公車走了。我們不如走路回家吧。

items.en: Nobody else wants the last piece of cake, so I may as well eat it.
items.zh: 沒有人要最後一塊蛋糕，那我乾脆吃掉吧。

items.en: The shop is closed today. We may as well go back tomorrow.
items.zh: 那家店今天沒開。我們不如明天再來吧。

items.en: It's raining too hard to play tennis. We may as well watch a film.
items.zh: 雨太大不能打網球。我們不如看部電影吧。

items.en: There's nothing on TV. I may as well go to bed early.
items.zh: 電視沒什麼好看的。我不如早點睡覺。

items.en: The train is an hour late, so we may as well get a coffee.
items.zh: 火車誤點一個小時，我們不如去喝杯咖啡吧。

examples.heading: ③ You may as well + 原形動詞：給對方建議

items.en: The meeting won't start for twenty minutes. You may as well sit down.
items.zh: 會議還要二十分鐘才開始。你不如先坐下。

items.en: You may as well throw those old shoes away. Nobody will wear them.
items.zh: 你不如把那雙舊鞋丟掉吧。沒有人會穿。

items.en: You may as well take the bigger size. It's the same price.
items.zh: 你不如買大一號的。價錢一樣。

items.en: You may as well ask her. The worst she can say is no.
items.zh: 你不如直接問她。她頂多說不要。

items.en: If you're going to the post office, you may as well post my letter too.
items.zh: 如果你要去郵局，乾脆也幫我寄信吧。

items.en: You may as well keep the book. I've already read it.
items.zh: 你乾脆留著那本書吧。我已經讀過了。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + may as well + know / tell：說出真相

items.en: After a long silence, she said, "You may as well know. I'm ill."
items.zh: 沉默了很久，她說：你不如就知道吧。我生病了。

items.en: You may as well know the truth. I've lost my job.
items.zh: 你不如知道真相吧。我丟了工作。

items.en: I may as well tell you now. We're moving to Canada.
items.zh: 我不如現在就告訴你吧。我們要搬去加拿大了。

items.en: Everyone will find out soon, so we may as well tell them today.
items.zh: 大家很快就會知道，我們不如今天就告訴他們。

items.en: You may as well hear it from me. The project has been cancelled.
items.zh: 你不如從我這裡聽到吧。這個專案取消了。（被動）

items.en: I may as well admit it. I forgot your birthday.
items.zh: 我不如承認吧。我忘了你的生日。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + may as well + 原形動詞：做了也沒有壞處

items.en: If the weather is this bad, I may as well stay at home and read.
items.zh: 天氣這麼糟，我不如待在家裡看書。

items.en: There's only one wall left, so we may as well finish the job now.
items.zh: 只剩一面牆了，我們不如現在就把工作做完。

items.en: He may as well apply for the job. He's got nothing to lose.
items.zh: 他不如去應徵那份工作。他沒什麼好損失的。

items.en: Since the tickets are free, we may as well go.
items.zh: 既然票是免費的，我們不如去吧。

items.en: The phone is broken. I may as well buy a new one.
items.zh: 手機壞了。我不如買一支新的。

items.en: The kids are already wet, so they may as well jump in the pool.
items.zh: 孩子們已經濕了，乾脆讓他們跳進游泳池吧。

items.en: We've missed the first half, so we may as well wait for the next show.
items.zh: 我們錯過了前半場，不如等下一場吧。

title: It may well be that after leaving school they become our employees.
translation: 我認為他們很可能會在這些付款問題上達成協議。
name: may well 強調意外的可能
sentences: The two companies have talked for weeks. I think they may well come to an agreement on the payment problems.
If we keep working at this speed, we may well finish the project early.
With this new coach, the team may well reach the final.
If she keeps practising, she may well become a professional singer.
The book may well become a film one day.
Our little shop may well grow into a big business.
You may well be right about the date. Let me check.
That restaurant may well be the best in town.
The old painting in the attic may well be worth a lot of money.
He may well be the oldest man in the village.
This may well be the hottest summer for fifty years.
Her idea may well be the answer to our problem.
It may well be that the new road brings more customers to the town.
It may well be that the problem is in the software, not the machine.
It may well be that children learn more outside the classroom.
It may well be that she never got your letter.
It may well be that the cheaper hotel is better.
It may well be that people are happier with less.
Book early. The tickets may well sell out in a day.
Take a coat. The wind may well get stronger in the afternoon.
The new rules may well cause problems for small shops.
If you don't water the garden, the plants may well die.
The road may well be closed if it snows.
Without a map, we may well get lost in the forest.
You may well be tired, but we still have to finish this.
The plan may well save money, but it will take a long time.
He may well be clever, but he doesn't work hard.
The flat may well be cheap, but it's very far from the centre.
The test may well be difficult, but you're ready for it.
Prices may well go down, but nobody knows when.
The car may well be fast, but is it safe?

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + may well + 原形動詞：很有可能達成

items.en: The two companies have talked for weeks. I think they may well come to an agreement on the payment problems.
items.zh: 兩家公司談了好幾個星期。我想他們很有可能在付款的問題上達成協議。

items.en: If we keep working at this speed, we may well finish the project early.
items.zh: 如果我們保持這個速度，很有可能提早完成這個專案。

items.en: With this new coach, the team may well reach the final.
items.zh: 有了這個新教練，球隊很有可能打進決賽。

items.en: If she keeps practising, she may well become a professional singer.
items.zh: 如果她繼續練習，她很有可能成為職業歌手。

items.en: The book may well become a film one day.
items.zh: 這本書很有可能有一天會拍成電影。

items.en: Our little shop may well grow into a big business.
items.zh: 我們的小店很有可能發展成大企業。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + may well + be：很有可能是

items.en: You may well be right about the date. Let me check.
items.zh: 你對日期的說法很有可能是對的。我查一下。

items.en: That restaurant may well be the best in town.
items.zh: 那家餐廳很有可能是城裡最好的。

items.en: The old painting in the attic may well be worth a lot of money.
items.zh: 閣樓裡那幅舊畫很有可能很值錢。

items.en: He may well be the oldest man in the village.
items.zh: 他很有可能是村子裡年紀最大的人。

items.en: This may well be the hottest summer for fifty years.
items.zh: 這很有可能是五十年來最熱的夏天。

items.en: Her idea may well be the answer to our problem.
items.zh: 她的想法很有可能就是我們問題的答案。

examples.heading: ③ It may well be that + 子句：提出沒想到的可能

items.en: It may well be that the new road brings more customers to the town.
items.zh: 很有可能新路會為鎮上帶來更多客人。

items.en: It may well be that the problem is in the software, not the machine.
items.zh: 問題很有可能出在軟體，不在機器。

items.en: It may well be that children learn more outside the classroom.
items.zh: 孩子很有可能在教室外學到更多。

items.en: It may well be that she never got your letter.
items.zh: 她很有可能根本沒收到你的信。

items.en: It may well be that the cheaper hotel is better.
items.zh: 很有可能比較便宜的飯店比較好。

items.en: It may well be that people are happier with less.
items.zh: 很有可能人擁有少一點反而比較快樂。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + may well + 原形動詞：提醒可能的問題

items.en: Book early. The tickets may well sell out in a day.
items.zh: 早點訂。票很有可能一天就賣完。

items.en: Take a coat. The wind may well get stronger in the afternoon.
items.zh: 帶件外套。下午風很有可能變大。

items.en: The new rules may well cause problems for small shops.
items.zh: 新規定很有可能為小店帶來問題。

items.en: If you don't water the garden, the plants may well die.
items.zh: 如果你不幫花園澆水，植物很有可能會死。

items.en: The road may well be closed if it snows.
items.zh: 如果下雪，那條路很有可能會封閉。

items.en: Without a map, we may well get lost in the forest.
items.zh: 沒有地圖，我們很有可能在森林裡迷路。

examples.heading: ⑤ may well + 原形動詞, but + 句子：承認，再提出另一面

items.en: You may well be tired, but we still have to finish this.
items.zh: 你很有可能累了，可是我們還是要把這個做完。

items.en: The plan may well save money, but it will take a long time.
items.zh: 這個計畫很有可能省錢，可是要花很長的時間。

items.en: He may well be clever, but he doesn't work hard.
items.zh: 他很有可能很聰明，可是他不認真。

items.en: The flat may well be cheap, but it's very far from the centre.
items.zh: 那間公寓很有可能很便宜，可是離市中心很遠。

items.en: The test may well be difficult, but you're ready for it.
items.zh: 考試很有可能很難，可是你已經準備好了。

items.en: Prices may well go down, but nobody knows when.
items.zh: 價格很有可能會下降，可是沒有人知道什麼時候。

items.en: The car may well be fast, but is it safe?
items.zh: 這台車很有可能很快，可是它安全嗎？

title: It is probably in the sitting room on the table.
translation: 這一定會弄得亂七八糟。
name: 句中的情態副詞表示保留或強調
sentences: You played games in the sitting room last night. Your phone is probably in there on the table.
You wore your blue jacket yesterday, so your keys are probably still in its pocket.
The cat is probably asleep under the bed.
Dad is probably still at the office.
The scissors are probably in the kitchen drawer.
Your football boots are probably in the car.
We're painting the kitchen today. It's definitely going to get messy, so wear old clothes.
The sky over the hills has gone black. It's definitely going to pour soon.
The party is certainly going to be fun.
That old tree is definitely going to fall in the next storm.
The exam is definitely going to be hard this year.
The shop is certainly going to be busy on Saturday.
It's going to be very hot. You should probably wear a T-shirt and shorts, with trainers.
You should probably call your mum. She's worried.
We should probably leave now. It's getting late.
You should probably take an umbrella.
I should probably go to bed. I have school tomorrow.
You should probably ask the teacher first.
I'll probably be home by six.
Mum collects old teapots, so she'll definitely love this one.
The bus will probably be late again.
We'll definitely come to your party.
It'll probably snow in the mountains tonight.
Our neighbours will certainly complain about the noise from the party.
The lights in the bakery are off, so it is probably shut for the holiday.
That restaurant is definitely the best in town.
It's only April, so the lake is probably still freezing.
She is certainly the fastest runner in our class.
The film is probably too long for the children.
This is definitely the right road.
Grandpa has just arrived from Australia, so he is probably very sleepy.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + be + probably + 地方：猜東西在哪裡

items.en: You played games in the sitting room last night. Your phone is probably in there on the table.
items.zh: 你昨天晚上在客廳打電動。你的手機大概在那裡的桌子上。

items.en: You wore your blue jacket yesterday, so your keys are probably still in its pocket.
items.zh: 你昨天穿了藍色夾克，所以你的鑰匙大概還在它的口袋裡。

items.en: The cat is probably asleep under the bed.
items.zh: 貓大概在床底下睡覺。

items.en: Dad is probably still at the office.
items.zh: 爸爸大概還在辦公室。

items.en: The scissors are probably in the kitchen drawer.
items.zh: 剪刀大概在廚房的抽屜裡。

items.en: Your football boots are probably in the car.
items.zh: 你的足球鞋大概在車上。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + be + definitely / certainly + going to + 原形動詞

items.en: We're painting the kitchen today. It's definitely going to get messy, so wear old clothes.
items.zh: 我們今天要油漆廚房。一定會弄得很髒亂，所以穿舊衣服。

items.en: The sky over the hills has gone black. It's definitely going to pour soon.
items.zh: 山丘上的天空變黑了。一定很快就會下大雨。

items.en: The party is certainly going to be fun.
items.zh: 派對一定會很好玩。

items.en: That old tree is definitely going to fall in the next storm.
items.zh: 那棵老樹下次暴風雨一定會倒。

items.en: The exam is definitely going to be hard this year.
items.zh: 今年的考試一定會很難。

items.en: The shop is certainly going to be busy on Saturday.
items.zh: 那家店星期六一定會很多人。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + should probably + 原形動詞：委婉的建議

items.en: It's going to be very hot. You should probably wear a T-shirt and shorts, with trainers.
items.zh: 天氣會很熱。你大概應該穿T恤和短褲，配運動鞋。

items.en: You should probably call your mum. She's worried.
items.zh: 你大概應該打給你媽媽。她很擔心。

items.en: We should probably leave now. It's getting late.
items.zh: 我們大概應該現在走了。很晚了。

items.en: You should probably take an umbrella.
items.zh: 你大概應該帶把傘。

items.en: I should probably go to bed. I have school tomorrow.
items.zh: 我大概應該去睡了。我明天要上學。

items.en: You should probably ask the teacher first.
items.zh: 你大概應該先問老師。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + will + probably / definitely + 原形動詞

items.en: I'll probably be home by six.
items.zh: 我大概六點前會到家。

items.en: Mum collects old teapots, so she'll definitely love this one.
items.zh: 媽媽收集舊茶壺，所以她一定會很喜歡這一個。

items.en: The bus will probably be late again.
items.zh: 公車大概又會誤點。

items.en: We'll definitely come to your party.
items.zh: 我們一定會去你的派對。

items.en: It'll probably snow in the mountains tonight.
items.zh: 今天晚上山上大概會下雪。

items.en: Our neighbours will certainly complain about the noise from the party.
items.zh: 我們的鄰居一定會抱怨派對的噪音。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + be + probably / definitely + 形容詞

items.en: The lights in the bakery are off, so it is probably shut for the holiday.
items.zh: 麵包店的燈都關了，所以大概放假沒開。

items.en: That restaurant is definitely the best in town.
items.zh: 那家餐廳一定是城裡最好的。

items.en: It's only April, so the lake is probably still freezing.
items.zh: 現在才四月，所以湖水大概還冰得要命。

items.en: She is certainly the fastest runner in our class.
items.zh: 她一定是我們班跑得最快的。

items.en: The film is probably too long for the children.
items.zh: 那部電影對孩子們來說大概太長了。

items.en: This is definitely the right road.
items.zh: 這一定是對的路。

items.en: Grandpa has just arrived from Australia, so he is probably very sleepy.
items.zh: 爺爺剛從澳洲回來，所以他大概很睏。

title: You would certainly meet a lot of cool people, and you'd probably find it great.
translation: 你大概該帶防曬乳，因為天氣會很熱。
name: 情態動詞加情態副詞
sentences: If you chose the big school in the centre of town, you would certainly meet a lot of cool people, and you'd probably find it great.
A dog would certainly make your grandmother less lonely.
You would probably enjoy the film more in English.
A week by the sea would certainly help you forget about work.
The children would probably prefer pizza to fish.
A bigger kitchen would certainly make cooking easier.
It's going to be hot at the beach, so you should probably bring sun cream and some food.
You should probably book a table before Saturday.
We should probably leave before the traffic gets bad.
You should probably tell your boss about the mistake.
I should probably start my essay this weekend.
You should probably wear boots. The path is muddy.
Don't be sad about this summer. Next year you can surely go somewhere with your friends.
With your talent, you can surely become a professional singer.
If you practise every day, you can surely pass the test.
You've saved enough money, so you can surely buy a new bike.
You speak French well, so you can surely get a job in Paris.
With a map, you can surely find the way.
I will definitely visit you when I'm in London.
The roadworks will probably finish before the end of the month.
She will definitely win a prize for her painting.
We will probably need more chairs for the party.
The new road will definitely help the local shops.
It will probably take an hour to get there.
We might possibly go to Italy in the summer.
The meeting could possibly move to Friday.
She might possibly be at her sister's house.
The weather could possibly get worse tonight.
They might possibly sell the farm next year.
The price could possibly go up again.
I might possibly be a little late tomorrow.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + would + certainly / probably + 原形動詞

items.en: If you chose the big school in the centre of town, you would certainly meet a lot of cool people, and you'd probably find it great.
items.zh: 如果你選城中心那所大學校，你一定會認識很多很酷的人，而且你大概會覺得很棒。

items.en: A dog would certainly make your grandmother less lonely.
items.zh: 一隻狗一定會讓你奶奶比較不寂寞。

items.en: You would probably enjoy the film more in English.
items.zh: 你看英文版的電影大概會比較喜歡。

items.en: A week by the sea would certainly help you forget about work.
items.zh: 在海邊待一個星期一定會幫你忘掉工作。

items.en: The children would probably prefer pizza to fish.
items.zh: 孩子們大概會比較喜歡披薩，不喜歡魚。

items.en: A bigger kitchen would certainly make cooking easier.
items.zh: 大一點的廚房一定會讓煮飯比較容易。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + should + probably + 原形動詞：委婉的建議

items.en: It's going to be hot at the beach, so you should probably bring sun cream and some food.
items.zh: 海灘會很熱，所以你大概應該帶防曬乳和一些食物。

items.en: You should probably book a table before Saturday.
items.zh: 你大概應該在星期六前訂位。

items.en: We should probably leave before the traffic gets bad.
items.zh: 我們大概應該在塞車之前出發。

items.en: You should probably tell your boss about the mistake.
items.zh: 你大概應該把那個錯告訴你的老闆。

items.en: I should probably start my essay this weekend.
items.zh: 我大概應該這個週末開始寫作文。

items.en: You should probably wear boots. The path is muddy.
items.zh: 你大概應該穿靴子。小路很泥濘。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + can + surely + 原形動詞：鼓勵對方

items.en: Don't be sad about this summer. Next year you can surely go somewhere with your friends.
items.zh: 別為今年夏天難過。明年你一定可以跟朋友去哪裡玩。

items.en: With your talent, you can surely become a professional singer.
items.zh: 以你的天分，你一定可以成為職業歌手。

items.en: If you practise every day, you can surely pass the test.
items.zh: 如果你每天練習，你一定可以通過考試。

items.en: You've saved enough money, so you can surely buy a new bike.
items.zh: 你存了夠多的錢，所以你一定可以買一台新的腳踏車。

items.en: You speak French well, so you can surely get a job in Paris.
items.zh: 你法文說得很好，所以你一定可以在巴黎找到工作。

items.en: With a map, you can surely find the way.
items.zh: 有了地圖，你一定可以找到路。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + will + definitely / probably + 原形動詞

items.en: I will definitely visit you when I'm in London.
items.zh: 我在倫敦的時候一定會去看你。

items.en: The roadworks will probably finish before the end of the month.
items.zh: 道路施工大概會在月底前結束。

items.en: She will definitely win a prize for her painting.
items.zh: 她的畫一定會得獎。

items.en: We will probably need more chairs for the party.
items.zh: 派對我們大概會需要多一些椅子。

items.en: The new road will definitely help the local shops.
items.zh: 新的道路一定會幫助當地的商店。

items.en: It will probably take an hour to get there.
items.zh: 到那裡大概要一個小時。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + might / could + possibly + 原形動詞：很不確定

items.en: We might possibly go to Italy in the summer.
items.zh: 我們夏天也許可能會去義大利。

items.en: The meeting could possibly move to Friday.
items.zh: 會議可能會改到星期五。

items.en: She might possibly be at her sister's house.
items.zh: 她也許可能在她姊姊家。

items.en: The weather could possibly get worse tonight.
items.zh: 今天晚上天氣可能會變得更糟。

items.en: They might possibly sell the farm next year.
items.zh: 他們明年也許可能會賣掉農場。

items.en: The price could possibly go up again.
items.zh: 價格可能會再上漲。

items.en: I might possibly be a little late tomorrow.
items.zh: 我明天也許可能會晚一點到。

title: It is highly unlikely that the goods could vanish from your warehouse without anyone noticing.
translation: 貨物極不可能在沒人發現的情況下從你們的倉庫消失。
name: 副詞修飾形容詞表示強調
sentences: It is highly unlikely that the bank made a mistake.
It is highly likely that interest rates will rise this year.
It's highly unusual for him to miss a meeting.
It is highly unlikely that the shop will give you a refund.
It is highly probable that the minister knew about the problem.
It's highly unlikely that we'll see each other again.
It is painfully obvious that the team needs a new coach.
It was painfully clear that she didn't want to be there.
It is perfectly clear that the rules have changed.
It's perfectly possible that the letter got lost in the post.
It is perfectly normal to feel nervous before an exam.
It was painfully obvious that the actor had forgotten his lines.
It's perfectly reasonable that you want more time.
It is absolutely essential that you bring your passport.
It's absolutely certain that the factory will close.
It is extremely important that you keep this information private.
It is absolutely impossible to finish the job by Friday.
It's extremely difficult to get a visa for that country.
It is absolutely vital that we protect the forest.
It is extremely unlikely that he will apologise.
It is deeply worrying that so many young people can't find work.
It was bitterly disappointing that we lost in the last minute.
It's incredibly lucky that nobody was hurt.
It is deeply unfair that the workers lost their pensions.
It's incredibly kind of you to drive us home.
The traffic in the city centre is painfully slow at rush hour.
Her reasons for leaving the club are perfectly understandable.
This medicine is highly effective against headaches.
The new manager is extremely popular with the staff.
Her decision was absolutely right.
The results were deeply disappointing for the whole team.

examples.heading: ① It is + highly + 形容詞

items.en: It is highly unlikely that the bank made a mistake.
items.zh: 銀行極不可能出錯。

items.en: It is highly likely that interest rates will rise this year.
items.zh: 今年利率極有可能上升。

items.en: It's highly unusual for him to miss a meeting.
items.zh: 他缺席會議是非常少見的事。

items.en: It is highly unlikely that the shop will give you a refund.
items.zh: 那家店極不可能退錢給你。

items.en: It is highly probable that the minister knew about the problem.
items.zh: 部長極有可能知道這個問題。

items.en: It's highly unlikely that we'll see each other again.
items.zh: 我們極不可能再見面了。

examples.heading: ② It is + painfully / perfectly + 形容詞

items.en: It is painfully obvious that the team needs a new coach.
items.zh: 再明顯不過，這支隊伍需要新教練。

items.en: It was painfully clear that she didn't want to be there.
items.zh: 再清楚不過，她不想待在那裡。

items.en: It is perfectly clear that the rules have changed.
items.zh: 規定已經改了，這點非常清楚。

items.en: It's perfectly possible that the letter got lost in the post.
items.zh: 那封信非常有可能在郵寄途中弄丟了。

items.en: It is perfectly normal to feel nervous before an exam.
items.zh: 考試前覺得緊張是完全正常的。

items.en: It was painfully obvious that the actor had forgotten his lines.
items.zh: 再明顯不過，那個演員忘詞了。

items.en: It's perfectly reasonable that you want more time.
items.zh: 你想要更多時間是完全合理的。

examples.heading: ③ It is + absolutely / extremely + 形容詞

items.en: It is absolutely essential that you bring your passport.
items.zh: 你一定要帶護照。

items.en: It's absolutely certain that the factory will close.
items.zh: 工廠一定會關閉，這點絕對確定。

items.en: It is extremely important that you keep this information private.
items.zh: 你要把這個資訊保密，這極為重要。

items.en: It is absolutely impossible to finish the job by Friday.
items.zh: 星期五前完成這項工作是絕對不可能的。

items.en: It's extremely difficult to get a visa for that country.
items.zh: 要拿到那個國家的簽證極為困難。

items.en: It is absolutely vital that we protect the forest.
items.zh: 我們一定要保護森林，這極為重要。

items.en: It is extremely unlikely that he will apologise.
items.zh: 他極不可能道歉。

examples.heading: ④ It is + deeply / bitterly / incredibly + 形容詞

items.en: It is deeply worrying that so many young people can't find work.
items.zh: 這麼多年輕人找不到工作，令人非常擔心。

items.en: It was bitterly disappointing that we lost in the last minute.
items.zh: 我們在最後一分鐘輸了，令人非常失望。

items.en: It's incredibly lucky that nobody was hurt.
items.zh: 沒有人受傷，真是非常幸運。（被動）

items.en: It is deeply unfair that the workers lost their pensions.
items.zh: 工人失去了退休金，這非常不公平。

items.en: It's incredibly kind of you to drive us home.
items.zh: 你開車送我們回家，真是太好了。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + is + 副詞 + 形容詞

items.en: The traffic in the city centre is painfully slow at rush hour.
items.zh: 尖峰時間市中心的交通慢得要命。

items.en: Her reasons for leaving the club are perfectly understandable.
items.zh: 她退出社團的理由完全可以理解。

items.en: This medicine is highly effective against headaches.
items.zh: 這種藥對頭痛非常有效。

items.en: The new manager is extremely popular with the staff.
items.zh: 新經理非常受員工歡迎。

items.en: Her decision was absolutely right.
items.zh: 她的決定完全正確。

items.en: The results were deeply disappointing for the whole team.
items.zh: 這個結果讓整個團隊非常失望。

title: It is almost certain that we'll have fights in the future, but we will probably overcome them.
translation: 我們將來幾乎一定會吵架，不過我們大概都能克服。
name: 副詞修飾形容詞表示委婉
sentences: It is almost certain that the price of petrol will go up.
It is nearly certain that the shop will raise its prices.
It is almost certain that the meeting will run over time.
It's almost impossible that nobody saw the accident.
It is nearly certain that the team will go down this season.
It's almost certain that she'll get the job.
It's nearly certain that our flight will leave late tonight.
It is quite probable that the flight will be delayed.
It's fairly likely that we'll need more chairs.
It is quite possible that he forgot to send the email.
It's fairly certain that the shop will close next year.
It is quite likely that the rain will stop by noon.
It is fairly clear that the plan needs more work.
It's quite possible that I'm wrong about this.
It's reasonably certain that the bridge will open in May.
If the shop is closed, which is fairly likely on a Sunday, we'll go to the market.
The results, which are fairly predictable, will come out next week.
A small delay is quite likely, so leave early.
His story is fairly believable.
A change in the timetable is quite possible.
Her answer was rather surprising.
The weather forecast is fairly accurate this week.
It is not entirely clear that the new system is better.
It's not completely certain that the concert will go ahead.
It is not entirely true that all teenagers are lazy.
It's not entirely impossible that they will change their minds.
It is not completely clear who will pay for the repairs.
It is not entirely certain that the company made a profit.
It's almost certain that we'll disagree, but we will probably find a solution.
It is quite likely that the train will be late, so we'll probably take a taxi.
It is fairly certain that it will rain, so the party will probably move indoors.

examples.heading: ① It is + almost / nearly + 形容詞 + that + 子句

items.en: It is almost certain that the price of petrol will go up.
items.zh: 油價幾乎一定會上漲。

items.en: It is nearly certain that the shop will raise its prices.
items.zh: 那家店幾乎一定會漲價。

items.en: It is almost certain that the meeting will run over time.
items.zh: 會議幾乎一定會超過時間。

items.en: It's almost impossible that nobody saw the accident.
items.zh: 幾乎不可能沒有人看到那場意外。

items.en: It is nearly certain that the team will go down this season.
items.zh: 這支隊伍這一季幾乎一定會降級。

items.en: It's almost certain that she'll get the job.
items.zh: 她幾乎一定會得到那份工作。

items.en: It's nearly certain that our flight will leave late tonight.
items.zh: 我們今晚的班機幾乎一定會晚起飛。

examples.heading: ② It is + quite / fairly + 形容詞 + that + 子句

items.en: It is quite probable that the flight will be delayed.
items.zh: 班機相當有可能會延誤。（被動）

items.en: It's fairly likely that we'll need more chairs.
items.zh: 我們還算有可能需要更多椅子。

items.en: It is quite possible that he forgot to send the email.
items.zh: 他相當有可能忘了寄那封電子郵件。

items.en: It's fairly certain that the shop will close next year.
items.zh: 那家店明年會關門，這一點還算確定。

items.en: It is quite likely that the rain will stop by noon.
items.zh: 雨中午前停的可能性相當高。

items.en: It is fairly clear that the plan needs more work.
items.zh: 這個計畫還需要再改，這點還算清楚。

items.en: It's quite possible that I'm wrong about this.
items.zh: 這件事我相當有可能弄錯了。

items.en: It's reasonably certain that the bridge will open in May.
items.zh: 那座橋五月會通車，這一點還算確定。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + is + 程度副詞 + 形容詞

items.en: If the shop is closed, which is fairly likely on a Sunday, we'll go to the market.
items.zh: 如果那家店沒開（星期天還算有可能），我們就去市場。

items.en: The results, which are fairly predictable, will come out next week.
items.zh: 結果相當容易預測，下星期會公布。

items.en: A small delay is quite likely, so leave early.
items.zh: 有一點延誤相當有可能，所以早點出發。

items.en: His story is fairly believable.
items.zh: 他的說法還算可信。

items.en: A change in the timetable is quite possible.
items.zh: 時刻表相當有可能會改。

items.en: Her answer was rather surprising.
items.zh: 她的回答有點令人意外。

items.en: The weather forecast is fairly accurate this week.
items.zh: 這週的天氣預報還算準。

examples.heading: ④ It is + not entirely / not completely + 形容詞 + that + 子句

items.en: It is not entirely clear that the new system is better.
items.zh: 新系統比較好這一點並不完全清楚。

items.en: It's not completely certain that the concert will go ahead.
items.zh: 音樂會不完全確定會照常舉行。

items.en: It is not entirely true that all teenagers are lazy.
items.zh: 所有青少年都很懶，這並不完全正確。

items.en: It's not entirely impossible that they will change their minds.
items.zh: 他們改變主意並不是完全不可能。

items.en: It is not completely clear who will pay for the repairs.
items.zh: 誰要付修理費並不完全清楚。

items.en: It is not entirely certain that the company made a profit.
items.zh: 那家公司有沒有獲利並不完全確定。

examples.heading: ⑤ 程度副詞加形容詞加 probably：更委婉

items.en: It's almost certain that we'll disagree, but we will probably find a solution.
items.zh: 我們幾乎一定會意見不合，不過我們大概會找到解決辦法。

items.en: It is quite likely that the train will be late, so we'll probably take a taxi.
items.zh: 火車相當有可能會誤點，所以我們大概會搭計程車。

items.en: It is fairly certain that it will rain, so the party will probably move indoors.
items.zh: 會下雨這一點還算確定，所以派對大概會移到室內。

title: She didn't dare think about him.
translation: 她不敢去想他。
name: didn't dare 加原形不定詞
sentences: She didn't dare think about what the test might show.
We didn't dare move until the guard walked away.
The boy didn't dare open his eyes during the storm.
I didn't dare breathe when the bear walked past our tent.
He didn't dare look down from the edge of the cliff.
They didn't dare make a sound while the soldiers searched the house.
She didn't dare turn around, because she heard footsteps behind her.
The children didn't dare go near the old well.
I didn't dare check my phone until the plane landed.
We didn't dare walk on the ice in case it broke.
She didn't dare tell her husband about the letter.
He didn't dare ask what had happened to his brother.
I didn't dare imagine what the doctor would say.
They didn't dare hope for good news.
My mother didn't dare read the rest of the letter.
He didn't dare admit that he had lost the money.
We didn't dare speak about the accident at dinner.
She didn't dare open the envelope with her exam results.
He didn't dare call her after their argument.
I didn't dare say what I really thought.
I didn't dare speak in case he got angry again.
We didn't dare leave the house because of the wolves.
She didn't dare sleep in case the baby woke up.
He didn't dare stop running in case they caught him.
I didn't dare touch anything because it all looked so expensive.
They didn't dare light a fire in case someone saw the smoke.
She didn't dare to look at the photographs.
We didn't dare to go back into the burning building.
He didn't dare to complain about the food.
I didn't dare to ask for more money.
They didn't dare to cross the bridge in the wind.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + didn't dare + 原形動詞：害怕

items.en: She didn't dare think about what the test might show.
items.zh: 她不敢去想檢查結果可能會是什麼。

items.en: We didn't dare move until the guard walked away.
items.zh: 警衛走開之前，我們都不敢動。

items.en: The boy didn't dare open his eyes during the storm.
items.zh: 暴風雨的時候，那個男孩不敢睜開眼睛。

items.en: I didn't dare breathe when the bear walked past our tent.
items.zh: 熊走過我們帳篷的時候，我連呼吸都不敢。

items.en: He didn't dare look down from the edge of the cliff.
items.zh: 他站在懸崖邊不敢往下看。

items.en: They didn't dare make a sound while the soldiers searched the house.
items.zh: 士兵搜房子的時候，他們一點聲音都不敢出。

items.en: She didn't dare turn around, because she heard footsteps behind her.
items.zh: 她不敢回頭，因為她聽到身後有腳步聲。

items.en: The children didn't dare go near the old well.
items.zh: 孩子們不敢靠近那口老井。

items.en: I didn't dare check my phone until the plane landed.
items.zh: 飛機降落之前，我不敢看手機。

items.en: We didn't dare walk on the ice in case it broke.
items.zh: 我們不敢走在冰上，怕冰會裂開。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + didn't dare + 原形動詞：不敢面對

items.en: She didn't dare tell her husband about the letter.
items.zh: 她不敢跟丈夫說那封信的事。

items.en: He didn't dare ask what had happened to his brother.
items.zh: 他不敢問他哥哥發生了什麼事。

items.en: I didn't dare imagine what the doctor would say.
items.zh: 我不敢想像醫生會說什麼。

items.en: They didn't dare hope for good news.
items.zh: 他們不敢期待好消息。

items.en: My mother didn't dare read the rest of the letter.
items.zh: 我媽媽不敢讀信的其他部分。

items.en: He didn't dare admit that he had lost the money.
items.zh: 他不敢承認他把錢弄丟了。

items.en: We didn't dare speak about the accident at dinner.
items.zh: 我們不敢在晚餐時談那場意外。

items.en: She didn't dare open the envelope with her exam results.
items.zh: 她不敢打開裝著考試成績的信封。

items.en: He didn't dare call her after their argument.
items.zh: 吵架之後，他不敢打電話給她。

items.en: I didn't dare say what I really thought.
items.zh: 我不敢說出我真正的想法。

examples.heading: ③ didn't dare + 原形動詞 + in case / because ...

items.en: I didn't dare speak in case he got angry again.
items.zh: 我不敢說話，怕他又生氣。

items.en: We didn't dare leave the house because of the wolves.
items.zh: 因為有狼，我們不敢離開房子。

items.en: She didn't dare sleep in case the baby woke up.
items.zh: 她不敢睡，怕寶寶醒來。

items.en: He didn't dare stop running in case they caught him.
items.zh: 他不敢停下來，怕被他們抓到。

items.en: I didn't dare touch anything because it all looked so expensive.
items.zh: 我什麼都不敢碰，因為看起來都很貴。

items.en: They didn't dare light a fire in case someone saw the smoke.
items.zh: 他們不敢生火，怕有人看到煙。

examples.heading: ④ didn't dare to + 原形動詞：加 to 的寫法

items.en: She didn't dare to look at the photographs.
items.zh: 她不敢看那些照片。

items.en: We didn't dare to go back into the burning building.
items.zh: 我們不敢回到失火的大樓裡。

items.en: He didn't dare to complain about the food.
items.zh: 他不敢抱怨那些食物。

items.en: I didn't dare to ask for more money.
items.zh: 我不敢要求更多錢。

items.en: They didn't dare to cross the bridge in the wind.
items.zh: 起風的時候，他們不敢過那座橋。

title: What we wear doesn't necessarily define who we are, but it does play a big part.
translation: 老一輩的人不一定會這樣看。
name: not necessarily 表示不一定
sentences: As a conclusion, while what we wear doesn't necessarily define who we are, it does play a big part in it.
Money doesn't necessarily make people happy.
A good degree doesn't necessarily lead to a good job.
Hard work doesn't necessarily bring success, but it helps.
A famous name doesn't necessarily mean good quality.
Living in the city doesn't necessarily mean a better life.
Expensive restaurants are not necessarily the best ones.
Old people are not necessarily bad with technology.
The fastest way is not necessarily the safest.
A big school is not necessarily better than a small one.
New things are not necessarily better than old ones.
Quiet students are not necessarily shy.
Young people love social media. This is not necessarily the way the older generation would see it, though.
This is not necessarily the best time to buy a house.
That is not necessarily the only answer.
This is not necessarily what the customers want.
Winning is not necessarily the most important thing.
A university degree is not necessarily the right choice for everyone.
Children don't necessarily need expensive toys to be happy.
People who live by the sea don't necessarily like swimming.
Teachers don't necessarily know all the answers.
Tourists don't necessarily want to see the famous places.
Good players don't necessarily make good coaches.
Students who talk a lot don't necessarily understand more.
If someone is quiet, it doesn't necessarily mean they're unhappy.
A low price doesn't necessarily mean poor quality.
Failing once doesn't necessarily mean you'll fail again.
Being tired doesn't necessarily mean you're ill.
A busy restaurant doesn't necessarily mean the food is good.
Getting a bad mark doesn't necessarily mean you're not clever.
Being rich doesn't necessarily mean being happy.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + doesn't + necessarily + 原形動詞：一般看法有例外

items.en: As a conclusion, while what we wear doesn't necessarily define who we are, it does play a big part in it.
items.zh: 總結來說，雖然我們穿什麼不一定代表我們是誰，可是它確實很重要。

items.en: Money doesn't necessarily make people happy.
items.zh: 錢不一定能讓人快樂。

items.en: A good degree doesn't necessarily lead to a good job.
items.zh: 好的學歷不一定能帶來好工作。

items.en: Hard work doesn't necessarily bring success, but it helps.
items.zh: 努力不一定帶來成功，可是有幫助。

items.en: A famous name doesn't necessarily mean good quality.
items.zh: 有名的品牌不一定代表好品質。

items.en: Living in the city doesn't necessarily mean a better life.
items.zh: 住在城市不一定代表比較好的生活。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + be + not necessarily + 形容詞：不一定是那樣

items.en: Expensive restaurants are not necessarily the best ones.
items.zh: 昂貴的餐廳不一定是最好的。

items.en: Old people are not necessarily bad with technology.
items.zh: 老人不一定不會用科技產品。

items.en: The fastest way is not necessarily the safest.
items.zh: 最快的路不一定最安全。

items.en: A big school is not necessarily better than a small one.
items.zh: 大學校不一定比小學校好。

items.en: New things are not necessarily better than old ones.
items.zh: 新東西不一定比舊東西好。

items.en: Quiet students are not necessarily shy.
items.zh: 安靜的學生不一定害羞。

examples.heading: ③ This is not necessarily + 名詞：不同的看法

items.en: Young people love social media. This is not necessarily the way the older generation would see it, though.
items.zh: 年輕人很喜歡社群媒體。不過，年長的一代不一定會這樣看。

items.en: This is not necessarily the best time to buy a house.
items.zh: 現在不一定是買房子的最好時機。

items.en: That is not necessarily the only answer.
items.zh: 那不一定是唯一的答案。

items.en: This is not necessarily what the customers want.
items.zh: 這不一定是顧客想要的。

items.en: Winning is not necessarily the most important thing.
items.zh: 贏不一定是最重要的事。

items.en: A university degree is not necessarily the right choice for everyone.
items.zh: 大學學歷不一定是每個人的正確選擇。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + don't + necessarily + 原形動詞：人不一定會這樣

items.en: Children don't necessarily need expensive toys to be happy.
items.zh: 孩子不一定需要昂貴的玩具才會快樂。

items.en: People who live by the sea don't necessarily like swimming.
items.zh: 住在海邊的人不一定喜歡游泳。

items.en: Teachers don't necessarily know all the answers.
items.zh: 老師不一定知道所有的答案。

items.en: Tourists don't necessarily want to see the famous places.
items.zh: 觀光客不一定想看有名的景點。

items.en: Good players don't necessarily make good coaches.
items.zh: 好的球員不一定能成為好的教練。

items.en: Students who talk a lot don't necessarily understand more.
items.zh: 話多的學生不一定懂得比較多。

examples.heading: ⑤ It doesn't necessarily mean + 子句

items.en: If someone is quiet, it doesn't necessarily mean they're unhappy.
items.zh: 如果有人很安靜，不一定代表他們不快樂。

items.en: A low price doesn't necessarily mean poor quality.
items.zh: 低價不一定代表品質差。

items.en: Failing once doesn't necessarily mean you'll fail again.
items.zh: 失敗一次不一定代表你會再失敗。

items.en: Being tired doesn't necessarily mean you're ill.
items.zh: 累不一定代表你生病了。

items.en: A busy restaurant doesn't necessarily mean the food is good.
items.zh: 人多的餐廳不一定代表東西好吃。

items.en: Getting a bad mark doesn't necessarily mean you're not clever.
items.zh: 拿到很差的分數不一定代表你不聰明。

items.en: Being rich doesn't necessarily mean being happy.
items.zh: 有錢不一定代表快樂。

title: As you may have noticed, there has been a delay setting up the new computer system.
translation: 我想，那次意外的事他可能已經原諒我了。
name: may have 表示過去的可能
sentences: As you may have noticed, the lift is out of order again.
As you may have heard, our manager is leaving at the end of the month.
As you may have seen in the news, the bridge will be closed for a week.
As you may have guessed, the party is a surprise for Mum.
As you may have read, the school is going to build a new gym.
He smiled at me today. I think he may have forgiven me for that accident!
I can't find my keys. I may have left them at the office.
She isn't answering. She may have gone to bed.
The road is wet. It may have rained in the night.
They're late. They may have missed the train.
He looks happy. He may have got the job.
I may have made a mistake in the last question.
If the parcel looks too small, you may have ordered the wrong size.
If you didn't read the contract, you may have agreed to pay extra.
You may have paid too much if you bought the ticket at the station.
You may have given your password to a stranger without knowing it.
By the time you arrive, the best seats may have gone.
You may have lost your data if you didn't save it.
You may have seen that your beautiful blue vase is not in your room any more. I'm afraid I broke it!
You may have noticed that your chocolate has gone. Sorry, I ate it.
You may have wondered why I didn't call. My phone was stolen.
You may have found my shoes in your car. I left them there last week.
You may have heard a loud noise last night. That was me falling over.
You may have realised that I forgot your birthday. I'm so sorry.
Call her again. She may not have heard the phone.
He may not have got my message.
They may not have known about the change of plan.
I may not have explained it very clearly.
My cousin may not have read the invitation before she booked her holiday.
The waiter may not have understood our order.
You may not have noticed, but I've had my hair cut.

examples.heading: ① as you may have + 過去分詞：對方可能已經知道

items.en: As you may have noticed, the lift is out of order again.
items.zh: 大家可能已經注意到，電梯又故障了。

items.en: As you may have heard, our manager is leaving at the end of the month.
items.zh: 大家可能已經聽說了，我們經理月底要離職。

items.en: As you may have seen in the news, the bridge will be closed for a week.
items.zh: 你可能已經在新聞上看到了，那座橋會封閉一個星期。（被動）

items.en: As you may have guessed, the party is a surprise for Mum.
items.zh: 你可能已經猜到了，這個派對是給媽媽的驚喜。

items.en: As you may have read, the school is going to build a new gym.
items.zh: 你可能已經讀到了，學校要蓋一座新的體育館。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + may have + 過去分詞：猜過去發生的事

items.en: He smiled at me today. I think he may have forgiven me for that accident!
items.zh: 他今天對我笑了。我想他可能已經原諒我那次出的意外了！

items.en: I can't find my keys. I may have left them at the office.
items.zh: 我找不到鑰匙。我可能把它們留在辦公室了。

items.en: She isn't answering. She may have gone to bed.
items.zh: 她沒接電話。她可能已經睡了。

items.en: The road is wet. It may have rained in the night.
items.zh: 路是濕的。夜裡可能下過雨。

items.en: They're late. They may have missed the train.
items.zh: 他們遲到了。他們可能錯過了火車。

items.en: He looks happy. He may have got the job.
items.zh: 他看起來很高興。他可能拿到那份工作了。

items.en: I may have made a mistake in the last question.
items.zh: 我最後一題可能寫錯了。

examples.heading: ③ you may have + 過去分詞：說可能的壞處

items.en: If the parcel looks too small, you may have ordered the wrong size.
items.zh: 如果包裹看起來太小，你可能訂錯尺寸了。

items.en: If you didn't read the contract, you may have agreed to pay extra.
items.zh: 如果你沒讀合約，你可能已經同意多付錢了。

items.en: You may have paid too much if you bought the ticket at the station.
items.zh: 如果你在車站買票，你可能付太多錢了。

items.en: You may have given your password to a stranger without knowing it.
items.zh: 你可能在不知情的情況下把密碼給了陌生人。

items.en: By the time you arrive, the best seats may have gone.
items.zh: 等你到了，最好的位子可能已經沒了。

items.en: You may have lost your data if you didn't save it.
items.zh: 如果你沒存檔，你的資料可能已經不見了。

examples.heading: ④ you may have + 過去分詞：承認自己做的事

items.en: You may have seen that your beautiful blue vase is not in your room any more. I'm afraid I broke it!
items.zh: 你可能已經發現你那個漂亮的藍色花瓶不在房間裡了。恐怕是我打破的！

items.en: You may have noticed that your chocolate has gone. Sorry, I ate it.
items.zh: 你可能已經發現你的巧克力不見了。抱歉，我吃掉了。

items.en: You may have wondered why I didn't call. My phone was stolen.
items.zh: 你可能在想為什麼我沒打電話。我的手機被偷了。（被動）

items.en: You may have found my shoes in your car. I left them there last week.
items.zh: 你可能已經在你車上找到我的鞋子。我上星期留在那裡的。

items.en: You may have heard a loud noise last night. That was me falling over.
items.zh: 你昨晚可能聽到一聲巨響。那是我跌倒了。

items.en: You may have realised that I forgot your birthday. I'm so sorry.
items.zh: 你可能已經發現我忘了你的生日。真的很抱歉。

examples.heading: ⑤ may not have + 過去分詞：可能沒有發生

items.en: Call her again. She may not have heard the phone.
items.zh: 再打給她一次。她可能沒聽到電話響。

items.en: He may not have got my message.
items.zh: 他可能沒收到我的訊息。

items.en: They may not have known about the change of plan.
items.zh: 他們可能不知道計畫改了。

items.en: I may not have explained it very clearly.
items.zh: 我可能沒解釋得很清楚。

items.en: My cousin may not have read the invitation before she booked her holiday.
items.zh: 我表妹訂假期之前，可能沒看到邀請函。

items.en: The waiter may not have understood our order.
items.zh: 服務生可能沒聽懂我們點的菜。

items.en: You may not have noticed, but I've had my hair cut.
items.zh: 你可能沒注意到，可是我剪頭髮了。

title: We didn't get a tour guide. We ought to have booked one!
translation: 我們早該請個導遊的！
name: ought to have 加過去分詞（肯定）
sentences: There were no guides at the museum, so we saw very little. We ought to have booked one!
I ought to have brought an umbrella. I'm soaking wet.
We ought to have left earlier. Now we've missed the start.
Mum said that boy wasn't a real friend, and she was right. I ought to have listened to her.
We drove to the castle, and it was closed on Mondays. We ought to have checked the opening times.
Now I'm sixty and I have no savings. I ought to have saved more money when I was young.
The water is polluted because of the petrol station. The government ought to have known that.
There was drilling outside our room every morning. The hotel ought to have told us about the building work.
The new heaters caught fire in some homes. The company ought to have warned its customers.
You ought to have asked me before you borrowed my car.
My son broke his arm at school, and nobody phoned me until four. The school ought to have contacted the parents immediately.
Our kitchen still has no walls. The builders ought to have finished the job last month.
One thing which I think ought to have been better managed was the boat trip on the Thames.
The concert is tomorrow, and we still haven't got our tickets. They ought to have been sent a week ago.
People have complained about the noise from the airport for ten years. The problem ought to have been solved years ago.
The holes in the road are full of ice now. It ought to have been repaired before winter.
Half of us had to stand at the back. The meeting ought to have been held in a bigger room.
The family moved away and the children only found out the day before. They ought to have been told the truth earlier.
Sorry, I forgot your birthday. I ought to have called you, but I was too busy.
We were starving when we arrived at the beach. We ought to have stopped for lunch, but we wanted to get there quickly.
Mia failed her chemistry exam. She ought to have studied harder, but she didn't have time.
Jack broke his friend's guitar. He ought to have said sorry, but he was too proud.
My parents sat in traffic for four hours. They ought to have taken the train, but they drove instead.
I'm so tired this morning. I ought to have gone to bed early, but I watched a film.
I posted the parcel on Monday, so it ought to have arrived by now.
Their flight left at six, so they ought to have landed in Rome by now.
The meeting started at nine. Surely it ought to have finished by now.
We painted the fence yesterday. It ought to have dried by now.
I sent the letter two weeks ago. You ought to have received it by now.
The dough has been in a warm place for an hour, so it ought to have risen by now.
She left the office at five. She ought to have got home by now.

examples.heading: ① We / I + ought to have + 過去分詞：後悔自己沒做

items.en: There were no guides at the museum, so we saw very little. We ought to have booked one!
items.zh: 博物館沒有導遊，所以我們看到的很少。我們應該先預約一個的！

items.en: I ought to have brought an umbrella. I'm soaking wet.
items.zh: 我應該帶傘的。我全身濕透了。

items.en: We ought to have left earlier. Now we've missed the start.
items.zh: 我們應該早點出發的。現在錯過開頭了。

items.en: Mum said that boy wasn't a real friend, and she was right. I ought to have listened to her.
items.zh: 媽媽說那個男生不是真正的朋友，她說對了。我當時應該聽她的話。

items.en: We drove to the castle, and it was closed on Mondays. We ought to have checked the opening times.
items.zh: 我們開車到城堡，結果星期一不開放。我們應該先查一下開放時間的。

items.en: Now I'm sixty and I have no savings. I ought to have saved more money when I was young.
items.zh: 我現在六十歲了，沒有存款。我年輕的時候應該多存點錢的。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + ought to have + 過去分詞：批評別人

items.en: The water is polluted because of the petrol station. The government ought to have known that.
items.zh: 水因為加油站被污染了。政府當時應該知道這一點的。

items.en: There was drilling outside our room every morning. The hotel ought to have told us about the building work.
items.zh: 每天早上我們房間外面都在鑽洞。飯店當時應該告訴我們有施工的事。

items.en: The new heaters caught fire in some homes. The company ought to have warned its customers.
items.zh: 新的暖氣機在一些家裡起火了。公司當時應該警告它的顧客。

items.en: You ought to have asked me before you borrowed my car.
items.zh: 你借我的車之前應該先問我的。

items.en: My son broke his arm at school, and nobody phoned me until four. The school ought to have contacted the parents immediately.
items.zh: 我兒子在學校摔斷了手臂，到四點才有人打電話給我。學校當時應該馬上聯絡家長。

items.en: Our kitchen still has no walls. The builders ought to have finished the job last month.
items.zh: 我們的廚房還沒有牆。工人上個月就應該完工了。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + ought to have been + 過去分詞：事情應該被處理得更好

items.en: One thing which I think ought to have been better managed was the boat trip on the Thames.
items.zh: 有一件事我覺得應該安排得更好，就是泰晤士河的乘船之旅。（被動）

items.en: The concert is tomorrow, and we still haven't got our tickets. They ought to have been sent a week ago.
items.zh: 音樂會明天就開始了，我們還沒收到票。票一個星期前就應該寄出了。（被動）

items.en: People have complained about the noise from the airport for ten years. The problem ought to have been solved years ago.
items.zh: 大家抱怨機場的噪音抱怨了十年。這個問題好幾年前就應該解決了。（被動）

items.en: The holes in the road are full of ice now. It ought to have been repaired before winter.
items.zh: 路上的坑洞現在都結冰了。這條路應該在冬天之前修好。（被動）

items.en: Half of us had to stand at the back. The meeting ought to have been held in a bigger room.
items.zh: 我們有一半的人只能站在後面。這次會議應該在大一點的房間舉行。（被動）

items.en: The family moved away and the children only found out the day before. They ought to have been told the truth earlier.
items.zh: 那家人搬走了，孩子們前一天才知道。他們應該早點被告知真相。（被動）

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + ought to have + 過去分詞, but + 句子

items.en: Sorry, I forgot your birthday. I ought to have called you, but I was too busy.
items.zh: 抱歉，我忘了你的生日。我應該打給你的，可是我太忙了。

items.en: We were starving when we arrived at the beach. We ought to have stopped for lunch, but we wanted to get there quickly.
items.zh: 我們到海灘的時候餓壞了。我們應該停下來吃午餐的，可是我們想快點到。

items.en: Mia failed her chemistry exam. She ought to have studied harder, but she didn't have time.
items.zh: Mia 化學考試沒及格。她應該更用功的，可是她沒有時間。

items.en: Jack broke his friend's guitar. He ought to have said sorry, but he was too proud.
items.zh: Jack 弄壞了朋友的吉他。他應該道歉的，可是他太驕傲了。

items.en: My parents sat in traffic for four hours. They ought to have taken the train, but they drove instead.
items.zh: 我爸媽塞車塞了四個小時。他們應該搭火車的，可是他們開車去了。

items.en: I'm so tired this morning. I ought to have gone to bed early, but I watched a film.
items.zh: 我今天早上好累。我應該早點睡的，可是我看了一部電影。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + ought to have + 過去分詞 + by now：現在應該已經

items.en: I posted the parcel on Monday, so it ought to have arrived by now.
items.zh: 我星期一寄出包裹，所以它現在應該已經到了。

items.en: Their flight left at six, so they ought to have landed in Rome by now.
items.zh: 他們的班機六點起飛，所以他們現在應該已經降落在羅馬了。

items.en: The meeting started at nine. Surely it ought to have finished by now.
items.zh: 會議九點開始。現在應該早就結束了吧。

items.en: We painted the fence yesterday. It ought to have dried by now.
items.zh: 我們昨天油漆了圍籬。它現在應該已經乾了。

items.en: I sent the letter two weeks ago. You ought to have received it by now.
items.zh: 我兩個星期前寄出那封信。你現在應該已經收到了。

items.en: The dough has been in a warm place for an hour, so it ought to have risen by now.
items.zh: 麵團放在溫暖的地方一個小時了，所以它應該已經發起來了。

items.en: She left the office at five. She ought to have got home by now.
items.zh: 她五點離開辦公室。她現在應該已經到家了。

title: The number of Dutch people eating a big, hot breakfast may not have been as high as in England, but it has certainly fallen.
translation: 工作能幫助他們認識別人，學到待在家裡可能學不到的技能。
name: may not have 加過去分詞
sentences: The town may not have been rich, but it had a fine theatre.
Life in the village may not have been easy, but people were happy.
The first computers may not have been fast, but they changed the world.
Earlier figures may not have been accurate.
The old school may not have been modern, but the teachers were excellent.
The weather may not have been perfect, but we had a great holiday.
Working outside the home helps couples meet other people and gain skills that they may not have got by staying at home.
Travelling gave me ideas which I may not have had at home.
The course taught me things that I may not have learned at university.
Volunteering gave her friends that she may not have met otherwise.
The trip showed the children places that they may not have seen on television.
I made some mistakes that you may not have noticed.
Call her again. She may not have seen your message.
The new waiter may not have written down your order correctly.
They may not have known that the shop was closed.
The students may not have read the whole chapter.
You may not have heard, but the meeting has moved to Friday.
The driver may not have seen the cyclist in the dark.
The king may not have written the letter himself.
People in the past may not have eaten as much sugar as we do.
The early settlers may not have known how cold the winters were.
The scientists may not have tested the drug on enough people.
The writer may not have planned the ending from the start.
The ancient Romans may not have used this road very often.
I may not have won the race, but I beat my best time.
The plan may not have worked perfectly, but we learned a lot.
She may not have said much, but she listened to everyone.
We may not have made much money, but the customers were happy.
He may not have studied art, but his paintings are wonderful.
The hotel may not have had a pool, but the beach was close.
The team may not have played well, but they never gave up.

examples.heading: ① may not have been + …：比較過去的情況

items.en: The town may not have been rich, but it had a fine theatre.
items.zh: 那個鎮以前可能不富有，可是有一座很好的劇院。

items.en: Life in the village may not have been easy, but people were happy.
items.zh: 以前村子裡的生活可能不輕鬆，可是大家很快樂。

items.en: The first computers may not have been fast, but they changed the world.
items.zh: 第一批電腦可能不快，可是它們改變了世界。

items.en: Earlier figures may not have been accurate.
items.zh: 早期的數字可能不準確。

items.en: The old school may not have been modern, but the teachers were excellent.
items.zh: 那所老學校可能不現代，可是老師都很優秀。

items.en: The weather may not have been perfect, but we had a great holiday.
items.zh: 天氣可能不完美，可是我們度了一個很棒的假。

examples.heading: ② that / which + 主詞 + may not have + 過去分詞

items.en: Working outside the home helps couples meet other people and gain skills that they may not have got by staying at home.
items.zh: 在外面工作讓夫妻認識其他人，學到待在家裡可能學不到的技能。

items.en: Travelling gave me ideas which I may not have had at home.
items.zh: 旅行給了我在家裡可能不會有的想法。

items.en: The course taught me things that I may not have learned at university.
items.zh: 這門課教了我在大學可能學不到的東西。

items.en: Volunteering gave her friends that she may not have met otherwise.
items.zh: 當志工讓她交到了原本可能不會認識的朋友。

items.en: The trip showed the children places that they may not have seen on television.
items.zh: 這趟旅行帶孩子們看了電視上可能看不到的地方。

items.en: I made some mistakes that you may not have noticed.
items.zh: 我犯了一些你可能沒注意到的錯。

examples.heading: ③ may not have + 過去分詞：猜別人沒做的事

items.en: Call her again. She may not have seen your message.
items.zh: 再打給她一次。她可能沒看到你的訊息。

items.en: The new waiter may not have written down your order correctly.
items.zh: 新來的服務生可能沒把你點的菜記對。

items.en: They may not have known that the shop was closed.
items.zh: 他們可能不知道那家店關了。

items.en: The students may not have read the whole chapter.
items.zh: 學生可能沒讀完整章。

items.en: You may not have heard, but the meeting has moved to Friday.
items.zh: 你可能沒聽說，可是會議改到星期五了。

items.en: The driver may not have seen the cyclist in the dark.
items.zh: 天黑了，司機可能沒看到騎腳踏車的人。

examples.heading: ④ may not have + 過去分詞：歷史和研究

items.en: The king may not have written the letter himself.
items.zh: 那封信可能不是國王親手寫的。

items.en: People in the past may not have eaten as much sugar as we do.
items.zh: 以前的人吃的糖可能沒有我們現在多。

items.en: The early settlers may not have known how cold the winters were.
items.zh: 早期的移民可能不知道冬天有多冷。

items.en: The scientists may not have tested the drug on enough people.
items.zh: 科學家可能沒有在夠多的人身上試驗這種藥。

items.en: The writer may not have planned the ending from the start.
items.zh: 作者可能一開始沒有計畫好結局。

items.en: The ancient Romans may not have used this road very often.
items.zh: 古羅馬人可能不常走這條路。

examples.heading: ⑤ may not have + 過去分詞, but + 句子：承認，再說重點

items.en: I may not have won the race, but I beat my best time.
items.zh: 我可能沒有贏得比賽，可是我打破了自己最好的紀錄。

items.en: The plan may not have worked perfectly, but we learned a lot.
items.zh: 這個計畫可能沒有完全成功，可是我們學到很多。

items.en: She may not have said much, but she listened to everyone.
items.zh: 她可能沒說很多話，可是她聽了每個人的意見。

items.en: We may not have made much money, but the customers were happy.
items.zh: 我們可能沒賺很多錢，可是顧客很滿意。

items.en: He may not have studied art, but his paintings are wonderful.
items.zh: 他可能沒學過藝術，可是他的畫很棒。

items.en: The hotel may not have had a pool, but the beach was close.
items.zh: 那家飯店可能沒有游泳池，可是海灘很近。

items.en: The team may not have played well, but they never gave up.
items.zh: 球隊可能踢得不好，可是他們從來沒有放棄。

title: The air conditioning cannot have been working properly, as the coach was too cold.
translation: 冷氣當時不可能正常運作，因為遊覽車上太冷了。
name: can't have 加過去分詞表示推斷
sentences: I live with my partner, and we can't have used so much electricity.
You can't have finished your homework already. You only started ten minutes ago.
He can't have seen me. He didn't say hello.
They can't have left yet. Their car is still outside.
She can't have forgotten the meeting. I reminded her this morning.
The thief can't have come in through the window. It was locked.
You can't have read the whole book in one evening!
We can't have taken the wrong road. I followed the signs.
The dog can't have eaten the cake. It was on the top shelf.
He can't have bought a new car. He has no money.
I can't have lost my keys. I had them a minute ago.
They can't have heard the news. They were on a plane all day.
It cannot have been such a disappointment for her.
It can't have been easy to grow up without a father.
The exam can't have been that difficult. Everyone passed.
That can't have been Tom at the station. He's in Paris.
The hotel can't have been very expensive. They only paid forty pounds.
She can't have been at home. Nobody answered the door.
It can't have been a real diamond. It was too cheap.
The air conditioning cannot have been working properly, as the coach was too cold.
He can't have been listening. He didn't answer the question.
She can't have been driving fast. There was too much traffic.
You can't have been waiting long. The bus has just left.
The children can't have been sleeping. I heard them laughing.
They can't have been telling the truth about the money.
It can't have been fun to wait in the rain for an hour.
That can't have been right. Let me check the bill again.
It can't have been cheap to fly the whole family to Australia.
It cannot have been pleasant to work in such a noisy office.
That can't have been the first time he did it.
It can't have been an accident. Someone did it on purpose.

examples.heading: ① can't / cannot + have + 過去分詞

items.en: I live with my partner, and we can't have used so much electricity.
items.zh: 我和伴侶一起住，我們不可能用了那麼多電。

items.en: You can't have finished your homework already. You only started ten minutes ago.
items.zh: 你不可能已經寫完功課了，你十分鐘前才開始。

items.en: He can't have seen me. He didn't say hello.
items.zh: 他不可能看到我，他沒跟我打招呼。

items.en: They can't have left yet. Their car is still outside.
items.zh: 他們不可能已經走了，他們的車還在外面。

items.en: She can't have forgotten the meeting. I reminded her this morning.
items.zh: 她不可能忘了開會，我今天早上提醒過她。

items.en: The thief can't have come in through the window. It was locked.
items.zh: 小偷不可能從窗戶進來，窗戶是鎖著的。

items.en: You can't have read the whole book in one evening!
items.zh: 你不可能一個晚上就讀完整本書！

items.en: We can't have taken the wrong road. I followed the signs.
items.zh: 我們不可能走錯路，我都照著路標走。

items.en: The dog can't have eaten the cake. It was on the top shelf.
items.zh: 狗不可能吃了蛋糕，蛋糕放在最上層的架子。

items.en: He can't have bought a new car. He has no money.
items.zh: 他不可能買了新車，他沒有錢。

items.en: I can't have lost my keys. I had them a minute ago.
items.zh: 我不可能弄丟鑰匙，我一分鐘前還拿著。

items.en: They can't have heard the news. They were on a plane all day.
items.zh: 他們不可能聽說了這個消息，他們一整天都在飛機上。

examples.heading: ② can't / cannot + have been + 形容詞 / 名詞 / 地點

items.en: It cannot have been such a disappointment for her.
items.zh: 那對她來說不可能是那麼大的失望。

items.en: It can't have been easy to grow up without a father.
items.zh: 沒有爸爸的成長過程不可能很輕鬆。

items.en: The exam can't have been that difficult. Everyone passed.
items.zh: 考試不可能那麼難，大家都過了。

items.en: That can't have been Tom at the station. He's in Paris.
items.zh: 在車站的不可能是 Tom，他在巴黎。

items.en: The hotel can't have been very expensive. They only paid forty pounds.
items.zh: 那家飯店不可能很貴，他們只付了四十英鎊。

items.en: She can't have been at home. Nobody answered the door.
items.zh: 她不可能在家，沒有人來應門。

items.en: It can't have been a real diamond. It was too cheap.
items.zh: 那不可能是真的鑽石，太便宜了。

examples.heading: ③ can't / cannot + have been + 動詞-ing

items.en: The air conditioning cannot have been working properly, as the coach was too cold.
items.zh: 冷氣當時不可能正常運作，因為遊覽車上太冷了。

items.en: He can't have been listening. He didn't answer the question.
items.zh: 他不可能有在聽，他沒有回答問題。

items.en: She can't have been driving fast. There was too much traffic.
items.zh: 她不可能開得很快，車太多了。

items.en: You can't have been waiting long. The bus has just left.
items.zh: 你不可能等很久，公車才剛開走。

items.en: The children can't have been sleeping. I heard them laughing.
items.zh: 孩子們不可能在睡覺，我聽到他們在笑。

items.en: They can't have been telling the truth about the money.
items.zh: 關於那筆錢，他們說的不可能是實話。

examples.heading: ④ It / That + can't have been + 形容詞 / 名詞

items.en: It can't have been fun to wait in the rain for an hour.
items.zh: 在雨裡等一個小時不可能好玩。

items.en: That can't have been right. Let me check the bill again.
items.zh: 那不可能是對的，我再看一次帳單。

items.en: It can't have been cheap to fly the whole family to Australia.
items.zh: 讓全家人飛去澳洲不可能便宜。

items.en: It cannot have been pleasant to work in such a noisy office.
items.zh: 在那麼吵的辦公室工作不可能愉快。

items.en: That can't have been the first time he did it.
items.zh: 那不可能是他第一次這麼做。

items.en: It can't have been an accident. Someone did it on purpose.
items.zh: 那不可能是意外，有人是故意的。

title: Could I possibly see you at 3.30?
translation: 不知道能不能約你 3:30 見個面？
name: could 加主詞加 possibly 的客氣請求
sentences: I'd like to talk about my essay. Could I possibly see you at 3.30 tomorrow?
Could I possibly borrow your notes from Monday's lecture?
Could I possibly leave work an hour early today?
Could I possibly use your phone? Mine has no battery.
Could I possibly have a glass of water?
Could I possibly change my appointment to Thursday?

title: Thinking of Christmas? Not necessarily.
translation: 在想聖誕節的事嗎？那可不一定。
name: not necessarily 當簡短回答
sentences: Presents, ribbons, wrapping paper. Thinking of Christmas? Not necessarily. People give presents all year round.
"Do I need a car to live in the countryside?" "Not necessarily. There's a good bus service."
"Is the most expensive phone the best?" "Not necessarily. Read the reviews first."
"Will the meeting take all morning?" "Not necessarily. It depends on the questions."
"Do vegetarians eat fish?" "Not necessarily. Most of them don't."
"Should I bring a coat?" "Not necessarily. It's warm during the day."
"Big cities are always dangerous." "Not necessarily. Mine feels very safe at night."
"Older people don't like new music." "Not necessarily. My grandma loves pop music."
"Homework helps you learn." "Not necessarily. Too much can make you tired."
"Cheap hotels are dirty." "Not necessarily. We stayed in a lovely one last year."
"Tall people are good at basketball." "Not necessarily. My brother is tall and terrible at it."
"Cats don't like water." "Not necessarily. My cat jumps in the bath."
"So you'll be rich one day," said my uncle. "Not necessarily," I said with a smile.
"You'll need to work late," said the manager. "Not necessarily," she replied.
"The train will be full," said Dad. "Not necessarily," said Mum. "It's a holiday."
"He must be angry with you," said Tom. "Not necessarily," said Anna.
"That means we've lost," said the captain. "Not necessarily," said the coach.
"You'll have to sell the house," said the lawyer. "Not necessarily," said the old man.
"Is it better to study in the morning?" "Not necessarily, but it works for me."
"Do I have to wear a suit?" "Not necessarily, but you should look smart."
"Will we need to book?" "Not necessarily, but it's safer."
"Is the new teacher strict?" "Not necessarily, but she likes quiet classes."
"Should we take the motorway?" "Not necessarily, but it's usually faster."
"Do you need a degree for this job?" "Not necessarily, but it helps."
"Everyone at the party will know each other." "Well, not necessarily. Some are new."
"The best players always win." "Well, not necessarily. Luck matters too."
"Your parents will say no." "Well, not necessarily. Let me ask them."
"Rain means the picnic is off." "Well, not necessarily. We could eat under the trees."
"Learning a language takes years." "Well, not necessarily. You can learn the basics quickly."
"A late start means a late finish." "Well, not necessarily. We can skip the break."
"Old cars break down all the time." "Well, not necessarily. Mine has never let me down."

examples.heading: ① "…？" "Not necessarily." + 理由：回答問題

items.en: Presents, ribbons, wrapping paper. Thinking of Christmas? Not necessarily. People give presents all year round.
items.zh: 禮物、緞帶、包裝紙。想到聖誕節了嗎？不一定喔。人們一整年都會送禮物。

items.en: "Do I need a car to live in the countryside?" "Not necessarily. There's a good bus service."
items.zh: 住在鄉下需要車嗎？不一定。那裡的公車很方便。

items.en: "Is the most expensive phone the best?" "Not necessarily. Read the reviews first."
items.zh: 最貴的手機是最好的嗎？不一定。先看評論。

items.en: "Will the meeting take all morning?" "Not necessarily. It depends on the questions."
items.zh: 會議會開一整個早上嗎？不一定。要看有多少問題。

items.en: "Do vegetarians eat fish?" "Not necessarily. Most of them don't."
items.zh: 素食者吃魚嗎？不一定。大部分不吃。

items.en: "Should I bring a coat?" "Not necessarily. It's warm during the day."
items.zh: 我應該帶外套嗎？不一定。白天很暖和。

examples.heading: ② "肯定句" "Not necessarily." + 理由：對方的看法有例外

items.en: "Big cities are always dangerous." "Not necessarily. Mine feels very safe at night."
items.zh: 大城市都很危險。不一定。我住的城市晚上感覺很安全。

items.en: "Older people don't like new music." "Not necessarily. My grandma loves pop music."
items.zh: 老人不喜歡新的音樂。不一定。我奶奶很喜歡流行音樂。

items.en: "Homework helps you learn." "Not necessarily. Too much can make you tired."
items.zh: 功課能幫你學習。不一定。太多會讓你很累。

items.en: "Cheap hotels are dirty." "Not necessarily. We stayed in a lovely one last year."
items.zh: 便宜的飯店都很髒。不一定。我們去年住了一家很棒的。

items.en: "Tall people are good at basketball." "Not necessarily. My brother is tall and terrible at it."
items.zh: 高的人很會打籃球。不一定。我哥哥很高，可是打得很爛。

items.en: "Cats don't like water." "Not necessarily. My cat jumps in the bath."
items.zh: 貓不喜歡水。不一定。我的貓會跳進浴缸。

examples.heading: ③ "Not necessarily," + 主詞 + said：故事裡的對話

items.en: "So you'll be rich one day," said my uncle. "Not necessarily," I said with a smile.
items.zh: 所以你有一天會很有錢，我叔叔說。不一定，我笑著說。

items.en: "You'll need to work late," said the manager. "Not necessarily," she replied.
items.zh: 你會需要加班，經理說。不一定，她回答。

items.en: "The train will be full," said Dad. "Not necessarily," said Mum. "It's a holiday."
items.zh: 火車會客滿，爸爸說。不一定，媽媽說。今天放假。

items.en: "He must be angry with you," said Tom. "Not necessarily," said Anna.
items.zh: 他一定在生你的氣，湯姆說。不一定，安娜說。

items.en: "That means we've lost," said the captain. "Not necessarily," said the coach.
items.zh: 那表示我們輸了，隊長說。不一定，教練說。

items.en: "You'll have to sell the house," said the lawyer. "Not necessarily," said the old man.
items.zh: 你必須賣掉房子，律師說。不一定，那位老人說。

examples.heading: ④ "…？" "Not necessarily, but …"：部分同意

items.en: "Is it better to study in the morning?" "Not necessarily, but it works for me."
items.zh: 早上讀書比較好嗎？不一定，可是對我有用。

items.en: "Do I have to wear a suit?" "Not necessarily, but you should look smart."
items.zh: 我一定要穿西裝嗎？不一定，可是你應該穿得體面一點。

items.en: "Will we need to book?" "Not necessarily, but it's safer."
items.zh: 我們需要預約嗎？不一定，可是比較保險。

items.en: "Is the new teacher strict?" "Not necessarily, but she likes quiet classes."
items.zh: 新老師很嚴格嗎？不一定，可是她喜歡安靜的課堂。

items.en: "Should we take the motorway?" "Not necessarily, but it's usually faster."
items.zh: 我們應該走高速公路嗎？不一定，可是通常比較快。

items.en: "Do you need a degree for this job?" "Not necessarily, but it helps."
items.zh: 做這份工作需要學位嗎？不一定，可是有幫助。

examples.heading: ⑤ Well, not necessarily. + 理由：委婉地不同意

items.en: "Everyone at the party will know each other." "Well, not necessarily. Some are new."
items.zh: 派對上每個人都會互相認識。嗯，不一定。有些人是新來的。

items.en: "The best players always win." "Well, not necessarily. Luck matters too."
items.zh: 最好的球員總是會贏。嗯，不一定。運氣也很重要。

items.en: "Your parents will say no." "Well, not necessarily. Let me ask them."
items.zh: 你爸媽會拒絕。嗯，不一定。讓我問問他們。

items.en: "Rain means the picnic is off." "Well, not necessarily. We could eat under the trees."
items.zh: 下雨表示野餐取消了。嗯，不一定。我們可以在樹下吃。

items.en: "Learning a language takes years." "Well, not necessarily. You can learn the basics quickly."
items.zh: 學一種語言要好幾年。嗯，不一定。基礎可以學得很快。

items.en: "A late start means a late finish." "Well, not necessarily. We can skip the break."
