The fridge is empty. My brother might have eaten everything.
The first people here might have arrived by boat.
The castle might have stood here for eight hundred years.
The old road might have been used by Roman soldiers.
My great-grandfather might have known the famous painter.
The village might have had a school in the 1800s.
People might have lived in these caves thousands of years ago.
If you had asked me, I might have helped you.
With more time, we might have won the match.
If the bus had been on time, I might have caught my flight.
Without your advice, I might have made a big mistake.
If it hadn't rained, we might have gone to the beach.
If she had studied harder, she might have passed.
With a better map, they might have found the hotel sooner.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + thought + 主詞 + might have + 過去分詞

items.en: When I saw the broken window, I thought a ball might have hit it.
items.zh: 我看到破掉的窗戶時，以為可能是被球打到了。

items.en: When she didn't call, I thought she might have had an accident.
items.zh: 她沒打電話來的時候，我以為她可能出事了。

items.en: We thought the shop might have closed down.
items.zh: 我們以為那家店可能倒了。

items.en: I thought I might have left the oven on, so I went back home.
items.zh: 我以為我可能沒關烤箱，所以回家了。

items.en: He thought he might have failed the exam, but he got an A.
items.zh: 他以為他考試可能沒過，可是他拿了 A。

items.en: She thought someone might have taken her bike.
items.zh: 她以為可能有人拿走了她的腳踏車。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + might have + led to / caused：可能的原因

items.en: Prices went up and people moved away. Many things might have led to these changes.
items.zh: 物價上漲，人們搬走了。很多原因可能導致了這些改變。

items.en: The heavy rain might have caused the flood.
items.zh: 大雨可能造成了水災。

items.en: A small mistake might have led to the accident.
items.zh: 一個小錯誤可能導致了那場意外。

items.en: The cold weather might have caused the crops to fail.
items.zh: 寒冷的天氣可能讓農作物歉收。

items.en: Bad food might have made the children ill.
items.zh: 不乾淨的食物可能讓孩子們生病了。

items.en: The new road might have brought more visitors to the town.
items.zh: 新的道路可能為鎮上帶來了更多遊客。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + might have + 過去分詞：猜發生了什麼事

items.en: The dog is wet. It might have jumped in the river.
items.zh: 狗是濕的。牠可能跳進河裡了。

items.en: There's mud on the floor. The kids might have come in through the garden.
items.zh: 地上有泥巴。孩子們可能從花園進來了。

items.en: The parcel is open. Someone might have looked inside.
items.zh: 包裹被打開了。可能有人看過裡面。

items.en: The plates are broken. The cat might have knocked them off the shelf.
items.zh: 盤子破了。貓可能把它們從架子上撞下來了。

items.en: He knows about the party. Somebody might have told him.
items.zh: 他知道派對的事。可能有人告訴他了。

items.en: The fridge is empty. My brother might have eaten everything.
items.zh: 冰箱空了。我哥哥可能把東西都吃光了。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + might have + 過去分詞：歷史和過去的事

items.en: The first people here might have arrived by boat.
items.zh: 最早到這裡的人可能是坐船來的。

items.en: The castle might have stood here for eight hundred years.
items.zh: 這座城堡可能在這裡矗立了八百年。

items.en: The old road might have been used by Roman soldiers.
items.zh: 這條舊路可能被羅馬士兵用過。（被動）

items.en: My great-grandfather might have known the famous painter.
items.zh: 我的曾祖父可能認識那位有名的畫家。

items.en: The village might have had a school in the 1800s.
items.zh: 這個村子在十九世紀可能有一所學校。

items.en: People might have lived in these caves thousands of years ago.
items.zh: 幾千年前人們可能住在這些洞穴裡。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + might have + 過去分詞：說另一種可能的結果

items.en: If you had asked me, I might have helped you.
items.zh: 如果你問了我，我可能會幫你。

items.en: With more time, we might have won the match.
items.zh: 如果時間多一點，我們可能會贏那場比賽。

items.en: If the bus had been on time, I might have caught my flight.
items.zh: 如果公車準時，我可能就趕上班機了。

items.en: Without your advice, I might have made a big mistake.
items.zh: 沒有你的建議，我可能會犯一個大錯。

items.en: If it hadn't rained, we might have gone to the beach.
items.zh: 如果沒下雨，我們可能就去海灘了。

items.en: If she had studied harder, she might have passed.
items.zh: 如果她讀書再認真一點，她可能就考過了。

items.en: With a better map, they might have found the hotel sooner.
items.zh: 如果有好一點的地圖，他們可能早點找到飯店。

title: The survey might not have asked an accurate sample of people.
translation: 這份調查訪問的對象可能不具代表性。
name: might not have 表示過去的可能
sentences: The questionnaire might not have reached people without the internet.
The figures might not have included part-time workers.
The researchers might not have spoken to enough young people.
The report might not have mentioned all the costs.
The study might not have lasted long enough to show real results.
The journalist might not have checked the facts.
Even though things might not have gone as you expected, please remember that this is a charity.
Even though the weather might not have been perfect, the festival was a success.
Even though you might not have won, you played really well.
Even though the food might not have been hot, the guests loved it.
Even though we might not have raised much money, everyone had a good time.
Even though the trip might not have been cheap, it was worth it.
The charity run might not have attracted many runners, but the whole town came to watch.
The charity sale might not have made much money, but it brought the neighbours together.
Your first concert might not have been perfect, but the audience loved it.
The new shop might not have made a profit yet, but it's getting busier.
Your speech might not have been very long, but it was clear.
The garden might not have won a prize, but it looks lovely.
Don't be angry with him. He might not have known the meeting was today.
The children might not have understood the rules of the game.
She might not have had time to answer your letter.
The new staff might not have been told about the fire drill.
Your friend might not have seen you wave.
The waiter might not have heard you ask for water.
People in the village might not have travelled far in those days.
The early cars might not have gone faster than a horse.
My grandparents might not have had a television until the 1960s.
The first settlers might not have planned to stay.
Children in the past might not have gone to school after the age of twelve.
The workers might not have earned enough to feed their families.
The town might not have had clean water until the new pipes came.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + might not have + 過去分詞：質疑調查和報告

items.en: The questionnaire might not have reached people without the internet.
items.zh: 這份問卷可能沒有送到沒網路的人手上。

items.en: The figures might not have included part-time workers.
items.zh: 這些數字可能沒有包括兼職員工。

items.en: The researchers might not have spoken to enough young people.
items.zh: 研究人員可能沒有訪問夠多年輕人。

items.en: The report might not have mentioned all the costs.
items.zh: 這份報告可能沒有提到所有的費用。

items.en: The study might not have lasted long enough to show real results.
items.zh: 這項研究可能進行得不夠久，看不出真正的結果。

items.en: The journalist might not have checked the facts.
items.zh: 那位記者可能沒有查證事實。

examples.heading: ② Even though + 主詞 + might not have + 過去分詞, + 句子

items.en: Even though things might not have gone as you expected, please remember that this is a charity.
items.zh: 雖然事情可能沒有照您預期的發展，請記得這是一個慈善活動。

items.en: Even though the weather might not have been perfect, the festival was a success.
items.zh: 雖然天氣可能不完美，節慶還是很成功。

items.en: Even though you might not have won, you played really well.
items.zh: 雖然你可能沒有贏，你踢得真的很好。

items.en: Even though the food might not have been hot, the guests loved it.
items.zh: 雖然食物可能不夠熱，客人還是很喜歡。

items.en: Even though we might not have raised much money, everyone had a good time.
items.zh: 雖然我們可能沒募到很多錢，大家都玩得很開心。

items.en: Even though the trip might not have been cheap, it was worth it.
items.zh: 雖然那趟旅行可能不便宜，可是很值得。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + might not have + 過去分詞, but + 句子：安慰

items.en: The charity run might not have attracted many runners, but the whole town came to watch.
items.zh: 慈善路跑可能沒吸引很多跑者，可是全鎮的人都來看了。

items.en: The charity sale might not have made much money, but it brought the neighbours together.
items.zh: 慈善義賣可能沒賺很多錢，可是讓鄰居們聚在一起。

items.en: Your first concert might not have been perfect, but the audience loved it.
items.zh: 你的第一場音樂會可能不完美，可是觀眾很喜歡。

items.en: The new shop might not have made a profit yet, but it's getting busier.
items.zh: 那家新店可能還沒賺錢，可是生意越來越好了。

items.en: Your speech might not have been very long, but it was clear.
items.zh: 你的演講可能不長，可是很清楚。

items.en: The garden might not have won a prize, but it looks lovely.
items.zh: 那座花園可能沒得獎，可是看起來很漂亮。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + might not have + 過去分詞：解釋別人為什麼沒做

items.en: Don't be angry with him. He might not have known the meeting was today.
items.zh: 別生他的氣。他可能不知道今天要開會。

items.en: The children might not have understood the rules of the game.
items.zh: 孩子們可能沒聽懂遊戲規則。

items.en: She might not have had time to answer your letter.
items.zh: 她可能沒時間回你的信。

items.en: The new staff might not have been told about the fire drill.
items.zh: 新員工可能沒被告知消防演習的事。（被動）

items.en: Your friend might not have seen you wave.
items.zh: 你朋友可能沒看到你揮手。

items.en: The waiter might not have heard you ask for water.
items.zh: 服務生可能沒聽到你要水。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + might not have + 過去分詞：說過去的情況

items.en: People in the village might not have travelled far in those days.
items.zh: 那個年代，村子裡的人可能沒去過很遠的地方。

items.en: The early cars might not have gone faster than a horse.
items.zh: 早期的汽車可能沒有比馬快。

items.en: My grandparents might not have had a television until the 1960s.
items.zh: 我祖父母可能到 1960 年代才有電視。

items.en: The first settlers might not have planned to stay.
items.zh: 最早的移民可能沒打算留下來。

items.en: Children in the past might not have gone to school after the age of twelve.
items.zh: 以前的孩子可能十二歲以後就不上學了。

items.en: The workers might not have earned enough to feed their families.
items.zh: 工人賺的錢可能不夠養家。

items.en: The town might not have had clean water until the new pipes came.
items.zh: 在新的水管來之前，這個鎮可能沒有乾淨的水。

title: As a result, our town shall have financial benefits, as people visiting the library will also visit the shops.
translation: 我們大概還能再活好幾年。
name: 情態動詞 shall 表示預測
sentences: With a new library in the centre, our town shall have financial benefits, as visitors will also use the shops.
If the council builds the sports centre, we shall have somewhere to go in the evening.
If more trees are planted on the main street, we shall breathe cleaner air in the centre.
With a weekly farmers' market, we shall buy fresher food and help local farms.
Once the cycle path is finished, we shall get to school much more safely.
With the new bus route, we shall reach the hospital in twenty minutes.
Thanks to modern medicine, we shall probably have several more years to live than our grandparents.
Many offices are closing their buildings. In twenty years, we shall probably work from home most of the time.
Electric cars are getting cheaper every year. We shall probably all drive one in the end.
Our children are learning Spanish and Chinese at school. I think we shall probably hear them speak three languages at home.
I read almost everything on my tablet now. I shall probably stop buying paper books.
Most of us shop online now. We shall probably need fewer shops in the future.
If the plan goes ahead, we shall certainly see more tourists in the old town.
The factory will employ four hundred people. We shall certainly see fewer people out of work.
If the tax on fuel goes up, we shall certainly pay more for food.
The festival has music, games and food for children. We shall certainly enjoy it as a family.
Our school has hired three excellent new teachers. We shall certainly see better results next year.
The museum gets twice as many visitors in summer. We shall certainly need more staff in July and August.
Self-driving cars are already on some roads. We shall see big changes in the way we travel.
Oil and gas will not last for ever. We shall have to find new ways to produce energy.
The climate is changing fast. In the next fifty years, we shall face many new problems.
Villages are getting smaller every year. In the future, we shall live mostly in big cities.
Robots can already clean floors and cut grass. Soon we shall have robots that do all the housework.
New telescopes are being sent into space. We shall learn more about space than ever before.
We shall do well this year, as more people are living in the town centre.
We shall be full all summer at the hotel, because the festival is so popular.
We shall sit in traffic even longer, as more families are buying cars.
We shall get many new neighbours, because the new railway stops in our village.
We shall sell more this year, as the new product is cheaper.
We shall need more classrooms, because many young families are moving here.
We shall see more fish in the river, as the factory has closed.

examples.heading: ① We shall + 原形動詞：建議書預測的好處

items.en: With a new library in the centre, our town shall have financial benefits, as visitors will also use the shops.
items.zh: 市中心有了新圖書館，我們鎮會得到經濟上的好處，因為來的人也會去逛商店。

items.en: If the council builds the sports centre, we shall have somewhere to go in the evening.
items.zh: 如果議會蓋了運動中心，我們晚上就有地方去了。

items.en: If more trees are planted on the main street, we shall breathe cleaner air in the centre.
items.zh: 如果主要街道種了更多樹，我們在市中心就會呼吸到比較乾淨的空氣。

items.en: With a weekly farmers' market, we shall buy fresher food and help local farms.
items.zh: 有了每週一次的農夫市集，我們會買到比較新鮮的食物，也能幫助本地農場。

items.en: Once the cycle path is finished, we shall get to school much more safely.
items.zh: 腳踏車道一完工，我們上學就會安全很多。

items.en: With the new bus route, we shall reach the hospital in twenty minutes.
items.zh: 有了新的公車路線，我們二十分鐘就會到醫院。

examples.heading: ② We shall + probably + 原形動詞：有一點把握的預測

items.en: Thanks to modern medicine, we shall probably have several more years to live than our grandparents.
items.zh: 多虧現代醫學，我們可能會比我們的祖父母多活好幾年。

items.en: Many offices are closing their buildings. In twenty years, we shall probably work from home most of the time.
items.zh: 很多公司正在關閉辦公大樓。二十年後，我們可能大部分時間都在家工作。

items.en: Electric cars are getting cheaper every year. We shall probably all drive one in the end.
items.zh: 電動車一年比一年便宜。我們最後可能都會開一台。

items.en: Our children are learning Spanish and Chinese at school. I think we shall probably hear them speak three languages at home.
items.zh: 我們的孩子在學校學西班牙文和中文。我想我們可能會聽到他們在家說三種語言。

items.en: I read almost everything on my tablet now. I shall probably stop buying paper books.
items.zh: 我現在幾乎都用平板閱讀。我可能會不再買紙本書。

items.en: Most of us shop online now. We shall probably need fewer shops in the future.
items.zh: 我們大部分人現在都在網路上購物。將來我們可能會需要比較少的商店。

examples.heading: ③ We shall + certainly + 原形動詞：很有把握的預測

items.en: If the plan goes ahead, we shall certainly see more tourists in the old town.
items.zh: 如果計畫進行，我們一定會在老城區看到更多觀光客。

items.en: The factory will employ four hundred people. We shall certainly see fewer people out of work.
items.zh: 那家工廠會雇用四百人。我們一定會看到失業的人變少。

items.en: If the tax on fuel goes up, we shall certainly pay more for food.
items.zh: 如果燃料稅提高，我們買食物一定會付比較多錢。

items.en: The festival has music, games and food for children. We shall certainly enjoy it as a family.
items.zh: 這個節慶有音樂、遊戲和兒童食物。我們全家一定會玩得很開心。

items.en: Our school has hired three excellent new teachers. We shall certainly see better results next year.
items.zh: 我們學校請了三位很棒的新老師。明年我們一定會看到更好的成績。

items.en: The museum gets twice as many visitors in summer. We shall certainly need more staff in July and August.
items.zh: 博物館夏天的遊客多一倍。七月和八月我們一定會需要更多人手。

examples.heading: ④ We shall + 原形動詞：說大家將來的情況

items.en: Self-driving cars are already on some roads. We shall see big changes in the way we travel.
items.zh: 有些路上已經有自動駕駛車了。我們會看到交通方式的大改變。

items.en: Oil and gas will not last for ever. We shall have to find new ways to produce energy.
items.zh: 石油和天然氣不會永遠用不完。我們必須找到新的能源生產方式。

items.en: The climate is changing fast. In the next fifty years, we shall face many new problems.
items.zh: 氣候改變得很快。在未來五十年，我們會面臨很多新問題。

items.en: Villages are getting smaller every year. In the future, we shall live mostly in big cities.
items.zh: 村子一年比一年小。將來我們大多會住在大城市。

items.en: Robots can already clean floors and cut grass. Soon we shall have robots that do all the housework.
items.zh: 機器人已經會掃地和割草了。不久我們就會有做所有家事的機器人。

items.en: New telescopes are being sent into space. We shall learn more about space than ever before.
items.zh: 新的望遠鏡正被送上太空。我們會比以往更了解太空。

examples.heading: ⑤ We shall + 原形動詞, as / because + 子句：預測和理由

items.en: We shall do well this year, as more people are living in the town centre.
items.zh: 我們今年生意會很好，因為有更多人住在市中心。

items.en: We shall be full all summer at the hotel, because the festival is so popular.
items.zh: 我們飯店整個夏天都會客滿，因為這個節慶很受歡迎。

items.en: We shall sit in traffic even longer, as more families are buying cars.
items.zh: 我們塞車的時間會更長，因為越來越多家庭在買車。

items.en: We shall get many new neighbours, because the new railway stops in our village.
items.zh: 我們會有很多新鄰居，因為新的鐵路在我們村子停靠。

items.en: We shall sell more this year, as the new product is cheaper.
items.zh: 我們今年會賣得更多，因為新產品比較便宜。

items.en: We shall need more classrooms, because many young families are moving here.
items.zh: 我們會需要更多教室，因為很多年輕家庭搬到這裡。

items.en: We shall see more fish in the river, as the factory has closed.
items.zh: 我們會在河裡看到更多魚，因為工廠關了。

title: My town is growing very fast. In twenty years' time it will be bigger than it is now.
translation: 我覺得 20 年後，我住的小鎮會比現在大，因為它發展得很快。
name: 情態動詞 will 表示預測
sentences: Lots of families are moving here. I think that in twenty years' time my town will be much bigger than it is now.
I think people will work from home more and more.
I think the price of petrol will go up again next year.
I think our team will win the league this season.
I think robots will do most of the housework in the future.
I think it will snow tonight. The sky looks very grey.
All your life you'll be able to see your parents, but after school it'll be harder to meet your old friends.
With the new railway, people will be able to reach the city in half an hour.
If the factory closes, it will be hard for people here to find jobs.
In a few years, you'll be able to speak English fluently.
The new bridge will be very useful for people in the village.
Next year the exams will be harder, so start studying now.
You're right. Without much sport you'll soon put on weight, won't you?
The shops will be very busy before Christmas, won't they?
The children will be tired after the long walk, won't they?
It'll be cold in the mountains at night, won't it?
Your parents will be proud of you, won't they?
The new teacher will be strict, won't she?
In ten years, most cars on the road will be electric.
In a few weeks, the trees will be full of blossom.
In fifty years, the sea will cover part of this beach.
In two years, my little sister will start school.
In a month, the new shopping centre will be finished.
In a few hours, the snow will start to melt.
Look at those dark clouds over the hills. The storm won't pass quickly.
My grandfather won't like his new mobile phone. He prefers the old one.
With so many people wanting to live here, house prices won't fall any time soon.
The match won't be easy. They're a very good team.
People won't stop buying books, even with the internet.
The bus won't be here for another twenty minutes.
You won't recognise the old school. They've changed everything.

examples.heading: ① I think + 主詞 + will + 原形動詞：說自己的預測

items.en: Lots of families are moving here. I think that in twenty years' time my town will be much bigger than it is now.
items.zh: 很多家庭搬來這裡。我想二十年後，我的家鄉會比現在大很多。

items.en: I think people will work from home more and more.
items.zh: 我想人們會越來越常在家工作。

items.en: I think the price of petrol will go up again next year.
items.zh: 我想明年油價會再上漲。

items.en: I think our team will win the league this season.
items.zh: 我想我們隊這一季會贏得聯賽冠軍。

items.en: I think robots will do most of the housework in the future.
items.zh: 我想以後機器人會做大部分的家事。

items.en: I think it will snow tonight. The sky looks very grey.
items.zh: 我想今天晚上會下雪。天空看起來很灰。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + will + be able to / be + 形容詞：預測以後的情況

items.en: All your life you'll be able to see your parents, but after school it'll be harder to meet your old friends.
items.zh: 你一輩子都能見到你的父母，可是畢業以後，要見到老朋友會比較難。

items.en: With the new railway, people will be able to reach the city in half an hour.
items.zh: 有了新鐵路，人們半小時就能到市區。

items.en: If the factory closes, it will be hard for people here to find jobs.
items.zh: 如果工廠關了，這裡的人會很難找到工作。

items.en: In a few years, you'll be able to speak English fluently.
items.zh: 再過幾年，你就能說流利的英文。

items.en: The new bridge will be very useful for people in the village.
items.zh: 新的橋對村子裡的人會很有用。

items.en: Next year the exams will be harder, so start studying now.
items.zh: 明年考試會比較難，所以現在就開始讀書。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + will + 原形動詞, won't + 代名詞？：預測並請對方同意

items.en: You're right. Without much sport you'll soon put on weight, won't you?
items.zh: 你說得對。不太運動的話，你很快就會變胖，對吧？

items.en: The shops will be very busy before Christmas, won't they?
items.zh: 聖誕節前商店會很多人，對吧？

items.en: The children will be tired after the long walk, won't they?
items.zh: 走了那麼久的路，孩子們會很累，對吧？

items.en: It'll be cold in the mountains at night, won't it?
items.zh: 晚上山上會很冷，對吧？

items.en: Your parents will be proud of you, won't they?
items.zh: 你爸媽會以你為榮，對吧？

items.en: The new teacher will be strict, won't she?
items.zh: 新老師會很嚴格，對吧？

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + will + 原形動詞 + in + 時間：預測什麼時候

items.en: In ten years, most cars on the road will be electric.
items.zh: 十年後，路上大部分的車都會是電動車。

items.en: In a few weeks, the trees will be full of blossom.
items.zh: 再過幾個星期，樹上就會開滿花。

items.en: In fifty years, the sea will cover part of this beach.
items.zh: 五十年後，海水會淹沒這個海灘的一部分。

items.en: In two years, my little sister will start school.
items.zh: 兩年後，我妹妹會開始上學。

items.en: In a month, the new shopping centre will be finished.
items.zh: 一個月後，新的購物中心會完工。

items.en: In a few hours, the snow will start to melt.
items.zh: 再過幾個小時，雪就會開始融化。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + won't + 原形動詞：預測不會發生

items.en: Look at those dark clouds over the hills. The storm won't pass quickly.
items.zh: 你看山丘上那些烏雲。暴風雨不會很快過去。

items.en: My grandfather won't like his new mobile phone. He prefers the old one.
items.zh: 我爺爺不會喜歡他的新手機。他比較喜歡舊的。

items.en: With so many people wanting to live here, house prices won't fall any time soon.
items.zh: 這麼多人想住在這裡，房價短時間內不會下跌。

items.en: The match won't be easy. They're a very good team.
items.zh: 這場比賽不會輕鬆。他們是一支很強的隊伍。

items.en: People won't stop buying books, even with the internet.
items.zh: 就算有了網路，人們也不會停止買書。

items.en: The bus won't be here for another twenty minutes.
items.zh: 公車還要二十分鐘才會到。

items.en: You won't recognise the old school. They've changed everything.
items.zh: 你會認不出那所老學校。他們把一切都改了。

title: How can each of us stay fit in this world of stress and fast-food restaurants?
translation: 在這個充滿壓力、到處都是速食店的世界，我們每個人要怎麼保持健康？
name: how can 修辭問句
sentences: How can each of us use less water at home?
How can we make our cities greener?
How can we protect our children from the dangers of the internet?
How can we reduce the amount of plastic we use?
How can each of us help people who live on the streets?
How can we keep old traditions alive?
How can we encourage young people to read more?
How can we make public transport more attractive?
How can we improve if nobody tells us what we did wrong?
How can children learn if the classes are so big?
How can people save money if prices keep rising?
How can anyone relax if their phone never stops ringing?
How can we trust politicians if they break their promises?
How can a small shop survive if everyone buys online?
How can students concentrate if the school is so noisy?
How can we enjoy nature if we destroy it?
How can anyone live on such a small salary?
How can people be so cruel to animals?
How can a child understand such a complicated story?
How can you call this music?
How can one person do the work of three?
How can we expect them to be happy in such conditions?
How can a game be so popular and so boring at the same time?
How can we save energy at home? The first step is to turn off lights we don't need.
How can you learn a language quickly? You need to use it every day.
How can a company keep its staff happy? It can start by listening to them.
How can parents help with homework? They can ask questions instead of giving answers.
How can we sleep better? Most experts say we should stop using screens at night.
How can a small town attract tourists? It can make the most of its history.
How can we stay positive in hard times? We can focus on small things that go well.
How can schools prepare students for the future? They can teach them to think for themselves.

examples.heading: ① How can + we / each of us + 原形動詞 ...?：引導思考

items.en: How can each of us use less water at home?
items.zh: 我們每個人在家要怎麼少用一點水？

items.en: How can we make our cities greener?
items.zh: 我們要怎麼讓城市更環保？

items.en: How can we protect our children from the dangers of the internet?
items.zh: 我們要怎麼保護孩子不受網路的危害？

items.en: How can we reduce the amount of plastic we use?
items.zh: 我們要怎麼減少使用塑膠？

items.en: How can each of us help people who live on the streets?
items.zh: 我們每個人要怎麼幫助露宿街頭的人？

items.en: How can we keep old traditions alive?
items.zh: 我們要怎麼讓古老的傳統延續下去？

items.en: How can we encourage young people to read more?
items.zh: 我們要怎麼鼓勵年輕人多讀書？

items.en: How can we make public transport more attractive?
items.zh: 我們要怎麼讓大眾運輸更吸引人？

examples.heading: ② How can + 主詞 + 原形動詞 ... if ...?：在那種條件下做不到

items.en: How can we improve if nobody tells us what we did wrong?
items.zh: 如果沒有人告訴我們哪裡做錯，我們要怎麼進步？

items.en: How can children learn if the classes are so big?
items.zh: 如果班級人數這麼多，孩子們要怎麼學習？

items.en: How can people save money if prices keep rising?
items.zh: 如果物價一直上漲，人們要怎麼存錢？

items.en: How can anyone relax if their phone never stops ringing?
items.zh: 如果手機一直響，誰能放鬆？

items.en: How can we trust politicians if they break their promises?
items.zh: 如果政治人物不守承諾，我們要怎麼相信他們？

items.en: How can a small shop survive if everyone buys online?
items.zh: 如果大家都在網路上買東西，小店要怎麼生存？

items.en: How can students concentrate if the school is so noisy?
items.zh: 如果學校這麼吵，學生要怎麼專心？

items.en: How can we enjoy nature if we destroy it?
items.zh: 如果我們破壞自然，要怎麼享受自然？

examples.heading: ③ How can + 主詞 + 原形動詞 ...?：表示不可能或不合理

items.en: How can anyone live on such a small salary?
items.zh: 這麼少的薪水，誰能過得下去？

items.en: How can people be so cruel to animals?
items.zh: 人怎麼能對動物這麼殘忍？

items.en: How can a child understand such a complicated story?
items.zh: 小孩怎麼能懂這麼複雜的故事？

items.en: How can you call this music?
items.zh: 這怎麼能叫做音樂？

items.en: How can one person do the work of three?
items.zh: 一個人怎麼能做三個人的工作？

items.en: How can we expect them to be happy in such conditions?
items.zh: 在這種條件下，我們怎麼能期待他們快樂？

items.en: How can a game be so popular and so boring at the same time?
items.zh: 一個遊戲怎麼能同時這麼受歡迎又這麼無聊？

examples.heading: ④ How can + 主詞 + 原形動詞 ...? + 接著回答

items.en: How can we save energy at home? The first step is to turn off lights we don't need.
items.zh: 我們在家要怎麼省電？第一步是關掉不需要的燈。

items.en: How can you learn a language quickly? You need to use it every day.
items.zh: 要怎麼很快學會一種語言？你必須每天用它。

items.en: How can a company keep its staff happy? It can start by listening to them.
items.zh: 公司要怎麼讓員工開心？可以先從傾聽他們開始。

items.en: How can parents help with homework? They can ask questions instead of giving answers.
items.zh: 父母要怎麼幫忙寫功課？他們可以問問題，不要直接給答案。

items.en: How can we sleep better? Most experts say we should stop using screens at night.
items.zh: 我們要怎麼睡得更好？大部分的專家說晚上應該停止使用螢幕。

items.en: How can a small town attract tourists? It can make the most of its history.
items.zh: 小鎮要怎麼吸引觀光客？它可以好好利用自己的歷史。

items.en: How can we stay positive in hard times? We can focus on small things that go well.
items.zh: 在困難的時候我們要怎麼保持樂觀？我們可以把注意力放在順利的小事上。

items.en: How can schools prepare students for the future? They can teach them to think for themselves.
items.zh: 學校要怎麼幫學生準備未來？它們可以教學生獨立思考。

title: He had written that he was sorry and that he should not have done it.
translation: 他之前寫說他很抱歉，他不應該那樣做。
name: should have 加過去分詞表示遺憾
sentences: I opened the envelope and read the letter. He had written that he was sorry and that he should not have done it.
She told me she shouldn't have shouted at the children.
The manager admitted that he shouldn't have ignored the complaints.
My brother said he shouldn't have borrowed my car without asking.
The driver said he shouldn't have been looking at his phone.
She wrote that she shouldn't have left without saying goodbye.
The festival was wonderful. You should have been there with me. I had a great time.
You should have been at the wedding. Everyone asked about you.
We all went out for dinner after the exam. You should have come.
You should have stayed longer. The best part was at the end.
You should have joined us on the boat trip. The sea was beautiful.
You should have been at the reunion. All our old classmates were there.
I should have studied medicine like my father wanted.
I should have bought that house when it was cheap.
I should have visited my grandfather more often before he died.
I should have said thank you to her before she left.
I should have learned to play an instrument as a child.
I should have kept in touch with my school friends.
I shouldn't have sold my old guitar. I miss it.
I shouldn't have believed his promises.
I shouldn't have left university after the first year.
I shouldn't have said such terrible things to my sister.
I shouldn't have moved so far away from my family.
I shouldn't have given up the piano.
The trip was badly planned. The company should have given us more information.
The road should have been finished last year.
The police should have arrived much sooner.
The school should have told the parents about the change.
The hotel should have warned us about the noise.
The doctor should have sent her to hospital immediately.
Our neighbours should have asked before they cut down the tree.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + said + 主詞 + shouldn't have + 過去分詞：轉述別人的後悔

items.en: I opened the envelope and read the letter. He had written that he was sorry and that he should not have done it.
items.zh: 我打開信封讀信。他在信裡寫說他很抱歉，他不應該那樣做。

items.en: She told me she shouldn't have shouted at the children.
items.zh: 她告訴我，她不應該對孩子們大吼的。

items.en: The manager admitted that he shouldn't have ignored the complaints.
items.zh: 經理承認他不應該忽視那些投訴。

items.en: My brother said he shouldn't have borrowed my car without asking.
items.zh: 我哥哥說他不應該沒問就借我的車。

items.en: The driver said he shouldn't have been looking at his phone.
items.zh: 司機說他不應該看手機的。

items.en: She wrote that she shouldn't have left without saying goodbye.
items.zh: 她寫說她不應該沒說再見就走。

examples.heading: ② You should have been there + with me：遺憾對方不在

items.en: The festival was wonderful. You should have been there with me. I had a great time.
items.zh: 節慶太棒了。你當時應該跟我在一起的。我玩得很開心。

items.en: You should have been at the wedding. Everyone asked about you.
items.zh: 你應該來參加婚禮的。每個人都問起你。

items.en: We all went out for dinner after the exam. You should have come.
items.zh: 考完試我們都出去吃晚餐了。你應該一起來的。

items.en: You should have stayed longer. The best part was at the end.
items.zh: 你應該多待一會的。最精彩的部分在最後。

items.en: You should have joined us on the boat trip. The sea was beautiful.
items.zh: 你應該跟我們一起去搭船的。海好美。

items.en: You should have been at the reunion. All our old classmates were there.
items.zh: 你應該來參加同學會的。我們以前的同學都在。

examples.heading: ③ I should have + 過去分詞：後悔沒做

items.en: I should have studied medicine like my father wanted.
items.zh: 我應該照我爸爸的希望念醫學的。

items.en: I should have bought that house when it was cheap.
items.zh: 那間房子便宜的時候，我應該買下來的。

items.en: I should have visited my grandfather more often before he died.
items.zh: 我爺爺過世前，我應該更常去看他的。

items.en: I should have said thank you to her before she left.
items.zh: 她離開之前，我應該跟她說謝謝的。

items.en: I should have learned to play an instrument as a child.
items.zh: 我小時候應該學一種樂器的。

items.en: I should have kept in touch with my school friends.
items.zh: 我應該跟我的同學保持聯絡的。

examples.heading: ④ I shouldn't have + 過去分詞：後悔做了

items.en: I shouldn't have sold my old guitar. I miss it.
items.zh: 我不應該賣掉我的舊吉他的。我很想念它。

items.en: I shouldn't have believed his promises.
items.zh: 我不應該相信他的承諾的。

items.en: I shouldn't have left university after the first year.
items.zh: 我不應該念完第一年就離開大學的。

items.en: I shouldn't have said such terrible things to my sister.
items.zh: 我不應該對我妹妹說那麼難聽的話的。

items.en: I shouldn't have moved so far away from my family.
items.zh: 我不應該搬到離家人那麼遠的地方的。

items.en: I shouldn't have given up the piano.
items.zh: 我不應該放棄鋼琴的。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + should have + 過去分詞：說不理想的情況

items.en: The trip was badly planned. The company should have given us more information.
items.zh: 這趟旅行計畫得很差。公司應該給我們更多資訊的。

items.en: The road should have been finished last year.
items.zh: 這條路應該去年就完工了。（被動）

items.en: The police should have arrived much sooner.
items.zh: 警察應該早一點到的。

items.en: The school should have told the parents about the change.
items.zh: 學校應該把改變告訴家長的。

items.en: The hotel should have warned us about the noise.
items.zh: 飯店應該先告訴我們有噪音的。

items.en: The doctor should have sent her to hospital immediately.
items.zh: 醫生應該馬上送她去醫院的。

items.en: Our neighbours should have asked before they cut down the tree.
items.zh: 我們的鄰居砍樹之前應該先問一下的。

title: I could have listened more to my team members.
translation: 我本來可以多聽聽團隊成員的意見的。
name: could have 表示後悔
sentences: I could have revised more before the exam.
I could have called my grandmother more often.
We could have left home a bit earlier.
I could have asked for help sooner.
I could have taken that job in Tokyo.
We could have saved more money when we were younger.
I could have told her how I felt.
I could have spent more time with my kids.
We could have booked a cheaper flight.
I could have checked the weather before we set off.
I could have rehearsed my speech one more time.
Looking back, I could have handled the argument better.
We could have bought that house for half the price ten years ago.
I could have bought the tickets when they were still cheap.
I could have written to him while he was in hospital.
I could have listened to my parents.
We could have taken the train instead of driving.
I could have said no, but I didn't want to upset him.
I could have gone to university, but I started working at eighteen.
We could have stayed another night, but we were in a hurry to get home.
I could have been kinder to my brother when we were kids.
I could have been a better friend to her.
We could have been more patient with each other.
I could have been less offhand with the new intern.
I wish I could have stayed longer.
I wish I could have been there for your birthday.
We wish we could have helped more.
I wish I could have met your father.
If only I could have seen her one more time.
If only we could have stopped him.

examples.heading: ① I / we + could have + 過去分詞

items.en: I could have revised more before the exam.
items.zh: 考試前我本來可以多複習一點的。

items.en: I could have called my grandmother more often.
items.zh: 我本來可以多打電話給我奶奶的。

items.en: We could have left home a bit earlier.
items.zh: 我們本來可以早一點出門的。

items.en: I could have asked for help sooner.
items.zh: 我本來可以早點找人幫忙的。

items.en: I could have taken that job in Tokyo.
items.zh: 我本來可以接下東京那份工作的。

items.en: We could have saved more money when we were younger.
items.zh: 我們年輕的時候本來可以多存一點錢的。

items.en: I could have told her how I felt.
items.zh: 我本來可以告訴她我的感受的。

items.en: I could have spent more time with my kids.
items.zh: 我本來可以多陪陪孩子的。

items.en: We could have booked a cheaper flight.
items.zh: 我們本來可以訂便宜一點的機票。

items.en: I could have checked the weather before we set off.
items.zh: 出發前我本來可以先看一下天氣的。

items.en: I could have rehearsed my speech one more time.
items.zh: 我本來可以把演講再排練一次的。

items.en: Looking back, I could have handled the argument better.
items.zh: 回頭想想，那次爭吵我本來可以處理得更好。

items.en: We could have bought that house for half the price ten years ago.
items.zh: 十年前我們本來可以用一半的價錢買下那間房子。

items.en: I could have bought the tickets when they were still cheap.
items.zh: 票還便宜的時候，我本來可以先買的。

items.en: I could have written to him while he was in hospital.
items.zh: 他住院的時候，我本來可以寫信給他的。

items.en: I could have listened to my parents.
items.zh: 我本來可以聽我爸媽的話的。

items.en: We could have taken the train instead of driving.
items.zh: 我們本來可以搭火車，不用開車的。

examples.heading: ② could have + 過去分詞, but ...

items.en: I could have said no, but I didn't want to upset him.
items.zh: 我本來可以拒絕的，可是我不想讓他不高興。

items.en: I could have gone to university, but I started working at eighteen.
items.zh: 我本來可以上大學的，可是我十八歲就開始工作了。

items.en: We could have stayed another night, but we were in a hurry to get home.
items.zh: 我們本來可以多住一晚，可是我們急著回家。

examples.heading: ③ I / we + could have been + 形容詞或名詞

items.en: I could have been kinder to my brother when we were kids.
items.zh: 我們小時候，我本來可以對我弟好一點。

items.en: I could have been a better friend to her.
items.zh: 我本來可以當她更好的朋友。

items.en: We could have been more patient with each other.
items.zh: 我們本來可以對彼此多一點耐心。

items.en: I could have been less offhand with the new intern.
items.zh: 我本來可以對那個新來的實習生別那麼隨便。

examples.heading: ④ I wish I could have + 過去分詞

items.en: I wish I could have stayed longer.
items.zh: 真希望我當時能待久一點。

items.en: I wish I could have been there for your birthday.
items.zh: 真希望你生日那天我能在場。

items.en: We wish we could have helped more.
items.zh: 真希望我們當時能多幫一點忙。

items.en: I wish I could have met your father.
items.zh: 真希望我有機會見到你爸爸。

examples.heading: ⑤ If only I could have + 過去分詞

items.en: If only I could have seen her one more time.
items.zh: 要是我能再見她一面就好了。

items.en: If only we could have stopped him.
items.zh: 要是我們當時攔得住他就好了。

title: My parents said it might be the last holiday where we are all together.
translation: Lisa 覺得那張彩券可能會中獎，所以拿給她爸爸看。
name: 間接引述中 might 當 may 的過去式
sentences: My parents said we might rent a house by the lake this summer.
The weatherman said it might snow at the weekend.
My friend said she might be late for the film.
The doctor said I might need glasses.
Dad said we might go to the zoo on Sunday.
The teacher said the test might be on Friday.
The mechanic said the repair might take a week.
Lisa found an old lottery ticket. She thought it might be a lucky one, so she showed it to her dad.
I thought the guests might be cold, so I lit the fire.
We thought it might rain, so we took our umbrellas.
Mum thought the bakery might sell birthday cakes, so she went in to ask.
He thought the answer might be in the dictionary.
My uncle thought the old boat might still float, so he pushed it into the lake.
My boss told me I might get a pay rise next year.
The guide told us the castle might be closed.
She told her mum she might stay at a friend's house.
The nurse told him he might feel a bit sleepy.
They told us the flight might be delayed.
My sister told me she might move to London.
I was afraid I might miss the train.
She was worried that her parents might be angry.
We were afraid the ice might break.
He was worried he might forget his lines in the play.
They were afraid the dog might bite.
I was worried that you might not come.
I wondered if you might help me with my homework.
She asked if she might use the phone.
We wondered if the rain might stop before lunch.
He asked if he might leave early.
I wondered if the shop might have a bigger size.
They asked if they might bring their dog.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + said + (that) + 主詞 + might + 原形動詞

items.en: My parents said we might rent a house by the lake this summer.
items.zh: 我爸媽說，我們今年夏天可能會在湖邊租一間房子。

items.en: The weatherman said it might snow at the weekend.
items.zh: 氣象播報員說週末可能會下雪。

items.en: My friend said she might be late for the film.
items.zh: 我朋友說她看電影可能會遲到。

items.en: The doctor said I might need glasses.
items.zh: 醫生說我可能需要戴眼鏡。

items.en: Dad said we might go to the zoo on Sunday.
items.zh: 爸爸說我們星期天可能會去動物園。

items.en: The teacher said the test might be on Friday.
items.zh: 老師說考試可能在星期五。

items.en: The mechanic said the repair might take a week.
items.zh: 修車師傅說修理可能要一個星期。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + thought + (that) + 主詞 + might + 原形動詞

items.en: Lisa found an old lottery ticket. She thought it might be a lucky one, so she showed it to her dad.
items.zh: 麗莎找到一張舊彩券。她以為那可能是中獎的彩券，所以拿給她爸爸看。

items.en: I thought the guests might be cold, so I lit the fire.
items.zh: 我想客人可能會冷，所以生了火。

items.en: We thought it might rain, so we took our umbrellas.
items.zh: 我們想可能會下雨，所以帶了雨傘。

items.en: Mum thought the bakery might sell birthday cakes, so she went in to ask.
items.zh: 媽媽以為那家麵包店可能有賣生日蛋糕，所以進去問。

items.en: He thought the answer might be in the dictionary.
items.zh: 他以為答案可能在字典裡。

items.en: My uncle thought the old boat might still float, so he pushed it into the lake.
items.zh: 我叔叔以為那艘舊船可能還浮得起來，所以把它推進湖裡。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞 + told + 人 + (that) + 主詞 + might + 原形動詞

items.en: My boss told me I might get a pay rise next year.
items.zh: 我老闆告訴我，我明年可能會加薪。

items.en: The guide told us the castle might be closed.
items.zh: 導遊告訴我們城堡可能沒開。

items.en: She told her mum she might stay at a friend's house.
items.zh: 她告訴她媽媽，她可能會在朋友家過夜。

items.en: The nurse told him he might feel a bit sleepy.
items.zh: 護理師告訴他，他可能會有點想睡。

items.en: They told us the flight might be delayed.
items.zh: 他們告訴我們班機可能會延誤。（被動）

items.en: My sister told me she might move to London.
items.zh: 我姊姊告訴我，她可能會搬到倫敦。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + was afraid / worried + (that) + 主詞 + might + 原形動詞

items.en: I was afraid I might miss the train.
items.zh: 我怕我可能會錯過火車。

items.en: She was worried that her parents might be angry.
items.zh: 她擔心她爸媽可能會生氣。

items.en: We were afraid the ice might break.
items.zh: 我們怕冰可能會破。

items.en: He was worried he might forget his lines in the play.
items.zh: 他擔心他在戲裡可能會忘詞。

items.en: They were afraid the dog might bite.
items.zh: 他們怕狗可能會咬人。

items.en: I was worried that you might not come.
items.zh: 我擔心你可能不會來。

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + wondered / asked + if + 主詞 + might + 原形動詞

items.en: I wondered if you might help me with my homework.
items.zh: 我在想你是不是可以幫我寫功課。

items.en: She asked if she might use the phone.
items.zh: 她問她可不可以用電話。

items.en: We wondered if the rain might stop before lunch.
items.zh: 我們在想雨會不會在午餐前停。

items.en: He asked if he might leave early.
items.zh: 他問他可不可以提早走。

items.en: I wondered if the shop might have a bigger size.
items.zh: 我在想那家店會不會有大一點的尺寸。

items.en: They asked if they might bring their dog.
items.zh: 他們問他們可不可以帶狗來。

title: The woman said she could put me up if I wanted.
translation: 那位女士說，如果我願意，她可以讓我借住她家。
name: could 在間接引述中當 can 的過去式
sentences: She said she could pick us up at the station.
My boss said I could leave early today.
The doctor said I could go home the next day.
He said that he could fix the bike in an hour.
They said we could stay as long as we liked.
The receptionist said that we could check in after two.
Ann said she could lend me her dictionary.
The man at the shop said he could order it for me.
My neighbour said she could water the plants while we were away.
The teacher said we could use our notes in the test.
You said you could speak a little French.
The guide said that we could take photos inside.
She told me she could help with the move.
The mechanic told us that he could have the car ready by Friday.
I told my mother I could cook dinner for once.
He told the manager he could work on Sunday.
They told us we could park behind the building.
I told them I couldn't come because I had to work.
She said she couldn't remember his name.
The bank said they couldn't change the date of the payment.
He told me he couldn't see anything without his glasses.
My sister said she couldn't stand the noise any longer.
The hotel said that they couldn't give us a refund.
He asked if he could borrow my pen.
She asked whether she could bring a friend.
A tourist asked me if I could take a photo of them.
The kids asked if they could stay up late.
I asked the waiter whether we could sit outside.
She explained that she couldn't drive at night.
He admitted that he couldn't swim.
The landlord promised that we could move in on the first.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + said (that) + 主詞 + could

items.en: She said she could pick us up at the station.
items.zh: 她說她可以到車站接我們。

items.en: My boss said I could leave early today.
items.zh: 我老闆說我今天可以早點走。

items.en: The doctor said I could go home the next day.
items.zh: 醫生說我隔天就可以回家。

items.en: He said that he could fix the bike in an hour.
items.zh: 他說他一個小時就能修好腳踏車。

items.en: They said we could stay as long as we liked.
items.zh: 他們說我們想待多久都可以。

items.en: The receptionist said that we could check in after two.
items.zh: 櫃檯人員說我們兩點以後可以入住。

items.en: Ann said she could lend me her dictionary.
items.zh: Ann 說她可以借我她的字典。

items.en: The man at the shop said he could order it for me.
items.zh: 店裡的人說他可以幫我訂。

items.en: My neighbour said she could water the plants while we were away.
items.zh: 我鄰居說我們不在的時候，她可以幫忙澆花。

items.en: The teacher said we could use our notes in the test.
items.zh: 老師說考試的時候我們可以看筆記。

items.en: You said you could speak a little French.
items.zh: 你說過你會說一點法文。

items.en: The guide said that we could take photos inside.
items.zh: 導遊說我們可以在裡面拍照。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + told + 受詞 + (that) + 主詞 + could

items.en: She told me she could help with the move.
items.zh: 她跟我說她可以幫忙搬家。

items.en: The mechanic told us that he could have the car ready by Friday.
items.zh: 技師跟我們說，他星期五之前可以把車修好。

items.en: I told my mother I could cook dinner for once.
items.zh: 我跟我媽說，這次晚餐可以由我來煮。

items.en: He told the manager he could work on Sunday.
items.zh: 他跟經理說他星期天可以上班。

items.en: They told us we could park behind the building.
items.zh: 他們跟我們說可以把車停在大樓後面。

examples.heading: ③ couldn't

items.en: I told them I couldn't come because I had to work.
items.zh: 我跟他們說我不能來，因為我得上班。

items.en: She said she couldn't remember his name.
items.zh: 她說她想不起他的名字。

items.en: The bank said they couldn't change the date of the payment.
items.zh: 銀行說他們不能更改付款日期。

items.en: He told me he couldn't see anything without his glasses.
items.zh: 他跟我說，他沒戴眼鏡什麼都看不到。

items.en: My sister said she couldn't stand the noise any longer.
items.zh: 我姊說她再也受不了那個噪音了。

items.en: The hotel said that they couldn't give us a refund.
items.zh: 飯店說他們不能退錢給我們。

examples.heading: ④ asked if / whether + 主詞 + could

items.en: He asked if he could borrow my pen.
items.zh: 他問能不能借我的筆。

items.en: She asked whether she could bring a friend.
items.zh: 她問能不能帶一個朋友來。

items.en: A tourist asked me if I could take a photo of them.
items.zh: 一個觀光客問我能不能幫他們拍張照。

items.en: The kids asked if they could stay up late.
items.zh: 孩子們問能不能晚點睡。

items.en: I asked the waiter whether we could sit outside.
items.zh: 我問服務生我們能不能坐在外面。

examples.heading: ⑤ explained、admitted、promised + that + 主詞 + could

items.en: She explained that she couldn't drive at night.
items.zh: 她解釋說她晚上不能開車。

items.en: He admitted that he couldn't swim.
items.zh: 他承認他不會游泳。

items.en: The landlord promised that we could move in on the first.
items.zh: 房東答應我們一號就可以搬進去。

title: She accepted the invitation and said that she would come on the 21st of June.
translation: 他跟我說我會喜歡，結果他說對了！
name: 間接引述中 would 當 will 的過去式
sentences: I invited the writer to our school. She accepted the invitation and said that she would come on the 21st of June.
My brother said he would pick me up after the concert.
The weather forecast said it would be sunny all weekend.
My parents said they would think about buying a dog.
The plumber said he would come back on Monday.
My friend said she would bring her guitar to the party.
He told me I would like the film, and he was right!
The doctor told my mum she would need to rest for a week.
My teacher told us the exam would be on Tuesday.
The guide told us the bus would leave at nine.
My grandmother told me she would teach me to knit.
The manager told the staff that the office would close early.
I was worried about him, so I felt better when he said that he would be at home.
I was so happy when she said she would visit us at Christmas.
We were relieved when the mechanic said the car would be fine.
I was surprised when my boss said I would get a pay rise.
The children were excited when Dad said we would go to the zoo.
I was disappointed when they said the shop would close.
My best friend promised she would keep my secret.
The company promised they would refund my money.
My dad promised he would come to my football match.
They promised they would write to us every month.
The new neighbours promised they would keep their dog quiet at night.
The builders promised the work would be finished by May.
She said she wouldn't be able to come to the meeting.
My sister said she wouldn't tell anyone.
The teacher said the test wouldn't be difficult.
He said he wouldn't need the car tomorrow.
They said it wouldn't take long to fix.
My mum said she wouldn't be home until late.
The shop assistant said the dress wouldn't fit me.

examples.heading: ① 主詞 + said + (that) + 主詞 + would + 原形動詞

items.en: I invited the writer to our school. She accepted the invitation and said that she would come on the 21st of June.
items.zh: 我邀請那位作家來我們學校。她接受了邀請，說她六月二十一日會來。

items.en: My brother said he would pick me up after the concert.
items.zh: 我哥哥說演唱會後他會來接我。

items.en: The weather forecast said it would be sunny all weekend.
items.zh: 天氣預報說整個週末都會是晴天。

items.en: My parents said they would think about buying a dog.
items.zh: 我爸媽說他們會考慮養狗。

items.en: The plumber said he would come back on Monday.
items.zh: 水管工人說他星期一會再來。

items.en: My friend said she would bring her guitar to the party.
items.zh: 我朋友說她會帶她的吉他去派對。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + told + 人 + (that) + 主詞 + would + 原形動詞

items.en: He told me I would like the film, and he was right!
items.zh: 他告訴我我會喜歡那部電影，他說對了！

items.en: The doctor told my mum she would need to rest for a week.
items.zh: 醫生告訴我媽媽她需要休息一個星期。

items.en: My teacher told us the exam would be on Tuesday.
items.zh: 我的老師告訴我們考試會在星期二。

items.en: The guide told us the bus would leave at nine.
items.zh: 導遊告訴我們巴士九點會出發。

items.en: My grandmother told me she would teach me to knit.
items.zh: 我奶奶告訴我她會教我織毛線。

items.en: The manager told the staff that the office would close early.
items.zh: 經理告訴員工辦公室會提早關門。

examples.heading: ③ I felt / was + 形容詞 + when + 主詞 + said + 主詞 + would + 原形動詞

items.en: I was worried about him, so I felt better when he said that he would be at home.
items.zh: 我很擔心他，所以他說他會在家的時候，我覺得好多了。

items.en: I was so happy when she said she would visit us at Christmas.
items.zh: 她說聖誕節會來看我們的時候，我好高興。

items.en: We were relieved when the mechanic said the car would be fine.
items.zh: 修車師傅說車子會沒事的時候，我們鬆了一口氣。

items.en: I was surprised when my boss said I would get a pay rise.
items.zh: 我老闆說我會加薪的時候，我很驚訝。

items.en: The children were excited when Dad said we would go to the zoo.
items.zh: 爸爸說我們會去動物園的時候，孩子們很興奮。

items.en: I was disappointed when they said the shop would close.
items.zh: 他們說那家店會關門的時候，我很失望。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞 + promised + (that) + 主詞 + would + 原形動詞

items.en: My best friend promised she would keep my secret.
items.zh: 我最好的朋友答應她會保守我的秘密。

items.en: The company promised they would refund my money.
items.zh: 那家公司答應他們會退錢給我。

items.en: My dad promised he would come to my football match.
items.zh: 我爸爸答應他會來看我的足球比賽。

items.en: They promised they would write to us every month.
items.zh: 他們答應每個月會寫信給我們。

items.en: The new neighbours promised they would keep their dog quiet at night.
items.zh: 新鄰居保證晚上會讓他們的狗安靜。

items.en: The builders promised the work would be finished by May.
items.zh: 工人保證工程五月前會完成。（被動）

examples.heading: ⑤ 主詞 + said + 主詞 + wouldn't + 原形動詞：轉述否定

items.en: She said she wouldn't be able to come to the meeting.
items.zh: 她說她不能來開會。

items.en: My sister said she wouldn't tell anyone.
items.zh: 我妹妹說她不會告訴任何人。

items.en: The teacher said the test wouldn't be difficult.
items.zh: 老師說考試不會很難。

items.en: He said he wouldn't need the car tomorrow.
items.zh: 他說他明天不會需要車子。

items.en: They said it wouldn't take long to fix.
items.zh: 他們說修理不會花很久。

items.en: My mum said she wouldn't be home until late.
items.zh: 我媽媽說她很晚才會回家。

items.en: The shop assistant said the dress wouldn't fit me.
items.zh: 店員說那件洋裝我穿不下。

title: Can't you see how exhausted you are?
translation: 你難道看不出來自己有多累嗎？
name: can't 表示責備和懇求
sentences: You've been so busy since you moved, but you can't forget your old friends.
You can't just leave without saying goodbye to Grandma.
You can't speak to your mother like that!
You cannot leave your bike in the hallway.
You can't eat chips every day. It's not good for you.
You can't keep borrowing money from your brother.
You can't blame the teacher for your bad marks.
You can't stay in bed all weekend.
You can't go on skipping breakfast every day.
He can't go on behaving like this at school.
We can't go on spending more than we earn.
You can't go on ignoring the problem.
She can't go on working sixty hours a week.
They can't go on arguing about the same thing every day.
You can't go on living on coffee and toast.
Can't you see the dog is hungry?
Can't you be quiet for five minutes?
Can't you see that she's trying to help you?
Can't you understand why I'm upset?
Can't you put your phone away during dinner?
Can't you think about anyone except yourself?
Can't you wait until I've finished talking?
Can't you hear the baby crying?
Please, you can't drive home tonight. You're too tired.
Listen, you can't give up now. You're nearly there.
Look, you can't keep this secret from your parents.
Please, you can't leave me here alone.
Listen, we can't let him walk home in this rain.
Please, Dad, you can't sell the house. We grew up here.
Look, you can't stay angry with her forever.
Please don't cry. You can't change what happened.

examples.heading: ① You can't / cannot + 原形動詞：責備

items.en: You've been so busy since you moved, but you can't forget your old friends.
items.zh: 你搬家以後一直很忙，可是你不能忘了老朋友。

items.en: You can't just leave without saying goodbye to Grandma.
items.zh: 你不能不跟奶奶說再見就走。

items.en: You can't speak to your mother like that!
items.zh: 你不能那樣跟你媽說話！

items.en: You cannot leave your bike in the hallway.
items.zh: 你不能把腳踏車放在走廊。

items.en: You can't eat chips every day. It's not good for you.
items.zh: 你不能每天吃薯條，那對你不好。

items.en: You can't keep borrowing money from your brother.
items.zh: 你不能一直跟你哥借錢。

items.en: You can't blame the teacher for your bad marks.
items.zh: 你不能把成績不好怪到老師身上。

items.en: You can't stay in bed all weekend.
items.zh: 你不能整個週末都待在床上。

examples.heading: ② 主詞 + can't go on + 動詞-ing

items.en: You can't go on skipping breakfast every day.
items.zh: 你不能再每天不吃早餐了。

items.en: He can't go on behaving like this at school.
items.zh: 他在學校不能再這樣下去了。

items.en: We can't go on spending more than we earn.
items.zh: 我們不能再這樣入不敷出了。

items.en: You can't go on ignoring the problem.
items.zh: 你不能再對這個問題視而不見了。

items.en: She can't go on working sixty hours a week.
items.zh: 她不能再每週工作六十個小時了。

items.en: They can't go on arguing about the same thing every day.
items.zh: 他們不能每天都為同一件事吵下去。

items.en: You can't go on living on coffee and toast.
items.zh: 你不能再只靠咖啡和吐司過日子了。

examples.heading: ③ Can't you + 原形動詞 ...?：懇求或不耐煩

items.en: Can't you see the dog is hungry?
items.zh: 你難道看不出來狗餓了嗎？

items.en: Can't you be quiet for five minutes?
items.zh: 你就不能安靜五分鐘嗎？

items.en: Can't you see that she's trying to help you?
items.zh: 你難道看不出來她是想幫你嗎？

items.en: Can't you understand why I'm upset?
items.zh: 你難道不懂我為什麼生氣嗎？

items.en: Can't you put your phone away during dinner?
items.zh: 你吃晚餐的時候就不能把手機收起來嗎？

items.en: Can't you think about anyone except yourself?
items.zh: 你就不能想想自己以外的人嗎？

items.en: Can't you wait until I've finished talking?
items.zh: 你就不能等我說完嗎？

items.en: Can't you hear the baby crying?
items.zh: 你沒聽到寶寶在哭嗎？

examples.heading: ④ Please / Listen / Look + you can't + 原形動詞：懇求

items.en: Please, you can't drive home tonight. You're too tired.
items.zh: 拜託，你今晚不能開車回家，你太累了。

items.en: Listen, you can't give up now. You're nearly there.
items.zh: 聽我說，你現在不能放棄，你快成功了。

items.en: Look, you can't keep this secret from your parents.
items.zh: 你看，你不能瞞著你爸媽這個祕密。

items.en: Please, you can't leave me here alone.
items.zh: 拜託，你不能把我一個人留在這裡。

items.en: Listen, we can't let him walk home in this rain.
items.zh: 聽我說，我們不能讓他在這種雨裡走路回家。

items.en: Please, Dad, you can't sell the house. We grew up here.
items.zh: 拜託，爸，你不能賣掉房子，我們在這裡長大的。

items.en: Look, you can't stay angry with her forever.
items.zh: 你看，你不能永遠生她的氣。

items.en: Please don't cry. You can't change what happened.
items.zh: 拜託別哭了，已經發生的事你改變不了。

title: Can you call me?
translation: 你可以打電話給我嗎？
name: can 表示請求
sentences: Can you call me when you get this message?
Can you come on Sunday at seven o'clock?
Can you send me your new address?
Can you get some bread from the bakery before it closes?
Can you wait for me outside the cinema?
Can you tell Anna about the meeting?
Can you bring a few folding chairs for the garden?
Can you lend me your charger until lunchtime?
Can you meet me at the bus stop at eight?
Can you feed the cat this evening?
Can you write your name on this form?
Can you answer the phone? I'm in the shower.
Can you keep my seat while I get a coffee?
Can you come to my house after school?
