items.en: Don't wait for me. I might not finish until seven.
items.zh: 不用等我。我可能七點才弄完。

items.en: The train may be late because of the snow.
items.zh: 火車可能會因為下雪誤點。

examples.heading: ② could：可能

items.en: "Where's my phone?" "It could be in your car."
items.zh: 我的手機在哪裡？可能在你車上。

items.en: Don't leave your bike there. Someone could take it.
items.zh: 別把腳踏車放那裡。可能會有人把它牽走。

items.en: "Who's that man with Anna?" "He could be her brother. They have the same eyes."
items.zh: 跟 Anna 在一起的那個男人是誰？可能是她哥哥。他們的眼睛長得一樣。

examples.heading: ③ should：建議

items.en: "The cinema bar is too noisy." "I agree. I think we should go somewhere else to have a drink after the film."
items.zh: 電影院的酒吧太吵了。我同意。我覺得看完電影我們應該換個地方喝一杯。

items.en: "I've had a headache for three days." "You should see a doctor."
items.zh: 我頭痛三天了。你應該去看醫生。

items.en: "I failed the test again." "You shouldn't give up. Let's study together."
items.zh: 我考試又不及格了。你不應該放棄。我們一起讀書吧。

items.en: "What should I wear to the interview?" "A dark suit is best."
items.zh: 面試我應該穿什麼？深色西裝最好。

items.en: Your English is really good. You should apply for that job.
items.zh: 你的英文真的很好。你應該去應徵那份工作。

examples.heading: ④ must / mustn't：必須和禁止

items.en: Visitors must sign in at the front desk.
items.zh: 訪客必須在櫃台登記。

items.en: I must remember to buy a card for Mum's birthday.
items.zh: 我一定要記得幫媽媽買生日卡。

items.en: "This is a secret. You mustn't tell anyone." "I promise."
items.zh: 這是秘密。你不可以告訴任何人。我保證。

items.en: "Can I use my phone in the exam?" "No, you mustn't."
items.zh: 考試的時候我可以用手機嗎？不行，不可以用。

items.en: My passport is old. I must renew it before our trip.
items.zh: 我的護照很舊了。我們旅行前我一定要去換新的。

examples.heading: ⑤ could / couldn't：過去的能力

items.en: When I was a child, I could climb any tree in the park.
items.zh: 我小時候可以爬上公園裡的任何一棵樹。

items.en: I had a bad cold last week, so I couldn't go to work.
items.zh: 我上星期重感冒，所以沒辦法去上班。

items.en: "Did you see the fireworks?" "Yes, we could see them from our window."
items.zh: 你有看到煙火嗎？有，我們從窗戶就看得到。

items.en: The music was so loud that we couldn't talk.
items.zh: 音樂太大聲了，我們沒辦法講話。

examples.heading: ⑥ could / may：請求和許可

items.en: "Could you lend me ten dollars until Friday?" "Sure, no problem."
items.zh: 你可以借我十塊錢，星期五還你嗎？好啊，沒問題。

items.en: Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the museum?
items.zh: 不好意思，可以請你告訴我去博物館怎麼走嗎？

items.en: "May I come in?" "Yes, please sit down."
items.zh: 我可以進來嗎？可以，請坐。

items.en: Guests may use the pool from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.
items.zh: 房客可以在早上七點到晚上九點使用游泳池。

examples.heading: ⑦ shall：提議

items.en: "It's really hot in here." "Shall I turn on the fan?"
items.zh: 這裡好熱。要我開電風扇嗎？

items.en: "Our guests arrive at six." "Shall I set the table now?"
items.zh: 客人六點到。要我現在擺餐具嗎？

items.en: "I'm bored." "Shall we go for a walk by the river?"
items.zh: 我好無聊。我們去河邊散散步好嗎？

items.en: "These bags are so heavy." "Shall I carry one for you?"
items.zh: 這些袋子好重。要我幫你拿一個嗎？

items.en: "Mum is coming for lunch on Sunday." "OK. What shall we cook for her?"
items.zh: 媽媽星期天要來吃午餐。好。我們要煮什麼給她吃？

title: Spring is the best time because there aren't too many tourists.
translation: 春天是最好的時節，因為觀光客沒那麼多。
name: there be 的否定句
sentences: "Can I take money out here?" "No, there isn't a bank in this village."
There isn't a lift, so we have to carry the sofa up the stairs.
Sorry, there isn't a table for four until eight o'clock.
There isn't a bus to the beach on Sundays.
"Can I have an egg sandwich?" "Sorry, there aren't any eggs left."
There aren't any chairs in the meeting room. Where did they go?
My village is boring. There aren't any shops or cafés.
There aren't any clean cups. Can you wash some?
The flat is very quiet. There isn't any noise at night.
"Can I have a coffee with milk?" "Sorry, there isn't any milk."
There isn't any information about the trip on the website yet.
We can't make a cake. There isn't any sugar.
June is nice here because there aren't too many insects yet.
There aren't many people at the gym on Friday nights.
Let's go now. There isn't much time.
"Is the city busy at night?" "Not really. There isn't much traffic after nine."
There aren't many good jobs in my town, so young people move away.
I looked at the card, but there wasn't any message on it.
There wasn't a cloud in the sky all day.
"Did you have a good holiday?" "Not really. There wasn't much sun."
There wasn't any hot water in the hotel, so I had a cold shower.
It was late, and there weren't any people on the bus.
When we arrived, there weren't any seats left.
"Was the concert good?" "Yes, but there weren't many people there."
There weren't any taxis at the station, so we walked.
"Isn't there a supermarket near here?" "No, the nearest one is in town."
Aren't there any vegetarian dishes on the menu?
"Wasn't there a park here before?" "Yes, but they built flats on it."
Hi Tom, there isn't any food in the fridge, so let's eat out tonight.
Dear Sir, I booked a double room, but there wasn't a bath in the room.
Mum, there aren't any towels in the bathroom. Can you bring one?

examples.heading: ① There isn't a / an + 單數名詞

items.en: "Can I take money out here?" "No, there isn't a bank in this village."
items.zh: 我可以在這裡領錢嗎？不行，這個村子沒有銀行。

items.en: There isn't a lift, so we have to carry the sofa up the stairs.
items.zh: 沒有電梯，所以我們得把沙發抬上樓梯。

items.en: Sorry, there isn't a table for four until eight o'clock.
items.zh: 抱歉，八點以前沒有四人桌。

items.en: There isn't a bus to the beach on Sundays.
items.zh: 星期天沒有去海灘的公車。

examples.heading: ② There aren't any + 複數名詞

items.en: "Can I have an egg sandwich?" "Sorry, there aren't any eggs left."
items.zh: 我可以點一個蛋三明治嗎？抱歉，蛋都賣完了。

items.en: There aren't any chairs in the meeting room. Where did they go?
items.zh: 會議室裡一張椅子都沒有。椅子都到哪裡去了？

items.en: My village is boring. There aren't any shops or cafés.
items.zh: 我的村子很無聊。一家商店或咖啡店都沒有。

items.en: There aren't any clean cups. Can you wash some?
items.zh: 沒有乾淨的杯子了。你可以洗幾個嗎？

examples.heading: ③ There isn't any + 不可數名詞

items.en: The flat is very quiet. There isn't any noise at night.
items.zh: 這間公寓很安靜。晚上一點聲音都沒有。

items.en: "Can I have a coffee with milk?" "Sorry, there isn't any milk."
items.zh: 我可以要一杯加牛奶的咖啡嗎？抱歉，沒有牛奶了。

items.en: There isn't any information about the trip on the website yet.
items.zh: 網站上還沒有這趟旅行的任何資訊。

items.en: We can't make a cake. There isn't any sugar.
items.zh: 我們沒辦法做蛋糕。沒有糖。

examples.heading: ④ There aren't many / There isn't much

items.en: June is nice here because there aren't too many insects yet.
items.zh: 這裡六月很舒服，因為蟲還不會太多。

items.en: There aren't many people at the gym on Friday nights.
items.zh: 星期五晚上健身房人不多。

items.en: Let's go now. There isn't much time.
items.zh: 我們現在走吧。時間不多了。

items.en: "Is the city busy at night?" "Not really. There isn't much traffic after nine."
items.zh: 這個城市晚上熱鬧嗎？還好。九點以後車子不多。

items.en: There aren't many good jobs in my town, so young people move away.
items.zh: 我住的小鎮好工作不多，所以年輕人都搬走了。

examples.heading: ⑤ There wasn't + 單數名詞 / 不可數名詞

items.en: I looked at the card, but there wasn't any message on it.
items.zh: 我看了那張卡片，可是上面沒有寫任何話。

items.en: There wasn't a cloud in the sky all day.
items.zh: 一整天天上一朵雲都沒有。

items.en: "Did you have a good holiday?" "Not really. There wasn't much sun."
items.zh: 你假期過得好嗎？不太好。沒什麼太陽。

items.en: There wasn't any hot water in the hotel, so I had a cold shower.
items.zh: 飯店沒有熱水，所以我洗了冷水澡。

examples.heading: ⑥ There weren't + 複數名詞

items.en: It was late, and there weren't any people on the bus.
items.zh: 那時很晚了，公車上一個人都沒有。

items.en: When we arrived, there weren't any seats left.
items.zh: 我們到的時候，已經沒有位子了。

items.en: "Was the concert good?" "Yes, but there weren't many people there."
items.zh: 演唱會好看嗎？好看，可是人不多。

items.en: There weren't any taxis at the station, so we walked.
items.zh: 車站一輛計程車都沒有，所以我們用走的。

examples.heading: ⑦ 問句：Isn't there ...? / Aren't there ...?

items.en: "Isn't there a supermarket near here?" "No, the nearest one is in town."
items.zh: 這附近沒有超市嗎？沒有，最近的在市區。

items.en: Aren't there any vegetarian dishes on the menu?
items.zh: 菜單上沒有素食的菜嗎？

items.en: "Wasn't there a park here before?" "Yes, but they built flats on it."
items.zh: 這裡以前不是有一座公園嗎？對，可是他們在那裡蓋了公寓。

examples.heading: ⑧ 寫信和留言

items.en: Hi Tom, there isn't any food in the fridge, so let's eat out tonight.
items.zh: 嗨 Tom，冰箱裡沒有食物了，我們今晚出去吃吧。

items.en: Dear Sir, I booked a double room, but there wasn't a bath in the room.
items.zh: 您好，我訂的是雙人房，可是房間裡沒有浴缸。

items.en: Mum, there aren't any towels in the bathroom. Can you bring one?
items.zh: 媽，浴室裡沒有毛巾。你可以拿一條來嗎？

title: She cried a lot, but she didn't give up.
translation: 她哭了很久，但是沒有放棄。
name: 不及物片語動詞（較多種）
sentences: "This puzzle is too hard." "Don't give up! You're nearly there."
I tried to learn the guitar, but I gave up after a month.
The teacher stopped for a moment and then carried on.
"Should I stop?" "No, carry on. It's a good story."
My life was too busy, so I just needed to hang out with friends for a while.
"What did you do at the weekend?" "Nothing much. We just hung out at the park."
I stayed up until two to finish my essay.
The kids can stay up late on Saturdays.
My phone died because the battery had run out.
"Can I have some more coffee?" "Sorry, it's run out."
The bus broke down, so we had to walk to school.
Our washing machine broke down again last night.
"What time are we leaving?" "We'll set off at seven to avoid the traffic."
They set off early and reached the top of the mountain by noon.
Please turn off your phones. The plane is about to take off.
Our flight took off two hours late.
"Calm down. Tell me what happened." "Someone took my bag!"
After the match, it took the fans an hour to calm down.
"You're driving too fast. Slow down!" "OK, OK."
The doctor told my dad to slow down and work less.
"Where did you grow up?" "In a small town near the sea."
When I grow up, I want to be a vet.
Our new neighbours moved in last week.
My brother is moving out next month. He's found a flat near his office.
"You look fit." "Thanks. I work out at the gym every morning."
My sister works out at home because the gym is too expensive.
Look out! There's a car coming!
"Look out! The floor is wet." "Thanks, I didn't see it."
Lisa was very sad, but she didn't give up.
"Why are you late? Did the car break down again?" "Yes, near the bridge."
Why didn't the plane take off on time?

examples.heading: ① give up / carry on

items.en: "This puzzle is too hard." "Don't give up! You're nearly there."
items.zh: 這個拼圖太難了。別放棄！你快完成了。

items.en: I tried to learn the guitar, but I gave up after a month.
items.zh: 我試過學吉他，可是一個月後就放棄了。

items.en: The teacher stopped for a moment and then carried on.
items.zh: 老師停了一下，然後繼續講。

items.en: "Should I stop?" "No, carry on. It's a good story."
items.zh: 我要停下來嗎？不用，繼續說。這個故事很好聽。

examples.heading: ② hang out / stay up

items.en: My life was too busy, so I just needed to hang out with friends for a while.
items.zh: 我的生活太忙了，所以我需要跟朋友出去玩一陣子。

items.en: "What did you do at the weekend?" "Nothing much. We just hung out at the park."
items.zh: 你週末做了什麼？沒什麼。我們就在公園閒晃。

items.en: I stayed up until two to finish my essay.
items.zh: 我熬夜到兩點寫完報告。

items.en: The kids can stay up late on Saturdays.
items.zh: 孩子們星期六可以晚睡。

examples.heading: ③ run out / break down

items.en: My phone died because the battery had run out.
items.zh: 我的手機關機了，因為電池沒電了。

items.en: "Can I have some more coffee?" "Sorry, it's run out."
items.zh: 可以再給我一點咖啡嗎？抱歉，沒了。

items.en: The bus broke down, so we had to walk to school.
items.zh: 公車拋錨了，所以我們得走路去學校。

items.en: Our washing machine broke down again last night.
items.zh: 我們的洗衣機昨晚又壞了。

examples.heading: ④ set off / take off

items.en: "What time are we leaving?" "We'll set off at seven to avoid the traffic."
items.zh: 我們幾點走？我們七點出發，避開車潮。

items.en: They set off early and reached the top of the mountain by noon.
items.zh: 他們很早出發，中午就到了山頂。

items.en: Please turn off your phones. The plane is about to take off.
items.zh: 請關手機。飛機要起飛了。

items.en: Our flight took off two hours late.
items.zh: 我們的班機晚了兩個小時起飛。

examples.heading: ⑤ calm down / slow down

items.en: "Calm down. Tell me what happened." "Someone took my bag!"
items.zh: 冷靜一點。跟我說發生了什麼事。有人拿走了我的包包！

items.en: After the match, it took the fans an hour to calm down.
items.zh: 比賽結束後，球迷過了一個小時才冷靜下來。

items.en: "You're driving too fast. Slow down!" "OK, OK."
items.zh: 你開太快了。慢一點！好啦好啦。

items.en: The doctor told my dad to slow down and work less.
items.zh: 醫生叫我爸放慢腳步，少工作一點。

examples.heading: ⑥ grow up / move in / move out

items.en: "Where did you grow up?" "In a small town near the sea."
items.zh: 你在哪裡長大的？在海邊的一個小鎮。

items.en: When I grow up, I want to be a vet.
items.zh: 我長大以後想當獸醫。

items.en: Our new neighbours moved in last week.
items.zh: 我們的新鄰居上星期搬進來了。

items.en: My brother is moving out next month. He's found a flat near his office.
items.zh: 我哥哥下個月要搬出去。他找到一間離公司很近的公寓。

examples.heading: ⑦ work out / look out

items.en: "You look fit." "Thanks. I work out at the gym every morning."
items.zh: 你看起來很健康。謝謝。我每天早上都去健身房運動。

items.en: My sister works out at home because the gym is too expensive.
items.zh: 我姊姊在家運動，因為健身房太貴了。

items.en: Look out! There's a car coming!
items.zh: 小心！有車來了！

items.en: "Look out! The floor is wet." "Thanks, I didn't see it."
items.zh: 小心！地板是濕的。謝謝，我沒看到。

examples.heading: ⑧ 否定和問句

items.en: Lisa was very sad, but she didn't give up.
items.zh: Lisa 很難過，可是她沒有放棄。

items.en: "Why are you late? Did the car break down again?" "Yes, near the bridge."
items.zh: 你怎麼遲到了？車子又拋錨了嗎？對，在橋附近。

items.en: Why didn't the plane take off on time?
items.zh: 飛機為什麼沒有準時起飛？

title: The following day, my grandpa didn't show up.
translation: 隔天，我爺爺沒有出現。
name: 不帶受詞的片語動詞（較多種）
sentences: We waited for an hour, but Tom never showed up.
"Did anyone come to the meeting?" "Only three people turned up."
She turned up at the party in a bright red dress.
The next morning, the plumber didn't show up, so we called again.
Some animals are dying out, so zoos are trying to protect them.
This old way of fishing has almost died out.
"Do people still wear these hats?" "No, that fashion never really caught on."
Online shopping caught on very quickly.
We got lost and ended up in the wrong town.
If you don't plan your time, you'll end up working all weekend.
"Where did you sleep?" "There were no rooms, so we ended up in a tent."
I only went in for milk, but I ended up spending fifty pounds.
"Are Sam and Lucy still together?" "No, they broke up last month."
The band broke up after their third album.
He started a degree in law, but he dropped out after a year.
Two runners dropped out because of the heat.
"Why did you throw away your shoes?" "They were falling apart."
After his business failed, his life fell apart.
Her grandfather passed away peacefully in his sleep.
I'm sorry to hear that your mother passed away.
In a class of thirty, one student really stood out.
Wear something bright so you stand out in the crowd.
After years of travelling, he wants to settle down.
"Are they still living abroad?" "No, they've settled down near her parents."
"How's your new job?" "The pay isn't great, but we get by."
She speaks a little Spanish, enough to get by on holiday.
My alarm didn't go off, so I was late for work.
The fire alarm went off in the middle of the night.
"You've won the first prize!" "Really? It hasn't sunk in yet."
It took a few days for the bad news to sink in.
When the teacher's words finally sank in, I felt ashamed.

examples.heading: ① show up / turn up

items.en: We waited for an hour, but Tom never showed up.
items.zh: 我們等了一個小時，可是 Tom 一直沒出現。

items.en: "Did anyone come to the meeting?" "Only three people turned up."
items.zh: 有人來開會嗎？只來了三個人。

items.en: She turned up at the party in a bright red dress.
items.zh: 她穿著一件鮮紅色的洋裝出現在派對上。

items.en: The next morning, the plumber didn't show up, so we called again.
items.zh: 隔天早上水電工沒來，所以我們又打了電話。

examples.heading: ② die out / catch on

items.en: Some animals are dying out, so zoos are trying to protect them.
items.zh: 有些動物快要滅絕了，所以動物園在努力保護牠們。

items.en: This old way of fishing has almost died out.
items.zh: 這種古老的捕魚方式幾乎已經消失了。

items.en: "Do people still wear these hats?" "No, that fashion never really caught on."
items.zh: 大家還戴這種帽子嗎？沒有，那種流行從來沒有真正紅起來。

items.en: Online shopping caught on very quickly.
items.zh: 網路購物很快就流行起來了。

examples.heading: ③ end up

items.en: We got lost and ended up in the wrong town.
items.zh: 我們迷路了，最後到了錯的小鎮。

items.en: If you don't plan your time, you'll end up working all weekend.
items.zh: 如果你不安排時間，最後整個週末都得工作。

items.en: "Where did you sleep?" "There were no rooms, so we ended up in a tent."
items.zh: 你們睡在哪裡？沒有房間了，所以我們最後睡帳篷。

items.en: I only went in for milk, but I ended up spending fifty pounds.
items.zh: 我只是進去買牛奶，結果最後花了五十英鎊。

examples.heading: ④ break up / drop out

items.en: "Are Sam and Lucy still together?" "No, they broke up last month."
items.zh: Sam 和 Lucy 還在一起嗎？沒有，他們上個月分手了。

items.en: The band broke up after their third album.
items.zh: 那個樂團出了第三張專輯後就解散了。

items.en: He started a degree in law, but he dropped out after a year.
items.zh: 他開始念法律系，可是一年後就退學了。

items.en: Two runners dropped out because of the heat.
items.zh: 有兩個跑者因為太熱退出了比賽。

examples.heading: ⑤ fall apart / pass away

items.en: "Why did you throw away your shoes?" "They were falling apart."
items.zh: 你為什麼把鞋子丟掉？它們快散了。

items.en: After his business failed, his life fell apart.
items.zh: 他的生意失敗以後，他的生活整個垮了。

items.en: Her grandfather passed away peacefully in his sleep.
items.zh: 她爺爺在睡夢中安詳過世。

items.en: I'm sorry to hear that your mother passed away.
items.zh: 聽說你母親過世了，我很遺憾。

examples.heading: ⑥ stand out / settle down

items.en: In a class of thirty, one student really stood out.
items.zh: 在一個三十人的班上，有一個學生特別突出。

items.en: Wear something bright so you stand out in the crowd.
items.zh: 穿亮一點的衣服，你在人群裡才會顯眼。

items.en: After years of travelling, he wants to settle down.
items.zh: 旅行了好幾年之後，他想安定下來。

items.en: "Are they still living abroad?" "No, they've settled down near her parents."
items.zh: 他們還住在國外嗎？沒有，他們在她爸媽附近安定下來了。

examples.heading: ⑦ get by / go off

items.en: "How's your new job?" "The pay isn't great, but we get by."
items.zh: 你的新工作怎麼樣？薪水不高，可是我們還過得去。

items.en: She speaks a little Spanish, enough to get by on holiday.
items.zh: 她會說一點西班牙文，度假時夠用了。

items.en: My alarm didn't go off, so I was late for work.
items.zh: 我的鬧鐘沒響，所以我上班遲到了。

items.en: The fire alarm went off in the middle of the night.
items.zh: 半夜火災警報響了。

examples.heading: ⑧ sink in

items.en: "You've won the first prize!" "Really? It hasn't sunk in yet."
items.zh: 你得了第一名！真的嗎？我還不敢相信。

items.en: It took a few days for the bad news to sink in.
items.zh: 過了幾天，大家才接受了這個壞消息。

items.en: When the teacher's words finally sank in, I felt ashamed.
items.zh: 老師的話我終於聽進去的時候，我覺得很慚愧。

title: Sometimes we need a person to look up to.
translation: 有時候我們需要一個可以尊敬的人。
name: 片語介系詞動詞的介系詞懸空
sentences: "Why did you become a nurse?" "My mum was a nurse. I had someone to look up to."
Young players need a good captain to look up to.
When I moved to London, I had no friends to hang out with and no one to get on with at work.
After the exam I'll have nothing to look forward to.
The new flat has a lot of problems to put up with, but it's cheap.
On a long walk, there are always things to look out for, like snakes and loose rocks.
My boss is a person I really look up to.
Rude customers are something every waiter has to put up with.
The plan that we came up with was simple and cheap.
"Is your new boss nice?" "Yes, she's someone I get on with."
The trip to Japan is the thing I'm looking forward to most this year.
These are the signs which drivers should look out for.
The paper we ran out of was the expensive kind.
"What are you looking forward to this summer?" "A week at the beach."
"Who did you look up to as a child?" "My uncle. He was a pilot."
"What did you come up with?" "Nothing yet. I need more time."
"How much noise do you have to put up with?" "Every night the music goes on until two."
"Which colleague do you get on with best?" "Probably Sam."
"What have we run out of?" "Eggs and milk."
Let me tell you what ideas I came up with for the party.
I can't believe what she has to put up with at home.
The guide told us what to look out for in the forest.
Ask the kids what they're looking forward to on the trip.
Dr Lee was looked up to by all her students.
Bullying in this school will not be put up with.
The old school rules were done away with last year.
This you will have to look out for: the last train leaves at eleven.
That kind of rude behaviour I won't put up with.
"Is that your cousin Ben?" "Yes. He's the one I never got on with as a kid."
The old printer is something we've learnt to put up with.
It was a challenge I hadn't come up against before.

examples.heading: ① 名詞 + to 不定詞

items.en: "Why did you become a nurse?" "My mum was a nurse. I had someone to look up to."
items.zh: 你為什麼當護士？我媽媽是護士。我有一個可以尊敬的榜樣。

items.en: Young players need a good captain to look up to.
items.zh: 年輕球員需要一個可以尊敬的好隊長。

items.en: When I moved to London, I had no friends to hang out with and no one to get on with at work.
items.zh: 我搬到倫敦的時候，沒有朋友可以一起出去，工作上也沒有處得來的人。

items.en: After the exam I'll have nothing to look forward to.
items.zh: 考完試以後我就沒有什麼可以期待的了。

items.en: The new flat has a lot of problems to put up with, but it's cheap.
items.zh: 新公寓有很多要忍受的問題，可是很便宜。

items.en: On a long walk, there are always things to look out for, like snakes and loose rocks.
items.zh: 走長路的時候，總是有要留意的東西，像蛇和鬆動的石頭。

examples.heading: ② 關係子句

items.en: My boss is a person I really look up to.
items.zh: 我的老闆是我很尊敬的人。

items.en: Rude customers are something every waiter has to put up with.
items.zh: 沒禮貌的客人是每個服務生都得忍受的事。

items.en: The plan that we came up with was simple and cheap.
items.zh: 我們想出來的計畫又簡單又便宜。

items.en: "Is your new boss nice?" "Yes, she's someone I get on with."
items.zh: 你的新老闆人好嗎？好啊，她是我處得來的人。

items.en: The trip to Japan is the thing I'm looking forward to most this year.
items.zh: 去日本旅行是我今年最期待的事。

items.en: These are the signs which drivers should look out for.
items.zh: 這些是開車的人要留意的標誌。

items.en: The paper we ran out of was the expensive kind.
items.zh: 我們用完的是比較貴的那種紙。

examples.heading: ③ wh 問句

items.en: "What are you looking forward to this summer?" "A week at the beach."
items.zh: 你這個夏天在期待什麼？去海邊玩一個星期。

items.en: "Who did you look up to as a child?" "My uncle. He was a pilot."
items.zh: 你小時候崇拜誰？我舅舅。他是飛行員。

items.en: "What did you come up with?" "Nothing yet. I need more time."
items.zh: 你想出什麼了？還沒有。我需要更多時間。

items.en: "How much noise do you have to put up with?" "Every night the music goes on until two."
items.zh: 你得忍受多少噪音？每天晚上音樂都放到兩點。

items.en: "Which colleague do you get on with best?" "Probably Sam."
items.zh: 你和哪個同事最處得來？大概是 Sam 吧。

items.en: "What have we run out of?" "Eggs and milk."
items.zh: 我們什麼用完了？雞蛋和牛奶。

examples.heading: ④ wh 子句

items.en: Let me tell you what ideas I came up with for the party.
items.zh: 我跟你說我想到哪些派對的點子。

items.en: I can't believe what she has to put up with at home.
items.zh: 真不敢相信她在家裡得忍受那些事。

items.en: The guide told us what to look out for in the forest.
items.zh: 導遊告訴我們在森林裡要留意什麼。

items.en: Ask the kids what they're looking forward to on the trip.
items.zh: 問問孩子們這趟旅行他們在期待什麼。

examples.heading: ⑤ 被動

items.en: Dr Lee was looked up to by all her students.
items.zh: 李博士的學生都很尊敬她。

items.en: Bullying in this school will not be put up with.
items.zh: 這所學校不會容忍霸凌。

items.en: The old school rules were done away with last year.
items.zh: 學校的舊規定去年廢除了。

examples.heading: ⑥ 受詞放在句首

items.en: This you will have to look out for: the last train leaves at eleven.
items.zh: 這一點你得注意：最後一班火車十一點開。

items.en: That kind of rude behaviour I won't put up with.
items.zh: 那種沒禮貌的行為我不會忍受。

examples.heading: ⑦ 其他片語介系詞動詞

items.en: "Is that your cousin Ben?" "Yes. He's the one I never got on with as a kid."
items.zh: 那是你表哥 Ben 嗎？對。他就是我小時候一直處不來的那個。

items.en: The old printer is something we've learnt to put up with.
items.zh: 那台舊印表機是我們已經學會忍受的東西。

items.en: It was a challenge I hadn't come up against before.
items.zh: 那是我以前沒遇過的挑戰。

title: There is one difficulty which we should deal with.
translation: 有一個難題是我們應該處理的。
name: 介系詞動詞的介系詞和受詞分開
sentences: "Is this the café you were talking about?" "Yes, the cakes are amazing."
Here's the report which I referred to in the meeting.
The hotel we stayed at was right next to the beach.
My grandmother is the person I worry about most.
"Who's that?" "That's the boy my sister used to play with."
There are some rules that all the students must agree to.
"Who are you waving at?" "My cousin. She's across the street."
"What are you laughing about?" "Nothing. Just a funny message."
"Which bus are you waiting for?" "The 23. It's late again."
"Who did you go to the cinema with?" "Some friends from work."
"What are you thinking about?" "My exam tomorrow."
I'd like to give you some ideas of what people in my town want to listen to.
Nobody knew what the teacher was talking about.
Tell me who you're angry with.
I don't understand what she's so worried about.
"Is my test result bad?" "No, there's nothing to worry about."
It's a long drive, so I need something to listen to.
When I moved here, I had no one to talk to.
My son is bored after school. He needs a hobby to focus on.
Rules about school clothes aren't strict here, but our clothes have to be clean and nice to look at.
"Is your new boss nice?" "Yes, she's easy to talk to."
My flatmate never cleans the kitchen. He's hard to live with.
"Did someone feed the cat?" "Yes, she's been looked after."
Your complaint will be dealt with by the manager.
This old song is still listened to by millions of people.
The new park was talked about for months before it opened.
The company has one problem with which it must deal immediately.
Dear Sir, I am writing about the position for which I applied last week.
The students to whom I spoke were very helpful.
To whom should we send the invitation?
This is the project on which our team has worked for two years.

examples.heading: ① 關係子句

items.en: "Is this the café you were talking about?" "Yes, the cakes are amazing."
items.zh: 這就是你說的那家咖啡店嗎？對，蛋糕超好吃。

items.en: Here's the report which I referred to in the meeting.
items.zh: 這就是我開會時提到的報告。

items.en: The hotel we stayed at was right next to the beach.
items.zh: 我們住的旅館就在海邊。

items.en: My grandmother is the person I worry about most.
items.zh: 我奶奶是我最擔心的人。

items.en: "Who's that?" "That's the boy my sister used to play with."
items.zh: 那是誰？那是我姊姊小時候常一起玩的男生。

items.en: There are some rules that all the students must agree to.
items.zh: 有一些規定是所有學生都必須同意的。

examples.heading: ② wh 問句

items.en: "Who are you waving at?" "My cousin. She's across the street."
items.zh: 你在對誰揮手？我表姊。她在對街。

items.en: "What are you laughing about?" "Nothing. Just a funny message."
items.zh: 你在笑什麼？沒什麼。只是一則好笑的訊息。

items.en: "Which bus are you waiting for?" "The 23. It's late again."
items.zh: 你在等哪一班公車？23 號。它又遲到了。

items.en: "Who did you go to the cinema with?" "Some friends from work."
items.zh: 你跟誰去看電影？幾個同事。

items.en: "What are you thinking about?" "My exam tomorrow."
items.zh: 你在想什麼？明天的考試。

examples.heading: ③ wh 子句

items.en: I'd like to give you some ideas of what people in my town want to listen to.
items.zh: 我想給你一些想法，說說我們鎮上的人想聽什麼。

items.en: Nobody knew what the teacher was talking about.
items.zh: 沒有人知道老師在說什麼。

items.en: Tell me who you're angry with.
items.zh: 跟我說你在氣誰。

items.en: I don't understand what she's so worried about.
items.zh: 我不懂她到底在擔心什麼。

examples.heading: ④ 名詞 + to 不定詞

items.en: "Is my test result bad?" "No, there's nothing to worry about."
items.zh: 我的檢查結果不好嗎？不會，沒什麼好擔心的。

items.en: It's a long drive, so I need something to listen to.
items.zh: 這段車程很長，所以我需要一些可以聽的東西。

items.en: When I moved here, I had no one to talk to.
items.zh: 我剛搬來的時候，沒有人可以說話。

items.en: My son is bored after school. He needs a hobby to focus on.
items.zh: 我兒子放學後很無聊。他需要一個可以專心投入的嗜好。

examples.heading: ⑤ 形容詞 + to 不定詞

items.en: Rules about school clothes aren't strict here, but our clothes have to be clean and nice to look at.
items.zh: 這裡對學校服裝的規定不嚴格，可是我們的衣服要乾淨，看起來好看。

items.en: "Is your new boss nice?" "Yes, she's easy to talk to."
items.zh: 你的新老闆人好嗎？好啊，她很好溝通。

items.en: My flatmate never cleans the kitchen. He's hard to live with.
items.zh: 我室友從來不清廚房。跟他住很辛苦。

examples.heading: ⑥ 被動

items.en: "Did someone feed the cat?" "Yes, she's been looked after."
items.zh: 有人餵貓了嗎？有，有人照顧牠了。

items.en: Your complaint will be dealt with by the manager.
items.zh: 您的投訴會由經理處理。

items.en: This old song is still listened to by millions of people.
items.zh: 這首老歌至今仍有幾百萬人在聽。

items.en: The new park was talked about for months before it opened.
items.zh: 新公園開放之前，大家已經談論了好幾個月。

examples.heading: ⑦ 介系詞放在前面的正式語序

items.en: The company has one problem with which it must deal immediately.
items.zh: 公司有一個必須立刻處理的問題。

items.en: Dear Sir, I am writing about the position for which I applied last week.
items.zh: 先生您好，我寫信是關於我上週應徵的職位。

items.en: The students to whom I spoke were very helpful.
items.zh: 跟我說話的那些學生都很熱心幫忙。

items.en: To whom should we send the invitation?
items.zh: 我們應該把邀請函寄給誰？

items.en: This is the project on which our team has worked for two years.
items.zh: 這就是我們團隊做了兩年的專案。

title: I hope that you'll come.
translation: 我希望你會來。
name: 動詞加 that 子句當直接受詞
sentences: Thanks for the invitation. I hope that the weather is nice for your party.
We hope that you like your new room.
"Is your brother ill?" "Yes. I hope that he feels better soon."
I'm sending you a small present. I hope that you'll like it.
"When is the concert?" "I think that it begins on 21 May."
I think that this restaurant is the best in town.
My teacher thinks that I should read more.
"Where's Dad?" "I think that he's in the garden."
I know that you're busy, but can you call me tonight?
Everyone knows that the shop closes at six.
"Your phone is ringing." "I know that it's ringing, but I'm cooking."
Did you know that Anna has a sister in Canada?
My mother said that she can help us on Saturday.
The weather report says that it will be sunny.
"Is Tom coming?" "He said that he's too tired."
The sign says that dogs are not allowed in the park.
I heard that you're quite busy right now.
"I heard that you have a new car." "Yes, it's red!"
We heard that the new café is very good.
I was sad when I heard that you were ill.
"Should I take an umbrella?" "Yes, I think that it will rain this afternoon."
I hope that we can meet next week.
She said that she will call me later.
We know that the train will be late.
"Is Sam at home?" "I don't think that he's back from work yet."
I don't think that this bag is mine.
My dad doesn't think that it's a good idea.
She didn't know that the party was on Friday.
"Do you think that she likes me?" "Ask her!"
Did your mum say that we can stay for dinner?
"Do you know that the museum is free on Sundays?" "No, I didn't know that!"

examples.heading: ① hope that

items.en: Thanks for the invitation. I hope that the weather is nice for your party.
items.zh: 謝謝你的邀請。希望你們派對那天天氣很好。

items.en: We hope that you like your new room.
items.zh: 我們希望你喜歡你的新房間。

items.en: "Is your brother ill?" "Yes. I hope that he feels better soon."
items.zh: 你哥哥生病了嗎？對。我希望他很快好起來。

items.en: I'm sending you a small present. I hope that you'll like it.
items.zh: 我寄了一個小禮物給你。希望你會喜歡。

examples.heading: ② think that

items.en: "When is the concert?" "I think that it begins on 21 May."
items.zh: 演唱會是什麼時候？我想是五月二十一日開始。

items.en: I think that this restaurant is the best in town.
items.zh: 我覺得這家餐廳是城裡最好的。

items.en: My teacher thinks that I should read more.
items.zh: 我的老師覺得我應該多讀書。

items.en: "Where's Dad?" "I think that he's in the garden."
items.zh: 爸爸在哪裡？我想他在花園裡。

examples.heading: ③ know that

items.en: I know that you're busy, but can you call me tonight?
items.zh: 我知道你很忙，可是你今晚可以打給我嗎？

items.en: Everyone knows that the shop closes at six.
items.zh: 大家都知道這家店六點關門。

items.en: "Your phone is ringing." "I know that it's ringing, but I'm cooking."
items.zh: 你的手機在響。我知道在響，可是我在煮飯。

items.en: Did you know that Anna has a sister in Canada?
items.zh: 你知道 Anna 有個姊姊在加拿大嗎？

examples.heading: ④ say that

items.en: My mother said that she can help us on Saturday.
items.zh: 我媽說她星期六可以幫我們。

items.en: The weather report says that it will be sunny.
items.zh: 天氣預報說會出太陽。

items.en: "Is Tom coming?" "He said that he's too tired."
items.zh: Tom 要來嗎？他說他太累了。

items.en: The sign says that dogs are not allowed in the park.
items.zh: 告示上寫說公園裡不准帶狗。

examples.heading: ⑤ hear that

items.en: I heard that you're quite busy right now.
items.zh: 我聽說你現在很忙。

items.en: "I heard that you have a new car." "Yes, it's red!"
items.zh: 我聽說你買了新車。對啊，是紅色的！

items.en: We heard that the new café is very good.
items.zh: 我們聽說那家新咖啡店很好。

items.en: I was sad when I heard that you were ill.
items.zh: 我聽說你生病的時候很難過。

examples.heading: ⑥ 子句說以後的事

items.en: "Should I take an umbrella?" "Yes, I think that it will rain this afternoon."
items.zh: 我該帶傘嗎？要，我想今天下午會下雨。

items.en: I hope that we can meet next week.
items.zh: 我希望我們下星期能見面。

items.en: She said that she will call me later.
items.zh: 她說她晚點會打給我。

items.en: We know that the train will be late.
items.zh: 我們知道火車會誤點。

examples.heading: ⑦ 否定

items.en: "Is Sam at home?" "I don't think that he's back from work yet."
items.zh: Sam 在家嗎？我想他還沒下班回來。

items.en: I don't think that this bag is mine.
items.zh: 我想這個包包不是我的。

items.en: My dad doesn't think that it's a good idea.
items.zh: 我爸覺得這不是個好主意。

items.en: She didn't know that the party was on Friday.
items.zh: 她不知道派對是在星期五。

examples.heading: ⑧ 問句

items.en: "Do you think that she likes me?" "Ask her!"
items.zh: 你覺得她喜歡我嗎？去問她啊！

items.en: Did your mum say that we can stay for dinner?
items.zh: 你媽有說我們可以留下來吃晚餐嗎？

items.en: "Do you know that the museum is free on Sundays?" "No, I didn't know that!"
items.zh: 你知道博物館星期天免費嗎？不知道耶！

title: When I got there, I realized that I wasn't the only winner.
translation: 我到了那裡才發現，得獎的不只我一個。
name: 轉述動詞加 that 子句當受詞
sentences: On the way home, I realized that I had left my umbrella at the office.
"Why did you go back?" "I noticed that the back door was open."
After a week in the new job, she found that she really liked it.
We suddenly realized that the shop was closing.
I understand that you're angry, but please let me explain.
Many people believe that the old castle is haunted.
"Is the meeting still on?" "I believe that it's been moved to Thursday."
My parents finally understood that I wanted to study art.
I remember that we went to this beach when I was a child.
"Why are you here on a Sunday?" "I forgot that the office was closed today."
Don't forget that the shops close early on Christmas Eve.
We expect that prices will go up next year.
"Was the test hard?" "Yes. I didn't expect that it would be so long."
The pilot explained that the flight was late because of the snow.
"Did she say why she left?" "She mentioned that she wasn't feeling well."
The manager explained to us that the hotel was full.
He finally admitted that he had eaten the last biscuit.
"Did you two stop arguing?" "Yes, we agreed that we were both wrong."
The neighbours complained that our dog barked all night.
Everyone agreed that the film was too long.
After a long talk, we decided that we would sell the house.
"Are you staying in London?" "No, I've decided that I'll move back home."
My son promised that he would tidy his room.
The company has promised that nobody will lose their job.
"I'm so tired." "I suggest that you go to bed early tonight."
My teacher suggested that I should read more English books.
The guide suggested that we visit the museum in the morning.
I realized I didn't have any cash, so I paid by card.
"Do you know Anna?" "I remember we met at a party."
She admitted she was scared of the dark.
"Ben isn't answering his phone." "I suppose he's still at work."

examples.heading: ① realize / notice / find + that 子句

items.en: On the way home, I realized that I had left my umbrella at the office.
items.zh: 回家的路上，我才發現我把傘忘在辦公室了。

items.en: "Why did you go back?" "I noticed that the back door was open."
items.zh: 你為什麼回去？我注意到後門開著。

items.en: After a week in the new job, she found that she really liked it.
items.zh: 新工作做了一個星期，她發覺她真的很喜歡。

items.en: We suddenly realized that the shop was closing.
items.zh: 我們突然發現店要關門了。

examples.heading: ② understand / believe + that 子句

items.en: I understand that you're angry, but please let me explain.
items.zh: 我理解你很生氣，可是請讓我解釋。

items.en: Many people believe that the old castle is haunted.
items.zh: 很多人相信那座老城堡鬧鬼。

items.en: "Is the meeting still on?" "I believe that it's been moved to Thursday."
items.zh: 會議還照常開嗎？我記得是改到星期四了。

items.en: My parents finally understood that I wanted to study art.
items.zh: 我爸媽終於理解我想念藝術。

examples.heading: ③ remember / forget + that 子句

items.en: I remember that we went to this beach when I was a child.
items.zh: 我記得我小時候我們來過這個海灘。

items.en: "Why are you here on a Sunday?" "I forgot that the office was closed today."
items.zh: 你為什麼星期天在這裡？我忘了今天辦公室沒開。

items.en: Don't forget that the shops close early on Christmas Eve.
items.zh: 別忘了平安夜店家會提早關門。

examples.heading: ④ expect + that 子句

items.en: We expect that prices will go up next year.
items.zh: 我們預料明年價格會上漲。

items.en: "Was the test hard?" "Yes. I didn't expect that it would be so long."
items.zh: 考試難嗎？難。我沒想到會那麼長。

examples.heading: ⑤ explain / mention + that 子句

items.en: The pilot explained that the flight was late because of the snow.
items.zh: 機長解釋說班機因為下雪而誤點。

items.en: "Did she say why she left?" "She mentioned that she wasn't feeling well."
items.zh: 她有說她為什麼走嗎？她提到她不太舒服。

items.en: The manager explained to us that the hotel was full.
items.zh: 經理跟我們解釋說飯店客滿了。

examples.heading: ⑥ admit / agree / complain + that 子句

items.en: He finally admitted that he had eaten the last biscuit.
items.zh: 他終於承認最後一塊餅乾是他吃的。

items.en: "Did you two stop arguing?" "Yes, we agreed that we were both wrong."
items.zh: 你們兩個不吵了嗎？對，我們都同意兩個人都有錯。

items.en: The neighbours complained that our dog barked all night.
items.zh: 鄰居抱怨我們的狗叫了一整晚。

items.en: Everyone agreed that the film was too long.
items.zh: 大家都同意那部電影太長了。

examples.heading: ⑦ decide / promise + that 子句

items.en: After a long talk, we decided that we would sell the house.
items.zh: 談了很久以後，我們決定把房子賣掉。

items.en: "Are you staying in London?" "No, I've decided that I'll move back home."
items.zh: 你要留在倫敦嗎？不，我決定搬回老家。

items.en: My son promised that he would tidy his room.
items.zh: 我兒子答應會整理他的房間。

items.en: The company has promised that nobody will lose their job.
items.zh: 公司保證不會有人失業。

examples.heading: ⑧ suggest + that 子句

items.en: "I'm so tired." "I suggest that you go to bed early tonight."
items.zh: 我好累。我建議你今晚早點睡。

items.en: My teacher suggested that I should read more English books.
items.zh: 我的老師建議我多讀英文書。

items.en: The guide suggested that we visit the museum in the morning.
items.zh: 導遊建議我們早上去參觀博物館。

examples.heading: ⑨ 省略 that

items.en: I realized I didn't have any cash, so I paid by card.
items.zh: 我發現我沒帶現金，所以我刷卡。

items.en: "Do you know Anna?" "I remember we met at a party."
items.zh: 你認識 Anna 嗎？我記得我們在一個派對上見過。

items.en: She admitted she was scared of the dark.
items.zh: 她承認她怕黑。

items.en: "Ben isn't answering his phone." "I suppose he's still at work."
items.zh: Ben 沒接電話。我猜他還在上班。

title: You needn't come if you're busy.
translation: 你如果忙的話，就不用來了。
name: 半情態動詞 dare 和 need
sentences: Thanks, but you needn't drive me. I can take the bus.
You needn't worry about where we can stay. My aunt has a big house.
"Shall I bring some food?" "No, you needn't. We've got plenty."
You needn't shout. I can hear you.
The test is easy. You needn't study all night.
We needn't leave yet. The film starts at nine.
"Need I bring my passport?" "No, your ID card is enough."
Need I say more? You know what I mean.
"Need we book a table?" "No, it's never busy on Mondays."
My parents hate driving, but they daren't sell their car. They live far from the bus stop.
I daren't tell my mum about the broken vase.
She daren't go into the sea because of the jellyfish.
"Why don't you ask your boss for a day off?" "I daren't. We're too busy this month."
My little brother daren't sleep with the light off.
"I gave your old jacket to a friend." "How dare you give away my things!"
"I took your car this morning." "How dare you take it without asking!"
How dare he talk to my mother like that!
How dare they park in front of our garage again!
"There's a big spider on the wall. Dare you pick it up?" "No way!"
"Is the new restaurant good?" "I dare say it is. It's always full."
"Will the shops be open on Sunday?" "I dare say some of them will."
You don't need to take your shoes off. Come in.
"Do I need to print the ticket?" "No, you can show it on your phone."
My son doesn't need to wear glasses any more.
"Did you have to change trains?" "No, we didn't need to. The train went straight there."
Nobody dared to say anything when the boss was angry.
The dog was so big that I didn't dare go past it.
She doesn't dare to drive in the city at night.
You needn't wear a suit, but you mustn't wear shorts.
You needn't finish the book today, but you mustn't lose it. It's from the library.
"Need I call first?" "No, you needn't. Just come any time."

examples.heading: ① needn't：不必

items.en: Thanks, but you needn't drive me. I can take the bus.
items.zh: 謝謝，可是你不必開車送我。我可以搭公車。

items.en: You needn't worry about where we can stay. My aunt has a big house.
items.zh: 你不必擔心我們要住哪裡。我阿姨家很大。

items.en: "Shall I bring some food?" "No, you needn't. We've got plenty."
items.zh: 要我帶點吃的嗎？不用，你不必帶。我們有很多。

items.en: You needn't shout. I can hear you.
items.zh: 你不必用吼的。我聽得到。

items.en: The test is easy. You needn't study all night.
items.zh: 考試很簡單。你不必念一整晚。

items.en: We needn't leave yet. The film starts at nine.
items.zh: 我們還不用走。電影九點才開始。

examples.heading: ② Need I ...?：問句

items.en: "Need I bring my passport?" "No, your ID card is enough."
items.zh: 我需要帶護照嗎？不用，你的身分證就夠了。

items.en: Need I say more? You know what I mean.
items.zh: 還需要我多說嗎？你知道我的意思。

items.en: "Need we book a table?" "No, it's never busy on Mondays."
items.zh: 我們需要訂位嗎？不用，星期一從來不會客滿。

examples.heading: ③ daren't：不敢

items.en: My parents hate driving, but they daren't sell their car. They live far from the bus stop.
items.zh: 我爸媽很討厭開車，可是他們不敢把車賣掉。他們住得離公車站很遠。

items.en: I daren't tell my mum about the broken vase.
items.zh: 我不敢跟我媽說花瓶破了的事。

items.en: She daren't go into the sea because of the jellyfish.
items.zh: 她因為有水母，不敢下海。

items.en: "Why don't you ask your boss for a day off?" "I daren't. We're too busy this month."
items.zh: 你為什麼不跟老闆請一天假？我不敢。我們這個月太忙了。

items.en: My little brother daren't sleep with the light off.
items.zh: 我弟弟不敢關燈睡覺。

examples.heading: ④ How dare you ...!：生氣

items.en: "I gave your old jacket to a friend." "How dare you give away my things!"
items.zh: 我把你的舊外套送給朋友了。你怎麼敢把我的東西送人！

items.en: "I took your car this morning." "How dare you take it without asking!"
items.zh: 我今天早上開了你的車。你怎麼敢不問一聲就開走！

items.en: How dare he talk to my mother like that!
items.zh: 他怎麼敢那樣跟我媽說話！

items.en: How dare they park in front of our garage again!
items.zh: 他們怎麼敢又停在我們車庫前面！

examples.heading: ⑤ Dare you ...? 和 I dare say

items.en: "There's a big spider on the wall. Dare you pick it up?" "No way!"
items.zh: 牆上有一隻大蜘蛛。你敢把牠抓起來嗎？才不要！

items.en: "Is the new restaurant good?" "I dare say it is. It's always full."
items.zh: 那家新餐廳好吃嗎？我想應該不錯。它總是客滿。

items.en: "Will the shops be open on Sunday?" "I dare say some of them will."
items.zh: 星期天商店會開嗎？我想有些會開吧。

examples.heading: ⑥ 一般動詞：don't need to

items.en: You don't need to take your shoes off. Come in.
items.zh: 你不需要脫鞋。進來吧。

items.en: "Do I need to print the ticket?" "No, you can show it on your phone."
items.zh: 我需要把票印出來嗎？不用，你可以用手機出示。

items.en: My son doesn't need to wear glasses any more.
items.zh: 我兒子不需要再戴眼鏡了。

items.en: "Did you have to change trains?" "No, we didn't need to. The train went straight there."
items.zh: 你們得換車嗎？不用，我們不需要換。那班車直達。

examples.heading: ⑦ 一般動詞：don't dare (to)

items.en: Nobody dared to say anything when the boss was angry.
items.zh: 老闆生氣的時候，沒有人敢說話。

items.en: The dog was so big that I didn't dare go past it.
items.zh: 那隻狗好大，我不敢從牠旁邊走過去。

items.en: She doesn't dare to drive in the city at night.
items.zh: 她不敢晚上在市區開車。

examples.heading: ⑧ needn't 和 mustn't

items.en: You needn't wear a suit, but you mustn't wear shorts.
items.zh: 你不必穿西裝，可是不可以穿短褲。

items.en: You needn't finish the book today, but you mustn't lose it. It's from the library.
items.zh: 你不必今天看完這本書，可是不可以弄丟。這是圖書館的書。

items.en: "Need I call first?" "No, you needn't. Just come any time."
items.zh: 我需要先打電話嗎？不用，你不必打。隨時來就好。

title: You've got to bring paintbrushes, paper and paint.
translation: 你得帶畫筆、紙和顏料。
name: 半情態動詞 have (got) to
sentences: "Are you coming to the party?" "I can't. I have to work on Saturday."
All students have to wear a uniform at my school.
My dad has to take the train at six every morning.
"Why are you studying so late?" "I have to pass this exam."
The baby has to sleep at seven, so we eat early.
Dear class, for Saturday's lesson you've got to bring paintbrushes, paper and paint.
Sorry, I've got to go now. My bus is coming.
"Can you play tonight?" "No, I've got to finish my report."
She's got to be at the airport by five.
We've got to buy a present for Grandma before Sunday.
You've really got to try this cake. It's amazing!
The doctor was very busy, so I had to wait an hour.
Our flight was cancelled, and we had to stay one more night in Rome.
When I was young, I had to walk to school every day.
"Why were you late?" "I had to take my son to the dentist."
The shop is closed today. We'll have to come back tomorrow.
If you miss the last bus, you'll have to take a taxi.
My car is broken, so I'll have to cycle to work this week.
Dinner is on me. You don't have to pay.
You don't have to bring anything except your clothes. We have towels.
It's Sunday tomorrow, so the kids don't have to get up early.
My sister doesn't have to work on Fridays.
We didn't have to wait. The table was ready.
"Do I have to pay now?" "No, you can pay when you leave."
"Does your brother have to wear a suit to work?" "Only on Mondays."
"Have we got to finish this today?" "Yes, the boss wants it tonight."
"Did you have to show your passport?" "Yes, twice."
"What time have you got to be at work?" "At half past eight."
"Where's Anna?" "She's got to stay late at the office tonight."
Tom has got to see the doctor about his knee.
"Can your son come out to play?" "Not now. He has to tidy his room first."

examples.heading: ① have to：現在

items.en: "Are you coming to the party?" "I can't. I have to work on Saturday."
items.zh: 你要來派對嗎？沒辦法。我星期六得上班。

items.en: All students have to wear a uniform at my school.
items.zh: 我們學校所有學生都得穿制服。

items.en: My dad has to take the train at six every morning.
items.zh: 我爸每天早上六點就得搭火車。

items.en: "Why are you studying so late?" "I have to pass this exam."
items.zh: 你怎麼念書念到這麼晚？我得通過這個考試。

items.en: The baby has to sleep at seven, so we eat early.
items.zh: 寶寶七點就得睡覺，所以我們很早吃晚餐。

examples.heading: ② have got to：現在

items.en: Dear class, for Saturday's lesson you've got to bring paintbrushes, paper and paint.
items.zh: 各位同學，星期六的課你們得帶畫筆、紙和顏料。

items.en: Sorry, I've got to go now. My bus is coming.
items.zh: 抱歉，我現在得走了。我的公車來了。

items.en: "Can you play tonight?" "No, I've got to finish my report."
items.zh: 你今晚可以一起玩嗎？不行，我得把報告寫完。

items.en: She's got to be at the airport by five.
items.zh: 她五點以前得到機場。

items.en: We've got to buy a present for Grandma before Sunday.
items.zh: 星期天以前我們得幫奶奶買個禮物。

items.en: You've really got to try this cake. It's amazing!
items.zh: 你真的一定要吃吃看這個蛋糕。太好吃了！

examples.heading: ③ had to：過去

items.en: The doctor was very busy, so I had to wait an hour.
items.zh: 醫生很忙，所以我等了一個小時。

items.en: Our flight was cancelled, and we had to stay one more night in Rome.
items.zh: 我們的班機取消了，所以我們得在羅馬多待一晚。

items.en: When I was young, I had to walk to school every day.
items.zh: 我小時候每天都得走路上學。

items.en: "Why were you late?" "I had to take my son to the dentist."
items.zh: 你怎麼遲到了？我得帶我兒子去看牙醫。

examples.heading: ④ will have to：未來

items.en: The shop is closed today. We'll have to come back tomorrow.
items.zh: 這家店今天沒開。我們得明天再來。

items.en: If you miss the last bus, you'll have to take a taxi.
items.zh: 你要是錯過最後一班公車，就得搭計程車了。

items.en: My car is broken, so I'll have to cycle to work this week.
items.zh: 我的車壞了，所以這星期我得騎腳踏車上班。

examples.heading: ⑤ don't have to：不必

items.en: Dinner is on me. You don't have to pay.
items.zh: 晚餐我請。你不用付錢。

items.en: You don't have to bring anything except your clothes. We have towels.
items.zh: 除了衣服，你什麼都不用帶。我們有毛巾。

items.en: It's Sunday tomorrow, so the kids don't have to get up early.
items.zh: 明天是星期天，所以孩子們不用早起。

items.en: My sister doesn't have to work on Fridays.
items.zh: 我妹妹星期五不用上班。

items.en: We didn't have to wait. The table was ready.
items.zh: 我們不用等。位子已經準備好了。

examples.heading: ⑥ 問句

items.en: "Do I have to pay now?" "No, you can pay when you leave."
items.zh: 我現在就得付錢嗎？不用，你走的時候再付就好。

items.en: "Does your brother have to wear a suit to work?" "Only on Mondays."
items.zh: 你哥哥上班得穿西裝嗎？只有星期一要。

items.en: "Have we got to finish this today?" "Yes, the boss wants it tonight."
items.zh: 我們今天就得把這個做完嗎？對，老闆今晚就要。

items.en: "Did you have to show your passport?" "Yes, twice."
items.zh: 你得出示護照嗎？要，兩次。

items.en: "What time have you got to be at work?" "At half past eight."
items.zh: 你幾點得到公司？八點半。

examples.heading: ⑦ 第三人稱單數：has to / has got to

items.en: "Where's Anna?" "She's got to stay late at the office tonight."
items.zh: Anna 在哪裡？她今晚得在辦公室待到很晚。

items.en: Tom has got to see the doctor about his knee.
items.zh: Tom 得去看醫生，檢查他的膝蓋。

items.en: "Can your son come out to play?" "Not now. He has to tidy his room first."
items.zh: 你兒子可以出來玩嗎？現在不行。他得先整理房間。

title: We used to play together every single day!
translation: 我們以前每天都玩在一起！
name: 半情態動詞 used to、ought to
sentences: "Do you remember me? We used to play together every single day!"
When I was a student, I used to stay up until three in the morning.
Before the new road, my mum used to drive two hours to work.
"Do you still play tennis?" "No, but I used to play every weekend."
We used to spend every summer at my grandparents' farm.
There used to be a small bookshop on this corner. Now it's a bank.
My brother used to have long hair, but he cut it last year.
"Is this your old house?" "Yes, we used to live on the second floor."
This town used to be very quiet before the factory opened.
"You're so good at maths!" "Thanks, but I used to be terrible at it."
"You run every morning?" "Yes, but I didn't use to. I started last year."
My sister didn't use to be so shy. She was very talkative as a child.
We didn't use to have a car, so we went everywhere by bus.
"Did you use to live near here?" "Yes, in the blue building over there."
"Did your mum use to work in a hospital?" "Yes, she was a nurse."
"What did you use to do on Sunday afternoons?" "We went to the park."
You look tired. I think you ought to join a gym and walk more.
"My tooth really hurts." "You ought to see a dentist."
It's a long drive. We ought to leave before seven.
You ought to call your grandmother. She misses you.
Before the interview, you ought to read about the company.
He broke your phone, so he ought to pay for it.
Children ought to be in bed by nine on school nights.
"Mrs Wu helped me with my bags." "You ought to thank her with a card."
Everyone ought to learn how to swim.
You ought not to drive so fast in the rain.
You ought not to eat sweets before bed. They're bad for your teeth.
"Should I tell him about the party?" "No, you ought not to. It's a surprise."
I used to eat a lot of junk food. I know I ought to eat better now.
My grandpa used to smoke a lot. Now he tells everyone they ought to stop.
We used to meet every week. We ought to do that again.

examples.heading: ① used to：過去的習慣

items.en: "Do you remember me? We used to play together every single day!"
items.zh: 你還記得我嗎？我們以前每天都玩在一起！

items.en: When I was a student, I used to stay up until three in the morning.
items.zh: 我當學生的時候，常常熬到凌晨三點。

items.en: Before the new road, my mum used to drive two hours to work.
items.zh: 新路開通以前，我媽都要開兩個小時的車去上班。

items.en: "Do you still play tennis?" "No, but I used to play every weekend."
items.zh: 你還打網球嗎？沒有了，可是我以前每個週末都打。

items.en: We used to spend every summer at my grandparents' farm.
items.zh: 我們以前每年夏天都在我爺爺奶奶的農場過。

examples.heading: ② used to：過去的狀態

items.en: There used to be a small bookshop on this corner. Now it's a bank.
items.zh: 這個轉角以前有一家小書店。現在變成銀行了。

items.en: My brother used to have long hair, but he cut it last year.
items.zh: 我哥以前留長髮，可是他去年剪掉了。

items.en: "Is this your old house?" "Yes, we used to live on the second floor."
items.zh: 這是你以前的家嗎？對，我們以前住在二樓。

items.en: This town used to be very quiet before the factory opened.
items.zh: 工廠開之前，這個小鎮以前很安靜。

items.en: "You're so good at maths!" "Thanks, but I used to be terrible at it."
items.zh: 你數學好好！謝謝，可是我以前數學很爛。

examples.heading: ③ used to：否定

items.en: "You run every morning?" "Yes, but I didn't use to. I started last year."
items.zh: 你每天早上都跑步？對，可是我以前沒有。我去年才開始。

items.en: My sister didn't use to be so shy. She was very talkative as a child.
items.zh: 我妹以前沒這麼害羞。她小時候話很多。

items.en: We didn't use to have a car, so we went everywhere by bus.
items.zh: 我們以前沒有車，所以去哪裡都搭公車。

examples.heading: ④ used to：問句

items.en: "Did you use to live near here?" "Yes, in the blue building over there."
items.zh: 你以前住在這附近嗎？對，就是那邊那棟藍色的大樓。

items.en: "Did your mum use to work in a hospital?" "Yes, she was a nurse."
items.zh: 你媽媽以前在醫院工作嗎？對，她以前是護理師。

items.en: "What did you use to do on Sunday afternoons?" "We went to the park."
items.zh: 你們以前星期天下午都做什麼？我們去公園。

examples.heading: ⑤ ought to：建議

items.en: You look tired. I think you ought to join a gym and walk more.
items.zh: 你看起來很累。我覺得你應該去健身房，多走路。

items.en: "My tooth really hurts." "You ought to see a dentist."
items.zh: 我的牙齒好痛。你應該去看牙醫。

items.en: It's a long drive. We ought to leave before seven.
items.zh: 要開很久的車。我們應該七點以前出發。

items.en: You ought to call your grandmother. She misses you.
items.zh: 你應該打給你奶奶。她很想你。

items.en: Before the interview, you ought to read about the company.
items.zh: 面試前你應該先了解一下那家公司。

examples.heading: ⑥ ought to：說對的事

items.en: He broke your phone, so he ought to pay for it.
items.zh: 他弄壞了你的手機，所以他應該賠錢。

items.en: Children ought to be in bed by nine on school nights.
items.zh: 上學日的晚上，孩子九點以前應該要上床。

items.en: "Mrs Wu helped me with my bags." "You ought to thank her with a card."
items.zh: 吳太太幫我提了袋子。你應該寫張卡片謝謝她。

items.en: Everyone ought to learn how to swim.
items.zh: 每個人都應該學游泳。

examples.heading: ⑦ ought not to：否定

items.en: You ought not to drive so fast in the rain.
items.zh: 下雨天你不應該開這麼快。

items.en: You ought not to eat sweets before bed. They're bad for your teeth.
items.zh: 你睡前不應該吃糖果。對牙齒不好。

items.en: "Should I tell him about the party?" "No, you ought not to. It's a surprise."
items.zh: 我應該跟他說派對的事嗎？不，你不應該說。那是驚喜。

examples.heading: ⑧ used to 和 ought to 在同一段話裡

items.en: I used to eat a lot of junk food. I know I ought to eat better now.
items.zh: 我以前吃很多垃圾食物。我知道我現在應該吃得健康一點。

items.en: My grandpa used to smoke a lot. Now he tells everyone they ought to stop.
items.zh: 我爺爺以前抽很多菸。現在他跟每個人說他們應該戒菸。

items.en: We used to meet every week. We ought to do that again.
items.zh: 我們以前每個星期都見面。我們應該再像以前那樣見面。

title: There are many shops and schools.
translation: 這裡有很多商店和學校。
name: there are 加複數名詞片語
sentences: "How big is your new flat?" "There are two bedrooms and a small kitchen."
There are two bathrooms in our house, so we don't wait in the morning.
In my bedroom there are three windows.
There are four chairs in the kitchen, but there are five of us.
I like my area. There are many parks and quiet streets.
There are many good restaurants near my office.
In my city there are many old buildings.
There are many buses to the airport, so don't worry.
"Is the park nice?" "Yes. I think there are some animals in the park, like ducks."
There are some nice beaches near my town.
There are some books on the table for you.
On the wall there are some photos of my family.
"Is your English class big?" "No, there are only eight of us."
In our school there are two computer rooms.
There are three new people in my office this week.
"Are there many teachers?" "Yes, there are about fifty teachers."
Hi Anna, there are some letters for you on the kitchen table.
There are two tickets for the concert. Do you want to come?
Dad, there are some eggs in the fridge for your breakfast.
There are three messages for you on your phone.
"Why is it so noisy?" "There are lots of children in the garden next door."
There are many people at the beach on hot days.
There are two men at the door. They want to see you.
In my family there are five people.
In my bag there are two pens and a notebook.
There are two banks and a cinema in the main street.
"What's in the box?" "There are some cups and plates."
On the desk there are two pens. Take one.
Under the bed there are some old shoes.
In the fridge there are some apples and oranges.
Near the station there are lots of hotels.

examples.heading: ① 介紹家裡：There are + 數字 + 複數名詞

items.en: "How big is your new flat?" "There are two bedrooms and a small kitchen."
items.zh: 你的新公寓多大？有兩間臥室和一間小廚房。

items.en: There are two bathrooms in our house, so we don't wait in the morning.
items.zh: 我們家有兩間浴室，所以早上不用等。

items.en: In my bedroom there are three windows.
items.zh: 我的臥室有三扇窗戶。

items.en: There are four chairs in the kitchen, but there are five of us.
items.zh: 廚房有四張椅子，可是我們家有五個人。

examples.heading: ② 介紹附近：There are + many + 複數名詞

items.en: I like my area. There are many parks and quiet streets.
items.zh: 我喜歡我住的地區。這裡有很多公園和安靜的街道。

items.en: There are many good restaurants near my office.
items.zh: 我辦公室附近有很多好餐廳。

items.en: In my city there are many old buildings.
items.zh: 我住的城市有很多古老的建築。

items.en: There are many buses to the airport, so don't worry.
items.zh: 去機場的公車很多，所以別擔心。

examples.heading: ③ 介紹地方：There are + some + 複數名詞

items.en: "Is the park nice?" "Yes. I think there are some animals in the park, like ducks."
items.zh: 那座公園好玩嗎？好玩。我想公園裡有一些動物，像是鴨子。

items.en: There are some nice beaches near my town.
items.zh: 我住的小鎮附近有一些漂亮的海灘。

items.en: There are some books on the table for you.
items.zh: 桌上有幾本給你的書。

items.en: On the wall there are some photos of my family.
items.zh: 牆上有一些我家人的照片。

examples.heading: ④ 學校和工作：There are + 複數名詞片語

items.en: "Is your English class big?" "No, there are only eight of us."
items.zh: 你的英文班人多嗎？不多，我們只有八個人。

items.en: In our school there are two computer rooms.
items.zh: 我們學校有兩間電腦教室。

items.en: There are three new people in my office this week.
items.zh: 這星期我辦公室來了三個新人。

items.en: "Are there many teachers?" "Yes, there are about fifty teachers."
items.zh: 老師多嗎？多，大概有五十位老師。

examples.heading: ⑤ 寫信和留言：There are + 複數名詞片語

items.en: Hi Anna, there are some letters for you on the kitchen table.
items.zh: 嗨 Anna，廚房桌上有幾封給你的信。

items.en: There are two tickets for the concert. Do you want to come?
items.zh: 有兩張演唱會的票。你要一起去嗎？

items.en: Dad, there are some eggs in the fridge for your breakfast.
items.zh: 爸，冰箱裡有一些蛋給你當早餐。

items.en: There are three messages for you on your phone.
items.zh: 你的手機上有三則訊息。

examples.heading: ⑥ 人：There are + 複數名詞片語

items.en: "Why is it so noisy?" "There are lots of children in the garden next door."
items.zh: 怎麼這麼吵？隔壁的花園裡有很多小孩。

items.en: There are many people at the beach on hot days.
items.zh: 天氣熱的時候海灘上有很多人。

items.en: There are two men at the door. They want to see you.
items.zh: 門口有兩個男人。他們要見你。

items.en: In my family there are five people.
items.zh: 我家有五個人。

examples.heading: ⑦ 複數名詞 + and + 名詞

items.en: In my bag there are two pens and a notebook.
items.zh: 我的包包裡有兩支筆和一本筆記本。

items.en: There are two banks and a cinema in the main street.
items.zh: 大街上有兩家銀行和一家電影院。

items.en: "What's in the box?" "There are some cups and plates."
items.zh: 箱子裡有什麼？有一些杯子和盤子。

examples.heading: ⑧ 東西在哪裡：地點 + there are + 複數名詞片語

items.en: On the desk there are two pens. Take one.
items.zh: 桌上有兩支筆。拿一支去用。

items.en: Under the bed there are some old shoes.
items.zh: 床底下有一些舊鞋子。

items.en: In the fridge there are some apples and oranges.
items.zh: 冰箱裡有一些蘋果和柳橙。

items.en: Near the station there are lots of hotels.
items.zh: 車站附近有很多飯店。

items.zh: 我的村子很小，可是有一家不錯的餐廳。

examples.heading: ④ 地點在句首：地點 + there is + 單數名詞片語

examples.heading: ① There are a lot of + 複數名詞（介紹地方）

items.en: You should visit the old port. There are a lot of fishing boats.
items.zh: 你應該去舊港口看看。那裡有很多漁船。

items.en: It's a very interesting museum because there are a lot of pictures.
items.zh: 那間博物館很有趣，因為有很多畫。

items.en: There are a lot of parks in my city, so it's great for families.
items.zh: 我住的城市有很多公園，所以很適合家庭。

items.en: In my street there are a lot of old houses.
items.zh: 我住的街上有很多老房子。

items.en: "Is your town nice?" "Yes, there are a lot of good restaurants."
items.zh: 你住的小鎮好嗎？好，有很多不錯的餐廳。

examples.heading: ② There are a lot of + 複數名詞（人）

items.en: Spring is busy here. There are a lot of tourists in April.
items.zh: 這裡春天很忙。四月有很多觀光客。

items.en: There are a lot of students from China in my class.
items.zh: 我班上有很多從中國來的學生。

items.en: "Why are you late?" "There were a lot of people at the bus stop."
items.zh: 你怎麼遲到了？公車站有好多人。

items.en: There are a lot of children in the pool on Saturdays.
items.zh: 星期六游泳池裡有很多小孩。

examples.heading: ③ There are a lot of + 複數名詞（東西）

items.en: There are a lot of books in my bag, so it's very heavy.
items.zh: 我包包裡有很多書，所以很重。

items.en: Be careful. There are a lot of cars on this road.
items.zh: 小心。這條路上車子很多。

items.en: There are a lot of mistakes in your essay. Please check it again.
items.zh: 你的作文有很多錯誤。請再檢查一次。

items.en: There are a lot of clothes in the sale, and they are very cheap.
items.zh: 特價區有很多衣服，而且很便宜。

examples.heading: ④ There's a lot of + 複數名詞（口語）

items.en: "Are you at the party yet?" "Yes! There's a lot of people here."
items.zh: 你到派對了嗎？到了！這裡好多人。

items.en: Come and see the market. There's a lot of nice things to buy.
items.zh: 來看看市場吧。有很多好東西可以買。

items.en: Hurry up! There's a lot of people in the queue already.
items.zh: 快一點！已經有好多人在排隊了。

examples.heading: ⑤ There is a lot of + 不可數名詞

items.en: Let's leave early. There is a lot of traffic in the morning.
items.zh: 我們早點出門吧。早上車很多。

items.en: "Is the work hard?" "Not really, but there is a lot of paperwork."
items.zh: 工作辛苦嗎？還好，可是文書工作很多。

items.en: There's a lot of noise from the street at night.
items.zh: 晚上街上很吵。

items.en: There is a lot of rain in this area in winter.
items.zh: 這個地區冬天雨很多。

examples.heading: ⑥ There are lots of + 複數名詞

items.en: "What can kids do here?" "There are lots of things to do on the beach."
items.zh: 小孩在這裡可以做什麼？海灘上有很多事可以做。

items.en: There are lots of birds in the garden this morning.
items.zh: 今天早上花園裡有很多鳥。

items.en: There are lots of ways to learn English online.
items.zh: 在網路上學英文有很多方法。

examples.heading: ⑦ 問句和過去

items.en: "Are there a lot of shops near your hotel?" "Yes, it's right in the center."
items.zh: 你的飯店附近商店多嗎？多，就在市中心。

items.en: When I was young, there were a lot of fields here.
items.zh: 我小時候，這裡有很多田。

items.en: There was a lot of snow last winter.
items.zh: 去年冬天下了很多雪。

items.en: "I went to the new mall yesterday." "Were there a lot of shops open?"
items.zh: 我昨天去了新的購物中心。開的店多嗎？

examples.heading: ⑧ 寫信：There are a lot of + 複數名詞

items.en: Dear Sam, my new school is great. There are a lot of clubs and sports.
items.zh: 親愛的 Sam，我的新學校很棒。有很多社團和運動。

items.en: Hi Mum, the hotel is lovely. There are a lot of flowers in the garden.
items.zh: 嗨，媽，飯店很棒。花園裡有很多花。

items.en: In my new job there are a lot of meetings, but my boss is nice.
items.zh: 我的新工作有很多會議，可是老闆人很好。

items.en: There are a lot of things I want to tell you, so call me soon.
items.zh: 我有好多事想跟你說，所以快點打給我。

title: There is some information about the new art class.
translation: 這裡有一些新美術課的資訊。
name: there is 加不可數名詞
sentences: Read the leaflet. There is some useful information about the museum.
"Can I make a cup of tea?" "Sure. There's some milk in the fridge."
I need my bag back. There's some money in it.
There is some bread on the table if you're hungry.
There's some coffee in the pot. Help yourself.
Let's take the train. There's a lot of traffic in the city centre.
There is a lot of snow on the roads this morning.
"Why can't you come out?" "There's a lot of homework this week."
There is a lot of noise from the flat upstairs.
In this book there is a lot of useful advice for new parents.
"Is there any rice?" "There's a little left. Not much."
There's no milk. Can you buy some on your way home?
Hurry up! There's no time for breakfast.
There is no water in the bottle.
The baby dropped her cup. Be careful! There's water on the floor.
There is sugar in this tea. I asked for no sugar.
There's cheese in this sandwich. I don't eat cheese.
There is some soup in the pot for dinner.
"Is there any juice?" "Yes, there's some orange juice in the fridge."
There is a lot of furniture in my grandmother's house.
There's some paper in the printer, so you can print your essay.
At the airport there is a lot of luggage on the belt.
There is a lot of work to do before the meeting.
"Is there any news about the job?" "Yes, there's some good news!"
On the website there is some information about the hotel.
In the kitchen there's some cake for you.
On my shirt there is some coffee. I need to change.
In the car there's some water for the trip.
Under the sofa there is a lot of dust.
There are some apples, and there is some cheese. Let's have a picnic.
There is a lot of money in the bank, but there are a lot of bills too.

examples.heading: ① There is some + 不可數名詞

items.en: Read the leaflet. There is some useful information about the museum.
items.zh: 讀一下這張傳單。上面有一些博物館的實用資訊。

items.en: "Can I make a cup of tea?" "Sure. There's some milk in the fridge."
items.zh: 我可以泡杯茶嗎？當然。冰箱裡有一些牛奶。

items.en: I need my bag back. There's some money in it.
items.zh: 我要拿回我的包包。裡面有一些錢。

items.en: There is some bread on the table if you're hungry.
items.zh: 你餓的話，桌上有一些麵包。

items.en: There's some coffee in the pot. Help yourself.
items.zh: 壺裡有一些咖啡。自己倒吧。

examples.heading: ② There is a lot of + 不可數名詞

items.en: Let's take the train. There's a lot of traffic in the city centre.
items.zh: 我們搭火車吧。市中心車很多。

items.en: There is a lot of snow on the roads this morning.
items.zh: 今天早上路上有很多雪。

items.en: "Why can't you come out?" "There's a lot of homework this week."
items.zh: 你為什麼不能出來？這星期功課很多。

items.en: There is a lot of noise from the flat upstairs.
items.zh: 樓上那間公寓很吵。

items.en: In this book there is a lot of useful advice for new parents.
items.zh: 這本書裡有很多給新手爸媽的實用建議。

examples.heading: ③ There is a little / no + 不可數名詞

items.en: "Is there any rice?" "There's a little left. Not much."
items.zh: 還有飯嗎？還剩一點點。不多。

items.en: There's no milk. Can you buy some on your way home?
items.zh: 沒有牛奶了。你回家的路上可以買一些嗎？

items.en: Hurry up! There's no time for breakfast.
items.zh: 快一點！沒時間吃早餐了。

items.en: There is no water in the bottle.
items.zh: 瓶子裡沒有水。

examples.heading: ④ There is + 不可數名詞（前面沒有字）

items.en: The baby dropped her cup. Be careful! There's water on the floor.
items.zh: 寶寶把杯子打翻了。小心！地上有水。

items.en: There is sugar in this tea. I asked for no sugar.
items.zh: 這杯茶有加糖。我說了不要糖的。

items.en: There's cheese in this sandwich. I don't eat cheese.
items.zh: 這個三明治裡有起司。我不吃起司的。

examples.heading: ⑤ 在家裡：There is + 不可數名詞

items.en: There is some soup in the pot for dinner.
items.zh: 鍋子裡有一些湯當晚餐。

items.en: "Is there any juice?" "Yes, there's some orange juice in the fridge."
items.zh: 有果汁嗎？有，冰箱裡有一些柳橙汁。

items.en: There is a lot of furniture in my grandmother's house.
items.zh: 我奶奶家有很多家具。

items.en: There's some paper in the printer, so you can print your essay.
items.zh: 印表機裡有一些紙，所以你可以印你的作文。

examples.heading: ⑥ 旅行和工作：There is + 不可數名詞

items.en: At the airport there is a lot of luggage on the belt.
items.zh: 機場的行李轉盤上有很多行李。

items.en: There is a lot of work to do before the meeting.
items.zh: 開會之前有很多工作要做。

items.en: "Is there any news about the job?" "Yes, there's some good news!"
items.zh: 工作有消息了嗎？有，有好消息！

items.en: On the website there is some information about the hotel.
items.zh: 網站上有一些飯店的資訊。

examples.heading: ⑦ 東西在哪裡：地點 + there is + 不可數名詞

items.en: In the kitchen there's some cake for you.
items.zh: 廚房裡有一些蛋糕給你。

items.en: On my shirt there is some coffee. I need to change.
items.zh: 我的襯衫上沾到一些咖啡。我得換衣服。

items.en: In the car there's some water for the trip.
items.zh: 車上有一些水，路上喝。

items.en: Under the sofa there is a lot of dust.
items.zh: 沙發底下有很多灰塵。

examples.heading: ⑧ 可數和不可數的對比

items.en: There are some apples, and there is some cheese. Let's have a picnic.
items.zh: 有一些蘋果，也有一些起司。我們去野餐吧。

items.en: There is a lot of money in the bank, but there are a lot of bills too.
items.zh: 銀行裡有很多錢，可是帳單也很多。

title: In a large school, there might be a lot of people that you can meet.
translation: 在大型學校裡，你可能會認識很多人。
name: there 加情態動詞加 be
sentences: In twenty years there will be flying cars and buses, and big houses.
Don't worry, there will be plenty of food at the wedding.
There will be a short break after the first hour.
Next year there'll be a new swimming pool in our town.
Take an umbrella. There might be some rain later.
There may be a delay because of the snow.
Ask at the desk. There could be some tickets left.
There might be a lot of traffic on Friday evening.
There should be a bus every ten minutes, but it's been twenty.
There should be some milk in the fridge. I bought some yesterday.
There should be more bike lanes in this city.
In the countryside there wouldn't be so many people, and there's nothing to do.
If we lived by the sea, there would be no need for a car.
Without the music festival, there would be no tourists here in summer.
The door is locked. There must be someone inside.
My bill is too high. There must be a mistake.
There can't be another train tonight. It's after midnight.
There won't be any classes on Monday because it's a holiday.
There might not be enough chairs for everyone.
There shouldn't be any problems with your visa.
There won't be time to eat before the film.
Will there be food at the party, or should I eat first?
Could there be a problem with the battery?
Will there be a teacher on the trip?
In a big city, there might be more jobs that young people can do.
There will be someone at the station to meet you.
There should be a key under the mat for you.
There could be a café near the museum where we can eat.
There must be somebody who can fix this.
There may be students who need extra help.
There'll be a lot of things to do at the summer camp.

examples.heading: ① there will be

items.en: In twenty years there will be flying cars and buses, and big houses.
items.zh: 二十年後會有會飛的車子和公車，還有大房子。

items.en: Don't worry, there will be plenty of food at the wedding.
items.zh: 別擔心，婚禮上會有很多吃的。

items.en: There will be a short break after the first hour.
items.zh: 第一個小時結束後會有短暫的休息。

items.en: Next year there'll be a new swimming pool in our town.
items.zh: 明年我們鎮上會有一座新游泳池。

examples.heading: ② there might / may / could be

items.en: Take an umbrella. There might be some rain later.
items.zh: 帶把傘吧，晚一點可能會下雨。

items.en: There may be a delay because of the snow.
items.zh: 因為下雪，可能會延誤。

items.en: Ask at the desk. There could be some tickets left.
items.zh: 去櫃台問問看，可能還有票。

items.en: There might be a lot of traffic on Friday evening.
items.zh: 星期五晚上可能會塞車。

examples.heading: ③ there should be

items.en: There should be a bus every ten minutes, but it's been twenty.
items.zh: 應該每十分鐘就有一班公車，可是已經過了二十分鐘了。

items.en: There should be some milk in the fridge. I bought some yesterday.
items.zh: 冰箱裡應該有牛奶，我昨天買了一些。

items.en: There should be more bike lanes in this city.
items.zh: 這座城市應該要有更多自行車道。

examples.heading: ④ there would be

items.en: In the countryside there wouldn't be so many people, and there's nothing to do.
items.zh: 在鄉下不會有那麼多人，而且沒什麼事可以做。

items.en: If we lived by the sea, there would be no need for a car.
items.zh: 如果我們住在海邊，就不需要車子了。

items.en: Without the music festival, there would be no tourists here in summer.
items.zh: 要是沒有音樂節，夏天這裡就不會有觀光客。

examples.heading: ⑤ there must be / there can't be

items.en: The door is locked. There must be someone inside.
items.zh: 門鎖著，裡面一定有人。

items.en: My bill is too high. There must be a mistake.
items.zh: 我的帳單太高了，一定是哪裡弄錯了。

items.en: There can't be another train tonight. It's after midnight.
items.zh: 今晚不可能還有火車，已經過半夜了。

examples.heading: ⑥ 否定句

items.en: There won't be any classes on Monday because it's a holiday.
items.zh: 星期一放假，所以不會上課。

items.en: There might not be enough chairs for everyone.
items.zh: 椅子可能不夠大家坐。

items.en: There shouldn't be any problems with your visa.
items.zh: 你的簽證應該不會有問題。

items.en: There won't be time to eat before the film.
items.zh: 電影開始前不會有時間吃東西。

examples.heading: ⑦ 疑問句

items.en: Will there be food at the party, or should I eat first?
items.zh: 派對上會有吃的嗎？還是我應該先吃？

items.en: Could there be a problem with the battery?
items.zh: 會不會是電池有問題？

items.en: Will there be a teacher on the trip?
items.zh: 校外教學會有老師跟去嗎？

examples.heading: ⑧ there + 情態動詞 + be + 名詞片語 + 修飾語

items.en: In a big city, there might be more jobs that young people can do.
items.zh: 在大城市裡，可能會有更多年輕人可以做的工作。

items.en: There will be someone at the station to meet you.
items.zh: 車站會有人去接你。

items.en: There should be a key under the mat for you.
items.zh: 腳踏墊下面應該有一把要給你的鑰匙。

items.en: There could be a café near the museum where we can eat.
items.zh: 博物館附近可能有一家我們可以吃飯的咖啡店。

items.en: There must be somebody who can fix this.
items.zh: 一定有人能修好這個。

items.en: There may be students who need extra help.
items.zh: 可能有些學生需要額外的幫助。

items.en: There'll be a lot of things to do at the summer camp.
items.zh: 夏令營會有很多活動可以參加。

title: I figured out that there had to be matches somewhere.
translation: 我推斷某個地方一定有火柴。
name: there 加有情態意義的動詞和 be
sentences: The lights were on, so I knew there had to be someone at home.
I can't open this file. There has to be a better way.
There has to be a reason why she left so early.
There had to be a teacher with us on the trip.
In the library there need to be school books and also magazines.
There needs to be more space for bikes outside the station.
There needs to be a doctor at every match.
There need to be more buses at night.
There is going to be a theatre performance, a chess championship and swimming races.
There's going to be a party at Lisa's on Friday.
Look at those clouds. There's going to be a storm.
There are going to be some changes in the office next year.
There used to be a cinema here, but now it's a supermarket.
There used to be a lot of fish in this river.
When I was a child, there used to be a sweet shop on the corner.
Excuse me, there seems to be a problem with my card.
There seem to be some mistakes in your report.
There appears to be a leak under the sink.
There doesn't seem to be anyone at home.
There's supposed to be a bus at six, but it hasn't come.
There are supposed to be twenty people at the meeting.
There was supposed to be a free drink with the meal.
There doesn't have to be a big party. A small dinner is fine.
There didn't use to be so much traffic in our town.
The roads are clear, so there isn't going to be any delay.
There doesn't need to be a reason for everything.
Is there going to be music at the wedding?
Did there use to be a church here?
Does there have to be a manager in the shop all the time?
Is there supposed to be a key with the letter?
Why does there need to be a meeting about this?

examples.heading: ① there has to be / there had to be

items.en: The lights were on, so I knew there had to be someone at home.
items.zh: 燈開著，所以我知道家裡一定有人。

items.en: I can't open this file. There has to be a better way.
items.zh: 我打不開這個檔案，一定有更好的辦法。

items.en: There has to be a reason why she left so early.
items.zh: 她那麼早走一定有原因。

items.en: There had to be a teacher with us on the trip.
items.zh: 校外教學一定要有老師跟著我們。

examples.heading: ② there need(s) to be

items.en: In the library there need to be school books and also magazines.
items.zh: 圖書館裡需要有課本，也需要有雜誌。

items.en: There needs to be more space for bikes outside the station.
items.zh: 車站外面需要有更多停腳踏車的空間。

items.en: There needs to be a doctor at every match.
items.zh: 每場比賽都需要有一位醫生在場。

items.en: There need to be more buses at night.
items.zh: 晚上需要有更多班公車。

examples.heading: ③ there is going to be

items.en: There is going to be a theatre performance, a chess championship and swimming races.
items.zh: 會有戲劇表演、西洋棋錦標賽和游泳比賽。

items.en: There's going to be a party at Lisa's on Friday.
items.zh: 星期五 Lisa 家會有派對。

items.en: Look at those clouds. There's going to be a storm.
items.zh: 你看那些雲，暴風雨要來了。

items.en: There are going to be some changes in the office next year.
items.zh: 明年辦公室會有一些改變。

examples.heading: ④ there used to be

items.en: There used to be a cinema here, but now it's a supermarket.
items.zh: 這裡以前有一家電影院，現在變成超市了。

items.en: There used to be a lot of fish in this river.
items.zh: 這條河以前有很多魚。

items.en: When I was a child, there used to be a sweet shop on the corner.
items.zh: 我小時候，轉角那裡有一家糖果店。

examples.heading: ⑤ there seems to be / there appears to be

items.en: Excuse me, there seems to be a problem with my card.
items.zh: 不好意思，我的卡好像有問題。

items.en: There seem to be some mistakes in your report.
items.zh: 你的報告裡好像有一些錯誤。

items.en: There appears to be a leak under the sink.
items.zh: 水槽下面好像有地方漏水。

items.en: There doesn't seem to be anyone at home.
items.zh: 家裡好像沒人。

examples.heading: ⑥ there is supposed to be

items.en: There's supposed to be a bus at six, but it hasn't come.
items.zh: 照理說六點應該有一班公車，可是還沒來。

items.en: There are supposed to be twenty people at the meeting.
items.zh: 照理說會議應該有二十個人。

items.en: There was supposed to be a free drink with the meal.
items.zh: 照理說餐點應該附一杯免費飲料。

examples.heading: ⑦ 否定句

items.en: There doesn't have to be a big party. A small dinner is fine.
items.zh: 不一定要辦大派對，簡單吃個晚餐就好。

items.en: There didn't use to be so much traffic in our town.
items.zh: 我們鎮上以前沒有那麼多車。

items.en: The roads are clear, so there isn't going to be any delay.
items.zh: 路上很順，所以不會有任何延誤。

items.en: There doesn't need to be a reason for everything.
items.zh: 不是每件事都需要有理由。

examples.heading: ⑧ 疑問句

items.en: Is there going to be music at the wedding?
items.zh: 婚禮上會有音樂嗎？

items.en: Did there use to be a church here?
items.zh: 這裡以前有教堂嗎？

items.en: Does there have to be a manager in the shop all the time?
items.zh: 店裡一定要隨時有經理在嗎？

items.en: Is there supposed to be a key with the letter?
items.zh: 信裡照理說應該附一把鑰匙嗎？

items.en: Why does there need to be a meeting about this?
items.zh: 為什麼這件事需要開會？

title: I remember feeling very unhappy and confused all day long.
translation: 我記得我一整天都覺得很難過、很困惑。
name: 接不定詞或動詞-ing 意思不同的動詞
sentences: If you need to change the time, remember to contact him first.
"Did you lock the car?" "Yes, I remember locking it. I heard the beep."
Your exam is at nine tomorrow. Remember to set your alarm.
I remember crying on my first day at nursery.
Do you remember visiting this beach when we were kids?
"Why is the plant dead?" "Sorry, I forgot to water it while you were away."
Don't forget to turn off the oven before you leave.
I'll never forget seeing the mountains for the first time.
"What was the best day of your life?" "I'll never forget holding my daughter for the first time."
She forgot to send the email, so the client never got the price list.
We had been driving for five hours, so we stopped to have a coffee.
My dad stopped eating meat last year.
You're always so busy. Have you ever stopped to think about your future?
"Is your knee better?" "Yes, it stopped hurting yesterday."
After I had a baby, I needed to stop working for a while.
"Why are you so tired?" "I tried to finish the report last night, but I couldn't."
"I can't sleep." "Try drinking some warm milk before bed."
He tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy.
If the computer freezes, try turning it off and on again.
We regret to tell you that your order will arrive late.
"Do you regret leaving your job?" "No. I'm much happier now."
The school regrets to announce that the trip has been cancelled.
I regret not learning to swim when I was young.
He started as a waiter and went on to open his own restaurant.
The teacher asked them to be quiet, but they went on talking.
After winning the local race, she went on to win a national medal.
