The band went on playing until two in the morning.
"The grass is so long." "I know. It needs cutting."
I need to cut my hair. It's getting in my eyes.
Your shirt needs ironing before the interview.
"Can I help with the party?" "Yes, we need to buy more chairs."

examples.heading: ① remember + to + 原形動詞 / remember + 動詞-ing

items.en: If you need to change the time, remember to contact him first.
items.zh: 如果你要改時間，記得先跟他聯絡。

items.en: "Did you lock the car?" "Yes, I remember locking it. I heard the beep."
items.zh: 你鎖車了嗎？鎖了，我記得我鎖了。我有聽到嗶的一聲。

items.en: Your exam is at nine tomorrow. Remember to set your alarm.
items.zh: 你明天九點考試。記得設鬧鐘。

items.en: I remember crying on my first day at nursery.
items.zh: 我記得我上幼兒園第一天哭了。

items.en: Do you remember visiting this beach when we were kids?
items.zh: 你記得我們小時候來過這個海灘嗎？

examples.heading: ② forget + to + 原形動詞 / forget + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Why is the plant dead?" "Sorry, I forgot to water it while you were away."
items.zh: 這盆植物怎麼死了？抱歉，你不在的時候我忘了澆水。

items.en: Don't forget to turn off the oven before you leave.
items.zh: 出門前別忘了關烤箱。

items.en: I'll never forget seeing the mountains for the first time.
items.zh: 我永遠不會忘記第一次看到那些山的樣子。

items.en: "What was the best day of your life?" "I'll never forget holding my daughter for the first time."
items.zh: 你人生中最棒的一天是哪一天？我永遠不會忘記第一次抱我女兒的那一刻。

items.en: She forgot to send the email, so the client never got the price list.
items.zh: 她忘了寄那封信，所以客戶一直沒收到價目表。

examples.heading: ③ stop + to + 原形動詞 / stop + 動詞-ing

items.en: We had been driving for five hours, so we stopped to have a coffee.
items.zh: 我們開了五個小時的車，所以停下來喝杯咖啡。

items.en: My dad stopped eating meat last year.
items.zh: 我爸去年開始不吃肉了。

items.en: You're always so busy. Have you ever stopped to think about your future?
items.zh: 你總是那麼忙。你有沒有停下來想過自己的未來？

items.en: "Is your knee better?" "Yes, it stopped hurting yesterday."
items.zh: 你的膝蓋好點了嗎？好了，昨天就不痛了。

items.en: After I had a baby, I needed to stop working for a while.
items.zh: 我生了孩子以後，得暫時停止工作。

examples.heading: ④ try + to + 原形動詞 / try + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Why are you so tired?" "I tried to finish the report last night, but I couldn't."
items.zh: 你怎麼這麼累？我昨晚想把報告寫完，可是沒寫完。

items.en: "I can't sleep." "Try drinking some warm milk before bed."
items.zh: 我睡不著。睡前喝點溫牛奶試試看。

items.en: He tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy.
items.zh: 他想把箱子抬起來，可是太重了。

items.en: If the computer freezes, try turning it off and on again.
items.zh: 電腦當機的話，試試看把它關掉再開。

examples.heading: ⑤ regret + to + 原形動詞 / regret + 動詞-ing

items.en: We regret to tell you that your order will arrive late.
items.zh: 我們很遺憾地通知您，您的訂單會晚到。

items.en: "Do you regret leaving your job?" "No. I'm much happier now."
items.zh: 你後悔辭職嗎？不後悔。我現在快樂多了。

items.en: The school regrets to announce that the trip has been cancelled.
items.zh: 學校很遺憾地宣布，這次旅行取消了。

items.en: I regret not learning to swim when I was young.
items.zh: 我後悔小時候沒學游泳。

examples.heading: ⑥ go on + to + 原形動詞 / go on + 動詞-ing

items.en: He started as a waiter and went on to open his own restaurant.
items.zh: 他從服務生做起，後來開了自己的餐廳。

items.en: The teacher asked them to be quiet, but they went on talking.
items.zh: 老師叫他們安靜，可是他們繼續講話。

items.en: After winning the local race, she went on to win a national medal.
items.zh: 贏了地方的比賽以後，她接著拿到了全國賽的獎牌。

items.en: The band went on playing until two in the morning.
items.zh: 樂團一直演奏到凌晨兩點。

examples.heading: ⑦ need + to + 原形動詞 / need + 動詞-ing

items.en: "The grass is so long." "I know. It needs cutting."
items.zh: 草好長。我知道。該剪了。

items.en: I need to cut my hair. It's getting in my eyes.
items.zh: 我得剪頭髮了。頭髮都蓋到眼睛了。

items.en: Your shirt needs ironing before the interview.
items.zh: 面試前你的襯衫要燙一下。

items.en: "Can I help with the party?" "Yes, we need to buy more chairs."
items.zh: 派對有什麼我能幫忙的嗎？有，我們需要再買幾張椅子。

title: I look forward to hearing from you.
translation: 期待你的回信。
name: look forward to 加動詞-ing 或名詞
sentences: Thank you for your application. We look forward to meeting you on Friday.
Please send me the price list. I look forward to hearing from you.
Thanks for inviting me to speak. I look forward to seeing you all in May.
The hotel wrote: "We look forward to welcoming you next week."
Dear Ms Lee, I have attached my CV. I look forward to discussing the job with you.
I hope my answers are pertinent to your study. I look forward to reading the report.
Thanks again for your help. I look forward to working with you.
The meeting is at ten in Room 4. I look forward to our talk.
Thank you for the offer. I look forward to your reply.
Your order will arrive on Monday. We look forward to your next visit.
The tickets are in this email. We look forward to the show.
"Are you going to Tom's party?" "Yes, I'm really looking forward to it."
My kids are looking forward to the summer holidays.
We've booked the flights, and we're looking forward to the trip.
"How's work?" "Busy. I'm looking forward to the weekend."
My grandma is looking forward to her birthday dinner.
"See you on Saturday!" "Great, I'm looking forward to seeing you!"
She's looking forward to starting her new job.
We're looking forward to trying that new Thai restaurant.
My brother is looking forward to having his own room.
"Is your sister coming home?" "Yes, and we're looking forward to spending Christmas together."
I was looking forward to the match, but it rained all day.
The children were looking forward to going to the zoo, so they were sad when it closed early.
He was looking forward to meeting her parents, but they cancelled the dinner.
I'm not looking forward to the exam on Monday.
"Do you have to go to the dentist?" "Yes, and I'm not looking forward to it."
He isn't looking forward to telling his boss about the mistake.
"Are you looking forward to the wedding?" "Yes, very much!"
"What are you looking forward to most this year?" "Moving to a bigger flat."
My dad looks forward to his morning coffee every day.
Our teacher says she looks forward to reading our stories.
Every year Anna looks forward to the music festival.

examples.heading: ① 信和電子郵件的結尾：look forward to + 動詞-ing

items.en: Thank you for your application. We look forward to meeting you on Friday.
items.zh: 謝謝您的申請。我們期待星期五和您見面。

items.en: Please send me the price list. I look forward to hearing from you.
items.zh: 請把價目表寄給我。期待您的回覆。

items.en: Thanks for inviting me to speak. I look forward to seeing you all in May.
items.zh: 謝謝你們邀請我演講。期待五月和大家見面。

items.en: The hotel wrote: "We look forward to welcoming you next week."
items.zh: 飯店寫道：我們期待下週歡迎您光臨。

items.en: Dear Ms Lee, I have attached my CV. I look forward to discussing the job with you.
items.zh: 李小姐您好，我附上了我的履歷。期待和您談談這份工作。

items.en: I hope my answers are pertinent to your study. I look forward to reading the report.
items.zh: 希望我的回答對您的研究有用。期待讀到那份報告。

items.en: Thanks again for your help. I look forward to working with you.
items.zh: 再次謝謝您的幫忙。期待和您合作。

examples.heading: ② 信和電子郵件的結尾：look forward to + 名詞

items.en: The meeting is at ten in Room 4. I look forward to our talk.
items.zh: 會議十點在四號會議室。期待我們的談話。

items.en: Thank you for the offer. I look forward to your reply.
items.zh: 謝謝您提供這個機會。期待您的回覆。

items.en: Your order will arrive on Monday. We look forward to your next visit.
items.zh: 您的訂單星期一會送到。期待您下次光臨。

items.en: The tickets are in this email. We look forward to the show.
items.zh: 票在這封信裡。我們期待這場表演。

examples.heading: ③ 跟朋友說話：be looking forward to + 名詞

items.en: "Are you going to Tom's party?" "Yes, I'm really looking forward to it."
items.zh: 你要去 Tom 的派對嗎？要啊，我很期待。

items.en: My kids are looking forward to the summer holidays.
items.zh: 我的孩子們很期待暑假。

items.en: We've booked the flights, and we're looking forward to the trip.
items.zh: 我們訂好機票了，很期待這趟旅行。

items.en: "How's work?" "Busy. I'm looking forward to the weekend."
items.zh: 工作怎麼樣？很忙。我很期待週末。

items.en: My grandma is looking forward to her birthday dinner.
items.zh: 我奶奶很期待她的生日晚餐。

examples.heading: ④ 跟朋友說話：be looking forward to + 動詞-ing

items.en: "See you on Saturday!" "Great, I'm looking forward to seeing you!"
items.zh: 星期六見！太好了，好期待見到你！

items.en: She's looking forward to starting her new job.
items.zh: 她很期待開始新工作。

items.en: We're looking forward to trying that new Thai restaurant.
items.zh: 我們很期待去吃那家新開的泰國餐廳。

items.en: My brother is looking forward to having his own room.
items.zh: 我弟弟很期待有自己的房間。

items.en: "Is your sister coming home?" "Yes, and we're looking forward to spending Christmas together."
items.zh: 你姊姊要回家嗎？要，我們很期待一起過聖誕節。

examples.heading: ⑤ 過去：was looking forward to

items.en: I was looking forward to the match, but it rained all day.
items.zh: 我本來很期待那場比賽，可是下了一整天的雨。

items.en: The children were looking forward to going to the zoo, so they were sad when it closed early.
items.zh: 孩子們本來很期待去動物園，所以動物園提早關門讓他們很難過。

items.en: He was looking forward to meeting her parents, but they cancelled the dinner.
items.zh: 他本來很期待見她的父母，可是他們取消了晚餐。

examples.heading: ⑥ 否定和問句

items.en: I'm not looking forward to the exam on Monday.
items.zh: 我一點都不期待星期一的考試。

items.en: "Do you have to go to the dentist?" "Yes, and I'm not looking forward to it."
items.zh: 你得去看牙醫嗎？對，我一點都不期待。

items.en: He isn't looking forward to telling his boss about the mistake.
items.zh: 他一點都不想跟老闆說那個錯誤。

items.en: "Are you looking forward to the wedding?" "Yes, very much!"
items.zh: 你期待那場婚禮嗎？很期待！

items.en: "What are you looking forward to most this year?" "Moving to a bigger flat."
items.zh: 你今年最期待什麼？搬到大一點的公寓。

examples.heading: ⑦ 第三人稱單數：looks forward to

items.en: My dad looks forward to his morning coffee every day.
items.zh: 我爸每天都很期待早上那杯咖啡。

items.en: Our teacher says she looks forward to reading our stories.
items.zh: 我們老師說她很期待讀我們寫的故事。

items.en: Every year Anna looks forward to the music festival.
items.zh: Anna 每年都很期待那個音樂節。

title: It is very common in Argentina to hear people talk about the economic depression.
translation: 在阿根廷，常常會聽到大家在談經濟蕭條。
name: 感官動詞加受詞加原形不定詞
sentences: You often hear people complain about the price of houses in this city.
"Is your sister home?" "Yes, I heard her come in about ten minutes ago."
I heard the front door shut, and then the house was quiet.
Have you ever heard him sing? He has a beautiful voice.
We heard someone call our names from the back of the bus.
"Did Anna leave?" "Yes, I saw her get into a taxi."
I'd like to see my city develop without destroying the environment.
The police officer saw the man drop something into the river.
Did you see the ball hit the window?
I've never seen my dad cry before.
We watched the plane take off and then drove home.
The whole class watched the teacher light the candle.
"Did you see the goal?" "Yes, I watched him kick the ball into the net."
Thousands of people watched the president give his speech.
Did you notice anyone go into the office after six?
I didn't notice her leave the party.
The shop assistant noticed the boy put a chocolate bar in his pocket.
We sat in silence and listened to the old man tell his story.
Every night she listened to her daughter read a chapter of her book.
I love listening to my grandmother play the piano.
I felt something touch my foot under the table.
"What's wrong?" "I just felt the building move. Was that an earthquake?"
She felt her face go red when everyone looked at her.
"Where are my keys?" "I don't know. I didn't see you put them anywhere."
"Did you hear the phone ring?" "No, I was in the garden."
I've never heard her say a bad word about anyone.
Did anyone see the accident happen?
The suspect was seen to leave the building at ten o'clock.
The minister was heard to say that taxes would go up.
Two men were seen to enter the bank just before it closed.
The singer was never heard to complain about her fans.

examples.heading: ① hear + 受詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: You often hear people complain about the price of houses in this city.
items.zh: 在這座城市常常聽到大家抱怨房價。

items.en: "Is your sister home?" "Yes, I heard her come in about ten minutes ago."
items.zh: 你姊姊在家嗎？在，我大概十分鐘前聽到她進門。

items.en: I heard the front door shut, and then the house was quiet.
items.zh: 我聽到前門關上，接著屋子就安靜了。

items.en: Have you ever heard him sing? He has a beautiful voice.
items.zh: 你聽過他唱歌嗎？他的聲音很好聽。

items.en: We heard someone call our names from the back of the bus.
items.zh: 我們聽到有人從公車後面叫我們的名字。

examples.heading: ② see + 受詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: "Did Anna leave?" "Yes, I saw her get into a taxi."
items.zh: Anna 走了嗎？走了，我看到她上了計程車。

items.en: I'd like to see my city develop without destroying the environment.
items.zh: 我希望看到我的城市發展，又不破壞環境。

items.en: The police officer saw the man drop something into the river.
items.zh: 警察看到那個男人把東西丟進河裡。

items.en: Did you see the ball hit the window?
items.zh: 你有看到球打到窗戶嗎？

items.en: I've never seen my dad cry before.
items.zh: 我以前從來沒看過我爸哭。

examples.heading: ③ watch + 受詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: We watched the plane take off and then drove home.
items.zh: 我們看著飛機起飛，然後開車回家。

items.en: The whole class watched the teacher light the candle.
items.zh: 全班看著老師點蠟燭。

items.en: "Did you see the goal?" "Yes, I watched him kick the ball into the net."
items.zh: 你有看到那一球嗎？有，我看著他把球踢進網。

items.en: Thousands of people watched the president give his speech.
items.zh: 數千人看著總統發表演講。

examples.heading: ④ notice + 受詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: Did you notice anyone go into the office after six?
items.zh: 你有注意到六點以後有誰進了辦公室嗎？

items.en: I didn't notice her leave the party.
items.zh: 我沒注意到她什麼時候離開派對。

items.en: The shop assistant noticed the boy put a chocolate bar in his pocket.
items.zh: 店員注意到那個男孩把一條巧克力放進口袋。

examples.heading: ⑤ listen to + 受詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: We sat in silence and listened to the old man tell his story.
items.zh: 我們安靜地坐著，聽那位老先生講他的故事。

items.en: Every night she listened to her daughter read a chapter of her book.
items.zh: 每天晚上，她都聽女兒讀一章書。

items.en: I love listening to my grandmother play the piano.
items.zh: 我很喜歡聽我奶奶彈鋼琴。

examples.heading: ⑥ feel + 受詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: I felt something touch my foot under the table.
items.zh: 我感覺到桌子底下有東西碰了我的腳。

items.en: "What's wrong?" "I just felt the building move. Was that an earthquake?"
items.zh: 怎麼了？我剛剛感覺到大樓動了一下。是地震嗎？

items.en: She felt her face go red when everyone looked at her.
items.zh: 大家都看著她的時候，她感覺到自己的臉紅了。

examples.heading: ⑦ 否定和問句

items.en: "Where are my keys?" "I don't know. I didn't see you put them anywhere."
items.zh: 我的鑰匙在哪裡？不知道。我沒看到你把它們放在哪裡。

items.en: "Did you hear the phone ring?" "No, I was in the garden."
items.zh: 你有聽到電話響嗎？沒有，我在花園裡。

items.en: I've never heard her say a bad word about anyone.
items.zh: 我從來沒聽過她說任何人的壞話。

items.en: Did anyone see the accident happen?
items.zh: 有人看到車禍發生的經過嗎？

examples.heading: ⑧ 被動：be + 過去分詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: The suspect was seen to leave the building at ten o'clock.
items.zh: 有人看到嫌犯十點離開了大樓。

items.en: The minister was heard to say that taxes would go up.
items.zh: 有人聽到部長說稅會增加。

items.en: Two men were seen to enter the bank just before it closed.
items.zh: 有人看到兩個男人在銀行關門前走了進去。

items.en: The singer was never heard to complain about her fans.
items.zh: 從來沒有人聽過那位歌手抱怨她的歌迷。

title: Then I heard someone screaming.
translation: 接著我聽到有人在尖叫。
name: 感官動詞加受詞加動詞-ing
sentences: We were sitting in the tent when we heard an owl calling outside.
"Is the baby awake?" "Yes, I can hear her crying."
I heard the neighbours arguing again last night.
Did you hear someone knocking at the door?
From my room I can hear the trains going past all night.
"Where's Tom?" "I saw him talking to the teacher a minute ago."
When I looked out of the window, I saw the children playing in the snow.
In a zoo you can't see animals hunting the way they do in the wild.
I saw a man stealing a bike, so I called the police.
We sat on the beach and watched the sun going down.
My grandad loves watching the boats coming into the harbour.
She stood at the door and watched her son walking to school.
"Is he OK?" "I don't know. I noticed him looking at his phone all through the meeting."
Did you notice anyone waiting outside the shop?
I noticed the price going up every month.
On Sunday mornings I lie in bed and listen to the birds singing.
We listened to the rain falling on the roof.
The kids listened to their grandmother telling stories about the war.
I felt something crawling up my leg, and I screamed.
"Are you OK?" "Yes, but I can feel my heart beating fast."
We felt the ground shaking during the earthquake.
"Can you smell something burning?" "Oh no, my toast!"
As I walked past the bakery, I could smell bread baking.
I can smell gas leaking. Open the windows!
From the hotel room we could see people swimming in the lake.
I heard my little brother singing in the shower this morning.
She saw a group of tourists taking photos of her house.
We watched the old man feeding the ducks in the park.
"Who broke the window?" "A boy was seen running away from the house."
The two boys were heard shouting at each other in the street.
She was last seen walking towards the station.

examples.heading: ① hear + 受詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: We were sitting in the tent when we heard an owl calling outside.
items.zh: 我們坐在帳篷裡的時候，聽到外面有貓頭鷹在叫。

items.en: "Is the baby awake?" "Yes, I can hear her crying."
items.zh: 寶寶醒了嗎？醒了，我聽到她在哭。

items.en: I heard the neighbours arguing again last night.
items.zh: 我昨晚又聽到鄰居在吵架。

items.en: Did you hear someone knocking at the door?
items.zh: 你有聽到有人在敲門嗎？

items.en: From my room I can hear the trains going past all night.
items.zh: 我在房間裡整晚都聽得到火車經過的聲音。

examples.heading: ② see + 受詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Where's Tom?" "I saw him talking to the teacher a minute ago."
items.zh: Tom 在哪裡？我剛剛看到他在跟老師說話。

items.en: When I looked out of the window, I saw the children playing in the snow.
items.zh: 我往窗外看的時候，看到孩子們在雪地裡玩。

items.en: In a zoo you can't see animals hunting the way they do in the wild.
items.zh: 在動物園裡，你看不到動物像在野外那樣打獵。

items.en: I saw a man stealing a bike, so I called the police.
items.zh: 我看到一個男人在偷腳踏車，所以我報了警。

examples.heading: ③ watch + 受詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: We sat on the beach and watched the sun going down.
items.zh: 我們坐在海灘上，看著太陽慢慢下山。

items.en: My grandad loves watching the boats coming into the harbour.
items.zh: 我爺爺很喜歡看著船開進港口。

items.en: She stood at the door and watched her son walking to school.
items.zh: 她站在門口，看著她兒子走路去上學。

examples.heading: ④ notice + 受詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Is he OK?" "I don't know. I noticed him looking at his phone all through the meeting."
items.zh: 他還好嗎？不知道。我注意到他整場會議都在看手機。

items.en: Did you notice anyone waiting outside the shop?
items.zh: 你有注意到有人在店門外等嗎？

items.en: I noticed the price going up every month.
items.zh: 我注意到價格每個月都在漲。

examples.heading: ⑤ listen to + 受詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: On Sunday mornings I lie in bed and listen to the birds singing.
items.zh: 星期天早上，我躺在床上聽鳥叫。

items.en: We listened to the rain falling on the roof.
items.zh: 我們聽著雨打在屋頂上。

items.en: The kids listened to their grandmother telling stories about the war.
items.zh: 孩子們聽著奶奶講戰爭時的故事。

examples.heading: ⑥ feel + 受詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: I felt something crawling up my leg, and I screamed.
items.zh: 我感覺到有東西在我腿上爬，就尖叫了起來。

items.en: "Are you OK?" "Yes, but I can feel my heart beating fast."
items.zh: 你還好嗎？還好，可是我感覺得到心跳得好快。

items.en: We felt the ground shaking during the earthquake.
items.zh: 地震的時候，我們感覺到地面在搖晃。

examples.heading: ⑦ smell + 受詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Can you smell something burning?" "Oh no, my toast!"
items.zh: 你有聞到燒焦的味道嗎？糟了，我的吐司！

items.en: As I walked past the bakery, I could smell bread baking.
items.zh: 我經過麵包店的時候，聞得到麵包在烤的香味。

items.en: I can smell gas leaking. Open the windows!
items.zh: 我聞到瓦斯外洩的味道。把窗戶打開！

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞是名詞片語

items.en: From the hotel room we could see people swimming in the lake.
items.zh: 我們從飯店房間看得到有人在湖裡游泳。

items.en: I heard my little brother singing in the shower this morning.
items.zh: 今天早上我聽到我弟弟在淋浴時唱歌。

items.en: She saw a group of tourists taking photos of her house.
items.zh: 她看到一群觀光客在拍她的房子。

items.en: We watched the old man feeding the ducks in the park.
items.zh: 我們看著那位老先生在公園裡餵鴨子。

examples.heading: ⑨ 被動：be + 過去分詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Who broke the window?" "A boy was seen running away from the house."
items.zh: 誰打破了窗戶？有人看到一個男孩從那間房子跑走。

items.en: The two boys were heard shouting at each other in the street.
items.zh: 有人聽到那兩個男孩在街上互相大吼。

items.en: She was last seen walking towards the station.
items.zh: 最後一次有人看到她，她正走向車站。

title: We in the student committee would hate to see all that space go to waste.
translation: 我們學生委員會很不希望看到那麼大的空間白白浪費掉。
name: would hate to 加不定詞
sentences: I'd hate to wake the baby.
She would hate to miss your wedding.
We would hate to lose you.
I'd hate to be late on my first day.
They would hate to move again so soon.
He would hate to let the team down.
You'd hate to get lost in this city at night.
I would hate to think what this will cost.
Wouldn't you hate to hear about it from someone else?
My dad would hate to sell the old car.
I'd hate to give you the wrong idea.
She told me she would hate to work on weekends.
We'd hate to waste all this food.
The teacher would hate to punish the whole class.
I'd hate to say no to my best friend.
He'd hate to leave without saying goodbye.
Ann would hate to cook for twenty people.
I'd hate to forget her birthday again.
They'd hate to stand in the rain for two hours.
He would hate to be seen in that hat.
She'd hate to be left out.
She would hate to be called a quitter.
They would hate to be treated like children.
We would hate to see the park close.
I'd hate to see you get hurt.
The fans would hate to see their team lose at home.
My grandma would hate to see the old house fall down.
I'd hate not to say goodbye to her.
I'd hate not to have a chance to thank him.
We'd hate not to see you before you leave.
He would hate not to finish what he started.

examples.heading: ① would hate to + 原形動詞

items.en: I'd hate to wake the baby.
items.zh: 我很不想吵醒寶寶。

items.en: She would hate to miss your wedding.
items.zh: 她很不想錯過你的婚禮。

items.en: We would hate to lose you.
items.zh: 我們很不想失去你。

items.en: I'd hate to be late on my first day.
items.zh: 我很不想第一天就遲到。

items.en: They would hate to move again so soon.
items.zh: 他們很不想這麼快又搬家。

items.en: He would hate to let the team down.
items.zh: 他很不想讓球隊失望。

items.en: You'd hate to get lost in this city at night.
items.zh: 你一定不想晚上在這座城市迷路。

items.en: I would hate to think what this will cost.
items.zh: 這要花多少錢，我真不敢想。

items.en: Wouldn't you hate to hear about it from someone else?
items.zh: 要是從別人那裡聽到這件事，你不會很不舒服嗎？

items.en: My dad would hate to sell the old car.
items.zh: 我爸很不想賣掉那台舊車。

items.en: I'd hate to give you the wrong idea.
items.zh: 我很不想讓你誤會。

items.en: She told me she would hate to work on weekends.
items.zh: 她跟我說她很不想週末上班。

items.en: We'd hate to waste all this food.
items.zh: 我們很不想浪費這些食物。

items.en: The teacher would hate to punish the whole class.
items.zh: 老師很不想處罰全班。

items.en: I'd hate to say no to my best friend.
items.zh: 我很不想拒絕我最好的朋友。

items.en: He'd hate to leave without saying goodbye.
items.zh: 他很不想沒道別就離開。

items.en: Ann would hate to cook for twenty people.
items.zh: Ann 很不想幫二十個人做飯。

items.en: I'd hate to forget her birthday again.
items.zh: 我很不想又忘了她的生日。

items.en: They'd hate to stand in the rain for two hours.
items.zh: 他們很不想在雨中站兩個小時。

examples.heading: ② would hate to be + 過去分詞（被動）

items.en: He would hate to be seen in that hat.
items.zh: 他很不想被人看到他戴那頂帽子。

items.en: She'd hate to be left out.
items.zh: 她很不想被冷落。

items.en: She would hate to be called a quitter.
items.zh: 她很不想被人說是半途而廢的人。

items.en: They would hate to be treated like children.
items.zh: 他們很不想被當成小孩子看待。

examples.heading: ③ would hate to see + 受詞 + 原形動詞

items.en: We would hate to see the park close.
items.zh: 我們很不希望看到公園關閉。

items.en: I'd hate to see you get hurt.
items.zh: 我很不希望看到你受傷。

items.en: The fans would hate to see their team lose at home.
items.zh: 球迷很不希望看到自己的球隊在主場輸球。

items.en: My grandma would hate to see the old house fall down.
items.zh: 我奶奶很不希望看到那間老房子倒掉。

examples.heading: ④ would hate not to + 原形動詞

items.en: I'd hate not to say goodbye to her.
items.zh: 要是沒跟她道別，我會很難過。

items.en: I'd hate not to have a chance to thank him.
items.zh: 要是沒機會謝謝他，我會很遺憾。

items.en: We'd hate not to see you before you leave.
items.zh: 你走之前要是沒見到你，我們會很遺憾。

items.en: He would hate not to finish what he started.
items.zh: 他要是沒把開始做的事做完，會很不甘心。

title: I'd love to hear it!
translation: 我很想聽！
name: would love to 加不定詞
sentences: "My aunt makes amazing cakes." "I'd love to try one!"
I'd love to visit Iceland one day and see the northern lights.
"The band needs a singer for the concert." "I'd love to sing at the concert!"
My daughter would love to have a puppy for her birthday.
We'd love to see your wedding photos.
After this busy week, I'd love to sleep all weekend.
"We're having a barbecue in the garden on Friday. Can you come?" "I'd love to!"
"Do you want to go for a coffee?" "Yes, I'd love to."
"Shall we have dinner together next week?" "We'd love to. Just tell us the day."
"Would you like to join our book club?" "I'd love to. When do you meet?"
"Can you come skiing with us?" "I'd love to, but I've hurt my knee."
"Are you coming to the concert?" "I'd love to, but I don't have a ticket."
"Stay for another cup of tea!" "I'd love to, but my bus leaves at five."
I'd love to help you move, but I'm away that weekend.
My parents would love to meet you.
Tom would love to come with us, but he's sick.
"Does your son like football?" "Yes, he'd love to play for the school team."
The children would love to go to the beach again.
"Wouldn't you love to live by the sea?" "Oh yes, I'd love that."
"Look at that boat. Wouldn't you love to sail around the islands?" "Yes, I would!"
I'd love to be a teacher like my mum.
We'd love to have a bigger kitchen.
She'd love to be in the school play this year.
I'd love to have more time to read.
Thank you for your invitation. I'd love to come to your graduation.
Dear Anna, we'd love to see you this summer. Can you visit us in July?
I'd love to hear all about your new job. Write soon!
Your photos are beautiful. I'd love to go there one day.
"Would you like to try my soup?" "I'd love to. It smells great."
I'd like to go to the museum, but I'd love to see the castle.
"Would you like to dance?" "I'd love to!"

examples.heading: ① 說自己很想做的事

items.en: "My aunt makes amazing cakes." "I'd love to try one!"
items.zh: 我阿姨做的蛋糕很棒。我好想吃吃看！

items.en: I'd love to visit Iceland one day and see the northern lights.
items.zh: 我很想有一天去冰島看極光。

items.en: "The band needs a singer for the concert." "I'd love to sing at the concert!"
items.zh: 樂團的演唱會需要一個歌手。我很想在演唱會上唱歌！

items.en: My daughter would love to have a puppy for her birthday.
items.zh: 我女兒生日很想要一隻小狗。

items.en: We'd love to see your wedding photos.
items.zh: 我們很想看你的婚紗照。

items.en: After this busy week, I'd love to sleep all weekend.
items.zh: 忙完這個星期，我好想整個週末都在睡覺。

examples.heading: ② 回答邀請：I'd love to!

items.en: "We're having a barbecue in the garden on Friday. Can you come?" "I'd love to!"
items.zh: 我們星期五要在院子裡烤肉。你能來嗎？好啊，我很想去！

items.en: "Do you want to go for a coffee?" "Yes, I'd love to."
items.zh: 你要去喝杯咖啡嗎？好啊，我很想去。

items.en: "Shall we have dinner together next week?" "We'd love to. Just tell us the day."
items.zh: 我們下星期一起吃晚餐好嗎？好啊。告訴我們哪一天就好。

items.en: "Would you like to join our book club?" "I'd love to. When do you meet?"
items.zh: 你想加入我們的讀書會嗎？很想。你們什麼時候聚會？

examples.heading: ③ 不能去：I'd love to, but ...

items.en: "Can you come skiing with us?" "I'd love to, but I've hurt my knee."
items.zh: 你可以跟我們去滑雪嗎？我很想去，可是我膝蓋受傷了。

items.en: "Are you coming to the concert?" "I'd love to, but I don't have a ticket."
items.zh: 你要來演唱會嗎？我很想去，可是我沒有票。

items.en: "Stay for another cup of tea!" "I'd love to, but my bus leaves at five."
items.zh: 再留下來喝杯茶吧！我很想，可是我的公車五點開。

items.en: I'd love to help you move, but I'm away that weekend.
items.zh: 我很想幫你搬家，可是那個週末我不在。

examples.heading: ④ 主詞不是 I

items.en: My parents would love to meet you.
items.zh: 我爸媽很想見你。

items.en: Tom would love to come with us, but he's sick.
items.zh: Tom 很想跟我們一起去，可是他生病了。

items.en: "Does your son like football?" "Yes, he'd love to play for the school team."
items.zh: 你兒子喜歡足球嗎？喜歡，他很想進學校的球隊。

items.en: The children would love to go to the beach again.
items.zh: 孩子們很想再去海邊。

examples.heading: ⑤ 問句：Wouldn't you love to ...?

items.en: "Wouldn't you love to live by the sea?" "Oh yes, I'd love that."
items.zh: 你不會很想住在海邊嗎？喔，我很想。

items.en: "Look at that boat. Wouldn't you love to sail around the islands?" "Yes, I would!"
items.zh: 你看那艘船。你不會很想開船繞著那些島嗎？會，我很想！

examples.heading: ⑥ would love to + be / have

items.en: I'd love to be a teacher like my mum.
items.zh: 我很想跟我媽一樣當老師。

items.en: We'd love to have a bigger kitchen.
items.zh: 我們很想要一個大一點的廚房。

items.en: She'd love to be in the school play this year.
items.zh: 她今年很想參加學校的話劇。

items.en: I'd love to have more time to read.
items.zh: 我很想有更多時間看書。

examples.heading: ⑦ 寫信

items.en: Thank you for your invitation. I'd love to come to your graduation.
items.zh: 謝謝你的邀請。我很想參加你的畢業典禮。

items.en: Dear Anna, we'd love to see you this summer. Can you visit us in July?
items.zh: 親愛的 Anna，我們今年夏天很想見你。你七月可以來看我們嗎？

items.en: I'd love to hear all about your new job. Write soon!
items.zh: 我很想聽你說新工作的事。快回信！

items.en: Your photos are beautiful. I'd love to go there one day.
items.zh: 你的照片好美。我很想有一天去那裡。

examples.heading: ⑧ would love to 和 would like to

items.en: "Would you like to try my soup?" "I'd love to. It smells great."
items.zh: 你想嚐嚐我的湯嗎？很想。聞起來好香。

items.en: I'd like to go to the museum, but I'd love to see the castle.
items.zh: 我想去博物館，可是我更想去看城堡。

items.en: "Would you like to dance?" "I'd love to!"
items.zh: 你想跳舞嗎？好啊，很想！

title: I would prefer to pay in cash.
translation: 我比較希望用現金付款。
name: would prefer to 表示客氣
sentences: "Shall I gift-wrap it?" "No, thanks. I'd prefer to wrap it myself."
"Can I take your coat?" "That's kind, but I'd prefer to keep it on. I'm a bit cold."
"We have a table near the door." "I'd prefer to sit by the window, if possible."
The hotel offered us a room on the ground floor, but we said we would prefer to be higher up.
Thanks for your email. I would prefer to meet at six instead of four.
"Shall we have the meeting online?" "I'd prefer to meet in person."
My boss would prefer to discuss the plan on Monday morning.
"Is Saturday OK for the party?" "We'd prefer to have it on Sunday."
"Do you want to come with us?" "Thanks, but I'd prefer to stay at home tonight."
My grandmother would prefer to live in the countryside.
I'd prefer to go on holiday with my friends this year.
"Should I call you?" "I'd prefer to get a text message, actually."
"What happened with your ex?" "I'd prefer not to talk about it."
The singer would prefer not to answer questions about her family.
"Do you want some wine?" "I'd prefer not to drink. I'm driving."
Our neighbours would prefer not to have a party in the garden.
"Can I put your photo in the article?" "Sorry, I'd prefer not to have my photo in it."
I'd prefer to walk rather than wait for the bus in the rain.
We would prefer to cook at home rather than eat out every night.
Most students would prefer to study in the morning rather than stay up late.
"Train or plane?" "I'd prefer to take the train rather than fly."
"Would you prefer to sit inside or outside?" "Inside, please. It's windy."
Would you prefer to start now or after lunch?
"Would your son prefer to share a room?" "No, he'd like his own."
Would you prefer to pay now or when you collect the shoes?
Dear Sir, I would prefer to receive my tickets by post.
If possible, I would prefer to start work in September.
My client would prefer to settle the matter without going to court.
We would prefer to receive the payment before the end of the month.
"Where is Ben?" "He said he would prefer to eat in his room."
She told the doctor she would prefer to have the operation in the spring.
The children would prefer to play outside, but it's raining.

examples.heading: ① 跟店員、服務生說話：would prefer to

items.en: "Shall I gift-wrap it?" "No, thanks. I'd prefer to wrap it myself."
items.zh: 要幫您包裝嗎？不用，謝謝。我比較想自己包。

items.en: "Can I take your coat?" "That's kind, but I'd prefer to keep it on. I'm a bit cold."
items.zh: 需要幫您掛外套嗎？謝謝，不過我想穿著。我有點冷。

items.en: "We have a table near the door." "I'd prefer to sit by the window, if possible."
items.zh: 我們門口附近有一張桌子。可以的話，我比較想坐窗邊。

items.en: The hotel offered us a room on the ground floor, but we said we would prefer to be higher up.
items.zh: 飯店給我們一樓的房間，可是我們說比較想住高一點。

examples.heading: ② 約時間：would prefer to

items.en: Thanks for your email. I would prefer to meet at six instead of four.
items.zh: 謝謝你的來信。我比較希望六點見面，不要四點。

items.en: "Shall we have the meeting online?" "I'd prefer to meet in person."
items.zh: 我們線上開會好嗎？我比較想當面見。

items.en: My boss would prefer to discuss the plan on Monday morning.
items.zh: 我老闆比較想星期一早上討論這個計畫。

items.en: "Is Saturday OK for the party?" "We'd prefer to have it on Sunday."
items.zh: 派對星期六可以嗎？我們比較想星期天辦。

examples.heading: ③ 說自己的選擇：would prefer to

items.en: "Do you want to come with us?" "Thanks, but I'd prefer to stay at home tonight."
items.zh: 你要跟我們去嗎？謝謝，不過今晚我比較想待在家。

items.en: My grandmother would prefer to live in the countryside.
items.zh: 我奶奶比較想住在鄉下。

items.en: I'd prefer to go on holiday with my friends this year.
items.zh: 今年我比較想跟朋友去度假。

items.en: "Should I call you?" "I'd prefer to get a text message, actually."
items.zh: 我該打電話給你嗎？其實我比較想收到簡訊。

examples.heading: ④ 客氣地拒絕：would prefer not to

items.en: "What happened with your ex?" "I'd prefer not to talk about it."
items.zh: 你跟前任怎麼了？我不太想談這件事。

items.en: The singer would prefer not to answer questions about her family.
items.zh: 那位歌手不太想回答關於她家人的問題。

items.en: "Do you want some wine?" "I'd prefer not to drink. I'm driving."
items.zh: 你要喝點酒嗎？我還是不喝了。我要開車。

items.en: Our neighbours would prefer not to have a party in the garden.
items.zh: 我們的鄰居不太希望在花園辦派對。

items.en: "Can I put your photo in the article?" "Sorry, I'd prefer not to have my photo in it."
items.zh: 我可以把你的照片放進文章嗎？抱歉，我不太希望文章裡有我的照片。

examples.heading: ⑤ 比較兩個選擇：would prefer to ... rather than

items.en: I'd prefer to walk rather than wait for the bus in the rain.
items.zh: 我寧可走路，也不想在雨中等公車。

items.en: We would prefer to cook at home rather than eat out every night.
items.zh: 我們比較想在家煮飯，不想每天晚上都在外面吃。

items.en: Most students would prefer to study in the morning rather than stay up late.
items.zh: 大部分學生比較想早上讀書，不想熬夜。

items.en: "Train or plane?" "I'd prefer to take the train rather than fly."
items.zh: 搭火車還是飛機？我比較想搭火車，不想坐飛機。

examples.heading: ⑥ 問句：Would you prefer to ...?

items.en: "Would you prefer to sit inside or outside?" "Inside, please. It's windy."
items.zh: 您比較想坐裡面還是外面？裡面，謝謝。風很大。

items.en: Would you prefer to start now or after lunch?
items.zh: 你比較想現在開始，還是吃完午餐再開始？

items.en: "Would your son prefer to share a room?" "No, he'd like his own."
items.zh: 你兒子會比較想跟人同房嗎？不會，他想要自己一間。

items.en: Would you prefer to pay now or when you collect the shoes?
items.zh: 您比較想現在付錢，還是拿鞋子的時候再付？

examples.heading: ⑦ 寫信和電子郵件：would prefer to

items.en: Dear Sir, I would prefer to receive my tickets by post.
items.zh: 您好，我比較希望用郵寄的方式收到票。

items.en: If possible, I would prefer to start work in September.
items.zh: 可以的話，我比較希望九月開始上班。

items.en: My client would prefer to settle the matter without going to court.
items.zh: 我的客戶比較希望不上法院就解決這件事。

items.en: We would prefer to receive the payment before the end of the month.
items.zh: 我們比較希望在月底前收到款項。

examples.heading: ⑧ 第三人稱和過去的情境

items.en: "Where is Ben?" "He said he would prefer to eat in his room."
items.zh: Ben 在哪裡？他說他比較想在房間吃。

items.en: She told the doctor she would prefer to have the operation in the spring.
items.zh: 她跟醫生說她比較想春天動手術。

items.en: The children would prefer to play outside, but it's raining.
items.zh: 孩子們比較想在外面玩，可是在下雨。

title: I hope you will look carefully at the enclosed papers.
translation: 希望您能仔細看看隨信附上的文件。
name: 副詞插在動詞和介系詞中間
sentences: Before you sign the contract, look carefully at every page.
The doctor looked closely at the cut on my arm.
"Do you like my drawing?" The teacher looked quickly at it and said, "It's lovely."
If you look carefully at the photo, you can see a cat in the window.
I want to know more about horses and learn how to deal properly with them.
The new manager dealt quickly with the problem.
"Is the complaint finished?" "Yes, we dealt fairly with it."
Teachers have to deal patiently with noisy children.
Listen carefully to the question before you answer.
The students listened closely to the guide in the museum.
"Did he hear the news?" "Yes, he listened quietly to it and said nothing."
A good friend listens patiently to your problems.
"They offered me a job in Tokyo." "Think seriously about it before you say no."
We need to think carefully about the cost.
She thought hard about the question, but she couldn't answer it.
In the meeting, the boss talked openly about the company's problems.
My grandfather never talked much about the war.
The nurse spoke kindly to the frightened child.
"Was the shop assistant rude?" "No, she spoke politely to everyone."
The dog waited patiently for its owner outside the shop.
"Is your brother still at the hospital?" "Yes, we're waiting nervously for news."
Many small shops rely heavily on tourists.
The price depends mainly on the size of the room.
Please read the instructions and look at the diagram carefully.
"What did the coach say?" "He told us to listen to the referee carefully."
They dealt with the angry customer very politely.
I hope you will look carefully at the papers that I have sent with this letter.
We must deal seriously with the complaints from people who live near the airport.
The committee will think carefully about all the ideas that students have sent in.
Please listen closely to everything the flight attendant says during the safety talk.
Visitors should look carefully at the signs that show the way to the exits.

examples.heading: ① look + 副詞 + at

items.en: Before you sign the contract, look carefully at every page.
items.zh: 簽合約之前，每一頁都要仔細看。

items.en: The doctor looked closely at the cut on my arm.
items.zh: 醫生仔細看了我手臂上的傷口。

items.en: "Do you like my drawing?" The teacher looked quickly at it and said, "It's lovely."
items.zh: 你喜歡我的畫嗎？老師很快看了一眼，說：很好看。

items.en: If you look carefully at the photo, you can see a cat in the window.
items.zh: 如果你仔細看這張照片，可以看到窗戶裡有一隻貓。

examples.heading: ② deal + 副詞 + with

items.en: I want to know more about horses and learn how to deal properly with them.
items.zh: 我想多了解馬，學會怎麼好好照顧牠們。

items.en: The new manager dealt quickly with the problem.
items.zh: 新經理很快處理了這個問題。

items.en: "Is the complaint finished?" "Yes, we dealt fairly with it."
items.zh: 那個投訴處理完了嗎？處理完了，我們處理得很公平。

items.en: Teachers have to deal patiently with noisy children.
items.zh: 老師得耐心對待吵鬧的孩子。

examples.heading: ③ listen + 副詞 + to

items.en: Listen carefully to the question before you answer.
items.zh: 回答之前，先仔細聽問題。

items.en: The students listened closely to the guide in the museum.
items.zh: 在博物館裡，學生們仔細聽導覽員說話。

items.en: "Did he hear the news?" "Yes, he listened quietly to it and said nothing."
items.zh: 他聽到消息了嗎？聽到了，他靜靜聽完，什麼都沒說。

items.en: A good friend listens patiently to your problems.
items.zh: 好朋友會耐心聽你說煩惱。

examples.heading: ④ think + 副詞 + about

items.en: "They offered me a job in Tokyo." "Think seriously about it before you say no."
items.zh: 他們給了我東京的工作。拒絕之前好好想一想。

items.en: We need to think carefully about the cost.
items.zh: 我們得仔細考慮費用。

items.en: She thought hard about the question, but she couldn't answer it.
items.zh: 她努力想了這個問題，可是答不出來。

examples.heading: ⑤ talk / speak + 副詞 + about / to

items.en: In the meeting, the boss talked openly about the company's problems.
items.zh: 開會時，老闆坦白談了公司的問題。

items.en: My grandfather never talked much about the war.
items.zh: 我爺爺從來不太談戰爭的事。

items.en: The nurse spoke kindly to the frightened child.
items.zh: 護士溫柔地對那個嚇壞的孩子說話。

items.en: "Was the shop assistant rude?" "No, she spoke politely to everyone."
items.zh: 店員很沒禮貌嗎？沒有，她對每個人都很客氣。

examples.heading: ⑥ wait / rely / depend + 副詞 + 介系詞

items.en: The dog waited patiently for its owner outside the shop.
items.zh: 狗在店外耐心等主人。

items.en: "Is your brother still at the hospital?" "Yes, we're waiting nervously for news."
items.zh: 你哥哥還在醫院嗎？對，我們很緊張地在等消息。

items.en: Many small shops rely heavily on tourists.
items.zh: 很多小店很依賴觀光客。

items.en: The price depends mainly on the size of the room.
items.zh: 價錢主要看房間的大小。

examples.heading: ⑦ 副詞放在受詞後面

items.en: Please read the instructions and look at the diagram carefully.
items.zh: 請讀說明，仔細看圖。

items.en: "What did the coach say?" "He told us to listen to the referee carefully."
items.zh: 教練說了什麼？他叫我們仔細聽裁判的話。

items.en: They dealt with the angry customer very politely.
items.zh: 他們很有禮貌地應付那位生氣的客人。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞很長，副詞放在動詞和介系詞中間

items.en: I hope you will look carefully at the papers that I have sent with this letter.
items.zh: 希望您能仔細看看我隨信寄上的文件。

items.en: We must deal seriously with the complaints from people who live near the airport.
items.zh: 我們必須認真處理住在機場附近的居民的投訴。

items.en: The committee will think carefully about all the ideas that students have sent in.
items.zh: 委員會會仔細考慮學生們寄來的所有想法。

items.en: Please listen closely to everything the flight attendant says during the safety talk.
items.zh: 安全說明的時候，請仔細聽空服員說的每一句話。

items.en: Visitors should look carefully at the signs that show the way to the exits.
items.zh: 遊客應該仔細看指示出口方向的標誌。

title: His flatmate put him up to it.
translation: 是他室友慫恿他去做那件事的。
name: 有直接受詞的片語介系詞動詞
sentences: Who put you up to this?
His friends put him up to the joke.
Nobody let me in on the plan.
Can you fill me in on what happened at the meeting?
Let me in on what you two are planning.
I'll take you up on your offer.
Her teacher talked her out of quitting the team.
Shall I put you down for two tickets?
Could you put me through to the manager?
My aunt wants to fix me up with her neighbour's son.
The judge let him off with a warning.
I'm sorry I missed your party. I'll make it up to you.
Mum signed us up for swimming lessons.
She tipped me off about the surprise test.
Please leave me out of this.
They shut her out of the meeting.
His brother bailed him out of trouble again.
She'll talk you round to her point of view.
The contract ties us down to two years.
Could you help me out with the rent this month?
Bring it up with your teacher.
My coach pulled me up on my footwork.
Don't take your anger out on your sister.
I put the mistake down to tiredness.
They've put their house up for sale.
She handed the keys over to the new owner.
We talked the seller down to two hundred pounds.
He tried to pass the copy off as the real thing.
The teacher let the whole class in on the secret.
They talked every member of the club out of leaving.
The manager brought the staff round to the new plan.
We chalked the delay up to the weather.
That's an offer I'll take you up on.
I didn't know what I was letting myself in for.
Is this the plan they let you in on?
They handed over all the documents to the lawyer.
She signed up her son for football lessons.

examples.heading: ① 第一個受詞是代名詞

items.en: Who put you up to this?
items.zh: 誰叫你這樣做的？

items.en: His friends put him up to the joke.
items.zh: 是他朋友慫恿他開那個玩笑的。

items.en: Nobody let me in on the plan.
items.zh: 沒有人跟我說這個計畫。

items.en: Can you fill me in on what happened at the meeting?
items.zh: 會議上發生了什麼事，可以跟我說一下嗎？

items.en: Let me in on what you two are planning.
items.zh: 你們兩個在計畫什麼，也跟我說一下。

items.en: I'll take you up on your offer.
items.zh: 我接受你的提議。

items.en: Her teacher talked her out of quitting the team.
items.zh: 她的老師勸她不要退出球隊。

items.en: Shall I put you down for two tickets?
items.zh: 要幫你登記兩張票嗎？

items.en: Could you put me through to the manager?
items.zh: 可以幫我轉接給經理嗎？

items.en: My aunt wants to fix me up with her neighbour's son.
items.zh: 我阿姨想把我介紹給她鄰居的兒子。

items.en: The judge let him off with a warning.
items.zh: 法官只給了他一個警告，就放他走了。

items.en: I'm sorry I missed your party. I'll make it up to you.
items.zh: 抱歉我沒去你的派對。我會補償你。

items.en: Mum signed us up for swimming lessons.
items.zh: 我媽幫我們報名了游泳課。

items.en: She tipped me off about the surprise test.
items.zh: 她事先偷偷告訴我要突擊考試。

items.en: Please leave me out of this.
items.zh: 這件事請不要把我扯進去。

items.en: They shut her out of the meeting.
items.zh: 他們不讓她參加那場會議。

items.en: His brother bailed him out of trouble again.
items.zh: 他哥哥又幫他擺平了麻煩。

items.en: She'll talk you round to her point of view.
items.zh: 她會說服你接受她的想法。

items.en: The contract ties us down to two years.
items.zh: 這份合約把我們綁兩年。

items.en: Could you help me out with the rent this month?
items.zh: 這個月的房租，你可以幫我一下嗎？

items.en: Bring it up with your teacher.
items.zh: 這件事去跟你的老師說。

items.en: My coach pulled me up on my footwork.
items.zh: 教練糾正了我的步法。

examples.heading: ② 第一個受詞是名詞

items.en: Don't take your anger out on your sister.
items.zh: 不要把氣出在你妹妹身上。

items.en: I put the mistake down to tiredness.
items.zh: 我認為這個錯是太累造成的。

items.en: They've put their house up for sale.
items.zh: 他們把房子掛出來賣了。

items.en: She handed the keys over to the new owner.
items.zh: 她把鑰匙交給了新屋主。

items.en: We talked the seller down to two hundred pounds.
items.zh: 我們跟賣家把價錢殺到兩百英鎊。

items.en: He tried to pass the copy off as the real thing.
items.zh: 他想把複製品當成真品。

items.en: The teacher let the whole class in on the secret.
items.zh: 老師把這個秘密告訴了全班。

items.en: They talked every member of the club out of leaving.
items.zh: 他們說服社團的每個成員不要退出。

items.en: The manager brought the staff round to the new plan.
items.zh: 經理說服員工接受新計畫。

items.en: We chalked the delay up to the weather.
items.zh: 我們認為延誤是天氣造成的。

examples.heading: ③ 第二個受詞移到前面，介系詞留在句尾

items.en: That's an offer I'll take you up on.
items.zh: 這個提議我會接受。

items.en: I didn't know what I was letting myself in for.
items.zh: 我當時不知道自己會惹上什麼麻煩。

items.en: Is this the plan they let you in on?
items.zh: 這就是他們跟你說的那個計畫嗎？

examples.heading: ④ `hand over`、`sign up` 的第一個受詞放在小品詞後面

items.en: They handed over all the documents to the lawyer.
items.zh: 他們把所有文件交給了律師。

items.en: She signed up her son for football lessons.
items.zh: 她幫她兒子報名了足球課。

title: Would you mind telling Mr. and Mrs. Thomas?
translation: 可以麻煩你告訴 Thomas 先生和太太嗎？
name: 動詞加動詞-ing（少數動詞）
sentences: I can't make the meeting tomorrow. Would you mind telling the others?
"It's cold in here. Would you mind closing the window?" "No, not at all."
Excuse me, would you mind moving your bag? I'd like to sit down.
Would you mind speaking more slowly? My English isn't very good.
"Do you mind waiting a few minutes?" "That's fine. I'm not in a hurry."
I don't mind working late if you need help.
My dad doesn't mind cooking, but he hates washing up.
"Can we go out now?" "Not yet. I haven't finished doing my homework."
As soon as the workers finish painting the kitchen, we can move in.
She finished studying at ten and went straight to bed.
It stopped raining, so we went for a walk.
Please stop talking. The film is starting.
The baby kept crying all night, and nobody slept.
My computer keeps freezing. I think I need a new one.
The doctor told me to avoid eating late at night.
"Where should we eat?" "I suggest trying that new pizza place."
We're considering moving to a smaller flat.
We left at six to avoid getting stuck in traffic.
He suggested meeting at the café near the station.
"Do you want kids?" "Maybe. I can't imagine being a dad yet."
Since I moved to the city, I miss walking by the sea.
Before the concert, she practised singing every day.
Can you imagine winning all that money?
My grandparents miss seeing us every weekend.
"Let's drive." "I suggest not taking the car. Parking is a nightmare there."
I don't mind not having a big wedding.
Imagine not having to get up early!
She practised not looking at her notes during the speech.
My brother has finished building his new desk.
Ben kept asking me questions during the film.
We will consider opening another shop next year.
"Is your sister still at the gym?" "Yes, she's practising lifting heavier weights."

examples.heading: ① Would you mind + 動詞-ing？（請求）

items.en: I can't make the meeting tomorrow. Would you mind telling the others?
items.zh: 我明天沒辦法去開會。可以麻煩你告訴其他人嗎？

items.en: "It's cold in here. Would you mind closing the window?" "No, not at all."
items.zh: 這裡好冷。可以麻煩你關一下窗嗎？好，沒問題。

items.en: Excuse me, would you mind moving your bag? I'd like to sit down.
items.zh: 不好意思，可以麻煩你把包包移開嗎？我想坐下。

items.en: Would you mind speaking more slowly? My English isn't very good.
items.zh: 可以麻煩你說慢一點嗎？我的英文不太好。

examples.heading: ② Do you mind / I don't mind + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Do you mind waiting a few minutes?" "That's fine. I'm not in a hurry."
items.zh: 你介意等幾分鐘嗎？沒關係。我不趕時間。

items.en: I don't mind working late if you need help.
items.zh: 如果你需要幫忙，我不介意加班。

items.en: My dad doesn't mind cooking, but he hates washing up.
items.zh: 我爸不介意煮飯，可是他很討厭洗碗。

examples.heading: ③ finish + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Can we go out now?" "Not yet. I haven't finished doing my homework."
items.zh: 我們現在可以出去了嗎？還不行。我功課還沒寫完。

items.en: As soon as the workers finish painting the kitchen, we can move in.
items.zh: 工人一把廚房油漆完，我們就可以搬進去了。

items.en: She finished studying at ten and went straight to bed.
items.zh: 她十點讀完書，就直接去睡了。

examples.heading: ④ stop / keep + 動詞-ing

items.en: It stopped raining, so we went for a walk.
items.zh: 雨停了，所以我們出去散步。

items.en: Please stop talking. The film is starting.
items.zh: 請不要講話了。電影要開始了。

items.en: The baby kept crying all night, and nobody slept.
items.zh: 寶寶整晚一直哭，大家都沒睡。

items.en: My computer keeps freezing. I think I need a new one.
items.zh: 我的電腦一直當機。我想我需要一台新的。

examples.heading: ⑤ avoid / suggest / consider + 動詞-ing

items.en: The doctor told me to avoid eating late at night.
items.zh: 醫生叫我避免太晚吃東西。

items.en: "Where should we eat?" "I suggest trying that new pizza place."
items.zh: 我們要去哪裡吃？我建議試試那家新開的披薩店。

items.en: We're considering moving to a smaller flat.
items.zh: 我們在考慮搬到小一點的公寓。

items.en: We left at six to avoid getting stuck in traffic.
items.zh: 我們六點出門，免得塞車。

items.en: He suggested meeting at the café near the station.
items.zh: 他建議在車站附近的咖啡店見面。

examples.heading: ⑥ imagine / miss / practise + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Do you want kids?" "Maybe. I can't imagine being a dad yet."
items.zh: 你想要小孩嗎？也許吧。我還無法想像自己當爸爸。

items.en: Since I moved to the city, I miss walking by the sea.
items.zh: 我搬到城市以後，很懷念在海邊散步。

items.en: Before the concert, she practised singing every day.
items.zh: 演唱會之前，她每天練唱。

items.en: Can you imagine winning all that money?
items.zh: 你能想像贏到那麼多錢嗎？

items.en: My grandparents miss seeing us every weekend.
items.zh: 我爺爺奶奶很懷念每個週末見到我們的日子。

examples.heading: ⑦ 動詞 + not + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Let's drive." "I suggest not taking the car. Parking is a nightmare there."
items.zh: 我們開車去吧。我建議不要開車。那裡很難停車。

items.en: I don't mind not having a big wedding.
items.zh: 不辦盛大的婚禮，我不介意。

items.en: Imagine not having to get up early!
items.zh: 想像一下不用早起的感覺！

items.en: She practised not looking at her notes during the speech.
items.zh: 她練習演講時不看筆記。

examples.heading: ⑧ 不同的時態和人稱

items.en: My brother has finished building his new desk.
items.zh: 我哥已經把他的新書桌做好了。

items.en: Ben kept asking me questions during the film.
items.zh: 看電影的時候，Ben 一直問我問題。

items.en: We will consider opening another shop next year.
items.zh: 明年我們會考慮再開一家店。

items.en: "Is your sister still at the gym?" "Yes, she's practising lifting heavier weights."
items.zh: 你姊姊還在健身房嗎？對，她在練習舉更重的槓鈴。

title: I couldn't stand being there.
translation: 我受不了待在那裡。
name: 動詞後接動詞-ing（較多種動詞）
sentences: The hotel was so noisy. I couldn't stand staying there another night.
"Do you want to come shopping?" "No, thanks. I can't stand waiting in queues."
My grandmother can't bear living alone. She misses my grandfather every day.
My brother hates driving to work. He can't stand sitting in traffic every morning.
The student denied cheating in the exam, but the teacher had seen his notes.
"Did you eat the last piece of cake?" "OK, I admit eating it. Sorry!"
The driver admitted going too fast.
The minister denied having taken the money.
If you don't book now, you risk losing your seat.
"What does the job involve?" "It involves travelling a lot and meeting clients."
He didn't want to risk missing the last train, so he left early.
Being a nurse involves working at night and at weekends.
We delayed telling the children about the move until the end of term.
"Have you called the bank yet?" "No, I keep putting off calling them."
Don't put off seeing a doctor if the pain gets worse.
"You look healthy!" "Thanks. I gave up eating sugar three months ago."
Even after the rain started, the band carried on playing.
"Are you still learning Japanese?" "No, I gave up going to classes last year."
The teacher told us to carry on working while she answered the phone.
Thanks for the desk in your office. I really appreciate having a quiet place to work.
Did Sarah mention having a party on Saturday?
"Where should we eat in Rome?" "I'd recommend trying the little place near our hotel."
"Do you fancy going out for a curry tonight?" "Sounds great!"
Most people dislike being woken up early on Sundays.
"Any tips for the long flight?" "If you want to sleep, I'd recommend not drinking coffee."
The boy admitted not doing his homework.
I can't stand not knowing the end of a story.
"Why did you leave the team?" "I couldn't stand being shouted at by the coach."
Nobody likes being kept waiting.
The man admitted having stolen the bike.
He denied having been told about the meeting.

examples.heading: ① can't stand / can't bear + 動詞-ing

items.en: The hotel was so noisy. I couldn't stand staying there another night.
items.zh: 那家飯店太吵了。我受不了再住一晚。

items.en: "Do you want to come shopping?" "No, thanks. I can't stand waiting in queues."
items.zh: 你要一起去購物嗎？不了，謝謝。我受不了排隊。

items.en: My grandmother can't bear living alone. She misses my grandfather every day.
items.zh: 我奶奶受不了一個人住。她每天都很想念我爺爺。

items.en: My brother hates driving to work. He can't stand sitting in traffic every morning.
items.zh: 我哥很討厭開車上班。他受不了每天早上塞在車陣裡。

examples.heading: ② deny / admit + 動詞-ing

items.en: The student denied cheating in the exam, but the teacher had seen his notes.
items.zh: 那個學生否認考試作弊，可是老師看到了他的小抄。

items.en: "Did you eat the last piece of cake?" "OK, I admit eating it. Sorry!"
items.zh: 最後一塊蛋糕是你吃的嗎？好啦，我承認是我吃的。對不起！

items.en: The driver admitted going too fast.
items.zh: 司機承認他開太快了。

items.en: The minister denied having taken the money.
items.zh: 部長否認拿了那筆錢。

examples.heading: ③ risk / involve + 動詞-ing

items.en: If you don't book now, you risk losing your seat.
items.zh: 你現在不訂的話，可能會沒位子。

items.en: "What does the job involve?" "It involves travelling a lot and meeting clients."
items.zh: 這份工作要做什麼？要常出差，還要見客戶。

items.en: He didn't want to risk missing the last train, so he left early.
items.zh: 他不想冒險錯過末班車，所以提早走了。

items.en: Being a nurse involves working at night and at weekends.
items.zh: 當護士要上夜班，週末也要上班。

examples.heading: ④ delay / put off + 動詞-ing

items.en: We delayed telling the children about the move until the end of term.
items.zh: 我們拖到學期末才告訴孩子們要搬家。

items.en: "Have you called the bank yet?" "No, I keep putting off calling them."
items.zh: 你打電話給銀行了嗎？還沒，我一直拖著沒打。

items.en: Don't put off seeing a doctor if the pain gets worse.
items.zh: 如果痛得更厲害，不要拖著不去看醫生。

examples.heading: ⑤ give up / carry on + 動詞-ing

items.en: "You look healthy!" "Thanks. I gave up eating sugar three months ago."
items.zh: 你看起來很健康！謝謝。我三個月前戒糖了。

items.en: Even after the rain started, the band carried on playing.
items.zh: 就算開始下雨，樂團還是繼續演奏。

items.en: "Are you still learning Japanese?" "No, I gave up going to classes last year."
items.zh: 你還在學日文嗎？沒有，我去年就不去上課了。

items.en: The teacher told us to carry on working while she answered the phone.
items.zh: 老師接電話的時候，叫我們繼續做功課。

examples.heading: ⑥ appreciate / mention / recommend / fancy + 動詞-ing

items.en: Thanks for the desk in your office. I really appreciate having a quiet place to work.
items.zh: 謝謝你讓我用你辦公室的桌子。有個安靜的地方工作，我真的很感謝。

items.en: Did Sarah mention having a party on Saturday?
items.zh: Sarah 有提到星期六要辦派對嗎？

items.en: "Where should we eat in Rome?" "I'd recommend trying the little place near our hotel."
items.zh: 我們在羅馬要去哪裡吃？我推薦試試我們飯店附近那家小店。

items.en: "Do you fancy going out for a curry tonight?" "Sounds great!"
items.zh: 今晚想出去吃咖哩嗎？好啊！

items.en: Most people dislike being woken up early on Sundays.
items.zh: 大部分的人都不喜歡星期天一大早被吵醒。

examples.heading: ⑦ 動詞 + not + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Any tips for the long flight?" "If you want to sleep, I'd recommend not drinking coffee."
items.zh: 長途飛行有什麼建議嗎？想睡覺的話，我建議不要喝咖啡。

items.en: The boy admitted not doing his homework.
items.zh: 那個男孩承認沒有寫功課。

items.en: I can't stand not knowing the end of a story.
items.zh: 不知道故事的結局，我會受不了。

examples.heading: ⑧ being + 過去分詞、having + 過去分詞

items.en: "Why did you leave the team?" "I couldn't stand being shouted at by the coach."
items.zh: 你為什麼離開球隊？我受不了被教練吼。

items.en: Nobody likes being kept waiting.
items.zh: 沒有人喜歡被晾在一邊等。

items.en: The man admitted having stolen the bike.
items.zh: 那個男人承認偷了腳踏車。

items.en: He denied having been told about the meeting.
items.zh: 他否認有人告訴過他開會的事。

title: Would you mind me staying in your flat again?
translation: 你介意我再借住一次你的公寓嗎？
name: 動詞-ing 前加名詞或受格代名詞當主詞
sentences: I'm in Paris next week. Would you mind me sleeping on your sofa?
"Do you mind me opening the window? It's really hot." "No, go ahead."
Would you mind my friend joining us for dinner?
"Do you mind me asking how old you are?" "Not at all. I'm forty."
If your boss doesn't mind you leaving early, take Friday afternoon off.
My parents don't mind me coming home late at weekends.
I don't mind the kids watching TV after they finish their homework.
Our neighbours don't seem to mind the dog barking.
I couldn't be famous. I couldn't stand people taking pictures of me all day.
My dad hates people using their phones at dinner.
She can't stand her brother borrowing her things without asking.
Many teachers dislike students arriving late.
"Why do you go to that café?" "I love the owner chatting with everyone."
My grandmother likes us visiting her on Sundays.
I don't like you driving so fast.
"Mark is going to be a teacher." "Really? I can't imagine him standing in front of a class."
Can you imagine your parents dancing at a rock concert?
We imagined Iceland being a frozen land, but it was green in summer.
I remember my grandfather telling me stories by the fire.
"Do you remember us meeting for the first time?" "Of course. It was at Anna's party."
We really appreciate you coming all this way to see us.
I'd appreciate your sending the report before Friday.
Don't leave the door open. You risk the cat getting out.
We can't risk the children getting lost in the crowd.
If you park there, you risk your car being towed away.
Thank you for your letter. I hope you will forgive my not replying sooner.
The manager did not appreciate his leaving without notice.
Please excuse my arriving late. The train was delayed.
The headteacher did not like their using phones in class.
I can't stand the people upstairs playing loud music at night.
Do you remember the old man next door singing every morning?
My mum doesn't mind my friends staying over at weekends.

examples.heading: ① Would you mind / Do you mind + 新的主詞 + 動詞-ing？

items.en: I'm in Paris next week. Would you mind me sleeping on your sofa?
items.zh: 我下星期在巴黎。你介意我睡你家沙發嗎？

items.en: "Do you mind me opening the window? It's really hot." "No, go ahead."
items.zh: 你介意我開窗嗎？好熱。不介意，開吧。

items.en: Would you mind my friend joining us for dinner?
items.zh: 你介意我朋友跟我們一起吃晚餐嗎？

items.en: "Do you mind me asking how old you are?" "Not at all. I'm forty."
items.zh: 你介意我問你幾歲嗎？不介意。我四十歲。

examples.heading: ② mind + 新的主詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: If your boss doesn't mind you leaving early, take Friday afternoon off.
items.zh: 如果你老闆不介意你早走，星期五下午就休假吧。

items.en: My parents don't mind me coming home late at weekends.
items.zh: 我爸媽不介意我週末晚回家。

items.en: I don't mind the kids watching TV after they finish their homework.
items.zh: 孩子們做完功課後看電視，我不介意。

items.en: Our neighbours don't seem to mind the dog barking.
items.zh: 我們的鄰居好像不介意狗叫。

examples.heading: ③ can't stand / hate / dislike + 新的主詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: I couldn't be famous. I couldn't stand people taking pictures of me all day.
items.zh: 我當不了名人。我受不了大家整天拍我。

items.en: My dad hates people using their phones at dinner.
items.zh: 我爸很討厭有人在吃飯的時候用手機。

items.en: She can't stand her brother borrowing her things without asking.
items.zh: 她受不了她弟弟沒問就借她的東西。

items.en: Many teachers dislike students arriving late.
items.zh: 很多老師不喜歡學生遲到。

examples.heading: ④ like / love + 新的主詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Why do you go to that café?" "I love the owner chatting with everyone."
items.zh: 你為什麼去那家咖啡店？我很喜歡老闆跟每個人聊天。

items.en: My grandmother likes us visiting her on Sundays.
items.zh: 我奶奶喜歡我們星期天去看她。

items.en: I don't like you driving so fast.
items.zh: 我不喜歡你開那麼快。

examples.heading: ⑤ imagine + 新的主詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Mark is going to be a teacher." "Really? I can't imagine him standing in front of a class."
items.zh: Mark 要當老師了。真的嗎？我無法想像他站在全班面前。

items.en: Can you imagine your parents dancing at a rock concert?
items.zh: 你能想像你爸媽在搖滾演唱會上跳舞嗎？

items.en: We imagined Iceland being a frozen land, but it was green in summer.
items.zh: 我們以為冰島是一片冰天雪地，可是夏天的冰島是綠的。

examples.heading: ⑥ remember / appreciate + 新的主詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: I remember my grandfather telling me stories by the fire.
items.zh: 我記得我爺爺在火爐旁講故事給我聽。

items.en: "Do you remember us meeting for the first time?" "Of course. It was at Anna's party."
items.zh: 你記得我們第一次見面嗎？當然記得。是在 Anna 的派對上。

items.en: We really appreciate you coming all this way to see us.
items.zh: 你大老遠來看我們，我們真的很感謝。

items.en: I'd appreciate your sending the report before Friday.
items.zh: 如果您能在星期五前寄報告，我會很感謝。

examples.heading: ⑦ risk + 新的主詞 + 動詞-ing

items.en: Don't leave the door open. You risk the cat getting out.
items.zh: 別讓門開著。貓可能會跑出去。

items.en: We can't risk the children getting lost in the crowd.
items.zh: 我們不能冒險讓孩子們在人群中走失。

items.en: If you park there, you risk your car being towed away.
items.zh: 你把車停在那裡，可能會被拖吊。

examples.heading: ⑧ 所有格 + 動詞-ing（正式）

items.en: Thank you for your letter. I hope you will forgive my not replying sooner.
items.zh: 謝謝您的來信。希望您原諒我沒有早點回信。

items.en: The manager did not appreciate his leaving without notice.
items.zh: 經理很不滿他沒有通知就走了。

items.en: Please excuse my arriving late. The train was delayed.
items.zh: 請原諒我遲到。火車誤點了。

items.en: The headteacher did not like their using phones in class.
items.zh: 校長不喜歡他們在課堂上用手機。

examples.heading: ⑨ 新的主詞是名詞片語

items.en: I can't stand the people upstairs playing loud music at night.
items.zh: 我受不了樓上的人晚上放很大聲的音樂。

items.en: Do you remember the old man next door singing every morning?
items.zh: 你記得隔壁那位老先生每天早上唱歌嗎？

items.en: My mum doesn't mind my friends staying over at weekends.
items.zh: 我媽不介意我朋友週末來家裡過夜。

title: Another way is to turn the computers off in the evenings.
translation: 另一個辦法是晚上把電腦關掉。
name: 名詞受詞放在小品詞前面的片語動詞
sentences: Please turn the lights off when you leave the room.
"It's freezing in here." "I'll turn the heating on."
The teacher asked us to turn our phones off during the test.
Can you turn the oven on? I want to bake some bread.
The lights stopped working, so we had to call the electrician up.
"Have you told Grandma?" "Not yet. I'll call Grandma up tonight."
Can you pick the kids up from school today? I'm working late.
I'll pick your sister up at the station on my way home.
If we can make these changes, we might be able to work this problem out.
"The maths homework is so hard." "Let's work the answers out together."
They talked for hours and finally worked their differences out.
I'm glad that you have decided to take some time off. You need a rest.
"Are you going away this summer?" "Yes, I'm taking two weeks off in August."
My dad never takes a day off, even when he's ill.
She took a year off before university and travelled around Asia.
"Is that my jacket?" "Sorry, I'll give your jacket back tomorrow."
You have to give the keys back when you leave the hotel.
Can you bring the books back to the library? They're due today.
My parents brought some sweets back from Japan.
Put the knife down! You'll hurt yourself.
He put the phone down and started to cry.
"Someone's at the door." "I'm in the shower! Can you let the plumber in?"
Can you let the dog out? He needs a walk.
Don't forget to turn off the TV before you go to bed.
I need to call up the bank about my card.
We're trying to work out a plan for the weekend.
Please give back the books by Friday.
The company has turned off all the machines in the old factory.
He picked up the two boys who were waiting at the bus stop.
The council wants to bring back the old trams that ran through the town.
She called up all the friends she hadn't seen since school.

examples.heading: ① turn off / turn on

items.en: Please turn the lights off when you leave the room.
items.zh: 離開房間的時候，請把燈關掉。

items.en: "It's freezing in here." "I'll turn the heating on."
items.zh: 這裡好冷。我來開暖氣。

items.en: The teacher asked us to turn our phones off during the test.
items.zh: 老師叫我們考試時把手機關機。

items.en: Can you turn the oven on? I want to bake some bread.
items.zh: 你可以打開烤箱嗎？我想烤麵包。

examples.heading: ② call up / pick up

items.en: The lights stopped working, so we had to call the electrician up.
items.zh: 燈不亮了，所以我們得打電話叫電工。

items.en: "Have you told Grandma?" "Not yet. I'll call Grandma up tonight."
items.zh: 你跟奶奶說了嗎？還沒。我今晚打電話給奶奶。

items.en: Can you pick the kids up from school today? I'm working late.
items.zh: 你今天可以去學校接孩子嗎？我要加班。

items.en: I'll pick your sister up at the station on my way home.
items.zh: 我回家路上會去車站接你妹妹。

examples.heading: ③ work out

items.en: If we can make these changes, we might be able to work this problem out.
items.zh: 如果我們能做這些改變，也許就能解決這個問題。

items.en: "The maths homework is so hard." "Let's work the answers out together."
items.zh: 數學作業好難。我們一起把答案算出來吧。

items.en: They talked for hours and finally worked their differences out.
items.zh: 他們談了好幾個小時，終於化解了分歧。

examples.heading: ④ take time off

items.en: I'm glad that you have decided to take some time off. You need a rest.
items.zh: 我很高興你決定休假一陣子。你需要休息。

items.en: "Are you going away this summer?" "Yes, I'm taking two weeks off in August."
items.zh: 你今年夏天要出去玩嗎？要，我八月請兩個星期的假。

items.en: My dad never takes a day off, even when he's ill.
items.zh: 我爸從來不請假，生病也一樣。

items.en: She took a year off before university and travelled around Asia.
items.zh: 她上大學前休了一年，到亞洲各地旅行。

examples.heading: ⑤ give back / bring back

items.en: "Is that my jacket?" "Sorry, I'll give your jacket back tomorrow."
items.zh: 那是我的外套嗎？抱歉，我明天把外套還你。

items.en: You have to give the keys back when you leave the hotel.
items.zh: 離開飯店時要把鑰匙還回去。

items.en: Can you bring the books back to the library? They're due today.
items.zh: 你可以把書拿回圖書館還嗎？今天到期。

items.en: My parents brought some sweets back from Japan.
items.zh: 我爸媽從日本帶了一些糖果回來。

examples.heading: ⑥ put down / let in / let out

items.en: Put the knife down! You'll hurt yourself.
items.zh: 把刀放下！你會受傷的。

items.en: He put the phone down and started to cry.
items.zh: 他放下電話，哭了起來。

items.en: "Someone's at the door." "I'm in the shower! Can you let the plumber in?"
items.zh: 有人在門口。我在洗澡！你可以讓水電工進來嗎？

items.en: Can you let the dog out? He needs a walk.
items.zh: 你可以把狗放出去嗎？牠需要散步。

examples.heading: ⑦ 名詞受詞放在小品詞後面

items.en: Don't forget to turn off the TV before you go to bed.
items.zh: 睡覺前別忘了關電視。

items.en: I need to call up the bank about my card.
items.zh: 我得打電話給銀行問我的卡的事。

items.en: We're trying to work out a plan for the weekend.
items.zh: 我們在想週末的計畫。

items.en: Please give back the books by Friday.
items.zh: 請在星期五前把書還回來。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞很長，放在小品詞後面

items.en: The company has turned off all the machines in the old factory.
items.zh: 公司關掉了舊工廠裡所有的機器。

items.en: He picked up the two boys who were waiting at the bus stop.
items.zh: 他接了那兩個在公車站等的男孩。

items.en: The council wants to bring back the old trams that ran through the town.
items.zh: 市議會想把以前在城裡跑的舊電車找回來。

items.en: She called up all the friends she hadn't seen since school.
items.zh: 她打電話給所有畢業後就沒見過的朋友。

title: I opened the envelope and took out the letter.
translation: 我打開信封，把信拿了出來。
name: 受詞放在小品詞後的片語動詞
sentences: I opened my bag and took out my passport.
"Can you help me put away the shopping?" "Sure. Where do the eggs go?"
The dentist took out two of my teeth.
Please put away your phones. The exam starts now.
I won a writing contest, and I need to travel to Mexico City to pick up my award.
Dinner's ready! The children have to pick up their toys first.
The dry cleaner called. You can pick up your suit after four.
She turned off the phone and walked to the bathroom.
"It's hot in here." "I'll turn on the air conditioning."
Don't forget to turn off the oven when the cake is ready.
It was cold, so I put on a jumper.
"Can I come in?" "Yes, but take off your shoes, please."
He put on his best suit for the interview.
If I didn't need it for my degree, I would give up this class immediately.
"Do you still play tennis?" "No, I gave up tennis when I hurt my knee."
My grandfather gave up smoking when he was fifty.
She gave up her job to look after her baby.
"What do I need to do?" "Fill in this form and sign at the bottom."
All visitors must fill in a card at the front desk.
Let me write down your phone number.
The teacher told us to write down the new words.
I called the station to find out the time of the last train.
"What does this word mean?" "Look up the word in the dictionary."
"Her parents were very angry." "Did they find out the truth about the party?"
I looked up the address online before we left.
"Why is it so dark?" "Someone turned the lights off."
I put my coat on and went outside.
She took her keys out and opened the door.
"Is this your umbrella?" "Yes, thanks. I'll put it away."
"Here's the form." "OK, I'll fill it in now."
I bought a new phone, but I can't turn it on.

examples.heading: ① take out / put away

items.en: I opened my bag and took out my passport.
items.zh: 我打開包包，拿出護照。

items.en: "Can you help me put away the shopping?" "Sure. Where do the eggs go?"
items.zh: 你可以幫我把買的東西收好嗎？好啊。蛋要放哪裡？

items.en: The dentist took out two of my teeth.
items.zh: 牙醫拔了我兩顆牙。

items.en: Please put away your phones. The exam starts now.
items.zh: 請把手機收起來。考試現在開始。

examples.heading: ② pick up

items.en: I won a writing contest, and I need to travel to Mexico City to pick up my award.
items.zh: 我贏了寫作比賽，得去墨西哥市領獎。

items.en: Dinner's ready! The children have to pick up their toys first.
items.zh: 晚餐好了！孩子們得先把玩具撿起來。

items.en: The dry cleaner called. You can pick up your suit after four.
items.zh: 乾洗店打電話來了。你四點以後可以去拿西裝。

examples.heading: ③ turn off / turn on

items.en: She turned off the phone and walked to the bathroom.
items.zh: 她把手機關掉，走去浴室。

items.en: "It's hot in here." "I'll turn on the air conditioning."
items.zh: 這裡好熱。我來開冷氣。

items.en: Don't forget to turn off the oven when the cake is ready.
items.zh: 蛋糕好了別忘了關烤箱。

examples.heading: ④ put on / take off

items.en: It was cold, so I put on a jumper.
items.zh: 天氣很冷，所以我穿上一件毛衣。

items.en: "Can I come in?" "Yes, but take off your shoes, please."
items.zh: 我可以進來嗎？可以，可是請脫鞋。

items.en: He put on his best suit for the interview.
items.zh: 他穿上他最好的西裝去面試。

examples.heading: ⑤ give up

items.en: If I didn't need it for my degree, I would give up this class immediately.
items.zh: 如果不是學位需要，我會馬上退掉這堂課。

items.en: "Do you still play tennis?" "No, I gave up tennis when I hurt my knee."
items.zh: 你還打網球嗎？沒有，我膝蓋受傷以後就不打了。

items.en: My grandfather gave up smoking when he was fifty.
items.zh: 我爺爺五十歲時戒了菸。

items.en: She gave up her job to look after her baby.
items.zh: 她辭掉工作照顧寶寶。

examples.heading: ⑥ fill in / write down

items.en: "What do I need to do?" "Fill in this form and sign at the bottom."
items.zh: 我需要做什麼？填好這張表格，在最下面簽名。

items.en: All visitors must fill in a card at the front desk.
items.zh: 所有訪客都必須在櫃檯填一張卡片。

items.en: Let me write down your phone number.
items.zh: 我把你的電話號碼寫下來。

items.en: The teacher told us to write down the new words.
items.zh: 老師叫我們把新單字寫下來。

examples.heading: ⑦ find out / look up

items.en: I called the station to find out the time of the last train.
items.zh: 我打電話到車站問末班車的時間。

items.en: "What does this word mean?" "Look up the word in the dictionary."
items.zh: 這個字是什麼意思？去字典查這個字。

items.en: "Her parents were very angry." "Did they find out the truth about the party?"
items.zh: 她爸媽很生氣。他們知道派對的真相了嗎？

items.en: I looked up the address online before we left.
items.zh: 我們出發前，我在網路上查了地址。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞放在動詞和小品詞中間

items.en: "Why is it so dark?" "Someone turned the lights off."
items.zh: 怎麼這麼暗？有人把燈關了。

items.en: I put my coat on and went outside.
items.zh: 我穿上外套，走到外面。

items.en: She took her keys out and opened the door.
items.zh: 她拿出鑰匙，打開門。

examples.heading: ⑨ 受詞是代名詞

items.en: "Is this your umbrella?" "Yes, thanks. I'll put it away."
items.zh: 這是你的傘嗎？對，謝謝。我把它收起來。

items.en: "Here's the form." "OK, I'll fill it in now."
items.zh: 這是表格。好，我現在填。

items.en: I bought a new phone, but I can't turn it on.
items.zh: 我買了一支新手機，可是開不了機。

title: I can surf the internet and look up some useful information.
translation: 我可以上網查一些有用的資料。
name: 受詞放在小品詞後面的片語動詞（較多種）
sentences: "When does the museum open?" "I don't know. I'll look up the opening times."
Students use the internet to look up information for their projects.
We spent an hour trying to work out the answer.
Can you work out how much we each have to pay?
The hospital is carrying out tests on the new medicine.
The police carried out a search of the house.
My uncle set up his own company when he was twenty-five.
"Is the projector ready?" "Not yet. I'm still setting up the computer."
My teacher pointed out a few mistakes in my essay.
"The plan looks good." "Yes, but I should point out that it's very expensive."
At dinner, my dad brought up the subject of my exam results.
Don't bring up politics at the party. It always ends in an argument.
I had already booked my seat on the ferry, so I couldn't put off the trip.
She keeps putting off going to the doctor.
"Is the wedding still on?" "No, they called off the wedding last week."
The school called off the trip because of the storm.
A big company took over the small bakery on our street.
When the manager left, his assistant took over the project.
The teacher handed out the exam papers.
Volunteers were handing out free water at the marathon.
The concert finished very late, and after it I had to clean up the hall.
After the party, my flatmates helped me clean up the kitchen.
"How's your leg after the accident?" "Better. I'm swimming to build up my strength."
It takes years to build up a good business.
During the meeting, Anna pointed out that we had no money left for advertising.
"Did you find the address?" "Yes, I looked up where the hotel was."
Nobody could work out why the machine had stopped.
We need to find out what time the last bus leaves.
The town council has set up a centre for people who have lost their jobs.
The company is carrying out a survey of customers who shop online.
The organisers handed out maps of the park and lists of all the events.

examples.heading: ① look up / work out

items.en: "When does the museum open?" "I don't know. I'll look up the opening times."
items.zh: 博物館幾點開？不知道。我查一下開放時間。

items.en: Students use the internet to look up information for their projects.
items.zh: 學生用網路查專題要用的資料。

items.en: We spent an hour trying to work out the answer.
items.zh: 我們花了一個小時想答案。

items.en: Can you work out how much we each have to pay?
items.zh: 你可以算出我們每個人要付多少嗎？

examples.heading: ② carry out / set up

items.en: The hospital is carrying out tests on the new medicine.
items.zh: 醫院正在對新藥做試驗。

items.en: The police carried out a search of the house.
items.zh: 警方搜查了那間房子。

items.en: My uncle set up his own company when he was twenty-five.
items.zh: 我叔叔二十五歲時開了自己的公司。

items.en: "Is the projector ready?" "Not yet. I'm still setting up the computer."
items.zh: 投影機好了嗎？還沒。我還在架電腦。

examples.heading: ③ point out / bring up

items.en: My teacher pointed out a few mistakes in my essay.
items.zh: 老師指出了我作文裡的幾個錯誤。

items.en: "The plan looks good." "Yes, but I should point out that it's very expensive."
items.zh: 這個計畫看起來不錯。對，可是我得指出它很貴。

items.en: At dinner, my dad brought up the subject of my exam results.
items.zh: 吃晚餐時，我爸提起了我的考試成績。

items.en: Don't bring up politics at the party. It always ends in an argument.
items.zh: 派對上別提政治。每次都會吵起來。

examples.heading: ④ put off / call off

items.en: I had already booked my seat on the ferry, so I couldn't put off the trip.
items.zh: 我已經訂了渡輪的位子，所以不能延後這趟旅行。

items.en: She keeps putting off going to the doctor.
items.zh: 她一直拖著不去看醫生。

items.en: "Is the wedding still on?" "No, they called off the wedding last week."
items.zh: 婚禮還辦嗎？沒有，他們上星期取消婚禮了。

items.en: The school called off the trip because of the storm.
items.zh: 學校因為暴風雨取消了校外教學。

examples.heading: ⑤ take over / hand out

items.en: A big company took over the small bakery on our street.
items.zh: 一家大公司接手了我們街上那家小麵包店。

items.en: When the manager left, his assistant took over the project.
items.zh: 經理離開以後，他的助理接手了這個專案。

items.en: The teacher handed out the exam papers.
items.zh: 老師發下考卷。

items.en: Volunteers were handing out free water at the marathon.
items.zh: 志工在馬拉松比賽中發免費的水。

examples.heading: ⑥ clean up / build up

items.en: The concert finished very late, and after it I had to clean up the hall.
items.zh: 演唱會很晚才結束，結束後我還得打掃會場。

items.en: After the party, my flatmates helped me clean up the kitchen.
items.zh: 派對結束後，我的室友幫我打掃廚房。

items.en: "How's your leg after the accident?" "Better. I'm swimming to build up my strength."
items.zh: 車禍後你的腿怎麼樣？好多了。我在游泳，把體力練回來。

items.en: It takes years to build up a good business.
items.zh: 經營出一個好事業要好幾年。

examples.heading: ⑦ 受詞是 that 子句或 wh 子句

items.en: During the meeting, Anna pointed out that we had no money left for advertising.
items.zh: 開會時，Anna 指出我們已經沒有錢做廣告了。

items.en: "Did you find the address?" "Yes, I looked up where the hotel was."
items.zh: 你找到地址了嗎？找到了，我查了旅館在哪裡。

items.en: Nobody could work out why the machine had stopped.
items.zh: 沒有人想得出機器為什麼停了。

items.en: We need to find out what time the last bus leaves.
items.zh: 我們得查出末班公車幾點開。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞很長

items.en: The town council has set up a centre for people who have lost their jobs.
items.zh: 鎮議會設立了一個中心，幫助失業的人。

items.en: The company is carrying out a survey of customers who shop online.
items.zh: 公司正在對網購的顧客做調查。

items.en: The organisers handed out maps of the park and lists of all the events.
items.zh: 主辦單位發了公園地圖和所有活動的清單。

title: I'd better stop now and get on with my studying.
translation: 我最好就此打住，繼續唸我的書。
name: 片語介系詞動詞加受詞
sentences: "Sorry to interrupt." "That's OK. I'll get on with my work."
The teacher left the room and told us to get on with our reading.
Stop chatting and get on with your homework.
The rain stopped, so the players got on with the game.
"How's your new flatmate?" "Great. I get on with her really well."
He doesn't get on with his boss, so he wants a new job.
Do your children get on with each other?
I missed two weeks of school, so I have to catch up with the work.
You go ahead. I'll catch up with you at the station.
She walked so fast that I couldn't catch up with her.
After my holiday, it took me two days to catch up with my emails.
If you want a peaceful holiday, you should get away from the city.
Keep away from the edge of the cliff!
My doctor told me to keep away from sugar.
On Fridays I like to get away from my desk at lunchtime.
My brother has a cold, so I'm keeping away from him this week.
"Can you buy some bread?" "Sure. Have we run out of milk too?"
The car stopped because we ran out of petrol.
I'm running out of ideas for dinner.
The printer has run out of paper again.
My parents are looking forward to their holiday in Spain.
"Who is Mark going out with?" "A girl from his office."
She went out with him for two years.
"Where's the sugar?" "Sorry, we've run out of it."
Your sister is lovely. I get on with her very well.
That dog bites. Keep away from it.
The bus left, but I ran and caught up with it at the next stop.
It's late. I'd better get on with cooking dinner.
"Are you ready for the trip?" "Not yet. I need to get on with packing."
We're looking forward to visiting you next month.
After lunch, the workers got on with painting the house.

examples.heading: ① get on with + 受詞（繼續做）
