items.en: "Sorry to interrupt." "That's OK. I'll get on with my work."
items.zh: 抱歉打擾你。沒關係。我繼續工作。

items.en: The teacher left the room and told us to get on with our reading.
items.zh: 老師離開教室，叫我們繼續閱讀。

items.en: Stop chatting and get on with your homework.
items.zh: 別聊天了，繼續寫你的作業。

items.en: The rain stopped, so the players got on with the game.
items.zh: 雨停了，所以球員們繼續比賽。

examples.heading: ② get on with + 受詞（相處）

items.en: "How's your new flatmate?" "Great. I get on with her really well."
items.zh: 你的新室友怎麼樣？很好。我跟她處得很好。

items.en: He doesn't get on with his boss, so he wants a new job.
items.zh: 他和老闆處不好，所以想換工作。

items.en: Do your children get on with each other?
items.zh: 你的孩子們彼此處得好嗎？

examples.heading: ③ catch up with + 受詞

items.en: I missed two weeks of school, so I have to catch up with the work.
items.zh: 我缺了兩個星期的課，所以得把功課補上。

items.en: You go ahead. I'll catch up with you at the station.
items.zh: 你先走。我會在車站追上你。

items.en: She walked so fast that I couldn't catch up with her.
items.zh: 她走得好快，我追不上她。

items.en: After my holiday, it took me two days to catch up with my emails.
items.zh: 度假回來以後，我花了兩天才把電子郵件處理完。

examples.heading: ④ get away from / keep away from + 受詞

items.en: If you want a peaceful holiday, you should get away from the city.
items.zh: 想要一個安靜的假期，就該離開城市。

items.en: Keep away from the edge of the cliff!
items.zh: 離懸崖邊遠一點！

items.en: My doctor told me to keep away from sugar.
items.zh: 醫生叫我少碰糖。

items.en: On Fridays I like to get away from my desk at lunchtime.
items.zh: 星期五午餐時間，我喜歡離開辦公桌一下。

items.en: My brother has a cold, so I'm keeping away from him this week.
items.zh: 我哥哥感冒了，所以這星期我離他遠一點。

examples.heading: ⑤ run out of + 受詞

items.en: "Can you buy some bread?" "Sure. Have we run out of milk too?"
items.zh: 你可以買點麵包嗎？好啊。我們的牛奶也喝完了嗎？

items.en: The car stopped because we ran out of petrol.
items.zh: 車子停了，因為我們沒油了。

items.en: I'm running out of ideas for dinner.
items.zh: 我快想不出晚餐要煮什麼了。

items.en: The printer has run out of paper again.
items.zh: 印表機又沒紙了。

examples.heading: ⑥ look forward to / go out with + 受詞

items.en: My parents are looking forward to their holiday in Spain.
items.zh: 我爸媽很期待去西班牙度假。

items.en: "Who is Mark going out with?" "A girl from his office."
items.zh: Mark 在跟誰交往？他辦公室的一個女生。

items.en: She went out with him for two years.
items.zh: 她和他交往了兩年。

examples.heading: ⑦ 受詞是代名詞

items.en: "Where's the sugar?" "Sorry, we've run out of it."
items.zh: 糖在哪裡？抱歉，我們用完了。

items.en: Your sister is lovely. I get on with her very well.
items.zh: 你姊姊人很好。我跟她處得很好。

items.en: That dog bites. Keep away from it.
items.zh: 那隻狗會咬人。離牠遠一點。

items.en: The bus left, but I ran and caught up with it at the next stop.
items.zh: 公車開走了，可是我跑到下一站趕上了它。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞是動詞-ing

items.en: It's late. I'd better get on with cooking dinner.
items.zh: 很晚了。我最好繼續煮晚餐。

items.en: "Are you ready for the trip?" "Not yet. I need to get on with packing."
items.zh: 你準備好去旅行了嗎？還沒。我得繼續打包。

items.en: We're looking forward to visiting you next month.
items.zh: 我們很期待下個月去拜訪你。

items.en: After lunch, the workers got on with painting the house.
items.zh: 午餐後，工人們繼續油漆房子。

title: You should face up to the problem and tell everybody the truth.
translation: 你應該正視這個問題，把真相告訴大家。
name: 片語介系詞動詞（較多種）
sentences: "I lost the client's file." "You have to face up to it and tell the boss."
He finally faced up to the fact that he needed help.
Nobody owned up to breaking the window, so the whole class stayed late.
"Who ate the cake?" "Tom owned up to it in the end."
Kids look up to their older brothers and sisters.
"Who's your hero?" "My grandad. I've always looked up to him."
In the old days, some people looked down on women who worked.
Don't look down on him just because he's young.
We need a name for the café. Can anyone come up with something?
The team came up with a plausible answer to the problem.
"How did you come up with that idea?" "I was in the shower."
My neighbours play loud music every night. I can't put up with it.
"How do you put up with his jokes?" "I just don't listen."
The workers put up with the cold office all winter.
My doctor says I should cut down on coffee.
The school is trying to cut down on paper, so homework is online now.
"Are you still smoking?" "Yes, but I've cut down on it."
I'm sorry I missed your birthday. Let me make up for it with dinner.
He worked late every night to make up for the lost time.
Everyone said the film was great, but it didn't live up to the hype.
Her parents expect a lot. She works hard to live up to their hopes.
When the other kids laughed at me, my friend stood up for me.
You have to stand up for what you believe in.
He copied my homework and got away with it.
"She was late again and the boss said nothing." "She always gets away with it."
He dropped out of university after one year to start a business.
I'm staying home this weekend to catch up on some sleep.
The class goes so fast that I can't keep up with it.
"How was your holiday?" "Great, but now I have to catch up on my emails."
"Why is Dad angry?" "My brother finally owned up to taking his car."
She got away with leaving work early all week.
I want to cut down on spending money on clothes.

examples.heading: ① face up to / own up to

items.en: "I lost the client's file." "You have to face up to it and tell the boss."
items.zh: 我把客戶的檔案弄丟了。你得面對這件事，去跟老闆說。

items.en: He finally faced up to the fact that he needed help.
items.zh: 他終於承認自己需要幫忙。

items.en: Nobody owned up to breaking the window, so the whole class stayed late.
items.zh: 沒有人承認打破了窗戶，所以全班都留下來。

items.en: "Who ate the cake?" "Tom owned up to it in the end."
items.zh: 誰吃了蛋糕？最後 Tom 承認了。

examples.heading: ② look up to / look down on

items.en: Kids look up to their older brothers and sisters.
items.zh: 小孩子都很崇拜他們的哥哥姊姊。

items.en: "Who's your hero?" "My grandad. I've always looked up to him."
items.zh: 你最崇拜誰？我爺爺。我一直很尊敬他。

items.en: In the old days, some people looked down on women who worked.
items.zh: 以前有些人看不起出去工作的女人。

items.en: Don't look down on him just because he's young.
items.zh: 不要因為他年輕就看不起他。

examples.heading: ③ come up with

items.en: We need a name for the café. Can anyone come up with something?
items.zh: 我們的咖啡店需要一個名字。有人想得出來嗎？

items.en: The team came up with a plausible answer to the problem.
items.zh: 團隊想出了一個合理的解決辦法。

items.en: "How did you come up with that idea?" "I was in the shower."
items.zh: 你是怎麼想到那個點子的？我在洗澡的時候想到的。

examples.heading: ④ put up with

items.en: My neighbours play loud music every night. I can't put up with it.
items.zh: 我的鄰居每天晚上都大聲放音樂。我受不了了。

items.en: "How do you put up with his jokes?" "I just don't listen."
items.zh: 你怎麼受得了他的笑話？我就不聽啊。

items.en: The workers put up with the cold office all winter.
items.zh: 員工整個冬天都忍受著冰冷的辦公室。

examples.heading: ⑤ cut down on

items.en: My doctor says I should cut down on coffee.
items.zh: 我的醫生說我應該少喝咖啡。

items.en: The school is trying to cut down on paper, so homework is online now.
items.zh: 學校在試著少用紙，所以現在作業都在網路上交。

items.en: "Are you still smoking?" "Yes, but I've cut down on it."
items.zh: 你還在抽菸嗎？還在，可是我抽得比較少了。

examples.heading: ⑥ make up for / live up to

items.en: I'm sorry I missed your birthday. Let me make up for it with dinner.
items.zh: 抱歉我錯過了你的生日。讓我請你吃晚餐補償你。

items.en: He worked late every night to make up for the lost time.
items.zh: 他每天晚上都加班，把浪費掉的時間補回來。

items.en: Everyone said the film was great, but it didn't live up to the hype.
items.zh: 大家都說那部電影很棒，可是它沒有大家說的那麼好。

items.en: Her parents expect a lot. She works hard to live up to their hopes.
items.zh: 她爸媽期望很高。她很努力達到他們的期望。

examples.heading: ⑦ stand up for / get away with

items.en: When the other kids laughed at me, my friend stood up for me.
items.zh: 其他小孩笑我的時候，我的朋友替我說話。

items.en: You have to stand up for what you believe in.
items.zh: 你要堅持你相信的事。

items.en: He copied my homework and got away with it.
items.zh: 他抄了我的作業，結果沒被抓到。

items.en: "She was late again and the boss said nothing." "She always gets away with it."
items.zh: 她又遲到了，老闆什麼都沒說。她每次都沒事。

examples.heading: ⑧ drop out of / catch up on / keep up with

items.en: He dropped out of university after one year to start a business.
items.zh: 他念了一年大學就退學去創業。

items.en: I'm staying home this weekend to catch up on some sleep.
items.zh: 我這個週末要待在家補眠。

items.en: The class goes so fast that I can't keep up with it.
items.zh: 這堂課進度好快，我跟不上。

items.en: "How was your holiday?" "Great, but now I have to catch up on my emails."
items.zh: 你的假期怎麼樣？很棒，可是現在得處理積下來的電子郵件。

examples.heading: ⑨ 受詞是動詞-ing

items.en: "Why is Dad angry?" "My brother finally owned up to taking his car."
items.zh: 爸為什麼生氣？我哥終於承認他開走了爸的車。

items.en: She got away with leaving work early all week.
items.zh: 她整個星期都提早下班，也沒被說。

items.en: I want to cut down on spending money on clothes.
items.zh: 我想少花點錢買衣服。

title: I like to walk in the woods and look for mushrooms.
translation: 我喜歡去樹林裡散步，找蘑菇。
name: 介系詞動詞加受詞
sentences: "What are you doing under the bed?" "I'm looking for my phone."
My dad is looking for a new job.
"Can I help you?" "Yes, I'm looking for a blue T-shirt."
We looked for the cat all afternoon.
Look at that big dog!
The teacher looked at my homework and smiled.
"Is my hair OK?" "Let me look at it."
My grandma looks after my baby sister on Mondays.
Can you look after my plants when I'm on holiday?
"Who looks after your dog?" "My neighbour does."
I listen to music on the bus every morning.
"Are you listening to me?" "Sorry, what did you say?"
My parents listen to the radio at breakfast.
Listen to this song. It's my favourite.
"Where are you?" "I'm at the station. I'm waiting for you."
We waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
Please wait for me after class.
"Who is that man?" "I don't know. Talk to him."
I talk to my mum on the phone every Sunday.
In class we talked about our holidays.
"What did you talk about?" "Football, as usual."
"Do you want to come to the party?" "I don't know. I'll think about it."
She thinks about her family in Brazil every day.
I'm thinking about my exam tomorrow.
"How much is it?" "Don't worry, I'll pay for it."
My parents paid for my new bike.
At the café, I asked for a glass of water.
"Is the soup good?" "It's too salty. I'm going to ask for some water."
Here are your keys. I found them in the car. Were you looking for them?
My little brother is ill, so I'm looking after him today.
That's my favourite band. I listen to them every day.
"Is Anna here?" "No, but you can wait for her in the office."

examples.heading: ① look for

items.en: "What are you doing under the bed?" "I'm looking for my phone."
items.zh: 你在床底下做什麼？我在找我的手機。

items.en: My dad is looking for a new job.
items.zh: 我爸在找新工作。

items.en: "Can I help you?" "Yes, I'm looking for a blue T-shirt."
items.zh: 需要幫忙嗎？要，我在找一件藍色的 T 恤。

items.en: We looked for the cat all afternoon.
items.zh: 我們整個下午都在找那隻貓。

examples.heading: ② look at

items.en: Look at that big dog!
items.zh: 你看那隻大狗！

items.en: The teacher looked at my homework and smiled.
items.zh: 老師看了我的作業，笑了。

items.en: "Is my hair OK?" "Let me look at it."
items.zh: 我的頭髮還好嗎？我看看。

examples.heading: ③ look after

items.en: My grandma looks after my baby sister on Mondays.
items.zh: 星期一我奶奶照顧我的小妹妹。

items.en: Can you look after my plants when I'm on holiday?
items.zh: 我去度假的時候，你可以幫我照顧植物嗎？

items.en: "Who looks after your dog?" "My neighbour does."
items.zh: 誰幫你照顧狗？我的鄰居。

examples.heading: ④ listen to

items.en: I listen to music on the bus every morning.
items.zh: 我每天早上在公車上聽音樂。

items.en: "Are you listening to me?" "Sorry, what did you say?"
items.zh: 你有在聽我說話嗎？抱歉，你剛說什麼？

items.en: My parents listen to the radio at breakfast.
items.zh: 我爸媽吃早餐時聽廣播。

items.en: Listen to this song. It's my favourite.
items.zh: 你聽這首歌。這是我最喜歡的。

examples.heading: ⑤ wait for

items.en: "Where are you?" "I'm at the station. I'm waiting for you."
items.zh: 你在哪裡？我在車站。我在等你。

items.en: We waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
items.zh: 我們等公車等了二十分鐘。

items.en: Please wait for me after class.
items.zh: 下課後請等我。

examples.heading: ⑥ talk to / talk about

items.en: "Who is that man?" "I don't know. Talk to him."
items.zh: 那個男人是誰？我不知道。去跟他說話啊。

items.en: I talk to my mum on the phone every Sunday.
items.zh: 我每個星期天都跟我媽講電話。

items.en: In class we talked about our holidays.
items.zh: 上課時我們聊了我們的假期。

items.en: "What did you talk about?" "Football, as usual."
items.zh: 你們聊了什麼？足球，跟平常一樣。

examples.heading: ⑦ think about

items.en: "Do you want to come to the party?" "I don't know. I'll think about it."
items.zh: 你想來派對嗎？不知道。我想想看。

items.en: She thinks about her family in Brazil every day.
items.zh: 她每天都想著在巴西的家人。

items.en: I'm thinking about my exam tomorrow.
items.zh: 我在想明天的考試。

examples.heading: ⑧ pay for / ask for

items.en: "How much is it?" "Don't worry, I'll pay for it."
items.zh: 多少錢？別擔心，我來付。

items.en: My parents paid for my new bike.
items.zh: 我爸媽幫我付了新腳踏車的錢。

items.en: At the café, I asked for a glass of water.
items.zh: 在咖啡店，我要了一杯水。

items.en: "Is the soup good?" "It's too salty. I'm going to ask for some water."
items.zh: 湯好喝嗎？太鹹了。我要跟他們要一點水。

examples.heading: ⑨ 受詞是代名詞

items.en: Here are your keys. I found them in the car. Were you looking for them?
items.zh: 你的鑰匙在這裡。我在車上找到的。你剛剛在找它們嗎？

items.en: My little brother is ill, so I'm looking after him today.
items.zh: 我弟弟生病了，所以我今天照顧他。

items.en: That's my favourite band. I listen to them every day.
items.zh: 那是我最喜歡的樂團。我每天都聽他們的歌。

items.en: "Is Anna here?" "No, but you can wait for her in the office."
items.zh: Anna 在嗎？不在，可是你可以在辦公室等她。

title: Our company needs to train some staff on how to deal with customer complaints.
translation: 我們公司需要訓練一些員工處理客訴。
name: 介系詞動詞加受詞（較多種）
sentences: "There's a customer at the desk, and she's angry." "Don't worry, I'll deal with it."
New teachers often don't know how to deal with noisy classes.
The council dealt with the problem quickly.
"Will the match go ahead?" "It depends on the rain. They'll decide at noon."
The price depends on how many people come.
My grandma lives alone, but she can rely on her neighbours.
"Will you help me move on Sunday?" "Of course. You can rely on me."
I saw the job online, so I applied for it.
You need to apply for a visa before you travel.
"Did you get the scholarship?" "I don't know yet. I applied for it last month."
The guests complained about the noise from the bar.
My dad always complains about the traffic.
My room was dirty, so I called reception and complained about it.
The team consists of four engineers and a designer.
Breakfast consists of bread, eggs and coffee.
"Who is 'the boss' in your email?" "I'm referring to Mr Brown."
In his speech, the mayor referred to the new bridge.
"Do you believe in ghosts?" "No, but I don't like dark houses."
Our coach believes in hard work.
My sister suffers from headaches when she doesn't sleep enough.
Many people in the city suffer from stress.
"Let me pay." "No, I insist on paying. It's your birthday."
She finally succeeded in finding a flat near her office.
The students complained about having too much homework.
He doesn't believe in spending money on expensive clothes.
"Are the boys in trouble again?" "Yes, but their teacher will deal with them."
"This is the report I told you about." "Thanks. I'll refer to it in my talk."
Our dog is old, and he depends on us for everything.
"Can we eat outside tonight?" "That depends on how cold it gets."
Before the meeting, nobody agreed on what to do next.
The training deals with how to answer angry phone calls.

examples.heading: ① deal with

items.en: "There's a customer at the desk, and she's angry." "Don't worry, I'll deal with it."
items.zh: 櫃檯有個客人，她很生氣。別擔心，我來處理。

items.en: New teachers often don't know how to deal with noisy classes.
items.zh: 新老師常常不知道怎麼應付吵鬧的班級。

items.en: The council dealt with the problem quickly.
items.zh: 市議會很快處理了這個問題。

examples.heading: ② depend on / rely on

items.en: "Will the match go ahead?" "It depends on the rain. They'll decide at noon."
items.zh: 比賽會照常舉行嗎？要看雨下得怎樣。他們中午會決定。

items.en: The price depends on how many people come.
items.zh: 價錢要看來多少人。

items.en: My grandma lives alone, but she can rely on her neighbours.
items.zh: 我奶奶一個人住，可是她可以依靠鄰居。

items.en: "Will you help me move on Sunday?" "Of course. You can rely on me."
items.zh: 星期天你會幫我搬家嗎？當然。你可以信賴我。

examples.heading: ③ apply for

items.en: I saw the job online, so I applied for it.
items.zh: 我在網路上看到這份工作，所以就去應徵了。

items.en: You need to apply for a visa before you travel.
items.zh: 你要在出發前申請簽證。

items.en: "Did you get the scholarship?" "I don't know yet. I applied for it last month."
items.zh: 你拿到獎學金了嗎？還不知道。我上個月申請的。

examples.heading: ④ complain about

items.en: The guests complained about the noise from the bar.
items.zh: 客人抱怨酒吧傳來的噪音。

items.en: My dad always complains about the traffic.
items.zh: 我爸老是在抱怨交通。

items.en: My room was dirty, so I called reception and complained about it.
items.zh: 我的房間很髒，所以我打電話給櫃檯抱怨。

examples.heading: ⑤ consist of / refer to

items.en: The team consists of four engineers and a designer.
items.zh: 這個團隊由四位工程師和一位設計師組成。

items.en: Breakfast consists of bread, eggs and coffee.
items.zh: 早餐有麵包、蛋和咖啡。

items.en: "Who is 'the boss' in your email?" "I'm referring to Mr Brown."
items.zh: 你信裡說的『老闆』是誰？我指的是 Brown 先生。

items.en: In his speech, the mayor referred to the new bridge.
items.zh: 市長在演講中提到了那座新橋。

examples.heading: ⑥ believe in / suffer from

items.en: "Do you believe in ghosts?" "No, but I don't like dark houses."
items.zh: 你相信有鬼嗎？不信，可是我不喜歡暗暗的房子。

items.en: Our coach believes in hard work.
items.zh: 我們教練很重視努力。

items.en: My sister suffers from headaches when she doesn't sleep enough.
items.zh: 我姊姊睡不夠的時候就會頭痛。

items.en: Many people in the city suffer from stress.
items.zh: 城市裡很多人都有壓力。

examples.heading: ⑦ 受詞是動詞-ing

items.en: "Let me pay." "No, I insist on paying. It's your birthday."
items.zh: 我來付。不，一定要我付。今天是你生日。

items.en: She finally succeeded in finding a flat near her office.
items.zh: 她終於成功找到離公司很近的公寓。

items.en: The students complained about having too much homework.
items.zh: 學生們抱怨作業太多。

items.en: He doesn't believe in spending money on expensive clothes.
items.zh: 他不認為應該花錢買昂貴的衣服。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞是代名詞

items.en: "Are the boys in trouble again?" "Yes, but their teacher will deal with them."
items.zh: 那些男生又惹麻煩了嗎？對，可是他們的老師會處理他們。

items.en: "This is the report I told you about." "Thanks. I'll refer to it in my talk."
items.zh: 這就是我跟你說的報告。謝謝。我演講時會提到它。

items.en: Our dog is old, and he depends on us for everything.
items.zh: 我們的狗老了，什麼都要靠我們。

examples.heading: ⑨ 受詞是 wh 子句

items.en: "Can we eat outside tonight?" "That depends on how cold it gets."
items.zh: 我們今晚可以在外面吃嗎？要看會變多冷。

items.en: Before the meeting, nobody agreed on what to do next.
items.zh: 開會前，大家對下一步要做什麼沒有共識。

items.en: The training deals with how to answer angry phone calls.
items.zh: 這個訓練教的是怎麼接聽生氣的電話。

title: I will pick you up and arrange everything.
translation: 我會去接你，也會把一切安排好。
name: 片語動詞的代名詞受詞位置
sentences: "What time does your train arrive?" "At five." "OK, I'll pick you up."
My dad picks me up from school every day.
Your bag is on the floor. Pick it up, please.
Can you pick us up after the party?
Ring me up or send me an email if you have any questions.
I don't have Tom's number. Can you ring him up?
Could you come here by nine o'clock to help me out?
My neighbours are moving tomorrow, so we're going to help them out.
These old shoes are too small. You can throw them away.
"Is this milk OK?" "No, it's old. Throw it away."
That's my pen! Give it back!
I borrowed two books from the library, and I have to give them back on Friday.
"Here's your coat. It's cold outside." "Thanks, Mum. I'll put it on."
"Can I try these jeans on?" "Of course. You can try them on over there."
Your shoes are wet. Take them off before you come in.
I like this hat. Can I try it on?
The heater is broken. I can't turn it on.
"The TV is too loud." "Sorry, I'll turn it off."
Your phone is ringing. Turn it off, please. We're in a meeting.
"What time do you want breakfast?" "Wake me up at eight, please."
The baby is sleeping. Please don't wake her up.
The dog barks every morning and wakes us up.
"It's so hot in here." "Can you turn on the fan?"
I'll pick up the children from school today.
Don't throw away those boxes. We need them for the move.
She put on her best dress for the party.
Can you turn the music down? I'm on the phone.
Tom picked his sister up at the airport.
Take your shoes off, please. The floor is clean.
My brother threw his old guitar away last week.
Two waiters are ill today. Could you help the kitchen staff out?

examples.heading: ① pick up

items.en: "What time does your train arrive?" "At five." "OK, I'll pick you up."
items.zh: 你的火車幾點到？五點。好，我去接你。

items.en: My dad picks me up from school every day.
items.zh: 我爸每天去學校接我。

items.en: Your bag is on the floor. Pick it up, please.
items.zh: 你的包包在地上。請撿起來。

items.en: Can you pick us up after the party?
items.zh: 派對結束後你可以來接我們嗎？

examples.heading: ② ring up / help out

items.en: Ring me up or send me an email if you have any questions.
items.zh: 有問題的話打電話給我或寄電子郵件給我。

items.en: I don't have Tom's number. Can you ring him up?
items.zh: 我沒有 Tom 的號碼。你可以打給他嗎？

items.en: Could you come here by nine o'clock to help me out?
items.zh: 你可以九點前過來幫我一下嗎？

items.en: My neighbours are moving tomorrow, so we're going to help them out.
items.zh: 我的鄰居明天要搬家，所以我們要去幫忙。

examples.heading: ③ throw away / give back

items.en: These old shoes are too small. You can throw them away.
items.zh: 這雙舊鞋太小了。你可以丟掉。

items.en: "Is this milk OK?" "No, it's old. Throw it away."
items.zh: 這牛奶還能喝嗎？不行，過期了。丟掉吧。

items.en: That's my pen! Give it back!
items.zh: 那是我的筆！還給我！

items.en: I borrowed two books from the library, and I have to give them back on Friday.
items.zh: 我從圖書館借了兩本書，星期五要還。

examples.heading: ④ put on / take off / try on

items.en: "Here's your coat. It's cold outside." "Thanks, Mum. I'll put it on."
items.zh: 你的外套在這裡。外面很冷。謝謝媽。我會穿上。

items.en: "Can I try these jeans on?" "Of course. You can try them on over there."
items.zh: 我可以試穿這條牛仔褲嗎？當然。你可以在那邊試穿。

items.en: Your shoes are wet. Take them off before you come in.
items.zh: 你的鞋子濕了。進來前先脫掉。

items.en: I like this hat. Can I try it on?
items.zh: 我喜歡這頂帽子。可以試戴嗎？

examples.heading: ⑤ turn on / turn off

items.en: The heater is broken. I can't turn it on.
items.zh: 暖氣壞了。我打不開。

items.en: "The TV is too loud." "Sorry, I'll turn it off."
items.zh: 電視太大聲了。抱歉，我把它關掉。

items.en: Your phone is ringing. Turn it off, please. We're in a meeting.
items.zh: 你的手機在響。請關掉。我們在開會。

examples.heading: ⑥ wake up

items.en: "What time do you want breakfast?" "Wake me up at eight, please."
items.zh: 你想幾點吃早餐？請八點叫我起床。

items.en: The baby is sleeping. Please don't wake her up.
items.zh: 寶寶在睡覺。請不要吵醒她。

items.en: The dog barks every morning and wakes us up.
items.zh: 那隻狗每天早上都叫，把我們吵醒。

examples.heading: ⑦ 受詞是名詞，放在小品詞後面

items.en: "It's so hot in here." "Can you turn on the fan?"
items.zh: 這裡好熱。你可以開電扇嗎？

items.en: I'll pick up the children from school today.
items.zh: 今天我去學校接孩子。

items.en: Don't throw away those boxes. We need them for the move.
items.zh: 不要丟掉那些箱子。搬家要用。

items.en: She put on her best dress for the party.
items.zh: 她穿上最好的洋裝去參加派對。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞是名詞，放在動詞和小品詞中間

items.en: Can you turn the music down? I'm on the phone.
items.zh: 你可以把音樂調小聲嗎？我在講電話。

items.en: Tom picked his sister up at the airport.
items.zh: Tom 去機場接他妹妹。

items.en: Take your shoes off, please. The floor is clean.
items.zh: 請把鞋子脫掉。地板是乾淨的。

items.en: My brother threw his old guitar away last week.
items.zh: 我哥哥上星期把他的舊吉他丟掉了。

items.en: Two waiters are ill today. Could you help the kitchen staff out?
items.zh: 今天有兩個服務生生病了。你可以幫廚房的員工一下嗎？

title: Think it over and tell me what you decide to do.
translation: 你仔細想一想，再告訴我你決定怎麼做。
name: 代名詞受詞放在小品詞前的片語動詞
sentences: "We'd like to offer you the job." "Thank you. Can I think it over this weekend?"
It's a big decision, so think it over carefully.
I saw an ad for a new gym on TV, and I wanted to check it out.
"Have you seen that new band?" "No, but I'll check them out on Saturday."
I love shopping for clothes, but I hate trying them on.
"These shoes look nice." "Try them on. The mirror is over there."
She took the dress to the changing room and tried it on.
"My computer isn't working." "Don't worry, I'll sort it out."
There's a problem with your bill. The manager will sort it out.
"What's the capital of Peru?" "I don't know. Let's look it up."
I didn't know his phone number, so I looked it up online.
The match was going to be on Sunday, but the rain made them put it off.
"Have you been to the dentist?" "No, I keep putting it off."
We can't put the meeting off again. Let's have it tomorrow.
"Mr Lee is in a meeting." "OK. Can you ask him to call me back?"
I missed your call. I'll call you back after lunch.
My team needs me on Saturday. I can't let them down.
"You promised to come!" "I know. I'm sorry I let you down."
They offered him a job in Paris, but he turned it down.
"Can you hear the baby? Your radio is very loud." "Oh, sorry. I'll turn it down now."
"Where's your homework?" "I handed it in yesterday."
Write your answers on the paper and hand it in at the end of the exam.
"Can I borrow your bike?" "Sure, but give it back by six."
The shirt was too small, so I took it back to the shop.
I borrowed Tom's camera, and I have to bring it back tomorrow.
Can I try this jacket on?
Please hand your phones in before the exam.
Let's put off the trip until next month.
She turned down the offer because the pay was too low.
I'll look up the train times for you.
Can you sort out the problem with the printer?

examples.heading: ① think over / check out

items.en: "We'd like to offer you the job." "Thank you. Can I think it over this weekend?"
items.zh: 我們想給你這份工作。謝謝。我可以這個週末想一想嗎？

items.en: It's a big decision, so think it over carefully.
items.zh: 這是個重大的決定，所以好好想一想。

items.en: I saw an ad for a new gym on TV, and I wanted to check it out.
items.zh: 我在電視上看到一家新健身房的廣告，想去看看。

items.en: "Have you seen that new band?" "No, but I'll check them out on Saturday."
items.zh: 你看過那個新樂團嗎？沒有，可是我星期六會去看看。

examples.heading: ② try on

items.en: I love shopping for clothes, but I hate trying them on.
items.zh: 我很愛買衣服，可是很討厭試穿。

items.en: "These shoes look nice." "Try them on. The mirror is over there."
items.zh: 這雙鞋很好看。試穿看看。鏡子在那邊。

items.en: She took the dress to the changing room and tried it on.
items.zh: 她把洋裝拿進試衣間試穿。

examples.heading: ③ sort out / look up

items.en: "My computer isn't working." "Don't worry, I'll sort it out."
items.zh: 我的電腦壞了。別擔心，我來處理。

items.en: There's a problem with your bill. The manager will sort it out.
items.zh: 您的帳單有點問題。經理會處理。

items.en: "What's the capital of Peru?" "I don't know. Let's look it up."
items.zh: 秘魯的首都是哪裡？不知道。我們查一下吧。

items.en: I didn't know his phone number, so I looked it up online.
items.zh: 我不知道他的電話號碼，所以上網查了。

examples.heading: ④ put off

items.en: The match was going to be on Sunday, but the rain made them put it off.
items.zh: 比賽本來是星期天，可是下雨讓他們延期了。

items.en: "Have you been to the dentist?" "No, I keep putting it off."
items.zh: 你去看牙醫了嗎？還沒，我一直拖。

items.en: We can't put the meeting off again. Let's have it tomorrow.
items.zh: 我們不能再延後這個會議了。明天開吧。

examples.heading: ⑤ call back / let down

items.en: "Mr Lee is in a meeting." "OK. Can you ask him to call me back?"
items.zh: 李先生在開會。好。你可以請他回我電話嗎？

items.en: I missed your call. I'll call you back after lunch.
items.zh: 我錯過了你的電話。午餐後回電給你。

items.en: My team needs me on Saturday. I can't let them down.
items.zh: 我的隊伍星期六需要我。我不能讓他們失望。

items.en: "You promised to come!" "I know. I'm sorry I let you down."
items.zh: 你答應過要來的！我知道。抱歉讓你失望了。

examples.heading: ⑥ turn down / hand in

items.en: They offered him a job in Paris, but he turned it down.
items.zh: 他們給了他巴黎的工作，可是他拒絕了。

items.en: "Can you hear the baby? Your radio is very loud." "Oh, sorry. I'll turn it down now."
items.zh: 你聽得到寶寶的聲音嗎？你的收音機很大聲。喔，抱歉。我現在就調小聲。

items.en: "Where's your homework?" "I handed it in yesterday."
items.zh: 你的作業呢？我昨天交了。

items.en: Write your answers on the paper and hand it in at the end of the exam.
items.zh: 把答案寫在紙上，考試結束時交上來。

examples.heading: ⑦ give back / take back / bring back

items.en: "Can I borrow your bike?" "Sure, but give it back by six."
items.zh: 我可以借你的腳踏車嗎？好啊，可是六點前要還我。

items.en: The shirt was too small, so I took it back to the shop.
items.zh: 那件襯衫太小了，所以我拿回店裡退。

items.en: I borrowed Tom's camera, and I have to bring it back tomorrow.
items.zh: 我借了 Tom 的相機，明天得拿回去還他。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞是名詞

items.en: Can I try this jacket on?
items.zh: 我可以試穿這件外套嗎？

items.en: Please hand your phones in before the exam.
items.zh: 考試前請把手機交出來。

items.en: Let's put off the trip until next month.
items.zh: 我們把旅行延到下個月吧。

items.en: She turned down the offer because the pay was too low.
items.zh: 她拒絕了那個工作機會，因為薪水太低。

items.en: I'll look up the train times for you.
items.zh: 我幫你查火車時刻。

items.en: Can you sort out the problem with the printer?
items.zh: 你可以處理印表機的問題嗎？

title: I tried to clean it up as much as possible.
translation: 我盡量把它清乾淨了。
name: 片語動詞中間放受詞代名詞（較多種）
sentences: "Wasn't there a party here last night?" "Yes. The living room was a mess, but I tried to clean it up as much as possible."
The kids spilled juice on the floor, and their dad cleaned it up.
We bought an old house and fixed it up ourselves.
The old bike was rusty, so my grandad fixed it up for me.
I'd heard a lot about the band, so I went to check them out last week.
"There's a new café on the corner." "Let's check it out after work."
The instructions were in Japanese, but I figured them out.
"How did you open the box?" "It took a while, but I figured it out."
"Should we buy the flat?" "Let's talk it over with your parents first."
They had a problem with the plan, so they talked it over at lunch.
Before you quit, talk it over with your manager.
The company had a big loss, but the boss played it down.
"Was she upset about the mistake?" "No, she just laughed it off."
People made jokes about his accent, but he laughed them off.
I told him he looked ill, but he brushed it off.
The doctor warned her about her heart, but she brushed the warning off.
"Did you lose all your photos?" "No, luckily I'd backed them up."
Save your work and back it up every evening.
I told the teacher what happened, and my friends backed me up.
"Can the car be repaired?" "No, the insurance company has written it off."
After the first year, many people wrote the business off, but it did well.
The guard asked for my passport, so I handed it over.
"Where are the keys?" "I handed them over to the new tenants."
I asked him when he'd pay, but I couldn't pin him down.
"When is the meeting?" "I don't know. Try to pin her down."
I cleaned up the kitchen before my parents came home.
We need to figure out a way to get there on time.
The government tried to play down the problem.
Always back up your files before you update your computer.
The thief handed over the bag when the police arrived.
She laughed off the rumours about her new job.

examples.heading: ① clean up / fix up

items.en: "Wasn't there a party here last night?" "Yes. The living room was a mess, but I tried to clean it up as much as possible."
items.zh: 昨晚這裡不是辦過派對嗎？對。客廳很亂，可是我盡量清乾淨了。

items.en: The kids spilled juice on the floor, and their dad cleaned it up.
items.zh: 孩子們把果汁灑在地上，爸爸把它擦乾淨了。

items.en: We bought an old house and fixed it up ourselves.
items.zh: 我們買了一間舊房子，自己整修。

items.en: The old bike was rusty, so my grandad fixed it up for me.
items.zh: 那台舊腳踏車生鏽了，所以我爺爺幫我修好了。

examples.heading: ② check out / figure out

items.en: I'd heard a lot about the band, so I went to check them out last week.
items.zh: 我聽說了很多那個樂團的事，所以上星期去聽了聽。

items.en: "There's a new café on the corner." "Let's check it out after work."
items.zh: 轉角開了一家新咖啡店。下班後去看看吧。

items.en: The instructions were in Japanese, but I figured them out.
items.zh: 說明書是日文的，可是我弄懂了。

items.en: "How did you open the box?" "It took a while, but I figured it out."
items.zh: 你是怎麼打開這個盒子的？花了點時間，可是我想出來了。

examples.heading: ③ talk over

items.en: "Should we buy the flat?" "Let's talk it over with your parents first."
items.zh: 我們該買那間公寓嗎？我們先跟你爸媽好好談談。

items.en: They had a problem with the plan, so they talked it over at lunch.
items.zh: 他們對計畫有意見，所以午餐時好好討論了一下。

items.en: Before you quit, talk it over with your manager.
items.zh: 辭職之前，先跟你的經理好好談談。

examples.heading: ④ play down / laugh off / brush off

items.en: The company had a big loss, but the boss played it down.
items.zh: 公司虧了一大筆錢，可是老闆輕描淡寫地帶過。

items.en: "Was she upset about the mistake?" "No, she just laughed it off."
items.zh: 她對那個錯誤很難過嗎？沒有，她一笑置之。

items.en: People made jokes about his accent, but he laughed them off.
items.zh: 大家拿他的口音開玩笑，可是他一笑置之。

items.en: I told him he looked ill, but he brushed it off.
items.zh: 我跟他說他看起來氣色不好，可是他不當一回事。

items.en: The doctor warned her about her heart, but she brushed the warning off.
items.zh: 醫生警告她心臟有問題，可是她不當一回事。

examples.heading: ⑤ back up

items.en: "Did you lose all your photos?" "No, luckily I'd backed them up."
items.zh: 你的照片都不見了嗎？沒有，還好我有備份。

items.en: Save your work and back it up every evening.
items.zh: 把你的工作存檔，每天晚上備份。

items.en: I told the teacher what happened, and my friends backed me up.
items.zh: 我把發生的事告訴老師，我的朋友都支持我的說法。

examples.heading: ⑥ write off / hand over

items.en: "Can the car be repaired?" "No, the insurance company has written it off."
items.zh: 車子還能修嗎？不能，保險公司認定報廢了。

items.en: After the first year, many people wrote the business off, but it did well.
items.zh: 第一年過後很多人都不看好這家公司，可是它做得很好。

items.en: The guard asked for my passport, so I handed it over.
items.zh: 警衛要看我的護照，所以我把它交出去了。

items.en: "Where are the keys?" "I handed them over to the new tenants."
items.zh: 鑰匙在哪裡？我交給新房客了。

examples.heading: ⑦ pin down

items.en: I asked him when he'd pay, but I couldn't pin him down.
items.zh: 我問他什麼時候付錢，可是沒辦法逼他給個確切的答覆。

items.en: "When is the meeting?" "I don't know. Try to pin her down."
items.zh: 會議是什麼時候？不知道。你逼她給個確定的時間吧。

examples.heading: ⑧ 受詞是名詞

items.en: I cleaned up the kitchen before my parents came home.
items.zh: 我爸媽回家前，我把廚房打掃乾淨了。

items.en: We need to figure out a way to get there on time.
items.zh: 我們得想個辦法準時到那裡。

items.en: The government tried to play down the problem.
items.zh: 政府試圖淡化這個問題。

items.en: Always back up your files before you update your computer.
items.zh: 更新電腦之前，一定要先備份檔案。

items.en: The thief handed over the bag when the police arrived.
items.zh: 警察到的時候，小偷交出了包包。

items.en: She laughed off the rumours about her new job.
items.zh: 她對關於她新工作的謠言一笑置之。

title: I want to invite you for dinner.
translation: 我想邀請你來吃晚餐。
name: 動詞加不定詞
sentences: Dear Mrs Chen, I want to invite you for dinner on Friday.
"What do you want to eat?" "Pizza, please!"
My son wants to be a firefighter when he grows up.
We wanted to see the film, but the tickets were sold out.
"Do you want to come to the beach with us?" "Yes, I'd love that."
On Sunday mornings I like to go to the zoo with my kids.
Sometimes I don't like to go out because it's very cold.
My grandma loves to tell stories about her childhood.
"What do you like to do at the weekend?" "I like to cook for my friends."
I need to buy some milk on the way home.
"Are you OK?" "I'm tired. I need to sleep."
"Can I go to the party tonight?" "Yes, but you need to be home by eleven."
"Does your sister need to take the bus to school?" "No, my dad drives her."
I'm trying to learn Japanese, but it's hard.
Please try to arrive before nine.
He tried to open the box, but it was locked.
Thank you for the lovely weekend. I hope to see you again soon.
My parents hope to visit Japan next spring.
We hope to finish the new kitchen by Christmas.
My daughter learned to ride a bike when she was five.
"Can you drive?" "Not yet. I'm learning to drive this year."
We were at the beach when it started to rain.
The baby started to cry when the dog barked.
I don't want to go to school today. I feel sick.
My brother doesn't like to share his toys.
We didn't want to wake the baby, so we talked quietly.
You don't need to bring anything. We have everything.
"Do you want to dance?" "Sure, why not?"
"Does Tom like to play football?" "Yes, he plays every day."
"Did you want to talk to me?" "Yes, do you have a minute?"
"Where do you want to go for your birthday?" "To the new Italian restaurant."

examples.heading: ① want to

items.en: Dear Mrs Chen, I want to invite you for dinner on Friday.
items.zh: 陳太太您好，我想邀請您星期五來吃晚餐。

items.en: "What do you want to eat?" "Pizza, please!"
items.zh: 你想吃什麼？披薩，拜託！

items.en: My son wants to be a firefighter when he grows up.
items.zh: 我兒子長大想當消防員。

items.en: We wanted to see the film, but the tickets were sold out.
items.zh: 我們本來想看那部電影，可是票賣完了。

items.en: "Do you want to come to the beach with us?" "Yes, I'd love that."
items.zh: 你想跟我們去海邊嗎？好啊，我很想去。

examples.heading: ② like to / love to

items.en: On Sunday mornings I like to go to the zoo with my kids.
items.zh: 星期天早上我喜歡帶孩子去動物園。

items.en: Sometimes I don't like to go out because it's very cold.
items.zh: 有時候天氣太冷，我就不喜歡出門。

items.en: My grandma loves to tell stories about her childhood.
items.zh: 我奶奶很喜歡講她小時候的故事。

items.en: "What do you like to do at the weekend?" "I like to cook for my friends."
items.zh: 你週末喜歡做什麼？我喜歡煮飯給朋友吃。

examples.heading: ③ need to

items.en: I need to buy some milk on the way home.
items.zh: 我回家路上得買點牛奶。

items.en: "Are you OK?" "I'm tired. I need to sleep."
items.zh: 你還好嗎？我很累。我需要睡覺。

items.en: "Can I go to the party tonight?" "Yes, but you need to be home by eleven."
items.zh: 我今晚可以去派對嗎？可以，可是你得十一點以前回家。

items.en: "Does your sister need to take the bus to school?" "No, my dad drives her."
items.zh: 你妹妹得搭公車上學嗎？不用，我爸開車載她。

examples.heading: ④ try to

items.en: I'm trying to learn Japanese, but it's hard.
items.zh: 我正在試著學日文，可是很難。

items.en: Please try to arrive before nine.
items.zh: 請盡量九點以前到。

items.en: He tried to open the box, but it was locked.
items.zh: 他試著打開那個箱子，可是箱子鎖住了。

examples.heading: ⑤ hope to

items.en: Thank you for the lovely weekend. I hope to see you again soon.
items.zh: 謝謝你讓我度過一個很棒的週末。希望很快能再見到你。

items.en: My parents hope to visit Japan next spring.
items.zh: 我爸媽希望明年春天去日本。

items.en: We hope to finish the new kitchen by Christmas.
items.zh: 我們希望聖誕節前把新廚房弄好。

examples.heading: ⑥ learn to / start to

items.en: My daughter learned to ride a bike when she was five.
items.zh: 我女兒五歲就學會騎腳踏車了。

items.en: "Can you drive?" "Not yet. I'm learning to drive this year."
items.zh: 你會開車嗎？還不會。我今年在學開車。

items.en: We were at the beach when it started to rain.
items.zh: 我們在海邊的時候開始下雨了。

items.en: The baby started to cry when the dog barked.
items.zh: 狗一叫，寶寶就開始哭了。

examples.heading: ⑦ 否定

items.en: I don't want to go to school today. I feel sick.
items.zh: 我今天不想上學。我不舒服。

items.en: My brother doesn't like to share his toys.
items.zh: 我弟弟不喜歡分享他的玩具。

items.en: We didn't want to wake the baby, so we talked quietly.
items.zh: 我們不想吵醒寶寶，所以小聲說話。

items.en: You don't need to bring anything. We have everything.
items.zh: 你什麼都不用帶。我們都有了。

examples.heading: ⑧ 問句

items.en: "Do you want to dance?" "Sure, why not?"
items.zh: 你想跳舞嗎？好啊，有何不可？

items.en: "Does Tom like to play football?" "Yes, he plays every day."
items.zh: Tom 喜歡踢足球嗎？喜歡，他每天都踢。

items.en: "Did you want to talk to me?" "Yes, do you have a minute?"
items.zh: 你想跟我說話嗎？對，你有空嗎？

items.en: "Where do you want to go for your birthday?" "To the new Italian restaurant."
items.zh: 你生日想去哪裡？去那家新開的義大利餐廳。

title: Please remember to bring your pajamas and your toothbrush.
translation: 請記得帶你的睡衣和牙刷。
name: 動詞加不定詞（較多種動詞）
sentences: Hi Leo, you're staying with us on Saturday. Please remember to bring your pajamas and your toothbrush.
The party starts at seven. Don't forget to come!
Remember to turn off the lights when you leave the office.
"Did you remember to call the dentist?" "Oh no, I forgot."
Don't forget to water the plants while we're away.
I forgot to buy milk, so we can't have tea.
My brother always forgets to close the fridge.
Sorry I'm late. I forgot to set my alarm.
I bought warm clothes because I hope to go to England this year.
"Are you going home for the holidays?" "No, we plan to stay in Taipei this year."
"What are you doing when you finish school?" "I'm planning to study medicine."
My parents hope to retire by the sea.
It was raining, so we decided to stay at home and watch a film.
After ten years in the bank, she decided to open a café.
"Which phone did you buy?" "I decided to keep my old one."
Dad promised to take us to the zoo on Sunday.
"Will you call me when you arrive?" "I promise to call."
"Can we keep the puppy?" "OK. Mum has agreed to let him stay."
The neighbours agreed to turn the music down after ten.
When my car broke down, a kind man offered to help.
My sister offered to drive me to the airport.
The taxi driver refused to take us because our dog was too big.
My old laptop is so slow. It refuses to open more than two programs.
It was very late, so I decided not to call her.
She promised not to tell anyone about the surprise party.
Please try not to make any noise. The baby is asleep.
We agreed not to spend too much on presents this year.
"When did you decide to learn Korean?" "After my trip to Seoul."
"Have you remembered to pack the tickets?" "Yes, they're in my bag."
"Are you planning to come to the meeting tomorrow?" "Yes, but I'll be a bit late."
I'll try to finish the report by Friday, but I can't promise.

examples.heading: ① remember to / don't forget to

items.en: Hi Leo, you're staying with us on Saturday. Please remember to bring your pajamas and your toothbrush.
items.zh: 嗨，Leo，你星期六要來我們家住。請記得帶你的睡衣和牙刷。

items.en: The party starts at seven. Don't forget to come!
items.zh: 派對七點開始。別忘了要來！

items.en: Remember to turn off the lights when you leave the office.
items.zh: 離開辦公室的時候記得關燈。

items.en: "Did you remember to call the dentist?" "Oh no, I forgot."
items.zh: 你有記得打給牙醫嗎？糟了，我忘了。

items.en: Don't forget to water the plants while we're away.
items.zh: 我們不在的時候，別忘了幫植物澆水。

examples.heading: ② forget to

items.en: I forgot to buy milk, so we can't have tea.
items.zh: 我忘了買牛奶，所以我們不能喝奶茶了。

items.en: My brother always forgets to close the fridge.
items.zh: 我弟弟總是忘了關冰箱。

items.en: Sorry I'm late. I forgot to set my alarm.
items.zh: 抱歉我遲到了。我忘了設鬧鐘。

examples.heading: ③ hope to / plan to

items.en: I bought warm clothes because I hope to go to England this year.
items.zh: 我買了保暖的衣服，因為我希望今年能去英國。

items.en: "Are you going home for the holidays?" "No, we plan to stay in Taipei this year."
items.zh: 你們放假要回家嗎？不，我們今年打算待在台北。

items.en: "What are you doing when you finish school?" "I'm planning to study medicine."
items.zh: 你畢業後要做什麼？我打算讀醫學。

items.en: My parents hope to retire by the sea.
items.zh: 我爸媽希望退休後住在海邊。

examples.heading: ④ decide to

items.en: It was raining, so we decided to stay at home and watch a film.
items.zh: 在下雨，所以我們決定待在家看電影。

items.en: After ten years in the bank, she decided to open a café.
items.zh: 在銀行工作十年之後，她決定開一家咖啡廳。

items.en: "Which phone did you buy?" "I decided to keep my old one."
items.zh: 你買了哪一支手機？我決定繼續用舊的。

examples.heading: ⑤ promise to / agree to

items.en: Dad promised to take us to the zoo on Sunday.
items.zh: 爸爸答應星期天帶我們去動物園。

items.en: "Will you call me when you arrive?" "I promise to call."
items.zh: 你到了會打給我嗎？我答應會打。

items.en: "Can we keep the puppy?" "OK. Mum has agreed to let him stay."
items.zh: 我們可以養這隻小狗嗎？好。媽媽同意讓牠留下來。

items.en: The neighbours agreed to turn the music down after ten.
items.zh: 鄰居同意十點以後把音樂關小聲。

examples.heading: ⑥ offer to / refuse to

items.en: When my car broke down, a kind man offered to help.
items.zh: 我的車拋錨的時候，有個好心的男人主動說要幫忙。

items.en: My sister offered to drive me to the airport.
items.zh: 我姊主動說要開車送我去機場。

items.en: The taxi driver refused to take us because our dog was too big.
items.zh: 那個計程車司機不肯載我們，因為我們的狗太大了。

items.en: My old laptop is so slow. It refuses to open more than two programs.
items.zh: 我的舊筆電好慢。它開不了兩個以上的程式。

examples.heading: ⑦ 不定詞的否定：not to

items.en: It was very late, so I decided not to call her.
items.zh: 已經很晚了，所以我決定不打給她。

items.en: She promised not to tell anyone about the surprise party.
items.zh: 她答應不把驚喜派對的事告訴任何人。

items.en: Please try not to make any noise. The baby is asleep.
items.zh: 請盡量不要發出聲音。寶寶睡著了。

items.en: We agreed not to spend too much on presents this year.
items.zh: 我們說好今年不在禮物上花太多錢。

examples.heading: ⑧ 問句和不同的時態

items.en: "When did you decide to learn Korean?" "After my trip to Seoul."
items.zh: 你什麼時候決定學韓文的？去首爾玩了以後。

items.en: "Have you remembered to pack the tickets?" "Yes, they're in my bag."
items.zh: 你記得把票放進行李了嗎？記得，在我包包裡。

items.en: "Are you planning to come to the meeting tomorrow?" "Yes, but I'll be a bit late."
items.zh: 你明天打算來開會嗎？會，可是我會晚一點到。

items.en: I'll try to finish the report by Friday, but I can't promise.
items.zh: 我會盡量在星期五前把報告寫完，可是我不能保證。

title: My room seems to be very cold and unfriendly.
translation: 我的房間好像很冷，一點都不溫馨。
name: 動詞加不定詞（多種動詞）
sentences: "Is Tom OK?" "I don't know. He seems to be upset about something."
The new manager appears to know a lot about the business.
This printer doesn't seem to work. Can you have a look?
Your plan seems to be practicable, but it will cost a lot.
It was too cold at the beach, so we decided to go home early.
"Why did you change class?" "I decided to study with a different teacher."
"Why do you cycle to work?" "I choose to cycle because it keeps me fit."
My boss agreed to give me Friday off.
The traffic was terrible, but we managed to catch the train.
"Did you find the hotel?" "Yes, we managed to find it in the end."
The team failed to win a single game this season.
The letter failed to arrive in time.
We can't afford to go on holiday this year.
The little boy refused to eat his vegetables.
"You're late again!" "Sorry. I promise to be on time tomorrow."
My neighbour offered to water my plants while I was away.
The taxi driver refused to take us to the airport in the snow.
When his mum came in, he pretended to be asleep.
In winter, people tend to stay at home more.
You worked really hard. You deserve to have a rest.
She pretended not to see me in the street.
I've decided not to buy that phone. It's too expensive.
"Don't tell Mum." "OK, I promise not to say anything."
Most people choose not to work on Sundays.
The baby seems to be sleeping. Let's talk quietly.
The prices appear to be going up every month.
"What's Anna doing?" "She seems to be studying, but I think she's on her phone."
It's freezing in here. Someone seems to have left the window open.
"Where's Dad?" "He appears to have gone out. His coat isn't here."
The shop seems to have closed down. The windows are empty.
He pretended to have read the book, but he didn't know the ending.

examples.heading: ① seem / appear + 不定詞

items.en: "Is Tom OK?" "I don't know. He seems to be upset about something."
items.zh: Tom 還好嗎？不知道。他好像在為什麼事難過。

items.en: The new manager appears to know a lot about the business.
items.zh: 新經理看起來很懂這一行。

items.en: This printer doesn't seem to work. Can you have a look?
items.zh: 這台印表機好像壞了。你可以看一下嗎？

items.en: Your plan seems to be practicable, but it will cost a lot.
items.zh: 你的計畫看起來可行，可是要花很多錢。

examples.heading: ② decide / choose / agree + 不定詞

items.en: It was too cold at the beach, so we decided to go home early.
items.zh: 海邊太冷了，所以我們決定早點回家。

items.en: "Why did you change class?" "I decided to study with a different teacher."
items.zh: 你為什麼換班？我決定跟另一位老師學。

items.en: "Why do you cycle to work?" "I choose to cycle because it keeps me fit."
items.zh: 你為什麼騎腳踏車上班？我選擇騎車，因為這樣能保持身材。

items.en: My boss agreed to give me Friday off.
items.zh: 我老闆同意讓我星期五休假。

examples.heading: ③ manage / fail + 不定詞

items.en: The traffic was terrible, but we managed to catch the train.
items.zh: 交通很糟，可是我們還是趕上了火車。

items.en: "Did you find the hotel?" "Yes, we managed to find it in the end."
items.zh: 你們找到飯店了嗎？找到了，最後找到了。

items.en: The team failed to win a single game this season.
items.zh: 這支球隊這一季一場都沒贏。

items.en: The letter failed to arrive in time.
items.zh: 那封信沒有及時寄到。

examples.heading: ④ afford / refuse / promise / offer + 不定詞

items.en: We can't afford to go on holiday this year.
items.zh: 我們今年沒錢去度假。

items.en: The little boy refused to eat his vegetables.
items.zh: 小男孩不肯吃他的蔬菜。

items.en: "You're late again!" "Sorry. I promise to be on time tomorrow."
items.zh: 你又遲到了！對不起。我保證明天準時。

items.en: My neighbour offered to water my plants while I was away.
items.zh: 我不在的時候，鄰居主動說要幫我澆花。

items.en: The taxi driver refused to take us to the airport in the snow.
items.zh: 計程車司機不肯在下雪天載我們去機場。

examples.heading: ⑤ pretend / tend / deserve + 不定詞

items.en: When his mum came in, he pretended to be asleep.
items.zh: 他媽媽進來的時候，他假裝睡著了。

items.en: In winter, people tend to stay at home more.
items.zh: 冬天的時候，大家往往比較常待在家裡。

items.en: You worked really hard. You deserve to have a rest.
items.zh: 你真的很努力。你應該好好休息一下。

items.en: She pretended not to see me in the street.
items.zh: 她在街上假裝沒看到我。

examples.heading: ⑥ 動詞 + not to + 原形動詞

items.en: I've decided not to buy that phone. It's too expensive.
items.zh: 我決定不買那支手機了。太貴了。

items.en: "Don't tell Mum." "OK, I promise not to say anything."
items.zh: 別告訴媽媽。好，我保證什麼都不說。

items.en: Most people choose not to work on Sundays.
items.zh: 大部分的人選擇星期天不工作。

examples.heading: ⑦ 動詞 + to be + 動詞-ing

items.en: The baby seems to be sleeping. Let's talk quietly.
items.zh: 寶寶好像在睡覺。我們小聲講話吧。

items.en: The prices appear to be going up every month.
items.zh: 物價好像每個月都在漲。

items.en: "What's Anna doing?" "She seems to be studying, but I think she's on her phone."
items.zh: Anna 在做什麼？她好像在讀書，可是我覺得她在玩手機。

examples.heading: ⑧ 動詞 + to have + 過去分詞

items.en: It's freezing in here. Someone seems to have left the window open.
items.zh: 這裡好冷。好像有人沒關窗。

items.en: "Where's Dad?" "He appears to have gone out. His coat isn't here."
items.zh: 爸爸呢？他好像出去了。他的外套不在。

items.en: The shop seems to have closed down. The windows are empty.
items.zh: 那家店好像收掉了。櫥窗都空了。

items.en: He pretended to have read the book, but he didn't know the ending.
items.zh: 他假裝讀過那本書，可是他不知道結局。

title: I think I left my phone in your kitchen.
translation: 我想我把手機忘在你家廚房了。
name: 動詞加省略 that 的受詞子句
sentences: "Where's my phone?" "I think you left it in the car."
I think you should go and see the Twin Towers when you're in Kuala Lumpur.
"Is this the right bus?" "I don't think it is. Ask the driver."
My sister thinks the new teacher is great.
I thought you were at work today.
I know it's impossible for you to come during the exams.
"Sorry I'm late." "It's OK. I know the traffic is bad today."
Did you know Tom is moving to Spain?
We all knew she was the best player in the team.
It's my birthday on Friday, buddy. I hope you can make it.
"I have a job interview tomorrow." "Good luck! I hope it goes well."
Here is your key, Mr Brown. We hope everything in the room is OK.
"The road is closed." "Really? I hope there's another way to the airport."
My mother said you can come to our house at 6.30.
"What did the doctor say?" "She said I need to rest for a week."
The man at the desk said the room would be ready at two.
Everyone says this café makes the best coffee in town.
"Who's at the door?" "I guess it's the pizza."
I guess you're tired after the long flight.
I feel we should leave now, before it gets dark.
"Did you lock the door?" "Yes, I'm sure I locked it."
Are you sure this is the right address?
I don't think we have enough milk for breakfast.
"Is Anna coming tonight?" "I don't know. She didn't say she was."
Do you think it'll be sunny tomorrow?
"Do you think he likes the present?" "He's smiling, so yes!"
"Where's Dad?" "He said he was going to the shop."
When I saw his face, I knew something was wrong.
I thought the film started at eight, but it started at seven.
Hi Sam, I think I saw your brother at the gym today.
Dear Grandma, I hope you're feeling better now.
Thanks for the photos. I know you worked hard on them.

examples.heading: ① think + 子句

items.en: "Where's my phone?" "I think you left it in the car."
items.zh: 我的手機在哪裡？我想你忘在車上了。

items.en: I think you should go and see the Twin Towers when you're in Kuala Lumpur.
items.zh: 你去吉隆坡的時候，我覺得你應該去看雙子星大樓。

items.en: "Is this the right bus?" "I don't think it is. Ask the driver."
items.zh: 這是對的公車嗎？我想不是。問問司機。

items.en: My sister thinks the new teacher is great.
items.zh: 我姊姊覺得新老師很棒。

items.en: I thought you were at work today.
items.zh: 我以為你今天在上班。

examples.heading: ② know + 子句

items.en: I know it's impossible for you to come during the exams.
items.zh: 我知道考試期間你不可能來。

items.en: "Sorry I'm late." "It's OK. I know the traffic is bad today."
items.zh: 抱歉我遲到了。沒關係。我知道今天交通很糟。

items.en: Did you know Tom is moving to Spain?
items.zh: 你知道 Tom 要搬去西班牙嗎？

items.en: We all knew she was the best player in the team.
items.zh: 我們都知道她是隊上最好的球員。

examples.heading: ③ hope + 子句

items.en: It's my birthday on Friday, buddy. I hope you can make it.
items.zh: 兄弟，星期五是我生日。希望你能來。

items.en: "I have a job interview tomorrow." "Good luck! I hope it goes well."
items.zh: 我明天有個工作面試。祝你好運！希望一切順利。

items.en: Here is your key, Mr Brown. We hope everything in the room is OK.
items.zh: Brown 先生，這是您的鑰匙。希望房間裡的一切都沒問題。

items.en: "The road is closed." "Really? I hope there's another way to the airport."
items.zh: 那條路封了。真的嗎？希望有別的路可以去機場。

examples.heading: ④ say + 子句

items.en: My mother said you can come to our house at 6.30.
items.zh: 我媽說你可以六點半來我們家。

items.en: "What did the doctor say?" "She said I need to rest for a week."
items.zh: 醫生怎麼說？她說我需要休息一星期。

items.en: The man at the desk said the room would be ready at two.
items.zh: 櫃檯的男人說房間兩點會準備好。

items.en: Everyone says this café makes the best coffee in town.
items.zh: 大家都說這家咖啡店的咖啡是城裡最好的。

examples.heading: ⑤ guess / feel / be sure + 子句

items.en: "Who's at the door?" "I guess it's the pizza."
items.zh: 誰在門口？我猜是披薩到了。

items.en: I guess you're tired after the long flight.
items.zh: 我猜你搭了那麼久的飛機一定很累。

items.en: I feel we should leave now, before it gets dark.
items.zh: 我覺得我們應該現在走，趁天還沒黑。

items.en: "Did you lock the door?" "Yes, I'm sure I locked it."
items.zh: 你鎖門了嗎？鎖了，我確定我鎖了。

items.en: Are you sure this is the right address?
items.zh: 你確定這是對的地址嗎？

examples.heading: ⑥ 否定和問句

items.en: I don't think we have enough milk for breakfast.
items.zh: 我想我們的牛奶不夠吃早餐。

items.en: "Is Anna coming tonight?" "I don't know. She didn't say she was."
items.zh: Anna 今晚會來嗎？不知道。她沒說她會來。

items.en: Do you think it'll be sunny tomorrow?
items.zh: 你覺得明天會出太陽嗎？

items.en: "Do you think he likes the present?" "He's smiling, so yes!"
items.zh: 你覺得他喜歡這個禮物嗎？他在笑，所以喜歡啊！

examples.heading: ⑦ 動詞用過去式

items.en: "Where's Dad?" "He said he was going to the shop."
items.zh: 爸爸在哪裡？他說他要去商店。

items.en: When I saw his face, I knew something was wrong.
items.zh: 我一看到他的臉，就知道出事了。

items.en: I thought the film started at eight, but it started at seven.
items.zh: 我以為電影八點開始，結果七點就開始了。

examples.heading: ⑧ 在訊息和信裡

items.en: Hi Sam, I think I saw your brother at the gym today.
items.zh: 嗨 Sam，我想我今天在健身房看到你哥哥了。

items.en: Dear Grandma, I hope you're feeling better now.
items.zh: 親愛的奶奶，希望您現在覺得好一點了。

items.en: Thanks for the photos. I know you worked hard on them.
items.zh: 謝謝你的照片。我知道你花了很多心思。

title: You asked me to tell you about one of my friends.
translation: 你要我跟你介紹我的一個朋友。
name: 請求和命令動詞加受詞加不定詞
sentences: Thanks for your letter. You asked me to describe my village.
"Why are you still here?" "Mr Brown asked me to wait for him."
My neighbour asked us to keep the noise down after ten.
The room was very cold, so I asked the hotel to send up another blanket.
The teacher told us to open our books at page twenty.
"Why are you wearing a coat?" "Mum told me to take one. It might rain."
The police told everyone to leave the building.
My knee hurts, so the physio told me to stop running for a month.
Your parents want you to go on holiday with them this summer.
I would like you to come to a picnic on Saturday.
"Do you want me to drive?" "Yes, please. I'm really tired."
We would like you to come to our office on Monday to discuss the contract.
My boss wants me to work on Saturday again.
They invited us to stay with them in Italy.
Please remind me to call the dentist tomorrow.
"Did you buy the milk?" "No! Why didn't you remind me to get it?"
The bank advised us to keep our cards in a safe place.
My friend invited me to join her band.
The officer ordered the soldiers to stop.
The captain ordered everyone to put on a life jacket.
The guide warned us to stay on the path.
I have to go now. My dad told me not to be late for dinner.
The guide warned us not to swim in the river.
I asked my brother not to touch my computer.
The doctor advised him not to eat so much salt.
When we arrived, we were asked to wait outside.
All passengers are reminded to keep their bags with them.
"Why did you leave the party early?" "I was told to be home by eleven."
The students were told not to use their phones during the exam.
"What did the manager ask you to do?" "She asked me to check the stock."
This room is for staff only. Who told you to come in here?
Would you like me to carry your bag?

examples.heading: ① ask + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: Thanks for your letter. You asked me to describe my village.
items.zh: 謝謝你的來信。你要我描述一下我的村子。

items.en: "Why are you still here?" "Mr Brown asked me to wait for him."
items.zh: 你怎麼還在這裡？Brown 先生叫我等他。

items.en: My neighbour asked us to keep the noise down after ten.
items.zh: 我的鄰居請我們十點以後小聲一點。

items.en: The room was very cold, so I asked the hotel to send up another blanket.
items.zh: 房間很冷，所以我請飯店再送一條毯子上來。

examples.heading: ② tell + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: The teacher told us to open our books at page twenty.
items.zh: 老師叫我們把課本翻到第二十頁。

items.en: "Why are you wearing a coat?" "Mum told me to take one. It might rain."
items.zh: 你為什麼穿外套？媽媽叫我帶的。可能會下雨。

items.en: The police told everyone to leave the building.
items.zh: 警察叫大家離開大樓。

items.en: My knee hurts, so the physio told me to stop running for a month.
items.zh: 我的膝蓋痛，所以物理治療師叫我一個月不要跑步。

examples.heading: ③ want / would like + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: Your parents want you to go on holiday with them this summer.
items.zh: 你爸媽要你今年夏天跟他們去度假。

items.en: I would like you to come to a picnic on Saturday.
items.zh: 我希望你星期六來參加野餐。

items.en: "Do you want me to drive?" "Yes, please. I'm really tired."
items.zh: 要我來開車嗎？好，拜託。我好累。

items.en: We would like you to come to our office on Monday to discuss the contract.
items.zh: 我們希望您星期一來我們辦公室討論合約。

items.en: My boss wants me to work on Saturday again.
items.zh: 我老闆又要我星期六上班。

examples.heading: ④ invite / remind / advise + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: They invited us to stay with them in Italy.
items.zh: 他們邀請我們去義大利住他們家。

items.en: Please remind me to call the dentist tomorrow.
items.zh: 明天請提醒我打電話給牙醫。

items.en: "Did you buy the milk?" "No! Why didn't you remind me to get it?"
items.zh: 你買牛奶了嗎？沒有！你怎麼沒提醒我買？

items.en: The bank advised us to keep our cards in a safe place.
items.zh: 銀行勸我們把卡放在安全的地方。

items.en: My friend invited me to join her band.
items.zh: 我朋友邀請我加入她的樂團。

examples.heading: ⑤ order / warn + 受詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: The officer ordered the soldiers to stop.
items.zh: 軍官命令士兵們停下來。

items.en: The captain ordered everyone to put on a life jacket.
items.zh: 船長命令大家穿上救生衣。

items.en: The guide warned us to stay on the path.
items.zh: 導遊警告我們要走在步道上。

examples.heading: ⑥ 動詞 + 受詞 + not to + 原形動詞

items.en: I have to go now. My dad told me not to be late for dinner.
items.zh: 我得走了。我爸叫我吃晚飯不要遲到。

items.en: The guide warned us not to swim in the river.
items.zh: 導遊警告我們不要在河裡游泳。

items.en: I asked my brother not to touch my computer.
items.zh: 我叫我弟弟不要碰我的電腦。

items.en: The doctor advised him not to eat so much salt.
items.zh: 醫生勸他不要吃那麼多鹽。

examples.heading: ⑦ 被動：be + 過去分詞 + to + 原形動詞

items.en: When we arrived, we were asked to wait outside.
items.zh: 我們到的時候，被要求在外面等。

items.en: All passengers are reminded to keep their bags with them.
items.zh: 提醒所有乘客隨身攜帶行李。

items.en: "Why did you leave the party early?" "I was told to be home by eleven."
items.zh: 你為什麼那麼早離開派對？家裡叫我十一點前到家。

items.en: The students were told not to use their phones during the exam.
items.zh: 學生們被告知考試時不准用手機。

examples.heading: ⑧ 問句

items.en: "What did the manager ask you to do?" "She asked me to check the stock."
items.zh: 經理叫你做什麼？她叫我清點庫存。

items.en: This room is for staff only. Who told you to come in here?
items.zh: 這間是員工專用的房間。誰叫你進來的？

items.en: Would you like me to carry your bag?
items.zh: 要我幫你提包包嗎？

title: Nisha told me you had an accident last week.
translation: Nisha 跟我說你上禮拜出了意外。
name: 動詞加間接受詞和 that 子句
sentences: "How is Tom?" "Not great. His wife told me he has a bad cold."
I told my boss I was ill, so I stayed at home.
Did I tell you that my sister has a new car?
We were hungry, but the waiter told us the chef had gone home.
"Why are you so happy?" "My teacher told me I passed the exam!"
Please tell your parents that the school trip is on Friday.
You promised me that you would help me paint my bedroom.
"Can I have a dog?" "I promise you we'll talk about it at the weekend."
He promised his mum he would be home by ten.
The shop promised us the sofa would arrive on Monday.
The test results showed the doctor that my leg was broken.
Her smile showed me she liked the present.
This photo shows us that the old town was very small.
"Remind me that I have a meeting at three." "OK, I'll call you at half past two."
My phone reminded me it was Anna's birthday.
The teacher reminded the class that the library closes early on Fridays.
My grandfather taught me that hard work is important.
That trip taught us we needed a bigger tent.
Living alone taught her that she can look after herself.
Mia told the police she saw a man in a red coat.
Please tell the driver you want to get off at the bank.
I promised my best friend I would keep her secret.
The guide told the tourists the museum was free on Sundays.
"Did she tell you she was leaving?" "No, I had no idea."
Who told you that the party was cancelled?
"Didn't I tell you the shop was closed?" "Oh, sorry. I forgot."
You didn't tell me the meeting was at nine!
Nobody told us the train was late, so we waited for an hour.
My son didn't tell me he had homework.
"Does your boss know about the new job?" "No, I haven't told anyone that I'm leaving."
He never told his parents that he failed the test.

examples.heading: ① tell + 間接受詞 + 子句

items.en: "How is Tom?" "Not great. His wife told me he has a bad cold."
items.zh: Tom 怎麼樣？不太好。他太太跟我說他得了重感冒。

items.en: I told my boss I was ill, so I stayed at home.
items.zh: 我跟老闆說我生病了，所以我待在家。

items.en: Did I tell you that my sister has a new car?
items.zh: 我有跟你說過我姊姊買了新車嗎？

items.en: We were hungry, but the waiter told us the chef had gone home.
items.zh: 我們很餓，可是服務生跟我們說廚師已經回家了。

items.en: "Why are you so happy?" "My teacher told me I passed the exam!"
items.zh: 你為什麼這麼開心？老師跟我說我考試及格了！

items.en: Please tell your parents that the school trip is on Friday.
items.zh: 請跟你們的家長說校外教學是星期五。

examples.heading: ② promise + 間接受詞 + 子句

items.en: You promised me that you would help me paint my bedroom.
items.zh: 你答應過我會幫我油漆臥室。

items.en: "Can I have a dog?" "I promise you we'll talk about it at the weekend."
items.zh: 我可以養狗嗎？我答應你，我們週末會談這件事。

items.en: He promised his mum he would be home by ten.
items.zh: 他答應他媽媽十點前會回家。

items.en: The shop promised us the sofa would arrive on Monday.
items.zh: 店家答應我們沙發星期一會送到。

examples.heading: ③ show + 間接受詞 + 子句

items.en: The test results showed the doctor that my leg was broken.
items.zh: 檢查結果讓醫生看出我的腿斷了。

items.en: Her smile showed me she liked the present.
items.zh: 她的笑容讓我看出她喜歡這個禮物。

items.en: This photo shows us that the old town was very small.
items.zh: 這張照片讓我們看到舊城區以前很小。

examples.heading: ④ remind + 間接受詞 + 子句

items.en: "Remind me that I have a meeting at three." "OK, I'll call you at half past two."
items.zh: 提醒我三點有個會。好，我兩點半打給你。

items.en: My phone reminded me it was Anna's birthday.
items.zh: 我的手機提醒我今天是 Anna 的生日。

items.en: The teacher reminded the class that the library closes early on Fridays.
items.zh: 老師提醒全班圖書館星期五提早關門。

examples.heading: ⑤ teach + 間接受詞 + 子句

items.en: My grandfather taught me that hard work is important.
items.zh: 我爺爺教會我努力很重要。

items.en: That trip taught us we needed a bigger tent.
items.zh: 那次旅行讓我們學到我們需要一個大一點的帳篷。

items.en: Living alone taught her that she can look after herself.
items.zh: 一個人住讓她學到她能照顧好自己。

examples.heading: ⑥ 間接受詞是名詞

items.en: Mia told the police she saw a man in a red coat.
items.zh: Mia 跟警察說她看到一個穿紅外套的男人。

items.en: Please tell the driver you want to get off at the bank.
items.zh: 請跟司機說你要在銀行那站下車。

items.en: I promised my best friend I would keep her secret.
items.zh: 我答應我最好的朋友會幫她保守秘密。

items.en: The guide told the tourists the museum was free on Sundays.
items.zh: 導遊跟遊客說博物館星期天免費。

examples.heading: ⑦ 問句

items.en: "Did she tell you she was leaving?" "No, I had no idea."
items.zh: 她有跟你說她要走了嗎？沒有，我完全不知道。

items.en: Who told you that the party was cancelled?
items.zh: 誰跟你說派對取消了？

items.en: "Didn't I tell you the shop was closed?" "Oh, sorry. I forgot."
items.zh: 我不是跟你說店關了嗎？喔，抱歉。我忘了。

examples.heading: ⑧ 否定

items.en: You didn't tell me the meeting was at nine!
items.zh: 你沒跟我說會議是九點！

items.en: Nobody told us the train was late, so we waited for an hour.
items.zh: 沒有人跟我們說火車誤點，所以我們等了一個小時。

items.en: My son didn't tell me he had homework.
items.zh: 我兒子沒跟我說他有作業。

items.en: "Does your boss know about the new job?" "No, I haven't told anyone that I'm leaving."
items.zh: 你老闆知道新工作的事嗎？不知道，我還沒跟任何人說我要離職。

items.en: He never told his parents that he failed the test.
items.zh: 他從來沒跟爸媽說他考試沒過。

title: When I said to my friends that I had met him, they didn't believe me.
translation: 我跟朋友說我見過他，他們都不相信。
name: 轉述動詞加介系詞片語加 that 子句
sentences: When I said to my mum that I wanted to leave school, she was very upset.
"What did he say to you?" "He said to me that he was sorry."
You should say to your parents that you want to go on holiday with your friends.
Nobody said to us that the meeting had moved to Room 5.
"Why can't we come in?" The guard explained to us that the museum was closed for repairs.
I explained to the teacher that I had been ill.
The doctor explained to my dad that he needed an operation.
Can you explain to them that the flight is delayed?
"Is Sam leaving?" "Yes, he mentioned to me that he'd found a new job."
Did Anna mention to you that she's having a party?
I mentioned to the waiter that I don't eat meat.
He finally admitted to his wife that he had lost his job.
"Did you break the vase?" "Yes. I admitted to Mum that it was me."
She admitted to her friends that she was scared of flying.
We complained to the hotel manager that the room was dirty.
My neighbour complained to me that my music was too loud.
The students complained to the head teacher that the classroom was too cold.
We were lost, so I suggested to the others that we ask at the café.
My teacher suggested to me that I should try for a scholarship.
The young player wanted to prove to the coach that he was ready.
I pointed out to my boss that the report had a mistake.
"Why is she angry?" "I said to her that her dress was too short."
He explained to us that he couldn't come because of work.
They complained to him that the food was cold.
My son admitted to me that he hadn't done his homework.
He admitted that he had made a mistake.
The guide explained that the castle was over 800 years old.
"Did they like the hotel?" "No, they complained that it was noisy."
She mentioned that her brother lives in Paris.
My dad suggested that we leave early to avoid the traffic.
The news says that more people are cycling to work this year.

examples.heading: ① say to + 人 + that

items.en: When I said to my mum that I wanted to leave school, she was very upset.
items.zh: 我跟我媽說我想休學的時候，她很難過。

items.en: "What did he say to you?" "He said to me that he was sorry."
items.zh: 他跟你說了什麼？他跟我說他很抱歉。

items.en: You should say to your parents that you want to go on holiday with your friends.
items.zh: 你應該跟你爸媽說你想和朋友去度假。

items.en: Nobody said to us that the meeting had moved to Room 5.
items.zh: 沒有人跟我們說會議改到五號會議室了。

examples.heading: ② explain to + 人 + that

items.en: "Why can't we come in?" The guard explained to us that the museum was closed for repairs.
items.zh: 我們為什麼不能進去？警衛跟我們解釋說博物館在整修，所以沒開。

items.en: I explained to the teacher that I had been ill.
items.zh: 我跟老師解釋說我之前生病了。

items.en: The doctor explained to my dad that he needed an operation.
items.zh: 醫生跟我爸解釋說他需要動手術。

items.en: Can you explain to them that the flight is delayed?
items.zh: 你可以跟他們解釋班機延誤了嗎？

examples.heading: ③ mention to + 人 + that

items.en: "Is Sam leaving?" "Yes, he mentioned to me that he'd found a new job."
items.zh: Sam 要走了嗎？對，他跟我提到他找到新工作了。

items.en: Did Anna mention to you that she's having a party?
items.zh: Anna 有跟你提到她要辦派對嗎？

items.en: I mentioned to the waiter that I don't eat meat.
items.zh: 我跟服務生提到我不吃肉。

examples.heading: ④ admit to + 人 + that

items.en: He finally admitted to his wife that he had lost his job.
items.zh: 他終於向太太承認他丟了工作。

items.en: "Did you break the vase?" "Yes. I admitted to Mum that it was me."
items.zh: 花瓶是你打破的嗎？對。我跟媽媽承認是我。

items.en: She admitted to her friends that she was scared of flying.
items.zh: 她向朋友承認她怕坐飛機。

examples.heading: ⑤ complain to + 人 + that

items.en: We complained to the hotel manager that the room was dirty.
items.zh: 我們向飯店經理抱怨房間很髒。

items.en: My neighbour complained to me that my music was too loud.
items.zh: 我的鄰居向我抱怨我的音樂太大聲。

items.en: The students complained to the head teacher that the classroom was too cold.
items.zh: 學生們向校長抱怨教室太冷。

examples.heading: ⑥ suggest / prove / point out to + 人 + that

items.en: We were lost, so I suggested to the others that we ask at the café.
items.zh: 我們迷路了，所以我向其他人建議去咖啡店問路。

items.en: My teacher suggested to me that I should try for a scholarship.
items.zh: 我的老師建議我試著申請獎學金。

items.en: The young player wanted to prove to the coach that he was ready.
items.zh: 那個年輕球員想向教練證明他準備好了。

items.en: I pointed out to my boss that the report had a mistake.
items.zh: 我向老闆指出報告裡有一個錯誤。

examples.heading: ⑦ 聽話的人是代名詞

items.en: "Why is she angry?" "I said to her that her dress was too short."
items.zh: 她為什麼生氣？我跟她說她的洋裝太短了。

items.en: He explained to us that he couldn't come because of work.
items.zh: 他跟我們解釋說他因為工作不能來。

items.en: They complained to him that the food was cold.
items.zh: 他們向他抱怨食物是冷的。

items.en: My son admitted to me that he hadn't done his homework.
items.zh: 我兒子向我承認他沒寫作業。

examples.heading: ⑧ 不說出聽話的人

items.en: He admitted that he had made a mistake.
items.zh: 他承認他犯了錯。

items.en: The guide explained that the castle was over 800 years old.
items.zh: 導遊解釋說那座城堡有八百多年的歷史了。

items.en: "Did they like the hotel?" "No, they complained that it was noisy."
items.zh: 他們喜歡那家飯店嗎？不喜歡，他們抱怨很吵。

items.en: She mentioned that her brother lives in Paris.
items.zh: 她提到她哥哥住在巴黎。

items.en: My dad suggested that we leave early to avoid the traffic.
items.zh: 我爸建議我們早點出發，避開車潮。

items.en: The news says that more people are cycling to work this year.
items.zh: 新聞說今年騎腳踏車上班的人變多了。

title: I love listening to music, especially hip-hop music.
translation: 我很愛聽音樂，尤其是嘻哈音樂。
name: 表示喜好的動詞加不定詞或動詞-ing
sentences: Hi, I'm Kenji. I love playing the drums in my free time.
"What do you do at the weekend?" "I love cooking and also baking."
My kids love playing in the snow.
My grandfather loves telling us about his time in the army.
We love sitting in the garden on summer evenings.
"Do you play any sports?" "Yes, I love to play football."
My mum loves to cook for big family dinners.
She loves to read in bed before she goes to sleep.
They love to travel, so they save all their money for holidays.
I hate wearing trousers in summer. It's too hot.
My son hates going to bed early on Saturdays.
"Do you want to go to the gym with me?" "No, thanks. I hate exercising."
My dad hates waiting at the doctor's.
I hate to watch any sports on TV. It's so boring.
She hates to be late, so she always leaves early.
My cat hates to get wet.
We hate to leave the dog alone at home.
"Shall we take a taxi?" "I prefer walking. It's only ten minutes."
My sister prefers studying in the library.
Most of my friends prefer chatting online.
I prefer to play football, but I often go to the gym.
"Do you want to eat out?" "I prefer to stay in tonight."
My boss prefers to get reports by email.
I prefer walking to driving in the city.
My son prefers playing games to doing homework.
We prefer to stay at home rather than go out on rainy days.
"Shall we watch TV?" "I prefer reading to watching TV, actually."
"Do you love living in London?" "Yes, but I don't love paying the rent!"
"Do you prefer to work in the morning or at night?" "In the morning."
"Does your daughter hate getting up early?" "Yes, every school day!"
I don't hate cleaning, but I prefer to cook.

examples.heading: ① love + 動詞-ing

items.en: Hi, I'm Kenji. I love playing the drums in my free time.
items.zh: 嗨，我是 Kenji。我空閒時很愛打鼓。

items.en: "What do you do at the weekend?" "I love cooking and also baking."
items.zh: 你週末都做什麼？我很愛煮飯，也愛烤東西。

items.en: My kids love playing in the snow.
items.zh: 我的孩子很愛在雪地裡玩。

items.en: My grandfather loves telling us about his time in the army.
items.zh: 我爺爺很愛跟我們講他當兵的事。

items.en: We love sitting in the garden on summer evenings.
items.zh: 我們很愛在夏天的傍晚坐在院子裡。

examples.heading: ② love + to + 原形動詞

items.en: "Do you play any sports?" "Yes, I love to play football."
items.zh: 你有做什麼運動嗎？有，我很愛踢足球。

items.en: My mum loves to cook for big family dinners.
items.zh: 我媽很愛為家族聚餐煮飯。

items.en: She loves to read in bed before she goes to sleep.
items.zh: 她很愛睡前躺在床上看書。

items.en: They love to travel, so they save all their money for holidays.
items.zh: 他們很愛旅行，所以把錢都存下來去度假。

examples.heading: ③ hate + 動詞-ing

items.en: I hate wearing trousers in summer. It's too hot.
items.zh: 我很討厭夏天穿長褲。太熱了。

items.en: My son hates going to bed early on Saturdays.
items.zh: 我兒子很討厭星期六早睡。

items.en: "Do you want to go to the gym with me?" "No, thanks. I hate exercising."
items.zh: 你要跟我去健身房嗎？不了，謝謝。我很討厭運動。

items.en: My dad hates waiting at the doctor's.
items.zh: 我爸很討厭在診所等。

examples.heading: ④ hate + to + 原形動詞

items.en: I hate to watch any sports on TV. It's so boring.
items.zh: 我很討厭看電視上的任何運動比賽。好無聊。

items.en: She hates to be late, so she always leaves early.
items.zh: 她很討厭遲到，所以總是很早出門。

items.en: My cat hates to get wet.
items.zh: 我的貓很討厭弄濕。

items.en: We hate to leave the dog alone at home.
items.zh: 我們很討厭把狗單獨留在家。

examples.heading: ⑤ prefer + 動詞-ing

items.en: "Shall we take a taxi?" "I prefer walking. It's only ten minutes."
items.zh: 我們要搭計程車嗎？我比較喜歡走路。只要十分鐘。

items.en: My sister prefers studying in the library.
items.zh: 我妹比較喜歡在圖書館念書。

items.en: Most of my friends prefer chatting online.
items.zh: 我大部分的朋友比較喜歡在網路上聊天。

examples.heading: ⑥ prefer + to + 原形動詞

items.en: I prefer to play football, but I often go to the gym.
items.zh: 我比較喜歡踢足球，可是我常常去健身房。

items.en: "Do you want to eat out?" "I prefer to stay in tonight."
items.zh: 你想出去吃嗎？我今晚比較想待在家。

items.en: My boss prefers to get reports by email.
items.zh: 我老闆比較喜歡用電子郵件收報告。

examples.heading: ⑦ prefer 比較兩件事

items.en: I prefer walking to driving in the city.
items.zh: 在市區，比起開車，我比較喜歡走路。

items.en: My son prefers playing games to doing homework.
items.zh: 比起寫功課，我兒子比較喜歡打電動。

items.en: We prefer to stay at home rather than go out on rainy days.
items.zh: 下雨天我們寧願待在家，也不想出門。

items.en: "Shall we watch TV?" "I prefer reading to watching TV, actually."
items.zh: 我們要看電視嗎？其實比起看電視，我比較喜歡看書。

examples.heading: ⑧ 否定和問句

items.en: "Do you love living in London?" "Yes, but I don't love paying the rent!"
items.zh: 你很喜歡住在倫敦嗎？喜歡，可是我不喜歡付房租！

items.en: "Do you prefer to work in the morning or at night?" "In the morning."
items.zh: 你比較喜歡早上還是晚上工作？早上。

items.en: "Does your daughter hate getting up early?" "Yes, every school day!"
items.zh: 你女兒很討厭早起嗎？對，每個上學日都是！

items.en: I don't hate cleaning, but I prefer to cook.
items.zh: 我不討厭打掃，可是我比較喜歡煮飯。

title: I'd like to invite you to dinner on Sunday.
translation: 我想邀請你星期天來吃晚餐。
name: would like to 加不定詞
sentences: Hi Ben, I'd like to show you our new garden. Are you free on Sunday?
We'd like to invite you to our wedding in June.
I'd like to take you out for lunch to say thank you.
Good morning. I'd like to open a bank account, please.
I'd like to meet you to give you some information about the shops near your hotel.
"Can I help you?" "Yes, I'd like to try on these jeans."
I'd like to visit my grandparents this weekend.
After university, I'd like to work abroad for a year.
My mother would like to speak to the manager.
The students would like to ask you some questions.
Our son would like to learn the guitar.
Tom says he'd like to come with us to the lake.
"Good evening, Sunny Hostel." "Hello. I would like to cancel a booking for tomorrow."
Dear Ms Wang, I would like to apply for the job of shop assistant.
"Good morning, City Hotel. How can I help you?" "Hello, I'd like to change my booking."
We would like to tell you about our new opening hours.
"Would you like to come to my party on Saturday?" "Yes, I'd love to!"
Would you like to see my photos from Japan?
"Would you like to sit down?" "Thanks, I'm fine."
Would your children like to play in the garden?
"Would you like to have a coffee after work?" "Sure, where?"
"What would you like to do tonight?" "Let's stay in and watch a film."
"Where would you like to go for your holiday?" "Somewhere warm."
"What would you like to eat?" "Something light, please."
"Would you like to join our team?" "I'd like to, but I don't have time."
"Do you want to come to the cinema?" "Yes, I'd like to."
"Would you like to stay for dinner?" "I'd like to, but my mum is waiting for me."
I wouldn't like to live in a big city. It's too noisy.
My sister goes to bed at nine, so she wouldn't like to work at night.
It's a very cold country. I wouldn't like to go there in winter.
"Would you like to be famous?" "No, I wouldn't like to."

examples.heading: ① I'd like to：邀請

items.en: Hi Ben, I'd like to show you our new garden. Are you free on Sunday?
items.zh: 嗨，Ben，我想帶你看看我們的新花園。你星期天有空嗎？

items.en: We'd like to invite you to our wedding in June.
items.zh: 我們想邀請你參加我們六月的婚禮。

items.en: I'd like to take you out for lunch to say thank you.
items.zh: 我想請你吃午餐，謝謝你。

examples.heading: ② I'd like to：說自己想做的事

items.en: Good morning. I'd like to open a bank account, please.
items.zh: 早安。我想開一個銀行帳戶。

items.en: I'd like to meet you to give you some information about the shops near your hotel.
items.zh: 我想跟你見個面，給你一些飯店附近商店的資訊。

items.en: "Can I help you?" "Yes, I'd like to try on these jeans."
items.zh: 需要幫忙嗎？好，我想試穿這件牛仔褲。

items.en: I'd like to visit my grandparents this weekend.
items.zh: 我這個週末想去看我爺爺奶奶。

items.en: After university, I'd like to work abroad for a year.
items.zh: 大學畢業以後，我想去國外工作一年。

examples.heading: ③ 主詞是第三人稱單數或複數

items.en: My mother would like to speak to the manager.
items.zh: 我媽想跟經理說話。

items.en: The students would like to ask you some questions.
items.zh: 學生們想問你幾個問題。

items.en: Our son would like to learn the guitar.
items.zh: 我們兒子想學吉他。

items.en: Tom says he'd like to come with us to the lake.
items.zh: Tom 說他想跟我們一起去湖邊。

examples.heading: ④ 正式的信和電話

items.en: "Good evening, Sunny Hostel." "Hello. I would like to cancel a booking for tomorrow."
items.zh: 晚安，Sunny Hostel。你好。我想取消明天的訂房。

items.en: Dear Ms Wang, I would like to apply for the job of shop assistant.
items.zh: 王小姐您好，我想應徵店員的工作。

items.en: "Good morning, City Hotel. How can I help you?" "Hello, I'd like to change my booking."
items.zh: 早安，City Hotel，需要什麼服務？你好，我想更改我的訂房。

items.en: We would like to tell you about our new opening hours.
items.zh: 我們想告訴您我們新的營業時間。

examples.heading: ⑤ Would you like to ...?：邀請

items.en: "Would you like to come to my party on Saturday?" "Yes, I'd love to!"
items.zh: 你星期六想來我的派對嗎？好啊，我很想去！

items.en: Would you like to see my photos from Japan?
items.zh: 你想看我在日本拍的照片嗎？

items.en: "Would you like to sit down?" "Thanks, I'm fine."
items.zh: 你想坐下嗎？謝謝，我沒關係。

items.en: Would your children like to play in the garden?
items.zh: 你的孩子們想去院子裡玩嗎？

items.en: "Would you like to have a coffee after work?" "Sure, where?"
items.zh: 下班後想喝杯咖啡嗎？好啊，去哪裡？

examples.heading: ⑥ 問對方想做什麼

items.en: "What would you like to do tonight?" "Let's stay in and watch a film."
items.zh: 你今晚想做什麼？我們待在家看電影吧。

items.en: "Where would you like to go for your holiday?" "Somewhere warm."
items.zh: 你想去哪裡度假？暖和的地方。
